We evaluate A2HTrans on 14 Android applications spanning diverse sizes and domains using Claude-Sonnet-4.6 as the underlying migration model. Compared with Claude Code, A2HTrans preserves 8.3% more functional completeness, improves behavioral correctness by 8.0%, and reduces migration time by 28.8%. These results demonstrate that structured agentic execution substantially improves the reliability and efficiency of project-level cross-platform software migration.

title: Infinite dimensional Gaussian limits for the giant component of inhomogeneous random graphs
abstract: We prove Gaussian limits for the type measure of the giant component in sparse inhomogeneous random graphs. Countable types yield convergence in a weighted Hilbert space under boundedness, irreducibility, supercriticality, and a uniform tail condition on the empirical type weights. For types on a finite dimensional closed Riemannian manifold, smooth kernels yield convergence in a negative Sobolev space for any Borel type distribution. We allow deterministic types and first order kernel perturbations; independent type sampling adds an independent Gaussian term. The proof combines a seeded exploration identity, Hilbert space martingale limits, tail estimates, and inversion of the branching operator outside the giant. Finite types with random parameters are covered. A heat kernel example gives explicit variances for all spectral modes.

title: Monotonicity of Wang's recursive sequence and logarithmically complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the inverse tangent
abstract: In this paper, we study a sequence $b_n$, posed by Fei Wang, which is defined by $b_1=\frac13$ and a convolution-type recursive relation. We derive the generating functions of $nb_n$ and of $b_n$, the latter of which is $\ln\frac{\operatorname{arctanh}x}{x}$, and represent $b_n$ as a moment integral over $[0,1]$ with a positive density. From this representation we prove that the sequence $b_n$ is positive and logarithmically convex, that the sequence $nb_n$ is strictly decreasing, and that the ratio $\frac{b_{n+1}}{b_n}$ is strictly increasing in $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with limit $1$, which answers Wang's problem. We also give a determinantal expression and closed-form formulas for $b_n$ involving Stirling numbers of the first kind and partial Bell polynomials. Finally, we prove that the function $\frac1{\arctan x}$ is logarithmically completely monotonic on $(0,\infty)$.

title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact Kähler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.

title: Optimal Dividends and Voluntary Liquidation under Omega-Type Regulatory Termination
abstract: We study a joint optimal dividend and voluntary liquidation problem for a company whose surplus follows a spectrally negative Lévy process and is subject to Omega-type regulatory termination. Dividend payments are modeled as a singular control, while voluntary liquidation is an optimal stopping decision with a state-dependent liquidation payoff. When the surplus falls below a regulatory solvency threshold, an Omega clock accumulates the time spent in distress and may terminate the firm before voluntary liquidation occurs. Under dynamic programming and continuity assumptions for an auxiliary Markov subproblem, we characterize its value as the smallest controlled stochastic supersolution of the associated quasi-variational inequality. We prove that any regular stochastic solution with a dividend barrier coincides with the value function over all admissible dividend and liquidation policies, and hence is unique within this class. Using $ω$-scale functions, we construct single-band, singleton, and no-liquidation candidates, establish sufficient conditions for global optimality, and give conditions under which these candidates supply the unique regular barrier stochastic solution. Brownian and Cramér--Lundberg examples illustrate how regulatory parameters affect dividend and liquidation boundaries and generate transitions between policy regimes.

title: Dhara: Evidence-Oriented Retrieval for Indian Knowledge Systems
abstract: Relevant evidence in Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) collections may be distributed across passages in different parts of a work, including verses, translations, and commentaries. Locating it requires matching natural-language questions and partially remembered verse fragments to source passages. We present Dhara, a retrieval engine combining hybrid search, chapter- and book-level Entity Notes (EN), Fuzzy Verse Retrieval (FVR), and neural reranking. Five comparisons on the 325 questions in Dhara Bench examine retrieval representations against BM25, EN's contribution, reranker quality and computation time, FVR, and Gemini. BGE-M3 single-vector retrieval exceeds BM25 in nDCG@10, Recall@20, and MRR@20 across all categories. Its scores are broadly comparable to ColBERTv2, with mean retrieval times of 0.108 s and 0.962 s under the same hardware configuration and a smaller memory footprint for chunk storage on disk. Adding EN to a direct branch with a matched candidate count improves nDCG@10 in all twelve categories with Qwen and ten with BGE; the combined ranking is capped at the same candidate count. Qwen improves nDCG@10, Precision@5, and MRR@20 over BGE in every category, at approximately 6.72 times the overall estimated serial computation time. FVR increases Verse-category nDCG@10 by approximately 20 percentage points with either reranker. Gemini is evaluated after source mapping and manual review with relevance annotations visible. The Qwen pipeline with EN and FVR has higher Recall@20 than Gemini in ten categories and stronger complete-evidence retrieval in Multi-hop questions, while Gemini retains early-relevance advantages in several categories. The results inform retrieval choices according to evidence requirements and resource budgets.

title: On the sharpness of a Liouville exponent in a competitive elliptic Schrödinger system
abstract: We identify $p_*(n)=(n-1)/(n-3)$, $n\geq 5$, as the sharp exponent for Liouville theorems concerning a two-component elliptic Schrödinger system with self-focusing interactions and repulsive intercomponent coupling. We consider the strictly copositive regime, in which the repulsion strength is smaller than the geometric mean of the two self-interaction strengths. Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) established a Liouville-type nonexistence result in the range $1<p<p_*(n)$. For every $p_*(n)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct bounded, nontrivial, nonnegative entire solutions whenever the repulsion strength approaches the copositivity threshold from below. The construction combines a compact variational functional, a periodic spectral gap, and uniform exterior estimates that remove a truncation. Our result gives a negative answer to the open question posed by Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) of whether strict copositivity implies nonexistence of nontrivial nonnegative entire solutions throughout the Sobolev subcritical range when $n\geq 5$.

title: Decidability of Elementary Modal Logics is Undecidable
abstract: We study the decidability of modal satisfiability over classes of Kripke frames defined by universal first-order sentences. Although some such classes yield undecidable satisfiability problems, decidability is guaranteed for wide families of frame conditions, including universal Horn sentences and universal sentences implying transitivity. A more than decade-old open problem asks a natural question: can decidable and undecidable cases be distinguished algorithmically? We prove that this is impossible, already for equality-free universal frame conditions over a single binary relation. More precisely, there is no algorithm that, given such a condition, decides whether its associated local modal satisfiability problem is decidable. We first establish the result for conditions with equality and then eliminate equality by passing to quotients of worlds with identical incoming and outgoing edges.

title: Source-Anchored Visual Autoregression for Extreme Image Compression
abstract: In the extreme-low bitrate range below $0.01$ bpp, image compression becomes a constrained generation problem: the reconstruction depends on inferring plausible missing details while staying close to the input image. Autoregressive token models provide an efficient coarse-to-fine prior for this setting, but the transmitted early-scale tokens often leave object identity and texture underdetermined, which can lead to source-inconsistent reconstructions. We introduce Source-Anchored Visual Autoregression (SAVAR), a generative codec built on Visual Autoregressive (VAR) modeling. SAVAR transmits early-scale tokens and a compact caption. The tokens provide image-specific layout information, while the caption supplies global semantics. SAVAR reconstructs a partial VQ-VAE latent from the retained scales, maps it to the start-of-sequence initialization, and uses the same latent to condition the caption embedding before adaptive layer normalization, separating two roles that are typically driven by a shared condition in VAR-style generation. On the Kodak and CLIC2020 datasets in the extreme-low range, SAVAR reduces perceptual distortion relative to matched ARPC retained-scale operating points, lowering LPIPS by about $8$--$9\%$ and DISTS by up to $22\%$ at a lower bpp. It reconstructs a $512 \times 512$ image in about $218$ ms on one NVIDIA L20X GPU, retaining fast autoregressive decoding in the evaluated setting.

title: When Self-Consistency Hurts: The Hidden Cost of Majority Voting in Small Language Models
abstract: We study prompted chain-of-thought (CoT) with self-consistency (SC), i.e. sampling N traces and plurality-voting, on small language models, a regime where per-query compute budgets are tight yet SC is commonly applied with a fixed sample budget inherited from large-model practice, regardless of instance difficulty. Across two model families (Qwen-2.5-0.5B, Gemma-3-1B) at FP16 and MLX-Q4 (4-bit quantisation in Apple's MLX framework), on GSM8K and MATH-500, we run 8 per-task and 4 task-pooled experiments at n=200-400 with 1,000x paired-bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs). Our first result is an upper bound: an oracle gate deciding per prompt whether to invoke SC reaches 109-174% of always-SC's accuracy at 23-30% of its compute in all 12/12 cases, so at N=5 always-SC is dominated everywhere on our grid. That margin is exactly the rate at which SC flips correct greedy answers to wrong, here 3-10.5% of prompts, which on Qwen-Q4 x MATH-500 exceeds the wrong-to-right rate and leaves always-SC 3 pt worse than always-greedy. Our second result is a deployable approximation: a gate over greedy-pass signals skips 45-99% of SC calls, with bootstrap CI half-widths under 5 pt, removing 36-79% of always-SC compute. Accuracy retention at those operating points has point estimates of 98.1-98.8%, which we report as point estimates because their CIs are wide (lower bounds 76-86%) over an SC accuracy of only 15-36%. The evidence covers N=5 on two <=1B families and two math benchmarks, which is the scope we claim. Code is available at https://github.com/heywanrong/SiftSC.

title: Holographic dissociation of tetraquark and hybrid meson in the spinning plasma
abstract: We explore the dissociation of the tetraquark \(Z_c\) and the hybrid meson \(π_1\) in a spinning quark-gluon plasma described by the planar limit of a spinning Myers-Perry black hole. Both states are treated within one holographic framework, using a non-quadratic dilaton profile whose parameters are fixed by the \(Z_c\) and \(π_1\) mass spectra. Spectral functions are computed in the longitudinal and transverse channels. The boost parameter and temperature both lower the peak height and broaden the width, and the effect is stronger in the transverse channel. In both channels, the heavier 2S states melt before the 1S states. Furthermore, the two exotic channels display distinct dissociation behaviors within the same effective framework. This provides a unified holographic approach to compare how different exotic states behavior, without requiring a dynamical calculation of their binding energies.

title: Weak Dissolution of Groups for Rearrangement
abstract: Suppose that $k$ of $n$ classrooms are to be dissolved and their students moved to the other classrooms so that the numbers of students in any two remaining classrooms differ by at most $d$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on the numbers of students for this to be possible whichever $k$ classrooms are dissolved. Moreover, we determine how small the largest classroom can be when this is possible. In particular, when all classrooms have different sizes, the smallest possible size of the largest classroom is $d+\lceil (n-d-1)(n-d)/(2k)\rceil$ if $k<(n-d-1)/2$, and it is $n$ or $n+1$ otherwise. This extends the results of Siriseriwan and Sripatak, who studied the case $d=0$.

title: Not Yet in the Profile: Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic User Profiling by Learning from Future Interactions
abstract: On the Web, user profiling builds compact user representations from interaction histories for efficient personalization, and dynamic user profiling updates them as users' behavior and preferences change. However, new user behavior can be ambiguous, and its interpretation differs across users. To address this, we introduce Uncertainty-aware Adaptive Profile Manager (UAPM), which separates the claims in a user profile from interpretations of new behavior that are not yet confirmed, through a Profile, a Buffer, and a Rulebook. UAPM records user-specific interpretation and update rules in the Rulebook, keeps ambiguous evidence in the Buffer outside the Profile as evidence for later decisions, and writes supported general and situational characteristics to the Profile. We train UAPM with Privileged On-Policy Distillation with Dual Specialization (POPD-DS), which learns from recorded future interactions during training without access to them at deployment. Its first stage, Dual Specialization, distills a stronger model into a current-only Student and a future-informed model that becomes the Teacher. In the second stage, privileged on-policy distillation (POPD), only the fixed Teacher receives future interactions and guides the Student's own management decisions alongside task rewards. Experiments on three Web personalization tasks show that UAPM outperforms multiple baselines under the same downstream input budget, improving on the best same-budget baseline by up to 5%.

title: Independence number and odd dominating models
abstract: A dominating $K_t$-model, introduced by Illingworth and Wood [J. Graph Theory, 2025], is a sequence $(T_1,\dots,T_t)$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint subtrees of $G$ such that every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour in $T_i$ for $1\leq i<j\leq t$. Let $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model. We prove two dominating-model analogues of improvements to the classical Duchet-Meyniel bound [Ann. Discrete Math., 1982]. The first extends a result of Kawarabayashi, Plummer, and Toft [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2005]. Every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $α(G)\geq2$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)\geq(n+ω(G))/(2α(G)-1)$. Second, we prove a constant-factor improvement of the Duchet-Meyniel bound for dominating models: every graph $G$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)>0.51075n/α(G)$. This qualitatively extends the results of Fox [SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2010] and Balogh and Kostochka [Discrete Math., 2011]. An odd dominating $K_t$-model is a dominating $K_t$-model with an assignment of one of two colours to each vertex of $V(T_1)\cup\dots\cup V(T_t)$, such that every edge of each $T_i$ is bichromatic and, for $1\leq i<j\leq t$, some edge between $T_i$ and $T_j$ is monochromatic. Let $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model. Our constant-factor improvement of the Duchet-Meyniel bound relies on our next result: every claw-free graph $G$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)\geq 2χ(G)/3$, generalising a result of Chudnovsky and Fradkin [J. Graph Theory, 2010]. The factor 2/3 is best possible [arXiv:2512.20392]. For $t\geq2$, we prove that every $n$-vertex graph with no odd dominating $K_t$-model has independence number at least $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$. For the stronger notion in which every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour of the same colour in $T_i$, we prove the analogous results with $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$ replaced by $(n+t-1)/(3t-3)$.

title: Synergizing CKM and ISAC for Environment-Aware Wireless Networks
abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) have emerged as two key technologies for sixth-generation (6G) and beyond wireless networks, enabling a new paradigm toward environment-aware system design. CKMs provide static or stochastic wireless environment information a priori by learning location-dependent mappings from transceiver positions to channel knowledge of various types, whereas ISAC exploits wireless signals to sense environmental objects in real time. CKM and ISAC have primarily been studied separately in prior works, while their integration offers a promising approach for enhancing the environment awareness of 6G networks and further improving both sensing and communication capabilities. On the one hand, sensing can support CKM construction by providing location-tagged measurements and richer environmental observations, while also enabling real-time CKM refinement in dynamic environments. On the other hand, CKM can enhance sensing by offering prior environmental information for clutter mitigation, and CKM and sensing information can be jointly leveraged to improve communications. This article provides an overview of the complementary interactions between CKMs and ISAC, with particular emphasis on three design approaches: sensing-assisted CKM construction and refinement, CKM-assisted sensing, and joint CKM- and sensing-enhanced communications. We also discuss future research directions for achieving environment-aware wireless networks.

title: On the Kőnig-Egerváry theorem for $k$-trees
abstract: The famous Kőnig-Egerváry theorem is equivalent to the statement that a graph is bipartite if and only if the matching number equals the vertex cover number for every induced subgraph. Bessy, Ochem, and Rautenbach (J. Graph Theory 91 (2019) 73-87) generalized this theorem to $k$-paths by introducing the class $\mathcal{G}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint paths of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such paths. They provided complete structural characterizations of graphs in $\mathcal{G}_k$ for $k \in \{3, 4\}$, and for odd $k$ when no cycle of order less than $k$ is present. Inspired by this nice work, we extend the Kőnig-Egerváry theorem to $k$-trees (i.e., trees with exactly $k$ vertices). We define the class $\mathcal{J}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint trees of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such trees, and provide complete structural descriptions of graphs in $\mathcal{J}_k$ for all $k \ge 3$.

title: Multi-Granularity Communication-Computing Resource Mapping for User Association in MEO-Assisted LEO Satellite Networks
abstract: Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite networks are evolving into spaceborne communication-computing infrastructures. Their user association must jointly account for the radio link and the CPU, GPU, NPU, memory, cache, storage, energy, queue, and thermal states that determine executable service capacity. This paper studies a MEO-assisted LEO architecture in which medium-Earth-orbit (MEO) regional state aggregators collect and relay time-stamped telemetry, the network operation control center (NOCC) maintains the global logical resource view and makes the final association decisions, and LEO satellites provide access and onboard execution. We develop a multigranularity representation and service-primitive-driven mapping that converts a service-level request into a target-LEO-dependent quantized resource vector. The integer formulation, exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) reference, and a capacity-aware primal-dual algorithm share the same mapped objective. Experiments use real-world service bandwidth traces, a 1584-satellite LEO shell, multiple traffic seeds, controlled load and mapping error, delayed telemetry, and temporal sessions. Relative to static mapping, the proposed method improves realized utility by 10.64% and lowers end-to-end outage by 5.70 percentage points. Target quantization reduces signaling by 19.84% with negligible utility loss. Additional load, delay, temporal, runtime, and exact-MILP audits delimit the operating region and remaining mapping uncertainty.

title: Viscot-steer: Disentangling and Transferring Visual Chain-of-Thought via Activation Steering
abstract: Visual chain-of-thought (visual-CoT), also known as "thinking with images", equips LVLMs with the ability to locate and use key visual evidence for reasoning. However, acquiring such visual-CoT capabilities requires costly post-training and tightly couples them to a specific backbone, making transfer to other LVLMs difficult. Existing cross-model transfer methods typically treat visual-CoT as a monolithic capability, using a unified representation that ignores the functional distinction between grounding and reasoning and introduces stage-irrelevant interventions. To address this problem, we propose Viscot-steer, a training-free activation steering framework for transferring visual-CoT capabilities across heterogeneous LVLMs. Specifically, Viscot-steer first disentangles visual-CoT into grounding and reasoning vectors and extracts them from the source-model layers associated with the corresponding capabilities. It then aligns the vectors with the activation space of the target model and steers the grounding and reasoning layers during bounding-box prediction and reasoning-trace generation, respectively. Across benchmarks covering high-resolution visual understanding, general visual perception and reasoning, and mathematical visual reasoning, Viscot-steer transfers capabilities from different visual-CoT models to architecturally diverse LVLMs and outperforms the strongest capability-transfer baseline by an average of 1.86 percentage points on the primary evaluation metrics.

title: DynOLAT: OLAT Video Prediction for Controllable Dynamic Full-Body Relighting
abstract: Accurate lighting response is essential for realistic dynamic human relighting, because shadows, highlights, and color changes should follow the target illumination in both direction and relative strength. Current learning-based relighting methods can generate visually plausible videos, but they often exhibit imprecise lighting responses: shadows and highlights may drift away from the target direction, and the output brightness may not faithfully follow the relative intensities in the target environment, making the result closer to appearance harmonization than controllable relighting. To address this issue, we propose DynOLAT, a generalizable OLAT video prediction framework for dynamic full-body humans. Instead of directly synthesizing a single relit appearance, our method predicts temporally consistent One-Light-At-a-Time (OLAT) basis videos from flat-lit inputs, and then linearly combines the predicted bases according to the target environment map. This OLAT-based formulation makes the directional response explicit in the predicted bases, while the relative lighting strength is determined by the linear weights derived from the environment map. We further introduce a dynamic capture pipeline and the first large-scale dynamic full-body OLAT dataset, comprising over 24 million frames from 224 identity-outfit combinations, where different outfits of the same person define separate combinations. Experiments show that DynOLAT responds more faithfully to variations in target lighting direction and relative intensity than the tested baselines, enabling controllable video relighting while preserving fine appearance details and temporal coherence. The dataset and processing tools will be publicly released to foster future research.

title: The first-order phase transitions and gravitational waves from an effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models
abstract: First-order phase transitions in the early Universe can generate stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds in frequency bands targeted by proposed deci-Hz observatories. We study the gravitational-wave consequences of the right-handed gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2)_{R_1}\times SU(2)_{R_2}\to SU(2)_R$ in a Pati-Salam effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models. The ultraviolet construction fixes the gauge structure and particle multiplicities, while the scalar masses and quartic couplings are treated as renormalized inputs below the supersymmetry-breaking scale. Using a one-loop finite-temperature potential with ring resummation, we follow a strongly supercooled transition at the few-TeV scale through nucleation, percolation, completion, and reheating. The leading-order friction diagnostic does not support a runaway wall, so sound waves dominate the gravitational-wave signal, with turbulence as a sub-leading contribution; the finite acoustic lifetime suppresses the peak. For the fast-wall reference case, the spectrum peaks at $f_{\rm peak}=0.611$ Hz with $h^2Ω_{\rm GW,peak}=1.232\times10^{-11}$, in the deci-Hz band targeted by DECIGO and BBO. We present its dependence on the wall speed, renormalization scale, and thermal screening, together with a noise-only comparison for several proposed detector configurations.

title: Deterministic Narrative Gravity: Bridging Theory of Mind and Historical Simulation through ABM-LLM Architectures
abstract: Historical social simulation faces a fundamental reproducibility challenge: the stochastic nature of large language models (LLMs) introduces a digital butterfly effect that prevents exact replication across multi-turn runs. Furthermore, the inability to control low-level server parameters in commercial LLM hosting environments severely limits reproducibility. To overcome this opacity, we present a deterministic multi-agent framework coupling LLMs to an Agent-Based Modelling (ABM) pipeline grounded in Theory of Mind (ToM) and Cognitive Archaeology, and validate exact artifact identity within local, pinned execution environments using SHA-256 hashing. Run locally at temperature zero with clean per-call model reloads, the system injects differentiated cognitive states per turn through dissonance-driven behavioural modes and gated internal voices. Evaluating seven model configurations spanning 4B to 31B parameters against an ablated baseline reveals clear operational boundaries. Small models ($\leq$8B) suffer from context capacity overload, producing repetitive, specular dialogue loops. However, at $\geq$12B parameters, the ABM scaffolding breaks the monotonous response patterns seen in ablation. Crucially, these scaffolded models exhibit spontaneous diegetic expansion: they coherently expand scenario lore through tactically motivated, anachronism-free details rather than escalating into aggression. By resisting the structural pull toward premature scene closure, scaffolded sessions sustain an open terminal Narrative Vector ($V_N = \mathrm{Open}$ in 12/21 overall; 9/9 in official $\geq$12B configurations) whereas unscaffolded ablation never does (0/21). This framework provides a transparent, auditable benchmark architecture for virtual archaeology, with the full pipeline released as open-source software to enable independent replication.

title: NumericalDiff: Numerical Program Differencing via Value-Based Trace Alignment and Intervention
abstract: Numerical programs implementing the same computational task can exhibit different numerical behavior because of their execution stacks, program representations, or program logic. Source text and final outputs alone provide limited diagnostic information: numerical differences can propagate through corresponding computations, while distinct executions can produce equal outputs. We present NumericalDiff, an execution-based method that records assignment-level numerical events, aligns traces using a tolerance-aware longest common subsequence independent of variable names and source locations, and optionally reexecutes after replacing one intermediate value with its counterpart. Among the original and all single-intervention executions, it lexicographically maximizes matched events and minimizes unmatched events. NumericalDiff supports code comparison across language and framework front ends, currently including NumPy, PyTorch, JAX, C, C++, Fortran, and Octave. We evaluate NumericalDiff on 36 controlled cases comprising 675 pair/input instances: 36 execution-stack, 588 program-representation, and 51 program-logic instances. All 24 operator-injection instances expose trace differences, including three with tolerance-equal final outputs, while complete trace alignment is achieved for all 441 canonical cross-representation instances. Within the 51 program-logic instances, intervention improves 24 alignments and raises macro-average matching coverage from 0.4210 to 0.6513. The results show that value-based trace alignment and reexecution can delimit propagated numerical differences across heterogeneous implementations.

title: Disentangling Where and When:Factored Spatio-Temporal Explanations for Video Action Recognition
abstract: Post-hoc explanation methods for video action recognition typically conflate spatial appearance and temporal dynamics into a single saliency or importance map. We propose a perturbation-based framework that disentangles these contributions into a spatial appearance mask ($M_a$) and a temporal motion mask ($M_m$). The two masks are jointly optimized against a frozen action recognition model through factored perturbation architecture, with nearest frame replacement to identify important temporal dynamics. A separation penalty discourages the appearance mask from spending budget on frames that the motion mask has already discarded. A ReLU-based area constraint penalizes explanations larger than an assigned budget. To evaluate these explanations, we introduce a separation protocol that sweeps spatial pixels and temporal frames independently, backed by proofs characterizing the proposed method. Across EPIC-Kitchens-55, EGTEA Gaze+, and Something-Something V2, our method attains the lowest deletion AUC against leading baselines while producing masks roughly five times sparser.

title: Spot Markets for AI Inference: Dynamic Capacity Allocation and Pricing on a Shared Accelerator Fleet
abstract: Inference providers size their accelerator fleets for the interactive peak and sell spare capacity through fixed discounts, such as batch tiers at half price. However, inference differs from conventional cloud capacity in four respects: capacity depends on the latency tier through batching, moving weights between models is slow and costly, spot demand can wait until its deadline, and power can bind. In this paper, we develop a framework for dynamic capacity allocation and pricing of AI inference on a shared accelerator fleet. We consider a provider that serves several models under a power cap and sells each model in an interactive tier with a speed promise and in a spot tier for preemptible work with a deadline. In each period, the provider chooses how many replicas of each model to keep loaded and what spot price to quote. We show that one interactive token displaces a fixed number $ρ_m>1$ of spot tokens, and that the optimal spot price lies midway between the interactive price and the effective cost of capacity in the deadline window, which is close to the prevailing half price only when the fleet is slack. We further show that a spot tier raises the optimal reliability of the interactive tier, and that placement should follow persistent demand shifts while prices absorb transients. Building on these results, we design a model predictive controller based on a linear program with explicit approximation bounds, which solves each period in milliseconds. Numerical experiments on a simulated week with a measured daily demand profile, a flash crowd, and a grid curtailment show that the controller raises profit by 7.4% over fixed half-price practice, captures 93% of the gain available with perfect forecasts, keeps the interactive promise through both events, and leaves spot buyers better off.

title: Replay Fidelity in LLM Agent Evaluation: Randomness, Hidden State, and Test Oracles in AppWorld
abstract: Reproducibility in large language model (LLM) agent evaluation depends on replay fidelity: which parts of an execution trace are reconstructed, controlled, and compared. This matters for agent debugging, failure analysis, and counterfactual evaluation of stateful tool use. We audit all 71 unsuccessful executions in a fixed historical AppWorld corpus using 284 isolated fixed-code replay attempts. Reconstructed declared settings admit 42 cases under printed-output, pre-oracle database-delta, and native-verdict/test-count checks; resetting the random-number generator before each interaction admits 68. The 26-case gap contracts to four under database/oracle checks, with one endpoint unknown. Mechanism studies identify four materialized-state discrepancies despite matching outputs and verdicts. In one admitted endpoint pair, an identical API call yields matching responses but different row effects; common future Python RNG removes that deterministic difference in two paired repetitions. A separate JWT credential-equality program and alignment controls expose authentication/write differences, with missing repetitions retained. For all 10 affected post-oracle export cases, native export from retained output trackers restores the reference comparison without changing original cached contents. A purposeful 12-case BFCL pilot shows no discrepancy under its tested public-state, return, and verdict checks. We preserve resource censoring and infrastructure deviations. The contribution is a bounded empirical characterization of replay eligibility, hidden state, and test-oracle integration, without estimating debugger accuracy, repair gains, or method-ranking distortion.

title: scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses
abstract: Predicting single-cell transcriptional responses to genetic and chemical interventions supports gene-function discovery and regulatory analysis. Existing studies often focus only on highly variable genes, restricting the expression changes available for downstream analysis. Cells exposed to the same intervention can also show heterogeneous expression responses, with coordinated gene programs active to different degrees. We propose scBIG++, a full-gene perturbation prediction framework that models this heterogeneity by connecting expression-adaptive gene modules with population-conditioned generation. To preserve shared gene structure while accommodating cellular variation, Gene-Relation Clustering organizes genes into common windows, within which Dynamic SoftSub learns expression-dependent submodule memberships. This shared organization enables Set-GCAE to exchange information about corresponding gene groups across control cells, placing individual representations in their source-population context. The cell representations initialize a latent flow, while their pooled summary and the perturbation representation condition response generation. Generated states are decoded into expression profiles covering all assayed protein-coding genes retained after preprocessing, supporting comprehensive analysis of perturbation-induced expression changes. Experiments across six genetic and chemical settings spanning 6,539--19,451 genes demonstrate competitive perturbation-effect recovery and full-gene expression reconstruction under unseen targets and combinations, cross-cell-line transfer, and held-out compounds. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/ttruan2426-dot/scBIG.

title: Edge Computing for Computer Vision in IoT: Feasibility and Directions
abstract: The convergence of decentralized architectures integrating Machine Learning, Computer Vision and Low Power Wide Area Networks is increasingly becoming an integral part of our daily existence. Internet of Things serves as a real-time data conduit enhancing decision making via embedded technology and continuous data exchange. This paper explores the feasibility of Edge Computing as a foundational pillar in this evolving landscape. We experiment under real world, dynamic conditions, evaluate the technological aspects, strategies, process flows and key observations under the broad Edge Computing domain. Research pathways include Multi-access Edge topologies in future 6G networks, model quantization, and satellite-enhanced communication platforms. Additionally, a discussion is added supporting the advanced AI functionalities, including zero-shot learning, multi modal perception, and decentralized generative AI, thereby broadening the scope of intelligent applications across various domains. The significance and research objective of this study are threefold: (1) evaluation of LoRaWAN and satellite IoT communication strategies, (2) analysis of CV workloads on edge hardware and (3) future research directions where Edge Computing can support low-latency, energy-efficient and socially impactful IoT applications. By explicitly addressing these aspects, we aim to establish a clear link between the technological feasibility, ultimately with a practical and socioeconomic relevance.

title: A Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs and a $3$-Design Obstruction for Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1,k,q-k+2]_q$, where $q\ge3$ is a prime power and $2\le k\le q$. We prove a conjecture of Wu and Zhou by showing that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$ do not form a $q$-ary $3$-design when $2\le k\le q-1$. Using shortening, we extend this obstruction to every nonempty weight class with $3\le w<q+1$. We also establish that each individual nonempty positive-weight class of $\mathcal{C}_k$ forms a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1,q-1)=1$. Consequently, every nonempty positive-weight class below full support has exact $q$-ary design strength $2$ when this coprimality condition holds, and $1$ otherwise.The three-design obstruction follows by applying a classical subset-product character identity to a marginal covering count for three prescribed nonzero symbols. The comparison between weights rests on a covering-count formulation of the classical MDS coset-weight relations. For every linear $[n,k,d]_q$ MDS code with $2\le k\le n-1$, this formulation shows that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at any one nonempty positive weight is equivalent to the same property at every nonempty positive weight.More generally, for $2\le t\le\min\{k,d\}$, we prove that the $q$-ary $t$-design property at any $t-1$ distinct nonempty positive weights forces it at all nonempty positive weights.

title: EbbFlow: PINN-Inspired Progressive Curriculum for MeanFlow Training
abstract: MeanFlow learns interval-average velocity for few-step generation, but its fixed temporal sampler mixes diagonal and interior supervision throughout training. We interpret temporal coordinates as collocation points: diagonal samples provide a stochastic boundary target, whereas finite intervals supply a differential-consistency target. The diagonal fraction controls how often the consistency component appears, while interval length enters its gradient through an explicit factor. Motivated by this distinction, EbbFlow uses Temporal Supervision Allocation (TSA) to schedule the diagonal fraction and interval geometry. It starts with diagonal supervision, then admits interior samples and expands their maximum interval; a left-anchored interval law preserves coverage across time. The per-sample loss, target, backbone, and inference procedure remain unchanged. In matched class-conditional ImageNet $256\times 256$ runs without classifier-free guidance (DiT-B/2, one training seed per method, 400k updates), EbbFlow achieves 50k-sample FID of 39.65 at one network evaluation and 36.02 at two-evaluation ODE sampling, versus 44.82 and 39.86 for MeanFlow. Gradient probes show a mid-training difference in component geometry. Ablations support allocation scheduling and left-anchored intervals, although a fixed full-horizon variant performs better at one evaluation. These results suggest that temporal sampling is a useful training control whose benefits depend on the inference protocol.

title: Grid-forming Control of Offshore Wind through a Diode-Rectifier HVDC System: a 2 GW Case Study
abstract: Diode-rectifier-unit (DRU)-based high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission considerably reduces the volume and weight of the offshore converter platform for remote wind farms and, hence, its cost, but shifts the task of forming and regulating the offshore AC network to the wind-turbine converters. This paper examines which grid-forming control strategy is the most suitable for DRU power transfer. The DRU commutation relationship shows that the delivered active power depends on the offshore voltage magnitude (but not on the converter voltage angle), so the angle-based active-power loop of virtual synchronous machine control is not closed through the rectifier. A $P-V/Q-ω$ grid-forming architecture, which regulates active power via the voltage magnitude and derives frequency from the reactive power error, is therefore adopted. Electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1GWaggregated grid-forming turbine on a 66 kV collector network with a $\pm$525 kV bipolar DRU link show that the commanded power is delivered over 800 to 1000MW with the offshore voltage held near nominal. The paper also examines how grid-forming operation changes the allocation of control duties within the Type-4 turbine: once the grid-side converter forms the network, DC link regulation must move to the machine-side converter, which limits the achievable bandwidth of the DC-link control. Extending the system to 2 GW with two 500 MW grid-following units achieves full power transfer in simulation, but with the grid-forming converter loaded beyond its continuous rating and a steady-state offshore frequency deviation of approximately 1.8 Hz.

title: Support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains
abstract: We study the spatial support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains. Under a local nondegeneracy condition, additive noise gives full distributional support at every fixed positive time. For the Dirichlet problem with nonlocal multiplicative noise, we prove that the solution is either identically zero or has full support; excluding the zero state requires a separate non-hitting assumption. For a Neumann model, nonzero initial mass excludes the zero state and yields full support. The proofs combine Galerkin approximation with terminal Malliavin estimates. Numerical results illustrate the propagation mechanisms.

title: SGA-Sparse: Training Native SwiGLU Gates for Activation-Sparse and Low-Bit LLMs
abstract: Activation sparsity can reduce FFN weight traffic during single-user LLM decoding, but active channels must be identified early enough to avoid fetching unused weights. In pretrained SwiGLU models, training-free routing with the native gate performs substantially worse than routing with the up activation at high sparsity. We show that this ordering reverses after sparsity-aware training. Based on this insight, we introduce SGA-Sparse, which converts pretrained SwiGLU LLMs into fixed-budget activation-sparse models by training the existing gate projection directly as a top-k router. SGA-Sparse updates all model parameters end-to-end while preserving the original SwiGLU activation and introducing no auxiliary router parameters. After approximately 30B training tokens, LLaMA models from 1B to 8B achieve uniform per-token 75-85% FFN channel sparsity while remaining within 0.2-2.7 pp of their original dense checkpoints in average zero-shot accuracy. Because post-training quantization degrades sparsity-trained checkpoints, we further study two complementary quantization-aware training (QAT) recipes: continued-QAT largely recovers performance at 4-bit weight quantization, while joint-QAT performs better for the more aggressive sub-4-bit target. To compare activation sparsity with dense low-bit quantization, we translate the sparsity-induced reduction in weight traffic into an equivalent bit-width. Under this unified weight-traffic metric, our 2.5- and 1.5-bit-equivalent models establish a new accuracy-traffic Pareto frontier: the 2.5-bit-equivalent models match dense 3-bit QAT accuracy, while the 1.5-bit-equivalent models approach dense 2-bit models and outperform dense ternary models by 1.3 pp on average. These results establish native-gate training as a practical approach for combining high FFN sparsity with low-bit weights.

title: Do Feature Interactions Break Explainability? Provable Explanations for Any-Order Neural Additive Models
abstract: Post-hoc explanation methods for neural networks are often heuristic and lack provable guarantees. A common alternative to such methods that was studied in recent years is to compute a cardinally-minimal subset of input features that is provably sufficient to determine the model's prediction. For general neural networks, however, finding such explanations is computationally intractable. In contrast, recent work showed that this problem becomes more tractable for a particular family of neural networks, namely neural additive models (NAMs), though standard NAMs are highly restrictive because they exclude feature interactions altogether. In this work, we study the computation of provably minimal and sufficient explanations for neural networks with restricted feature interactions, bridging the gap between fully general neural networks and purely additive models. We first prove that even with constant-order interactions, the problem is $Σ_2^P$-hard, implying that worst-case exponential complexity is unavoidable. We then identify two provably tractable settings: one based on sparsity in the interaction structure and another based on a stronger interaction-aware notion of sufficiency. Under either of these settings, we develop algorithms that compute provable explanations for neural networks with any-order interactions while retaining much of the computational efficiency of additive models. Empirically, we show that these explanations are significantly smaller and faster to obtain than those produced by standard algorithms, while being derived from models that achieve much higher accuracy than standard NAMs. Overall, our results help expand the class of neural networks that admit efficient provable explanations, while clarifying the fundamental role of feature interactions in shaping their complexity.

title: Electron cooling mediated by transverse optical phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$
abstract: Soft transverse optical (TO) phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$ couple to electrons through the polarization field, quadratically in the paraelectric phase and, additionally, linearly in the polar phase due to the onset of spontaneous polarization. We investigate heat flow between a three-dimensional electron gas and soft TO phonons. For two-TO-phonon scattering, the heat flow of hot electrons crosses over from $T^5$ to $T^3$ at the Bloch-Gruneisen temperature. In the polar phase, an additional one-TO-phonon channel emerges, yielding a softer temperature dependence of the heat flow, $T^3$ at low and $T$ at high temperatures, with the spectral weight set by the spontaneous polarization. This channel may dominate at low temperatures and leads to a nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the heat flow in the vicinity of the polar transition.

title: MCSA: Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation in SO(3) Equivariant GNNs for Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) based on Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs) have achieved remarkable progress in atomistic modeling. However, accurately representing atomic interactions across different spatial scales remains challenging. In this work, we investigate the radial spectral properties of SO(3)-equivariant message passing and establish that the cutoff radius controls the characteristic spatial-frequency scale of radial interactions. Based on this analysis, we propose Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation (MCSA), a plug-and-play module that aggregates radial kernels with different cutoff radii to enrich multi-scale geometric representations. To achieve efficient implementation, we exploit the compact support of radial kernels to fuse cutoff-dependent radial weights before angular tensor-product operations, avoiding redundant angular computations while preserving rotational equivariance. Extensive experiments across representative EGNN backbones demonstrate consistent improvements in energy, force, and stress prediction, as well as enhanced accuracy in higher-order properties, including phonon dispersion and lattice thermal conductivity. Further evaluations on layered materials with distinct interaction scales demonstrate the effectiveness of physically motivated cutoff selection. Code is available at: https://github.com/JF-Tan/MCSA.

title: Regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes in the EAST tokamak
abstract: The pedestal pressure profile plays a critical role in determining the overall confinement of tokamak fusion plasmas. This letter reports the first evidence on regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes (MTMs) via limiting the pedestal gradient, which was thought to be limited by kinetic ballooning modes over the last decades. This is observed in an ITER-baseline-like target plasma in the EAST tokamak. MTMs arrest the recovery of pedestal electron temperature (and hence pressure) by clamping its gradient at a critical value while leaving the density profile essentially unaffected. Global fluid and local gyrokinetic simulations confirm the excitation of MTMs when the pedestal electron temperature gradient exceeds a threshold value in this experiment. This finding reveals MTMs as an alternative electromagnetic micro-instability that imposes an additional constraint in determining the pedestal structure in tokamaks.

title: Welfare in Envy-free Contracts: When Agents Have Sparse Interests
abstract: We study welfare maximization under envy-free contracts, where a principal assigns tasks and offers success-contingent payments to heterogeneous agents with hidden effort. For unit-demand agents, we establish a sharp complexity boundary: the problem is polynomial-time solvable when each agent is interested in at most two tasks, but NP-hard with at most three interests. Our algorithm analyzes tree-structured dependencies among forced assignments and reduces optimization to maximum-weight independent set in a perfect graph. When agents may receive multiple tasks, no polynomial-time constant-factor approximation exists unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. Finally, with homogeneous success probabilities and rewards, we establish a welfare- and revenue-preserving equivalence between unit-demand contract design and envy-free pricing. This yields polynomial-time welfare maximization without restricting interests, while revenue maximization remains NP-hard.

title: GFM Control Automatic Compliance Toolbox
abstract: The increasing penetration of converter-interfaced generation reduces system inertia, short-circuit strength, and voltage support. European grid codes, including the ENTSO-E Network Code on Requirements for Generators and the ACER Demand Connection Code, now define disturbance-based validation procedures for grid-forming (GFM) generation and converter-based demand. Commercial RMS tools, however, lack an integrated workflow aligned with these recent requirements. This paper presents an automated Python-PowerFactory compliance toolbox and an RMS test bench for a co-located system comprising a 1 MW GFM photovoltaic (PV) plant, a 0.3 MW GFM battery energy storage system (BESS), and a 1 MW converter-interfaced dynamic load at a 20 kV point of common coupling fed from a 110 kV grid. Extended virtual synchronous machine models and a DCC-oriented load model are tested in batch, with results automatically extracted and plotted for assessment. Results show compliant RMS performance for the slower, electromechanical tests, while the paper identifies which tests require complementary electromagnetic transient (EMT) verification.

title: An elementary observation on the Robin problem for NLS
abstract: We present an infinite set of explicit solutions of the integrable focusing NLS equation on the half-line that are rapidly decaying and satisfy a homogeneous Robin condition but have very different behaviors on the wall $x=0$. We then argue that a similar phenomenon exists for a small non-homogeneous perturbation of the Robin problem. This renders a potential application of the unified transform method to non-linearizable Robin problems impossible.

title: Nonlinear Interference Estimation in Coherent Optical Systems: Principles and Applications
abstract: Accurate estimation of nonlinear interference (NLI) is important for monitoring and optimizing coherent optical networks. This invited paper reviews the main techniques proposed for receiver-side NLI estimation, with particular focus on longitudinal power monitoring (LPM). We discuss the principles, advantages and limitations of LPM-based NLI estimation, including recent experimental demonstrations. We then experimentally investigate the impact of the spatial step size and the number of averaged constellation blocks on estimation accuracy. The results show that accurate NLI estimation does not necessarily require a highly accurate power profile, with limited improvements obtained by increasing the number of averaged blocks. Finally, we discuss the main practical limitations and applications of NLI estimation, with particular attention to end-to-end and span-wise optical power optimization.

title: TLRS-DPO: Token-Level Risk Scoring for Better Direct Preference Optimization
abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a simple and widely used alternative to RLHF for aligning large language models (LLMs), but its sequence-level objective cannot precisely locate or suppress the local patterns that make an otherwise acceptable response unsafe or undesirable. We propose TLRS-DPO (Token-Level Risk Scoring for Better Direct Preference Optimization), which augments DPO with fine-grained token-level control while remaining fully offline and reference-based. TLRS-DPO introduces a token-level robust compensation term that converts the policy-reference log-ratio on rejected responses into localized risk scores, a curriculum-style schedule that gradually increases the strength of this compensation during training, and a risk-adaptive screening mechanism that selectively penalizes only high-risk tokens instead of entire sequences. This design bridges sequence-level preference fitting and token-level behavior control, and can be implemented as a drop-in modification to standard DPO trainers. Empirically, TLRS-DPO improves alignment quality and safety-relevant behavior with minimal impact on helpfulness compared to strong DPO baselines.

title: Joint Poisson Reconstruction for Prompt-Gamma-Enabled 68Ga/18F Dual-Isotope Quantitative PET Imaging
abstract: Objective:To enable simultaneous quantitative 68Ga/18F PET imaging despite low prompt-gamma triple-coincidence counts and random-triple contamination. Methods: We developed an expectation-maximization reconstruction method (PNR-EM) that jointly estimates pure-emitter, non-pure-emitter, and random-triple components using a Poisson model of prompt double, prompt triple, and delayed triple measurements. A consistent-delay strategy estimates random triples while preserving true-pair temporal correlations. Prompt doubles additionally constrain the non-pure component, and total variation regularization suppresses reconstruction noise. The method was evaluated with quantitative and Derenzo phantoms, a nine-well separation phantom, and tumor-bearing mice. Results: Phantom quantitation showed strong linearity (r2>0.99) and a maximum relative deviation below 9.9% relative to single-isotope references. The separated images largely preserved rod resolvability relative to their corresponding single-isotope references. The best PSNR, SSIM, and RMSE were 33.72 dB, 0.975, and 0.0206 for 18F, and 34.86 dB, 0.955, and 0.0181 for 68Ga in the 9-well phantom. The 68Ga RMSE was 41.4% lower than that of the best image-domain separation baseline. Tumor-bearing mouse imaging demonstrated in vivo separation of 68Ga-DOTA-NOC and 18F-FDG distributions. Conclusion: Joint estimation improved dual-isotope separation under the evaluated low-count conditions. Significance: To our knowledge, this study provides the first experimental demonstration of simultaneous 68Ga/18F PET separation using prompt-gamma coincidences, supporting simultaneous imaging of complementary metabolic and receptor-targeted tracer distributions.

title: LoMASA: A Local Multi-Agent Sales Assistant with Confidence-Gated Delegation for B2B Quoting
abstract: Frontline sales staff spend much of their day re-coordinating quotes after customers change quantities, ask for discounts or new payment terms, or costs move. We present LoMASA (Local Multi-Agent Sales Assistant), a training-free multi-agent system that runs entirely on one desktop computer. A 35B mixture-of-experts model (System-1) makes each decision in a single forward pass and reads its confidence from the probabilities of the answer options. A 27B dense model (System-2) writes customer replies and escalation briefs and is consulted when System-1 is unsure. Code computes every price, margin and option, and hard pricing rules cannot be overridden. On a test split of 500 simulated episodes with 1512 decisions built from public supply-chain data, the salesperson has to decide only 19.5% of decisions: 38.0% are settled automatically, with a median latency of 2.67 seconds, and 42.5% are escalated to a manager by the hard rules. On the automatically settled decisions LoMASA is as accurate as a rule baseline (0.894 vs.\ 0.894) and makes fewer commitments whose margin later falls below the floor (2.61% vs 4.53%); the price is additional escalations to the manager. Option probabilities are well calibrated without any training, unlike confidence stated in words by the same model. We also report where the design does not help: the 27B model rarely changes a decision.

title: Continuity of solutions to nonlocal nonlinear diffusion equations
abstract: We establish an explicit modulus of continuity for locally bounded weak solutions to nonlocal porous medium type equations with measurable kernels. The nonlocal tail is only assumed to be integrable in time. The result lays a solid foundation for the intrinsic Harnack estimates of these equations.

title: Algorithms for Soft Tree Containment on Tree-Child Networks
abstract: Phylogenetic networks generalize evolutionary trees by allowing lineages to merge. The Tree Containment problem asks whether a network $N$ displays a tree $T$ on the same taxa. When the polytomies of $T$ reflect uncertainty rather than simultaneous divergence, the relevant notion is soft display, in which $N$ may refine the polytomies of $T$. We take it in its asymmetric reading. Soft Tree Containment is NP-hard on reticulation-visible networks even at reticulation indegree three, and it was open for a non-binary tree and a tree-child network with multifurcating tree nodes or reticulations of indegree above two. We solve this case. A cluster characterization reduces soft display to realizing all clusters of $T$ by one switching, and in a tree-child network the vertices that can realize a cluster lie on a single chain. The per-cluster requirements then form a constraint network of width one, which arc consistency decides without search, and a $2$-SAT instance when $N$ is binary. This yields, to our knowledge, the first polynomial-time algorithm for soft Tree Containment on single-labelled tree-child networks of arbitrary reticulation indegree, and a linear-time algorithm when $T$ is binary. The same method decides the symmetric variant of the problem, in which the polytomies of $N$ may be resolved as well.

title: Precision Fragmentation Functions from Modern COMPASS SIDIS Data
abstract: We present a comparative account of three global determinations of collinear fragmentation functions (FFs) for charged pions, charged kaons, and unidentified charged hadrons. The HAPS-PiFF1.0, HAPS-KaFF1.0, and HAPS-hFF1.0 analyses combine single-inclusive $e^+e^-$ annihilation with charge-separated semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS), including the 2025 COMPASS proton-target measurements and the revised 2026 isoscalar-target results. Flexible neural-network parametrizations, Monte Carlo replicas, and NLO/NNLO perturbative setups are employed. The proton and isoscalar samples sharpen the flavor sensitivity of SIDIS, while gluon fragmentation remains comparatively weakly constrained. We discuss the effects of perturbative accuracy, the principal limitations, and prospects for future measurements.

title: FRESCO: A Novel Consistency Control for Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel Training
abstract: Asynchronous pipeline parallelism can accelerate distributed model training, but suffers from instability caused by inconsistent gradient computations. We identify a fundamental source of this inconsistency: error signals are coupled to forward-time features, not just parameter states. This means that parameters may evolve as long as they preserve forward-equivalence. Leveraging this insight, we introduce FRESCO, which frames asynchronous updates as a constrained optimization problem: it finds the minimal update modification that acts trivially on the activation subspace. We demonstrate that FRESCO consistently outperforms representative asynchronous baselines in LLM pre-training, with the gains most pronounced under deep pipelines and high inconsistency levels: at pipeline depth 32, it reaches the same loss as the strongest baseline with 43% fewer iterations and 30% less wall-clock time, while requiring 8~921$\times$ less memory overhead. Moving beyond the current limitations, FRESCO establishes a new foundation for high-utilization pipeline parallel training, providing a scalable path for large-model development on diverse, resource-constrained systems.

title: A Layer-wise Study of How Style Rewriting Breaks the Calibration of Zero-Shot LLM Fake-News Detectors
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly asked to judge whether a news article is true, and their stated confidence is often taken at face value. We test what happens to that confidence when an article's writing style, but not its facts, is manipulated, as in recent \emph{style attacks} on fake-news detectors. Tracing how the prediction and its confidence form layer by layer inside the network, we study three model families (LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B) on three fake-news benchmarks, and find the same three patterns in every model--dataset pairing. First, on the original articles the models are competent and largely honest judges: they settle on an answer, briefly become overconfident, and then correct their confidence in the final layers. Second, style-rewritten articles break this self-correction: the models become far less accurate, under the strongest attack, worse than random guessing, yet remain just as confident, so they are \emph{confidently wrong} precisely when a warning is most needed. Third, nearly all of the damage comes from rewriting into sensational or emotionally charged styles, while sober, neutral rewrites leave the models' honesty largely intact. The practical implication is that an LLM's confidence about veracity cannot be trusted as a safety signal when an article's style may have been manipulated.

title: Stretched near-groups
abstract: We study stretched near-group fusion categories over $\mathbb{C}$ of type $G+k|G|$ for abelian groups $G$ and positive integers $k$, describing the structure of the double including fusion rules, modular data, and Frobenius--Schur indicators under a variety of assumptions. For cyclic $G$, when enough invertible objects exist in the double, we describe all associated de-equivariantizations which connect the existence of stretched near-group fusion categories to the existence of other stretched quadratic categories. All of our results apply to the case $k=1$. In particular, the known existence of $C_{m^2}+m^2$ near-group categories for all positive integers $m$ implies the existence of Haagerup--Izumi fusion categories for all cyclic groups. As a further application, we provide a general conductor bound severely restricting the existence of stretched near-group categories, and for infinitely many abelian groups $G$ of square order, among them $C_4\times C_2^{2j}$ with $j\geq2$, we show that a near-group fusion category $G+k|G|$ exists if and only if $k=0$.

title: An $SU(5)$ GUT with non-holomorphic modular $S'_4$ symmetry: fermion masses, mixing and leptogenesis
abstract: A non-supersymmetric $SU(5)$ grand unified model is constructed based on the non-holomorphic modular $S'_4$ flavor symmetry, supplemented by a global Peccei--Quinn $U(1)_{PQ}$ symmetry that constrains the Yukawa couplings. Constructed from polyharmonic Maaß forms, these couplings allow the model to reproduce the observed charged-fermion masses and mixing as well as the neutrino oscillation parameters for both normal ordering (NO) and inverted ordering (IO), with all Pull values satisfying $|\mathcal{P}| < 0.8$. The model further yields specific predictions for yet-unmeasured parameters, including the absolute neutrino masses, the Dirac CP phase, the Majorana phases, and the effective Majorana mass $m_{ββ}$. We then study thermal leptogenesis by solving the density matrix equations. For a given benchmark point, the final baryon asymmetry depends solely on the single free parameter $b$ that sets the right-handed neutrino mass scale, and an appropriate choice of this parameter reproduces the observed value $η_B \simeq 6.12 \times 10^{-10}$. Finally, the correlation between this scale parameter and specific low-energy observables provides a potential bridge between the fermion flavor structure and early-Universe cosmology.

title: DeepSoMo: Deformable Object Motion Estimation under Proprioceptive Partial Observability via Predictive Latent Dynamics
abstract: Estimating the motion of deformable bodies in soft robotics from proprioceptive sensing is challenging due to partial observability, as internal observations provide only indirect access to global motion, contact, and shape evolution. In such settings, instantaneous observations are insufficient, and accurate estimation requires temporally consistent latent representations. This paper studies deformable motion estimation under proprioceptive partial observability from a latent dynamics perspective. We argue that a key requirement for long-horizon estimation is latent temporal consistency, where latent states remain predictive of future observations. To this end, we present DeepSoMo, a learning-based framework that enforces predictive structure in latent dynamics through a self-supervised latent prediction constraint. We evaluate the approach in a canonical deformable dynamics setting using high-fidelity finite-element simulation as a controlled source of ground truth. Results demonstrate consistent improvements in trajectory estimation, orientation recovery, shape reconstruction, and contact inference over architecture-matched recurrent baselines.

title: Saidzoda-Tajik-EmbeddingGemma-300M: Knowing Every Letter Is Not Reading Tajik
abstract: EmbeddingGemma-300M is a small open embedder whose tokenizer represents every Tajik letter, and as released it is weak at Tajik retrieval: on our Tajik law test the right passage is in its top ten results for 49.3% of questions, on tax documents for 45.9%, and on the human-written Belebele Tajik set for 69.8%, against 98.6% on the Russian version of the same set. We present Saidzoda-Tajik-EmbeddingGemma-300M, the same model fully fine-tuned for one epoch on 235,140 question and passage pairs written by our own Tajik language model for laws, tax documents, Wikipedia and web text, with the same mined hard negatives, English and Russian replay, loss, global batch, learning rate and epoch as our earlier Saidzoda-Tajik-E5-Large (arXiv:2611.00592) and BGE-M3 models. After training, law reaches 92.4% and tax 91.7%; on Belebele, the one test written by people, recall@10 rises from 69.8% to 92.6% and the first result is right for 76.6% of questions instead of 51.7%. A checkpoint at step 100 of 466 already holds 88% of the law gain at recall@10. At recall@10 the result is no more than 2.8 points below the two 560M models trained on the same pairs on law, tax and Wikipedia, within the intervals, with 768-dimensional vectors and about half their parameters; at recall@1, for which we have no intervals, it stays 7.0 points behind the E5 model on Belebele. The cost is a drop of 3.0 and 2.8 points in Russian and English recall@1, larger than for the two earlier models. We also report that, according to our run notes, a bfloat16 test run produced a non-finite loss at step 3 which the training framework logged as zero, so training was done in fp32. Our generated test questions come from the same model as the training questions, so we treat those scores as an upper limit until questions written by Tajik speakers exist.

title: Harmonic and Monogenic Representations of White Noise and its weighted harmonic Bergman estimates
abstract: Continuing Feichtinger's generalized stochastic process theory, we analyze harmonic and monogenic representations of white noise in Euclidean spaces. We define its convolution with square-integrable functions. Using the weighted Sobolev regularity of the white noise, we establish a high-dimensional Sokhotski-Plemelj formula for the white noise density. Furthermore, we embed these representations into new weighted Bergman spaces, proving that the weighted Bergman norms of the harmonic representations are bounded by the white noise's weighted Sobolev norms.

title: Hardware-Efficient Continuous-Variable Quantum Computation: Finite-$N$ Non-Gaussian Gates in a Floquet-Engineered Cavity-BEC
abstract: Continuous-variable (CV) quantum computation in bosonic modes offers a hardware-efficient route toward fault tolerance, yet synthesizing deterministic, macroscopic non-Gaussian gates with Wigner negativity remains challenging. Here, we establish two physical breakthroughs and two tensor-network innovations using a single-cavity 87Rb Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) as a macroscopic bosonic logical mode. Physically, building on our orthogonal optical dual-driving architecture, we propose deterministic, unitary Floquet-engineered Two-Axis Twisting (TAT) non-Gaussian gates without post-selection, and introduce a paradigm shift from quantum metrology to CV quantum computation: via a normal-ordered Holstein-Primakoff expansion and non-perturbative spin simulations, we show that the over-squeezed regime ($t>t_{opt}$, where Wineland squeezing $ξ_R^2$ degrades) harnesses finite-$N$ Bloch-sphere curvature - manifesting at $O(1/S)$ as cubic shearing and quartic Kerr $(a^\dagger a)^2$ interactions - to deterministically generate Wigner negativity. Methodologically, we formulate an exact automaton Matrix Product Operator in the compact SU(2) spin basis with an $N$-independent Liouvillian bond dimension ($D_L=6$), bypassing Fock cutoff errors ($N_{max}$) and $O(N^3)$ permutational-invariant scaling. Finally, we decouple $4^N$-dimensional Lindblad evolution from collective observation via an Exact Bilateral Dynamic Programming Dicke Projector with log-gamma normalization, extracting the $(N+1)\times(N+1)$ symmetric projection $\tildeρ_{n_L,n_R}$ without moment truncation while tracking symmetry retention $p_{sym}(t)$. Our proof-of-principle $N=50$ benchmark resolves deep Wigner negativity ($W_{min} \approx -0.214$ at $t=2.00μ$s, after $ξ_R^2 \approx 0.124$ at $t_{opt} \approx 0.64μ$s), establishing a scalable architecture for $N \sim 10^3-10^5$ macroscopic BEC processors.

title: Direct Light-Cone Reconstruction of the $B$-Meson Shape Function in HQET
abstract: The $B$-meson shape function encodes the nonperturbative residual-momentum dynamics of the heavy quark within heavy quark effective theory (HQET). From a Wilsonian perspective, HQET provides a natural framework for lattice calculations when the heavy quark mass is comparable to or exceeds the inverse lattice spacing. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a $B$-meson quasi-shape function directly in HQET and calculate its one-loop matching to the light-cone shape function, avoiding an intermediate matching step involving a full-QCD light-cone distribution. We determine the one-loop renormalization kernels and matching coefficients in both the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ and regularization-independent momentum-subtraction (RI/MOM) schemes for the quasi-shape function, while keeping the light-cone shape function in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme. The matching coefficients are obtained at leading power in the large-$v^z$ expansion and are independent of the infrared regulator. Our results provide the perturbative ingredients for a direct lattice HQET determination of the $B$-meson shape function.

title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.

title: FESOM2.8 in single precision: climate fidelity over six decades and performance on CPUs and GPUs
abstract: Halving the floating-point precision of an ocean model can make it substantially faster, but whether the rounding errors stay negligible over climate time scales has rarely been tested. We implement single precision in the global ocean-sea-ice model FESOM2 and compare 60-year hindcasts with double-precision controls. A first implementation lost salt steadily, accumulated a heat-content deficit of 129 ZJ, and shifted major ocean fronts. Controlled experiments trace the drift to the tracer update: small increments added to a large salinity value are rounded away, and the increments themselves are biased. Accumulating tracer tendencies and layer thicknesses in 64 bits, and carrying the rounding error of each tracer update into the next, removes the drift for at most 8% additional runtime. Single- and double-precision simulations then differ in heat content and mean state about as much as two double-precision runs with slightly perturbed initial conditions, sea ice differs by at most 0.2%, and he salinity difference is four orders of magnitude smaller than before. In the coupled model AWI-ESM3, single precision adds no detectable heat source or sink over 60 years. Single precision speeds up the 60-year hindcasts by a factor of 1.35, and the model by up to 1.66 on meshes of up to 5 km resolution; on GPUs, a C++/Kokkos version runs up to 1.27 times faster and needs 43% less memory. Whether reduced precision is safe for climate integrations is decided by long-term budgets, not by short tests.

title: Understanding When and Where Self-Supervised Speech Models Learn Phonemes and Prosodic Cues through Layer-Wise and Time-Resolved Probing
abstract: Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) encode a rich hierarchy of acoustic, prosodic, and phonetic information, yet when and where it emerges during pretraining remains unclear. We train frozen-encoder probes on every Transformer layer across pretraining checkpoints of two matched models: HuBERT-Base, whose stage 2 is a separately initialized model trained on new pseudo-label targets, and single-objective wav2vec 2.0-Base. Our five tasks span an acoustic-to-abstract gradient: absolute pitch (F0), speaker-relative pitch, lexical stress, phoneme boundaries, and 38-way phoneme identity. Acoustic-prosodic cues and phone boundaries are decodable from the earliest checkpoints and barely shift across layers, whereas phoneme identity is constructed during pretraining, re-localizing to upper-middle layers under HuBERT's stage-2 targets at a matched update count. Acquisition order therefore tracks abstraction from the acoustic surface, not the segmental/suprasegmental distinction, extending to prosody an account established for phonetic, lexical and syntactic structure; the no-switch wav2vec 2.0 shows no comparable re-localization.

title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
abstract: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.

title: The Outer Eshelby Problem in Amorphous Solids with Odd Dipole Screening
abstract: The so-called "2-dimensional Eshelby problem" was defined by JD Eshelby, where a circle is cut out of an elastic sheet, deformed into an ellipse, and forced back into the material. This creates a quadrupolar response which turned out to be very relevant for describing plastic deformations in amorphous solids.
