We systematically evaluate BiVerify on five challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks using multiple mainstream DeepSeek, GPT, and Gemini models. BiVerify exceeds the strongest representative public baseline evaluated in this work by 13.5 percentage points in average accuracy, with the margin reaching 31.2 percentage points on GPT. Further analysis shows that BiVerify's overall performance exceeds that of either verification direction alone.

title: Tiling of Hyperbolic Surface by Maximal Number of Tiles
abstract: Tilings of a closed hyperbolic surface by congruent $n$-gons with $n\ge 7$ is a finite problem. One extreme of the finite problem is that the number of tiles is maximal. The problem is related to edge-to-edge tilings of the Poincaré disk ${\bb H}^2$ by congruent $n$-gons, such that all vertices have degree 3 and the vertex sets satisfy certain balance condition. For the special case $n=7$, we show that the heptagon in any such tiling belongs to one of the four families, and tilings of ${\bb H}^2$ by generic heptagons in each family is unique. As a consequence, for any closed hyperbolic surface of Euler characteristic $χ$, we may classify all tilings of the surface by maximal number $-6χ$ of congruent generic heptagons in the four families.

title: A Simple Phase-King Protocol with Predictions
abstract: Inspired by recent work (Ben-David, Dzulfikar, Ellen, and Gilbert, $\textit{Byzantine Agreement with Predictions}$, PODC 2025) we study synchronous binary Byzantine Agreement in the learning-augmented setting, where each process receives predictions about which processes are honest or Byzantine. We present a deterministic Phase King protocol for the anauthenticated setting, combining early stopping with a specifically designed prediction-aware king selection procedure. For at most $t<n/3$ Byzantine processes, the protocol handles arbitrarily many prediction errors, improving upon the $O(n^{3/2})$ bound of Ben-David et al., and terminates within $O(P)$ communication rounds, where $P=1+\min\{\mathbf{B}/n,f\}$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the total number of incorrect prediction bits held by honest processes, and $f$ is the actual number of Byzantine processes. Our protocol uses $O(n^2P)$ messages and $O(n^2P\log n)$ bits, avoiding the initial cubic bit cost of exchanging complete prediction vectors. In comparison to very recent independent work (Dufay, Dzulfikar, and Gilbert, $\textit{Predictions Can Only Help! Communication Efficient Byzantine Agreement with Predictions}$, DISC 2026), which achieves the same error tolerance and round complexity but better communication bounds, our construction provides a much simpler Phase King approach that completely avoids involved preprocessing constructions, rendering it more practical, especially for achieving agreement in time-evolving networks. We believe that the novel prediction-aware king selection technique of our scheme is of independent interest and can find further applications in learning-augmented distributed consensus.

title: D3Tree: Learning to Prune Block-Diffusion Draft Trees for Efficient Verification
abstract: Block-diffusion drafters propose a whole block of tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees built from their position-wise marginals increase the expected accepted length of speculative decoding. Every tree node occupies a query row in target verification, so under concurrent serving low-yield branches compete with other requests for verification capacity. Existing tree methods select verified nodes by draft probability under a fixed or cost-selected per-request budget, and thus always retain a prefix of the drafter's ranking. We present D3Tree, which learns which nodes of a block-diffusion draft tree are worth verifying. A tree-size head with 2H+2 parameters predicts each candidate's conditional survival from the draft state, the candidate embedding, and its draft log-probability. Thresholding the product of these scores along parent chains yields an ancestor-closed subtree whose size adapts to each request and decoding round. The head is trained on a frozen drafter with conditional labels on the full candidate tree; an optional joint mode also steers the drafter toward the retained reference path. At serving time, D3Tree verifies whole trees under light load and, under heavy load, allocates one batch-wide node budget by predicted survival, sized to the target's matrix-multiplication tiles. Retained trees share one ancestor-masked target pass, while construction, pruning, and scheduling run on the GPU and overlap with the host. Across six vision-language verifiers and 17 text and multimodal benchmarks, D3Tree is fastest in 70 of 72 load settings, with 3.2-4.0x speedup over autoregressive decoding for one request and 1.3-1.8x at 64 concurrent requests, where fixed-budget trees fall below autoregressive speed. Under a time-varying arrival trace, it has the lowest mean end-to-end latency in every arrival phase.

title: LLM-based Multi-Criteria Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Efficient 5G UPF Selection
abstract: User plane function (UPF) selection in 5G networks is an active area of research, with various limited approaches proposed to enhance network efficiency and manage resources effectively. In this paper, we address this gap in the related literature by proposing a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) UPF selection method that utilizes a dynamic, multi-objective reward function and validating it on a real-world 5G emulation platform. The proposed method is based on the large language models' (LLMs) translation of network operator intents and the network data analytics function (NWDAF) abnormality alerts. The experimental results validated in the real-world experimental setup demonstrate that our dynamic DRL solution achieves an effective balance between latency, power consumption, and traffic distribution, outperforming the heuristic baselines and fixed DRL by 16.89%. These findings highlight the real-world applicability of our approach for dynamic, intent-driven UPF selection.

title: Optimal execution in a fractional setting with reinforcement learning
abstract: We consider the problem of optimal liquidation with linear market impact, as in the seminal work of Almgren and Chriss, but with an asset driven by a fractional Brownian motion. For $H \neq 1/2$, we observe that the deterministic solution given by Almgren and Chriss is no longer optimal. We develop a strategy to exploit the information induced by the correlation between price increments. The strategy is derived from a policy gradient algorithm, parameterized by a neural network, trained to maximise the CARA utility, for which our method allows for significant improvements.

title: Small Data Generative AI for Culturally Specific Artistic Creation: A Case Study on the Sonic Space of sarir
abstract: Large-scale generative AI (GenAI) models have become increasingly integrated into contemporary creative practice, yet they often reproduce cultural biases and fail to meaningfully engage with non-Western artistic traditions. In response, this paper explores a small-data approach that foregrounds artist-curated and culturally informed dataset creation and model training. Through a case study on sarir (the distinctive sound produced by the reed pen in Persian calligraphy), we demonstrate how small-data GenAI can operate within a highly situated cultural context that lies beyond the representational reach of large-scale GenAI models. We construct a bespoke sarir audio dataset and train two models, RAVE and StyleGAN2, adapting each to the sonic domain through audio synthesis and spectrogram generation. The resulting models learn the fine-grained timbral and gestural nuances of sarir, enabling both real-time interaction and extended generative output. By comparing these results with state-of-the-art text-to-audio models, we clearly demonstrate the disparity in their performance and highlight the expressive possibilities unlocked through the small data approach. This focused case study demonstrates the feasibility of small-data GenAI for culturally specific artistic creation and underscores the value of further investigations that extend this approach to other cultural materials and artistic domains.

title: Linear Objective Problems: A Complexity Framework for Bilevel Optimization
abstract: Many bilevel and robust optimization problems are complete for the second level of the polynomial hierarchy, but such results are usually proven one problem at a time with problem-specific reductions. A recurring obstacle is that the lower level must select an optimal solution rather than merely a feasible one, whereas standard reductions preserve only whether a solution exists, not which solutions are optimal. We introduce linear objective problems (LOP), a framework for optimization problems whose solutions are explicit subsets of a ground set and whose objective is linear in these elements. We define tight solution-embedding reductions, which map the optimal solutions of one problem element by element onto the optimal solutions of another, without having to recognize optimal solutions, which is coNP-hard in general. This gives a notion of LOP-completeness, with Satisfiability as the canonical complete problem, even with unit weights. We show that many classical problems are LOP-complete, including Vertex Cover, Dominating Set, TSP, Knapsack, and Steiner Tree, and we introduce a duality that transfers LOP-completeness between minimization and maximization problems. As our main application, we prove a meta-theorem for min-max regret optimization under interval uncertainty: for every LOP-complete problem, the min-max regret version is $Σ_2^p$-complete. Instead of a separate proof for each nominal problem, it suffices to show that the nominal problem is LOP-complete. This recovers known results for the interval min-max regret versions of Knapsack and Maximum Benefit Set Cover and yields completeness for over 50 further problems.

title: Fractional distance-edge-monitoring in lexicographic products
abstract: We give an exact formula for the fractional distance-edge-monitoring number of $G\circ H$, where $G$ is connected of order $m\ge2$ and $H$ has order $n\ge2$. By the previously established endpoint-monitoring property, the fractional monitoring program reduces to fractional vertex cover, whose linear-programming dual is fractional matching. Writing $d_c(H)$ for the critical difference of $H$, we obtain $\operatorname{dem}_{f}(G\circ H)=(mn-D(G,H))/2$, where $D(G,H)=\max_{A\in\mathcal{I}(G)}\bigl(d_c(H)|A|-n|N_G(A)|\bigr)$ and $\mathcal{I}(G)$ denotes the family of all independent sets of $G$, including the empty set, while $N_G(A)$ is the open neighborhood of $A$. This formula characterizes the products attaining $mn/2$ and gives an equality criterion for the fractional matching lower bound of Ma, Cheng, Mao and Wang. Under the stated hypotheses, the lower bound of Ma et al. is attained if and only if either factor has a fractional perfect matching or $H$ is edgeless. Two outer trees show that the factor orders and fractional matching numbers do not determine the product value.

title: Scenario-Based Assessment of Transport Electrification for Low-Carbon Urban Planning: A Case Study of Phu Quoc, Vietnam
abstract: Urban net-zero strategies require a defensible emissions boundary and quantitative estimates of the contribution achievable through individual mitigation measures. This study assesses road-transport electrification within a planned residential development in Phu Quoc, Vietnam, using the assumptions and scenario data of an urban-planning study originally prepared in 2022. A vehicle-class inventory combines population-dependent fleet projections, assumed travel activity, gasoline and diesel consumption, fuel-specific carbon dioxide (CO_2) factors, and electricity-related emissions from battery-electric vehicles. The reference case projects annual road-transport emissions of 59.41, 73.86, and 87.23 tCO_2 for 2022, 2025, and 2030, respectively. Three year-specific substitution scenarios, corresponding to nominal electric-vehicle shares of 25%, 50%, and 100%, yield source-reported avoided emissions of 9.43, 13.64, and 55.41 tCO_2/year, or 15.9%, 18.5%, and 63.5% of their respective baselines. However, a cross-scenario audit identifies an inconsistency in the 2025 mixed-fleet results under time-invariant vehicle-class emission-intensity ratios: under that additional assumption, 2025 avoided emissions would be 23.45 rather than 13.64 tCO_2/year. The original detailed vehicle-energy input tables are not included in the available source document, preventing definitive reconciliation. The study therefore provides a transparent, preliminary planning assessment rather than evidence of citywide net-zero attainment. Its principal value is a reproducible accounting structure and an explicit identification of the data, electricity-system, and infrastructure constraints that must be resolved before policy or investment decisions.

title: SegDis: Foreground Segmentation Followed by Type Discrimination for Salient and Camouflaged Object Detection
abstract: Salient and camouflaged object detection (SOD and COD) both recover foreground support, yet most joint methods output only a binary mask and therefore cannot distinguish the type. USC12K distinguishes the two types, but its baseline USCNet still binds foreground existence to the type within a single normalization, so the failure source cannot be attributed. Our cross-task study shows that foreground localization transfers between SOD and COD, whereas type discrimination does not: a COD-only model recovers foreground on SOD images but its type judgement follows the training distribution rather than the foreground-background relation, so the two decisions require separate mechanisms. SegDis factorizes the output into an explicit foreground probability and a conditional type probability given foreground: FLR provides high-quality task-agnostic support, and RTA refines the SOD/COD assignment from the foreground-background relation without a task identifier. Because support is explicit, each ground-truth foreground pixel is classified as correct-type, type-swapped, or missed, so foreground-recovery and type-assignment errors are diagnosed separately. With PVT-v2-B2, SegDis attains 68.98% FG-mIoU and 78.35% mIoU on USC12K at about one-eighth of USCNet's parameters; CSCS is 5.75.

title: Self-Supervised Collapse Prevention with Score-Based Entropy Maximization
abstract: Diffusion models have demonstrated the effectiveness of score-based objectives for generative modeling, yet their potential for self-supervised representation learning remains underexplored. We introduce Entropy-Based Regularization (EBReg), a framework that uses latent score estimation to regularize the latent distribution during self-supervised training. EBReg jointly learns an encoder and a latent score model, and utilizes the learned score to provide a diversity-preserving signal that prevents representational collapse. Motivated by a mutual-information lower bound, we formulate the objective as view alignment with smoothed marginal entropy maximization and optimize the marginal entropy without explicit density evaluation. The same score model can additionally be used at test time to refine corrupted representations toward the training latent distribution. Empirically, EBReg learns competitive representations on ImageNet-1K, achieving 75.57% linear-probe accuracy with ViT-L. Across diverse architectures, score-guided test-time adaptation further improves robustness on ImageNet-C, yielding an average relative accuracy gain of approximately 5%.

title: Negative Dynamical Friction in Dark Matter Spikes around Rotating Black Holes
abstract: Dark matter may affect extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) through orbital-energy exchange and a conservative metric response. Here we show that dark matter spikes around rotating massive black holes can drive negative dynamical friction, supplying orbital energy to secondary black holes on stable prograde circular orbits. The energy-gain region extends beyond the innermost stable circular orbit once the black-hole spin exceeds a model-dependent threshold. For an illustrative four-year inspiral with Milky Way--like halo parameters and mass ratio $q=10^{-5}$, the total dynamical-friction contribution produces a phase difference of order $10^2$ radians relative to vacuum. For the same system, the fixed-frequency environmental redshift correction is comparable in magnitude and opposite in sign to the first-order conservative self-force correction. Both environmental energy exchange and the conservative metric response are therefore essential to precision EMRI modeling.

title: Does Predictive Performance Translate to Causal Performance? Evaluating tabular foundation models as nuisance learners for causal effect estimation
abstract: Tabular foundation models based on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) achieve strong predictive performance, but their value for causal inference is unclear. We evaluated whether PFNs, which predict through in-context learning, could match or outperform conventional nuisance learners in supporting accurate causal estimation and reliable uncertainty quantification (inference). Learners modeled propensity scores and outcome regressions within doubly robust estimators of average causal effects, with and without cross-fitting, across synthetic and semi-synthetic settings with varying confounding complexity and effect heterogeneity. Under simple parametric data-generating processes, the PFNs were competitive with correctly specified parametric regressions and ensembles containing them. In more complex settings, they outperformed all conventional learners evaluated, including richly specified Super Learner ensembles, for both accuracy and uncertainty quantification. As sample size increased, only the two PFN models (TabPFN and Mitra) consistently approached nominal confidence interval coverage, whereas under-coverage persisted for conventional learners. In some settings, PFNs achieved near-nominal coverage and well-calibrated standard errors even without cross-fitting. At the smallest sample size (n=200) and in the higher-dimensional semi-synthetic settings, PFNs and other flexible learners exhibited poor coverage without cross-fitting. For PFNs, this appeared to be driven by propensity score overfitting consistent with in-sample memorization of treatment labels. These findings highlight the promise of prior-data fitted networks as in-context nuisance learners for causal estimation, while underscoring the need for further evaluation in challenging settings.

title: The comparison of density estimation for transfer learning in Banach, Hilbert, Euclidean spaces
abstract: Domain adaptation or DA methods are indispensable when target labels or computational resources are scarce, yet the domain kernel density and subspace alignment approaches completely assume a Hilbertian geometry. They measure distributional discrepancy with symmetric L2 divergences over Euclidean feature spaces or reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS). This preprint summarizes the manuscript Non-Hilbertian Domain Adaptation. Total Variation Alignment via L1 Density Regularization on Feature Manifolds, which proposes Banach Manifold Transfer Learning or BMTL. BMTL makes two coupled design decisions. The first one is that features are embedded on a geodesic manifold rather than treated as points of a flat Euclidean space, and the second one is that the density matching regularizer is formulated in an L1 Banach norm, whose minimization is equivalent, by Scheffe's theorem, to contracting the Total Variation or TV distance between domain densities, a bounded metric that weights all regions of the sample space uniformly. The L2 formulation, by contrast, squares deviations and therefore amplifies errors in the tails, over emphasizing density outliers that do not reflect meaningful distributional shift. Experiments on MNIST-USPS, COIL20, and Office+Caltech10 show consistent gains; the L1 variant beats an otherwise identical L2 ablation on every task, for example 92.44% vs. 89.80% on USPS->MNIST and surpasses the strongest baseline DMDA by +3.68% on average over twelve Office+Caltech transfers. This document situates the contribution with an explicit comparison of Euclidean, Hilbert, and Banach geometries.

title: Nonlinear Stability of Planar Shock Waves for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations in R^3
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the global nonlinear stability and large-time decay rates of small-amplitude planar viscous shock waves for the three-dimensional (3-D) full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier equations in the whole space $\R^3$. {We prove that if the initial perturbation is sufficiently small in $H^3(\R^3)\cap\Hm(\R^3)$, then the Cauchy problem admits a unique global strong solution that converges to the planar shock profile without any phase shift. In the moving shock frame, both the conservative and primitive perturbations decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/4}$ in $H^3(\R^3)$. Their time and transverse spatial derivatives decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/2}$, measured in $\Hm(\R^3)$ for the conservative perturbation and in $H^1(\R^3)$ for the primitive perturbation.} No zero-mass condition or spectral stability assumption is imposed. On the whole space $\R^3$, the main analytical difficulties stem from the continuous transverse low frequencies, the opposite signs of shock compression in $L^2(\R^3)$ and unweighted $\Hm(\R^3)$, and the absence of density dissipation in the continuity equation coupled with temperature variations. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce a density-weighted $\Hm(\R^3)$ multiplier built from the inverse entropy Hessian and a modified curl operator. Through entropy symmetrization and the curl projection, all second-order acoustic derivatives of the potential cancel out and the transverse acoustic modes are controlled, so that the normal Euler drift is governed by the compressive derivative of the characteristic speed. Combined with an effective momentum variable and a momentum--density cross estimate, this negative-order energy absorbs the unfavorable compression term in the $L^2$ energy and closes the $H^3(\R^3)$ a priori estimates without loss of derivatives.

title: Collective Chiral Response of Achiral Plasmonic Arrays Induced by Truncated Bloch-Floquet Effect
abstract: Chirality in plasmonic systems is commonly associated with structures differentiated by their handedness. Here, we demonstrate the emergence of collective chirality in structurally achiral periodic hole arrays induced by non-local surface-plasmon interactions. We attribute this effect to the transfer of the optical angular momentum in the system. While an individual sub-wavelength circular aperture is not expected to alter the total angular momentum, the periodic structure results in a coherent coupling of plasmons wavefronts, giving rise to a collective Bloch-Floquet-like response. The edge of the structure accumulates the helical phase that eventually results in a visible spin-dependent shifting of the plasmonic beam. We systematically study the effects of hole-array size, periodicity and the geometry. The observed phenomenon shows an unprecedented robustness and consistency. These results establish periodic plasmonic arrays as a platform for converting localized helicity-dependent responses into collective chirality, providing a route toward controlling chiral plasmonic wavefronts in structurally achiral systems.

title: Hausdorff Dimension of Escaping Sets of Transcendental Entire Functions in the Speiser Class
abstract: For every $d\in[1,2]$, we construct a transcendental entire function $f$ whose finite singular value is contained in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and whose escaping set has Hausdorff dimension $d$. For $d<2$, the construction combines spiral corridors with quasiconformal folding. A narrowing Archimedean spiral gives dimension one, while a logarithmic spiral with adjustable width gives intermediate dimensions. The endpoint $d=2$ is realized by the exponential map. This gives an affirmative answer to a question of Bishop posed in 2018.

title: What Travels Across Languages? Reading, Transfer and Erasure of Cross-Lingual Concept Subspaces in Bangla Idioms
abstract: Cross-lingual concept analysis requires distinguishing the information that a subspace retains from the classifiers and erasers that transfer through it. We study these operations in six frozen encoders using 10,359 Bangla (Bengali) idiom senses, eight input conditions, and figurative-class and sentiment labels. Class-mean directions provide the most consistent evidence of shared coarse meaning: in post hoc analyses, they outperform random-subspace, permuted-label and covariance-matched nulls in all 12 model-label tests under balanced accuracy. A prospective internal re-split supports idiom-alone sharing in 10 of 12 tests, spanning five encoders. The original confirmatory logistic-regression family rejects both planned nulls in 4 of 12 tests, where English directions gain only a few accuracy points above the majority-class floor (3.0-7.3). Classifier transfer depends on the input map and regularization: English-trained class-mean readouts beat both zero-shot nulls in 8 of 12 discovery tests, and stronger source-selected penalties improve transfer through logistic and LEACE directions. These readouts use Bangla-validation-selected layers and unlabeled target preprocessing. Input controls show greater coarse-class sharing for explicit glosses than for idiom counterparts. Reading, however, does not imply effective erasure: English-fitted LEACE removes less than one percentage point of Bangla figurative-class accuracy, compared with 4-11 points for Bangla-fitted LEACE; INLP shows a similar asymmetry. Pattern-filter analysis, covariance-weighted input maps and a binary Gaussian overlap bound explain how these operations can diverge. The analogous multiclass ordering is an empirical diagnostic, observed in 11 of 12 cells. The results support an estimator-sensitive account of cross-lingual concept sharing and motivate evaluating reading, classifier transfer, erasure and overlap separately.

title: Orthogonal Updates for the Win: Towards Accelerated Adaptive Minimax Optimization
abstract: Single-loop minimax methods are appealing for modern machine learning, but standard stochastic gradient updates can be unstable and oscillatory under tightly coupled primal-dual dynamics, making performance notoriously sensitive to stepsizes. To fundamentally improve stability, we develop an orthogonal update framework tailored to minimax optimization, which applies updates along orthogonalized directions to reduce update anisotropy. However, orthogonalization reshapes the optimization geometry and makes coordinating primal-dual stepsizes even more delicate. To overcome this challenge, we develop AdaSGDA, which equips orthogonal updates with an adaptive stepsize rule driven by accumulated gradient norms. This mechanism automatically balances coupled primal-dual progress under orthogonalization, yielding an effectively parameter-free method for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization. We prove that AdaSGDA avoids problem-dependent tuning while attaining the state-of-the-art $\mathcal{O}\left(T^{-1/4}\right)$ convergence rate. We further propose AdaSGDA-VR, which incorporates a carefully designed variance reduction scheme and achieves the faster $\mathcal{O}\left(T^{-1/3}\right)$ rate. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our methods deliver competitive performance compared to existing minimax optimization methods.

title: Uniform inference for $U$-statistics of exchangeable arrays under degeneracy
abstract: Many $U$-statistics of row-column exchangeable arrays become degenerate at natural null hypotheses: their convergence rates change and their limiting laws may or may not remain Gaussian. We establish conditions under which inference based on the classical unbiased variance estimator is uniformly valid across these changes, without knowledge of the degeneracy order. It is known that $U$-statistics can be decomposed into orthogonal projections indexed by bipartite graphs. Under uniform fourth-moment assumptions, we establish that the standardized statistic is asymptotically Gaussian and the classical unbiased variance estimator is ratio-consistent, as long as a certain measure of concentration for projections indexed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. Under compactness of the normalized projections, both properties hold if and only if the proportion of variance contributed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. The necessity of this condition follows from a general limit theorem for these $U$-statistics, in which each graph contributes to a Wiener chaos of order equal to its number of connected components. We note that the row-column jackknife variance estimator, although nonnegative, does not generally give a studentized statistic with a standard normal limit in degenerate regimes. We illustrate our theory with an application to estimation and testing based on a distance from product form, exhibiting Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits at various rates depending on the model. We also propose a conservative inference procedure that does not require a Gaussian limit, valid under additional moment and projection conditions.

title: Smooth approximations to character sums and zeta sums
abstract: We study smooth approximations to Dirichlet character sums and zeta sums. The uniform upper-bound consequence of the Granville--Soundararajan conjecture, when imposed on all nonprincipal characters including imprimitive ones, implies the Riemann hypothesis for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet \(L\)-function. The proof uses characters induced to moduli divisible by all small primes. In the other direction, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,χ)\), we establish the conjectured approximation uniformly for \(q^a\le x\le q\), where \(0<a\le1\) is fixed, with \(y=(\log q+(\log x)^2)(\log\log q)^C\) for every fixed \(C>6\). In this range both the character sum and its smooth restriction, and hence their difference, are exponentially small relative to the number of \(y\)-smooth integers coprime to \(q\). We establish the corresponding approximation for \(\sum_{n\le x}n^{-it}\) under the Riemann hypothesis for the zeta function, uniformly for \(T^a\le x\le T\) and \(2T\le t\le5T\). We also show that the full zeta-sum smooth-approximation conjecture implies the Lindelöf hypothesis.

title: Quantitative Homogenization and Global Lipschitz Estimates for Elasticity with Periodic Rigid Inclusions
abstract: We consider the pure traction problem for linear elasticity in a bounded domain containing an $\varepsilon$-periodic array of perfectly rigid inclusions. For compatible $L^2$ boundary tractions on a Lipschitz domain, we prove an $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ error estimate in $H^1$ for a smoothed first-order two-scale expansion. If the exterior and inclusion boundaries are $C^{2,β}$, we also obtain a global Lipschitz estimate, uniform in $\varepsilon$, for compatible $C^{0,σ}$ tractions, where $0<σ<β$. The displacement is normalized modulo rigid motions, and the estimate controls the full gradient in the matrix and the inclusions. The boundary argument uses a local Neumann comparison estimate whose constant is independent of the choice of inclusions retained in cells cut by an artificial localization boundary. We prove this estimate by combining cellwise rigidification, divergence-free stress extensions, and duality, and then apply a boundary Campanato iteration and local estimates at the microscopic scale.

title: Let the Gallery Learn Itself: Training-Free Iterative Side-View Face Recognition
abstract: What if a face recognition system could learn from every encounter without a single gradient update? We present Gallery Self-Evolution (GSE), a training-free framework where the gallery itself adapts at test time. The core mechanism---dedup-FIFO curation---archives novel appearance samples after successful recognition while permanently locking the enrollment template, bounded at 30 embeddings per identity. On CFP-FP and IJB-C benchmarks, GSE closes the side-view gap by +23 points at 45° yaw and boosts TAR@FAR=0.001 by +9.4 points, all at CPU-level cost. No retraining. No GPU. Just a gallery that grows smarter every time it meets you.

title: A Distributed Observer with Random Agent Activations over Random Communication Networks
abstract: This paper develops a distributed observer for the forward-Euler discretization of a continuous-time linear time-invariant system under random local operations and random communications. Under uniform stochastic strong connectivity, we establish almost sure exponential convergence of all local state estimates for sufficiently small discretization step sizes. We further examine how the underlying parameters and components affect the admissible range of the discretization step size and the guaranteed convergence rate bound. Unlike related approaches, the proposed method does not require each local unobservable subspace to admit an $A$-invariant complement.

title: Information--control limits for record-indistinguishable reset of a monitored qubit
abstract: A qubit that is continuously monitored from the moment it is prepared in its excited state writes evidence of that preparation into its measurement record. We ask how much control is needed to reset such a qubit to its ground state while keeping its complete record statistically close to the record of an undriven ground-state qubit. The qubit is measured in $σ_z$ at rate $Γ_m$ with efficiency $η$ and has no relaxation. For feedback that acts causally on the record, distinguishability is the Kullback--Leibler divergence $D$ of the controlled record law from the reference law, and the control cost is the quadratic effort $J$, the integrated squared Rabi frequency. We prove that every open-loop drive leaves $D$ infinite and that every admissible control obeys $DJ\geΓ_mU(η,D/κ_0)$, where $U$ is given by a one-parameter family of integrals and $κ_0=1-\ln2$. Our main result is the exact high-effort constant $\lim_{ε\downarrow0}\inf\{DJ/Γ_m: D\leε\}=K(η)$, where $K(η)=[\int_0^π\sqrt{2η(1+\cosθ)^2+(1-η)\sin^2θ}\,dθ]^2$; an explicit sequence of two-phase feedback policies attains it. The first term of the integrand is the population evidence that the record receives while the qubit is rotated toward the ground state. The second is the price of the impurity created when the unrecorded part of the measurement dephases the coherence that the rotation needs; the record receives this evidence later, when the measurement repurifies the qubit. The global constant $c(η)=\inf DJ/Γ_m$ satisfies $K/2\le F_2\le c\le K$, where $F_2$ is again given by an integral; $c$ is known exactly at $η=1$ and in the limit $η\to0$. With any nonzero relaxation rate the unconstrained infimum of $DJ$ vanishes, so $c(η)$ is specific to the relaxation-free model.

title: Self-Healing by design: Immune-system inspired autonomous cyber resilience
abstract: Digital innovations have strongly improved ship capabilities, including command, control & communication, navigation and combat management. In the wake of digitisation and geopolitical stress, resilience against cyber-attacks has become a key challenge. Autonomous Cyber Resilience (ACR) methods, inspired by features of the human immune system, provide a promising perspective. Proofs of concept of autonomous self-healing and self-protecting software have been realised in cloud environments using containerisation, monitoring and deployment technology. However, developing a suitable "cyber immune system" for more complex digital systems is still an intricate challenge. In this paper, we share insights on how ACR methods can be combined with resilience mechanisms present in critical naval and aeronautical manoeuvring systems. Using TNO's "OpPic" application, we show how TNO's Self-Healing for Cyber Security software can provide autonomous mission- and threat-adaptive resilience. On this basis, six guidelines for the design of autonomous cyber resilient systems are derived. The ultimate goal is to enable operators to oversee and control their system's "cyber immune response", to be able to continuously adapt to evolving threats and mission priorities.

title: High-Dimensional Maximally Entangled OAM States by Joint Pump and Modal-Space Engineering
abstract: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) generates correlated photon pairs that inherently exhibit high-dimensional spatial entanglement in orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes. In practice, the resulting two-photon states are typically not maximally entangled due to a highly non-uniform distribution of generated OAM modes. Although pump-beam engineering has emerged as a tool to prepare high-dimensional entangled states, it has usually been restricted to low-dimensional subspaces, i.e., small sets of selected OAM modes for each photon within the full infinite-dimensional two-photon Hilbert space. A general understanding of the requirements for the generation of maximally entangled states (MESs) for any dimensionality $d$ with $d>2$ is lacking. Here, we demonstrate how pump engineering enables the generation of high-dimensional MESs for arbitrary $d$ defined in $d \times d$ subspaces. By identifying the interplay between the spatial pump structure and the choice of OAM subspace, the required pump profile for a target MES is directly determined. Our results reveal that maximal entanglement with OAM requires a careful and nontrivial design of the effective high-dimensional Hilbert subspace.

title: Search-by-Answer Bias in Retrieval Models
abstract: Dense retrievers are meant to select passages that match a query's semantic specification. We show they suffer from search-by-answer bias: they favor passages that mention answer objects the model knows (scores as likely), over passages that support valid alternative answers. We test this with controlled factual contrasts from LAMA/TREx. For each retriever, we measure how strongly the model scores the canonical object over an alternative object using a token-prediction head, and ask whether this score predicts passage rankings. Across eight retrievers, including DPR, Spider variants, Contriever, E5, and Qwen3-Embedding, larger token-prediction scores consistently predict higher retrieval scores for passages containing the corresponding object. This holds when passages differ only in the answer object, and even when the passage that mentions the high-scoring object expresses a wrong relation. Dense retrieval thus exhibits search-by-answer bias during passage selection, shaping which evidence is retrieved.

title: Inverse problem in difference Galois theory
abstract: Let $C$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $K=C(x)$ with $σ(x)=x+1$. We show that every closed subgroup $G\subseteq\GL_n(C)$ with cyclic component group $G/G^\circ$ can be realized as the \PV{} group of a system $σY=A(x)Y$. Here $G^\circ$ denotes the identity component of $G$. Moreover, we can choose the coefficient matrix to have the formal expansion $A(x)=h+O(x^{-2})$ at infinity, where $h\in G(C)$ is semisimple. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture of van der Put and Singer in their monograph \emph{Galois Theory of Difference Equations} (Lecture Notes in Mathematics, vol.~1666). The original results in this paper were entirely generated by ChatGPT 6 and the MechMath Agent Team (MMAT) developed by the Key Laboratory of Mathematics Mechanization, AMSS, CAS. The author reviewed and simplified the initial proofs and verified the correctness of the results.

title: Decomposing Earth Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: Earth observation foundation models produce global metre-resolution embeddings that underpin work across agriculture, ecology, hydrology, and beyond. Yet these embeddings are opaque: each dimension entangles unrelated physical concepts, which makes them difficult to interpret and their robustness hard to assess. Here, we propose sparse autoencoders (SAEs) as a principled way to decompose Earth embeddings into sparse, approximately monosemantic features over an overcomplete dictionary. Because LLM judges of interpretations do not transfer to satellite pixels, and spatial autocorrelation matters, we introduce a tailored evaluation protocol. It scores any SAE on reconstruction at matched sparsity, alignment with reference concepts, and spatial scale, each against baselines that include an SAE whose decoder is a frozen random dictionary. On this protocol, SAEs reconstruct AlphaEarth and Tessera embeddings better than every baseline at matched sparsity. Their features align with far fewer reference concepts than raw embedding dimensions (on AlphaEarth, 88% align with at most one of 20 concept groups, most with none, against a median of 12 per raw dimension). They also carry more of their variance at fine spatial scales (23 to 32% within a 640 m patch for BatchTopK and Matryoshka, against 9%). An SAE with a frozen random decoder shares both properties, which therefore follow from sparsity, whereas only a learned dictionary reconstructs the embedding accurately: on AlphaEarth, trained SAEs leave eight times less variance unexplained. We test the sparse code on two applications, discovering land-cover sub-concepts and detecting out-of-distribution pixels by area-of-applicability estimation. Both indicate how sparse features could be used, but neither is yet reliable enough for practical use. Together, these results are a step toward Earth observation models whose features can be inspected.

title: RoCoMark: Robust Code Watermarking Against LLM-Based Functionality-Preserving Rewriting Attacks
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) present significant challenges to source tracing of generated code, as LLM rewriting can substantially alter the syntactic and structural characteristics of watermarked code. However, existing watermarking methods often suffer severe performance degradation under LLM-based functionality-preserving rewriting attacks. We attribute this vulnerability not merely to the intensity of rewriting, but to a fundamental distribution mismatch between the perturbations encountered during watermark training and the global, non-deterministic rewriting behaviors induced by LLMs. In order to deal with this challenge, we propose RoCoMark, a Robust Code waterMarking framework that explicitly learns and adapts to LLM rewriting behaviors. RoCoMark is a multi-round minimax game between the watermark embedder and LLM rewriter. In each round, the embedder first learns threat profiling from LLM-rewritten code by optimizing the watermark encoder through contrastive learning and knowledge distillation while mitigating catastrophic representation drift. Then the embedder improves strategies by optimizing the watermark encoder and extractor simultaneously. Finally, an adaptive attack-evolution mechanism based on Reflexion and short- and long-term memory pools is applied, enabling continuous interaction between the watermark embedder and evolving rewriting strategies. This iterative attacker-defender process progressively improves the robustness of the watermark against diverse and previously unseen LLM rewriting behaviors. Extensive experiments on four typical benchmarks, under attacks generated by five LLMs, show the effectiveness of RoCoMark. RoCoMark achieves an average detection AUROC of 74.2% and a Rewrite BitACC of 75.3%, while maintaining a code functionality pass rate above 99.7%.

title: Global Classification of the Flat Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
abstract: In every dimension $n\geq3$, we classify positive solutions of the flat Escobar--Yamabe equation on the Euclidean half-space with a possible isolated boundary singularity at the origin. Solutions with a removable singularity are boundary bubbles. Up to dilation, the nonremovable solutions are the cylindrical solution and a family of periodic Delaunay solutions uniquely parametrized by the necksize $ε\in (0,1)$, the minimum of the normalized boundary trace. In each fundamental period $T_ε$, the trace has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate minimum and a nondegenerate maximum. The period and the solution centered at the trace minimum and rescaled to period one depend smoothly on $ε$. As $ε\to 0$, $T_ε= \frac{4}{n-2}\log(1/ε)+O(1)$. As $ε\to 1$, the solutions converge to the cylindrical solution and their periods tend to that of its linearized oscillation. We use uniqueness in the odd and even classes for linear Robin equations to obtain reflection symmetry and continuation in the necksize.

title: The bilinear Hilbert transforms are not of restricted weak type $(1,1,1/2)$
abstract: For every real $α\neq0,1$, we show that the bilinear Hilbert transform \[ H_α(f_1,f_2)(x) =\text{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f_1(x-αy)\,f_2(x-y)\,\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{y} \] fails to map $L^1(\mathbb{R})\times L^1(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ when restricted to characteristic functions of sets of positive finite measure. The counterexample is quantitative and can be realized by sets that are finite unions of intervals of a common arbitrarily small length.

title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
abstract: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. We build and measure three deployments, CUDA kernels on the serving GPU, the same verified engine on an FPGA over PCIe, and a fixed-function block beside the accelerator. On decode routing from three open MoE families, Relief holds the balance near the per-step optimum at every group size and layer time measured. Scored as effective utilization relative to that optimum, the kernel alone matches or exceeds every deployable scheme at every group size, from the hundred-microsecond layer on. The on-die engine widens that lead at every point, recovering up to 37.3 percentage points over the deployed static placement, while adding 0.02% of a current accelerator's transistors.

title: A note on two functional inequalities
abstract: Motivated by some recent works on the following composite functional equation: $$f(x^2+yf(z)) = xf(x)+zf(y), \quad x, y, z \in \R,$$ we solve two related functional inequalities. In each case the solutions are only the constant zero function and the identity on $\R$.

title: Revisiting the conjectures of Shapiro and Schanuel
abstract: We tackle Shapiro's conjecture for exponential polynomials where the coefficients are polynomials, and show that it follows from Schanuel's conjecture. More concretely, given exponential polynomials $f$ and $g$ with infinitely many common zeros, we show that Schanuel's conjecture implies that there is an exponential polynomial $h$ vanishing precisely at all the common zeros of $f$ and $g$.

title: Industrial RPCVD growth of high-purity 28Si epilayers with 29Si content below 30 ppm for high-fidelity electron spin qubits
abstract: Silicon quantum-dot spin qubits are among the most promising routes to large-scale quantum computation, but the residual 29Si nuclear spins in natural silicon impose a hyperfine dephasing limit that must be overcome by isotopic purification. Here, we report the epitaxial growth of high-purity 28Si on float-zone silicon using an industrial reduced-pressure chemical vapor deposition (RPCVD) system. Secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) confirms an 28Si isotopic purity of 99.997%, with the 29Si concentration below 30 ppm. Through a systematic vacuum annealing matrix (850-1150 C), combined with atomic force microscopy and SIMS, we investigate the defect-mediated decomposition of the native oxide and the injection of non-equilibrium vacancies. We identify a thermal-budget window below 950 C within which the thin-layer structure of 28Si remains intact. At 1.5 K, magnetotransport measurements reveal a peak Hall mobility of 12,858 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and a quantum scattering lifetime of 0.659 ps, corresponding to a single-particle level broadening of 499 micro-eV. A double quantum dot fabricated on this platform exhibits a T2* of 0.62 us, a Hahn-echo coherence time of 28.8 us, and single-qubit gate fidelities of up to 99.9% measured by randomized benchmarking. Our results establish industrial RPCVD as a promising route toward high-coherence, high-fidelity silicon spin qubits.

title: Snowflake $q$-Flipping
abstract: We prove a weighted extension of Byun's snowflake-flipping theorem for cored hexagons with unit triangular holes along three crossing lines. The ratio of the tiling generating functions of two regions related by a snowflake flip is given by an explicit product. The result recovers Byun's theorem when all lozenge weights are 1 and resolves an open problem posed by the author in 2024. Our proof uses shuffling identities for semihexagons with dents on two sides.

title: Classification of 3-dimensional complex nilmanifolds - Teichmüller and moduli spaces
abstract: We classify complex nilmanifolds of dimension three by describing the Teichmüller and moduli spaces of left-invariant complex structures for every real six-dimensional nilmanifold.

title: Rate of convergence for the Wiener--Itô chaos in $W_p$ for $1\leq p<\infty$
abstract: Inspired by previous work of Nualart, Ledoux, Peccati, Nourdin, and others, we establish quantitative fourth moment theorems for random variables in a fixed Wiener--Itô chaos and for sums of two Wiener--Itô chaoses in the $W_p$-Wasserstein distance for $1\leq p<\infty$.

title: Linear Set Reconciliation with $O(d)$ Additive Redundancy
abstract: In set reconciliation, two parties holding sets $A, B \subseteq [n]$ with $|A \triangle B| \le d$ seek to recover their symmetric difference from short $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketches, which is equivalent to recovering a $d$-sparse vector $x = \mathbf{1}_{A \triangle B} \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ from its syndrome $Hx \in \mathbb{F}_2^m$. While the information-theoretic counting bound requires $L(n,d) := \log \sum_{i=0}^d \binom{n}{i} = d\log(n/d) + Θ(d)$ bits, existing polynomial-time schemes either use at least $d\lceil\log(n+1)\rceil$ bits (algebraic sketches, leaving an $Ω(d\log d)$-bit gap) or incur a multiplicative $(1+δ)L(n,d)$ overhead (peeling-based sketches), raising the question of whether $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits is achievable with fast updates and decoding. We construct a public-coin randomized $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketch of length $L(n,d) + O(d) + λ\log^{O(1)} n$ that recovers each fixed input of weight at most $d$ with probability at least $1 - 2^{-λ}$, with $\log^{O(1)} n$ update time and $d\exp(O((\log\log n)^2)) = dn^{o(1)}$ worst-case decoding time. In particular, for $n \le 2^{\operatorname{polylog}(d)}$ and $λ\le d^{1-Ω(1)}$, this achieves $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits with $\operatorname{polylog}(d)$ update time and $d^{1+o(1)}$ decoding time. Our construction encodes $d$ permuted rows via randomly scaled Pinsketch syndromes and sketches the resulting bit array column by column. Decoding columns sequentially from prefix predictions cancels recovered rows and exposes undecided rows as decoder-side hints, reducing each column to a hinted sparse recovery problem that we solve via a recursive sketch, HintSketch.

title: Elliptic $L^p$ Carleman estimates near the boundary, quantitative unique continuation, and applications to controllability and stabilization
abstract: This article deals with quantitative unique continuation results up to and from the boundary for second-order elliptic equations with variable coefficients via $L^p$ Carleman estimates. The coefficients in the leading part are assumed to be Lipschitz continuous, and the potentials in the lower order term are allowed to belong to almost scale-invariant $L^q$ spaces. As applications, following the method of Lebeau and Robbiano, we obtain a spectral estimate which yields the interior null controllability of the associated parabolic equation, with an explicit dependence of the control cost on the potential. We also prove the logarithmic decay of the energy for damped wave equations with unbounded dampings and potentials.

title: Offline Evaluation of Information-Theoretic Adaptive Bayesian Vector Magnetometry
abstract: An information-theoretic adaptive Bayesian framework for jointly estimating the longitudinal and transverse components of a magnetic field from the time-resolved optical response of a cold $^{87}$Rb ensemble is presented. A linearly polarized continuous-wave probe drives the $D_2$ $F{=}1 \rightarrow F'{=}0$ transition, producing coherent population trapping (CPT) lineshapes whose width, contrast, and transient dynamics depend sensitively on the ambient magnetic field. The full temporal signal, including early-time transient signal and the steady-state absorption, is compared against a precomputed Maxwell-Bloch forward model. The joint posterior distributions of the longitudinal and transverse components of the magnetic field are updated sequentially, while marginalizing over instrumental nuisance parameters arising from the finite resolution of the magnetic bias coil supply. At each step, the applied longitudinal bias field is chosen to maximize the expected Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the current prior and the anticipated posterior, the expected information gain. As a proof of principle, the protocol is validated in post-processing on pre-recorded experimental scans, and both field components converge to well localized field estimates with weak correlation between them, consistent with the distinct dependence of the CPT resonance position and lineshape on the field components. These results establish an information-theoretic framework for joint vector field estimation from transient cold-atom spectroscopy. However, there exists a systematic forward-model discrepancy, showing that posterior concentration alone does not establish accuracy and motivating nuisance-parameter inference in future online implementations.

title: Joint Design of Communication and Control in Center-Fed Pinching-Antenna Systems
abstract: An analytical and optimization framework for the joint design of communication and control (JDCC) in a center-fed pinching-antenna system (C-PASS) is proposed. Within this framework, the mathematical coupling between data throughput and closed-loop control cost is characterized for JDCC. The analysis captures the mutual interference between concurrently transmitted data and control streams during uplink state uploading and downlink command delivery. Based on this coupling, an achievable communication-control performance region is established for C-PASS. Accordingly, a throughput maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize digital and pinching beamforming subject to control-cost constraints. To address this problem, an alternating optimization algorithm is developed based on constraint reformulation and resource decomposition. The proposed framework reveals how control requirements shape achievable data throughput, guiding the joint beamforming design. Numerical results demonstrate that 1) the proposed C-PASS design achieves 110.2\% higher frame-average throughput than conventional PASS, and 2) the proposed concurrent data-control transmission protocol increases frame-average throughput by up to 66.7\% over separated transmission.

title: 2-Selmer in arithmetic progressions
abstract: We prove uniform asymptotics for the 2-Selmer cardinality in the congruent number family $y^2=x^3-D^2x$ with twisting parameter $D$ restricted to long arithmetic progressions.

title: The strong cylinder conjecture and Rédei's factorization conjecture in three dimensions
abstract: In this paper, we prove the strong cylinder conjecture, that is, for every prime $p$, a set of $p^2$ points in $\mathbb F_p^3$ that meets every affine plane in a multiple of $p$ points is a union of $p$ distinct parallel affine lines. We use this result to resolve Rédei's 1970 factorization conjecture in three dimensions: if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ contain zero and every vector in $\mathbb F_p^3$ has a unique expression $a+b$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$, then one of the two sets is contained in a plane through zero.

title: Fourth-Moment Theorems for Sums of Multiple Wigner Integrals
abstract: We derive quantitative free fourth-moment bounds for sums of two Wigner chaoses of opposite parity under mirror symmetry. The bound contains an explicit remainder consisting of internal contractions of the two kernels. In particular, vanishing of this remainder together with the fourth free cumulant implies convergence to the standard semicircular law. If the higher-order kernel is cyclically symmetric, the internal contractions can be moved to an endpoint and we obtain an explicit fourth-root bound without a remainder. For fully symmetric kernels we obtain a square-root bound under the $W_2$-Wasserstein distance. Using the operator-norm support estimate for Wigner integrals, we also extend these bounds to every $W_p$-Wasserstein distance , where $1\le p<\infty$.

title: Modeling individual and item differences in atypicality inferences with ACT-R
abstract: Humans engage in pragmatic reasoning when encountering mentions of highly predictable events. Such mentions may appear redundant, leading comprehenders to infer that the event is atypical, and accommodate this inference with an explanation for why it is atypical. However, these inferences are not drawn uniformly across individuals, and experimental items vary in inference rates due to differences in event typicality. We show that these patterns can be predicted with a resource-rational cognitive model in which comprehenders select interpretation strategies based on individual exploration tendencies and item-level predispositions. These parameters are estimated independently from participants' Raven's Matrices score, event typicality rating and language model based accommodation likelihood. Taken together with recent findings from reference games, our results motivate a new perspective on the mechanisms that support pragmatic inferences.

title: Differences Between Quantum Symmetries of Graphs and Graph $C^*$-algebras
abstract: We establish several characteristic differences between the quantum symmetry groups of directed graphs and their associated graph $C^*$-algebras in the frameworks of Banica and Joardar-Mandal, respectively, considering the family of finite directed graphs without isolated vertices and without multiple edges.

title: Monotonicity of Erdős sums
abstract: For $k \geq 1$ let $f_k = \sum_{Ω(n)=k} 1/(n\log n)$, where $Ω$ counts prime factors with multiplicity, and let $g_k$ be the same sum restricted to odd $n$. Lichtman showed that $f_k \to 1$, with a global minimum at $k=6$, and Gorodetsky, Lichtman and Wong that $f_k = 1 - 2^{-k}(a_1 k^2 + O(k \log(k+1)))$. We prove that $f_k < f_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 6$, and that $g_k > g_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 1$. The two statements come from one analytic distinction. Writing $\sum_k P_k(s) z^k = ζ(s)^z H(s,z)$, at $s=1$ the point $z=2$ lies on the first singular circle of $H$, and strictly inside the first singular circle of the product with the prime $2$ removed. We show that this distinction decides the direction in general. If the complement of a set of primes $\mathcal{P}$ is thin and its least element is at least $3$, the corresponding sums eventually decrease, so the second theorem is one case of a general phenomenon. The inequalities used at the last step of the first theorem are certified by interval arithmetic.

title: Solution Size Growth as an Obstacle to Iterative Refinement for Linear Optimization
abstract: Iterative refinement is a technique used to exponentially boost the precision of the solution to certain problems by solving a sequence of related problem instances. We study the size of the solutions arising from the sequence of problems produced by the iterative refinement algorithm when applied to linear optimization problems (LPs). We introduce a class of problems for which the size of such solutions can grow exponentially with the number of refinement iterations, and we show evidence that to avoid this undesirable behavior, a black-box LP solver would have to be \emph{lucky}---a concept introduced formally in this paper, by which we mean that the solver would have to return a solution of better quality than what is required by its termination tolerances. Furthermore, we show that the exponential scaling occurs if one uses a natural instantiation of the simplex algorithm using Bland's pivoting rule. We discuss the implications of our lower bound on the solution size for optimization algorithms whose running time depends polynomially on the solution size, such as quantum multiplicative weights update algorithms and quantum matrix games algorithms.

title: Universal robust nonadiabatic geometric quantum computation with shortened composite pulses on superconducting circuits
abstract: The nonadiabatic geometric quantum computation (NGQC) using the nonadiabatic geometric phases is a promising strategy to realize the high-fidelity quantum operation for large-scale quantum processing. However, conventional NQGC schemes combining with optimal control techniques to further improve the gate fidelity and robustness usually either comes at the cost of prolonged gate time or require complex pulse control and only are limited to several certain specific quantum gates or/and for a certain type error source. Thus, implementing universal and robust geometric gates with simple control while further suppressing gate times remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scheme for universal robust geometric gates with shortened composite pulses, where the pulse control is simple and enough available evolution parameters can be utilized to effectively reduce the sensitivity to universal systematic errors. Numerical simulations demonstrate that our universal geometric gates set exhibit much stronger error resilience than their conventional single-loop counterparts. Finally, we also verify the robustness advantage of our scheme on realistic superconducting quantum circuits with experimentally demonstrated technology. Therefore, our work paves an alternative way to achieve high-fidelity and robust geometric quantum computation against multiple errors.

title: GenRM-Flow: Generators are Process-aware Reward Models in Flow Matching
abstract: Aligning video generation models with human preference depends critically on the quality of the reward model that scores generated videos. Current video reward models, however, source their reward signal from a model's representational rather than generative capacity: they either repurpose vision-language models as pixel-space scorers, or train auxiliary scoring heads on top of frozen generator features. The generator's actual ability to predict velocities, denoise latents, and produce videos plays no role in scoring its own generations. We argue that this overlooks a structural property of offline preference learning. Any preference optimization objective that approximates an offline preference dataset mathematically targets a strictly defined KL-constrained optimal policy. By isolating the reward term from this analytical solution and mapping the exact generation log-likelihood to its flow-matching surrogate, the empirical reward emerges deterministically as the relative difference in continuous-time velocity-prediction errors. We formalize this equivalence into GenRM-Flow, a framework where a preference-tuned video generator inherently operates as a process-aware reward model directly in the noisy latent space. We further show theoretically that distinct fine-tuning objectives, whether contrastive like DPO and IPO or non-contrastive like RWR, are alternative optimization pathways toward the same optimal policy, each inducing a reward readout from the generator's velocity-prediction errors. Furthermore, the extracted process reward seamlessly substitutes external VLM scorers in FlowAWR. Operating purely on native latent outputs without auxiliary reward networks, this generative reward drives measurable improvements in downstream video generation.

title: How to isolate charm production mechanisms using charm-anticharm rapidity and azimuthal angle differences
abstract: Charm production in hadronic collisions proceeds via many different processes, which makes it hard to calculate from first principles. Using PYTHIA simulations, we study correlations between charm and anticharm hadrons and show that hard-process charm, final-state splitting charm, and initial-state-shower charm populate markedly different regions of rapidity and azimuthal-angle difference. In particular, selections on the pair rapidity separation, $Δy$, can strongly enrich or suppress the near-side final-state splitting contribution and thereby provide experimental sensitivity to the different production processes. A comparison with existing LHCb $D^0\bar{D}^0$ correlation measurements from Run 1 motivates more differential studies using the substantially larger LHC data sets now available. Extending such measurements to heavy-ion collisions could further distinguish medium modifications of charm produced directly in the hard scattering from charm originating from a parent gluon, providing a new handle on the different interactions of heavy quarks and gluons with the quark-gluon plasma.

title: Computationally Efficient Offline Policy Optimization with All-Policy Linear Realizability
abstract: We study offline policy optimization in finite-horizon Markov decision processes where every deterministic Markov policy has an action-value function linear in known features, with coefficient norm at most $B$. From independent complete trajectories of one unknown Markov behavior policy, and under all-policy occupancy coverage, we give an algorithm with $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ sample dependence and computational complexity polynomial in $\log(2+B)$. The algorithm performs exactly one convex regression per layer. Its stopped-return targets are the values of a single consistent Markov witness policy. A shared reference design and bounded prediction constraints convert fast clipped-regression error into pointwise confidence for the raw linear predictions. Truncated leverage controls the performance loss without requiring empirical covariance approximation at scale $B^{-2}$. Rounding confidence radii upward preserves the exact witness and yields a polynomial-time bit implementation for rational numerical inputs. The guarantees allow any fixed initial-state distribution; realizability and coverage need only be checked for deterministic policies. We also establish a covariance-coverage variant with uniform approximate realizability and polynomial dependence on $B$. A two-action lower bound shows that the accuracy exponent $2$ is necessary.

title: The Query Complexity of Envy-Free Division: Cake, Chores, and Mixed Resources
abstract: We study the query complexity of envy-free division for cake, chores, and resources with both positive and negative values. For arbitrary nonnegative nonatomic chore costs, we give a deterministic exact protocol using $2^{n\log_2 n+O(n)}$ queries and cuts. For both cake and chores, a Las Vegas protocol uses $O(n^{12}\log(2n))$ expected queries and $O(n^{11}\log(2n))$ expected cuts. Conversely, every exact protocol with fixed positive success probability requires $Ω(n^2)$ expected queries in general, even with arbitrarily many output cuts at no query cost. For mixed cake and chores, no uniform finite expected-query bound exists even when every Cut returns the leftmost root or every Cut returns the rightmost root. This holds for any fixed positive multiplicative approximation factor and success probability, already when all net totals are one. An additive impossibility holds on the same normalized domain.

title: Orbital texture of valence band and interband transitions of the type-II multiferroic van der Waals NiI$_2$
abstract: NiI$_2$ is a van der Waals semiconductor characterized by complex electronic and magnetic phases, holding promise towards functional applications. For this purpose, a detailed understanding of its band structure and its excitations is essential to elucidate the electronic and transport properties. We present a comprehensive description of the band structure and of the lowest valence-to-conduction band transition in bulk NiI$_2$, by means of time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations. We describe the orbital character of Ni and I manifolds, and identify the main momentum-resolved features of the valence band and the shallow minima of the conduction band. With this study, we provide a foundational understanding of the electronic structure of NiI$_2$ and its single-particle interband electronic excitation, a benchmark for theoretical models, and a framework for future investigations on this material.

title: Vietnamese Legal Ontology: Every legal answer, traced to the article that grounds it
abstract: A legal answer is only as good as the article it rests on. Vietnam's largest open legal corpus pairs 109,543 published questions and answers with 573,851 legal documents, yet its citations are free text: "Khoan 3 Dieu 101 cua Bo luat nay" ("Clause 3, Article 101 of this Code") names neither the code nor its version. Following the five stages of NVIDIA Auto Ontology, Discover, Ground, Validate, Expose and Learn, we turn four open datasets into a knowledge graph of 11.5 M nodes and 16.0 M edges in which every node and edge carries its source record and method, with no duplicate keys, dangling edges or schema violations. Of 67,868 cited provisions, 61,487 resolve to a dated law version, 51,694 to a parsed article, clause or point, and 19,012 are confirmed word for word. The ontology then shows what flat records hide. 36% of the 78,361 answers whose citations resolve now cite a law that is no longer in force; 2,525 verified citations point to an article number that says something else in the current law; 2,520 citations were re-versioned because their words match a different version than their date suggests; and 5,575 document numbers are shared by several local authorities, one of them by 72. Every number in this paper is computed from the graph.

title: Flex-DDCM: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Image Compression via Diffusion Trajectory Guidance
abstract: Recent zero-shot image compression methods exploit the powerful priors of pretrained diffusion models to produce perceptually pleasing reconstructions without compression-specific training. However, image compression serves not only human viewing but also machine analysis, while existing zero-shot codecs have limited flexibility in meeting the diverse reconstruction requirements of these applications. In this paper, we propose Flex-DDCM, a framework for zero-shot task-oriented image compression via diffusion trajectory guidance. Building on Turbo-DDCM, we adapt the coded diffusion trajectory through task-guided noise selection, embedding the effects of task guidance into the compressed representation. Guidance terms can be applied individually or combined, with timestep-dependent strengths controlling their influence throughout denoising. This design enables task adaptation without introducing additional decoding complexity. Experiments demonstrate flexible trade-offs among pixel fidelity, perceptual quality, and downstream task performance, with competitive performance against trained task-oriented codecs and faster decoding than Diff-ICMH.

title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
abstract: Wireless foundation models learn reusable representations across tasks, configurations, and deployment environments. Their pretraining requires environmental breadth, yet wireless datasets often sample few sites densely. We introduce Channels4World, a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes and a procedural method for generating them. Each scene links a generated environment and RF material assignments to 32 base-station (BS) positions, 16,384 UE positions, and aligned variable-length multipath and ordered interaction records at 3.5 and 7~GHz. The corpus comprises 52.43 billion physical BS-UE pairs, 104.86 billion frequency-specific evaluations, and a 29.14-TB packaged payload. Scene identity aligns geometry, placements, channels, and interactions across frequencies, allowing environmental breadth and within-scene observation density to vary independently. The public release offers predefined subsets at multiple scales and separate access to corpus components. A deterministic 90K/10K scene-level train-test split keeps both frequencies and all scene components together. We characterize morphology, RF materials, and transceiver placement across three generation profiles. Controlled propagation and path-retention analyses show that diffraction materially affects retained-link availability and multipath structure, while the retention policy reduces storage substantially with little loss in represented aggregate power. Under matched training exposure, models trained on broader scene collections perform better on held-out scenes, although an equal-episode control shows that scene count alone cannot explain the gain. By making environmental breadth explicit and controllable, Channels4World supports the development and evaluation of wireless foundation models for generalization across deployment environments.

title: Sharp coercivity estimates and stability loss for the Ginzburg-Landau energy
abstract: In this paper we investigate how the coercivity of the Hessian of the Ginzburg-Landau energy at local minimizers $u$ depends on the Ginzburg-Landau parameter $κ$ in the regime of large $κ$. This question is motivated by its crucial role in the numerical approximation of energy minimizers. Accounting for the degeneracy that is induced by phase invariance and possible additional neutral directions, we establish a universal lower bound of order $κ^2$ for the inverse coercivity constant $ρ_u(κ)$ of local minimizers with uniformly bounded Hessian kernel dimension. For nonvanishing states that satisfy a quantitative subcriticality condition, we prove a matching upper bound, showing that the quadratic scaling is sharp. On a fixed annulus with a fixed smooth magnetic potential, we then construct nonvanishing local minimizers for which $ρ_u(κ)\simeqκ^4$. Moreover, we exhibit branches of strictly stable local minimizers along which the inverse coercivity constant diverges as stability is lost. Consequently, no locally bounded upper estimate depending only on $κ$ can hold uniformly over all phase-nondegenerate local minimizers, even for a fixed domain and magnetic potential.

title: High-sensitivity sensing technology of 10 MHz radio frequency electric field based on Rydberg atoms
abstract: To address the pressing need for high-sensitivity, miniaturized electric field sensors in the short-wave communication band (3-30 MHz), this study proposes and demonstrates a radio frequency electric field quantum sensing scheme based on cesium atomic Rydberg states and the electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) effect. The scheme employs an all-infrared optical design, utilizing 852 nm probe light, 1470 nm dressing light, and 780 nm coupling light to efficiently prepare the 49P3/2 Rydberg state in a room-temperature cesium vapor cell, which is then probed non-destructively via ladder-type four-level EIT spectroscopy.

title: Singular parabolic Anderson models - From flat space to geometric contexts
abstract: These notes (which grew out of some lecture notes prepared for the first Aarhus Summer School in Analysis and Probability) are an introduction to the parabolic Anderson model (PAM), or otherwise stated the stochastic heat equation $\partial_{t} u \,=\, \tfrac{1}{2}Δ\, u \,+\, β\, u\,\dot{W}$. In this system, a multiplicative random potential $\dot{W}$ drives the solution away from the smooth spreading of the classical heat flow and toward intermittency. Namely one observes that mass concentrates, as time grows, on a few tall and widely separated peaks. Through the Feynman-Kac representation this analytic phenomenon has an equivalent probabilistic reading as the localization of a directed polymer in a random environment. We first develop this picture on the flat space $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, covering the construction of the driving noise, well-posedness of the equation, and two-sided bounds on the moment Lyapunov exponents that quantify intermittency. We then turn to the more original goal of the monograph: understanding how these phenomena, and the exponents attached to them, change when $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is replaced by a genuinely geometric background, such as a sub-Riemannian manifold or a fractal set. Throughout, the emphasis is on concepts, main results, and the intuition behind their proofs, rather than on exhaustive technical detail.

title: Ranks of fibers in random elliptic surfaces
abstract: For random integer polynomials $P$ of arbitrary degree we prove that for $100\%$ of elliptic surfaces $y^2=x^3-P(t)^2x$ the average 2-Selmer rank of the fibers is 3. Consequently, for $100\%$ these random elliptic surfaces we establish a lower bound for the proportion of fibers attaining algebraic rank $0$ and $1$.

title: Unlearning at Speed: Rapid Activation Dampening for Efficient Machine Unlearning in Real-World Face Recognition
abstract: Machine unlearning has become increasingly important in face recognition, where regulations like the GDPR empower users to request the removal of their personal data from deployed models. However, most existing unlearning methods are designed for closed-set classification with small-scale models and training data, and therefore do not generalize to real-world face recognition systems, which operate in an open-set setting with large-scale models and data. In this work, we propose Rapid Activation Dampening (RAD), a fast and targeted unlearning method tailored specifically for large-scale open-set face recognition. RAD approximates differences in average neuron activations between forget and retain identities, identifying and selectively suppressing neurons that are most associated with the targeted identity through a sensitivity-controlled dampening mechanism. We further propose the Forget Score (FS), which addresses the mismatch between existing unlearning metrics and open-set problems by providing a probabilistic interpretation of forgetting directly in the representation space. Experiments across several recent large-scale face recognition architectures and datasets show that RAD achieves strong forgetting while preserving overall model utility and substantially improving unlearning speed.
