title: Watching Itself Watch: Self-Auditing Visual Reliance for Video Reasoning
abstract: Video reasoning hinges on a small number of visually decisive tokens embedded in otherwise largely language-driven chains of thought. Yet prevailing post-training methods such as GRPO overlook this structure, assigning coarse trajectory-level rewards while requiring multiple rollouts and often costly external judges. We introduce Visually-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation (VIOS), a post-training framework that identifies where a model under-utilizes visual evidence and concentrates learning at those positions. Our key insight is that a model can audit its own visual reliance: the divergence between its next-token distributions with and without the video reveals how strongly each prediction depends on the visual input. Measuring this reliance for both a student and an answer-privileged teacher exposes a per-token reliance gap, identifying positions where the teacher exploits visual evidence that the student overlooks. VIOS translates this signal into dense, targeted supervision through three complementary components: an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher that co-evolves with the student, a contrastive objective that encourages predictions to depend on the video, and a reliance-gap gate that focuses learning on visually under-utilized tokens. Crucially, VIOS requires only a single on-policy rollout from a single model, without external rewards, judges, or larger teachers. Across 12 benchmarks spanning general, temporal, spatial, knowledge-intensive, and long-video understanding, VIOS consistently improves three model backbones and outperforms contemporary video-reasoning systems, while training in over 9x fewer steps, 60x fewer FLOPs, and 111x fewer generated tokens. Project page: https://vision.cs.utexas.edu/projects/VIOS/

title: BMO Vorticity Strong Ill-Posedness for the 2d Incompressible Euler Equation
abstract: For the two dimensional incompressible Euler equation, Yudovich, and independently Serfati, extended the classical existence and uniqueness class to include vorticity with mild singularity. This class is sometimes called the generalized Yudovich class. Then, Vishik extended the uniqueness class to include vorticity in BMO, allowing for stronger singularities than the generalized Yudovich class. In this work, we prove strong ill-posedness of vorticity in BMO.

title: UltraVoxelGS: Voxel-First Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction
abstract: We present UltraVoxelGS, a 3D ultrasound reconstruction method that achieves both fast reconstruction and physically faithful rendering for the first time, bringing live spatial feedback during 2D ultrasound scanning within reach. This is made possible by a feed-forward design that predicts a complete Gaussian scene representation from posed ultrasound images directly, entirely bypassing the per-scene optimization bottleneck that has confined prior methods to offline use. Realising such feed-forward prediction in this setting is non-trivial: unlike natural images, ultrasound slices share at most one-dimensional intersections and exhibit view-dependent appearance due to acoustic propagation and attenuation, violating the dense overlap and photometric consistency assumed by existing feed-forward Gaussian methods. Hence, to achieve fast reconstruction, we introduce a feed-forward voxel-to-Gaussian pass that decouples representation size from input count by lifting all posed slices into a fixed-size voxel support and predicting Gaussian parameters directly. For faithful rendering, we propose ultrasound-aware appearance rendering strategy factorize reflection from cumulative attenuation during training and exploit appearance continuity among spatially adjacent slices for efficient Render-time Appearance Adaptation. On both real-world and simulated datasets, UltraVoxelGS achieves best PSNR/SSIM compared with per-scene optimization baselines while reducing inference from 10-20 minutes to approximately 10 seconds (over 35 times faster) and scales to sequences exceeding 1,000 frames. Code is available at https://github.com/YuebyYue/UltraVoxelGS-camera-ready.

title: BharatSynthQA: A Context-Grounded Question Answering Dataset on Indian Temples and Religious Heritage
abstract: India's temples and other places of worship are among its richest repositories of cultural heritage, bringing together religious tradition, history, architecture, and art. Due to the widespread curiosity, people increasingly turn to Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistants for information about them. Current models are rarely trained or evaluated on this domain. We present BharatSynthQA, a passage grounded question answering (QA) dataset focused on Indian temples, which also covers other religious sites connected to them. Our pipeline crawls Wikipedia from topics seeded by authentic heritage sources, filters articles for topical relevance, and locations in India. Further it generates Boolean, factoid, and explanatory QA pairs with a fewshot prompted LLM. An LLM judge filters the pairs on answer correctness, retaining 98,677 of 131,494 generated pairs. Additionally, 300 human-annotated pairs are released separately as a reference set. Human evaluation of the subsample of this dataset showed 89.83% of the questions were formed correctly. Benchmarking five current LLMs shows that factoid token F1 is only 0.18-0.30 without the source passage but 0.73-0.77 with it, indicating that this domain is poorly captured in model knowledge. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/theshivam7/bharatsynth-qa to support research on culturally grounded QA and retrieval-augmented generation for Indian heritage.

title: Elastic frontogenesis sets the spectra of smooth elastic turbulence
abstract: Most turbulent flows are sustained by inertia, which transfers energy across scales and produces characteristic power-law spectra. Yet dilute polymer solutions also exhibit turbulence when inertia is negligible: in this state, known as elastic turbulence, the velocity field remains spatially smooth while both the velocity and the polymer conformation exhibit robust power-law spectra. How a smooth flow, lacking a hierarchy of eddies, generates such multiscale structure has remained unexplained. Here we show that the missing mechanism is elastic frontogenesis, whereby the flow spontaneously organizes polymer stress into thin sheets that are stretched within their plane and compressed across their thickness, causing their amplitude to grow as they become thinner. Because the fronts are sheet-like structures, this amplification-thinning law uniquely determines the polymer conformation spectrum, while the Stokes response transfers the same geometric scaling to the velocity field, reconciling broadband spectra with spatial smoothness. Being geometric rather than model-specific, elastic frontogenesis provides an organizing principle for viscoelastic flows and the viscoelastic analogue of vortex stretching in inertial turbulence.

title: Frank Elastic Anisotropy Induced by Anisotropic Attractive Interactions in Nematic Liquid Crystals
abstract: We present a mean-field theory to calculate the Frank elastic constants of a nematic liquid crystal with an anisotropic Maier--Saupe (MS) attractive interaction restricted to a cylindrical interaction volume of height $L_z$ and diameter $L_c$. The shape of the interaction volume is characterized by the aspect ratio $α_z=L_z/L_c$, which controls the spatial anisotropy of the attractive interaction. We derive expressions for the splay $(K_{11})$, twist $(K_{22})$, and bend $(K_{33})$ elastic constants and calculate them numerically as functions of concentration and temperature. At the special aspect ratio $α_z=\sqrt{3}/2$, the transverse and axial second moments are equal, yielding the one-constant relation $K_{11}=K_{22}=K_{33}$ over the full ranges of concentration and temperature considered. Away from this point, oblate and prolate interaction volumes produce distinct elastic anisotropies. Changes in concentration or temperature can also reverse the hierarchy of the three elastic constants.

title: CHO-Bench: How Do Context Hints Affect Ad Rankings in LLM Advertising?
abstract: LLM advertising selects advertisements based on user conversations, where user needs may extend beyond explicit product searches. ChatGPT Ads allows advertisers to provide natural-language context hints describing what they offer, who may find it useful, and when it may be useful, as additional information for ranking advertisements across diverse user conversations. However, how to effectively construct these hints remains unclear. We formulate Context Hint Optimization (CHO) as the problem of constructing context hints to improve an advertisement's ranking under a given budget. Drawing on established marketing frameworks, we develop seven context hint generation strategies covering What, Who, and When, along with a Unified strategy that combines all seven dimensions. We introduce CHO-Bench and conduct over 1.19 million paired evaluations across five datasets using embedding-based and LLM-based rankers. Our results show that context hints improve advertisement rankings under the evaluated offline rankers. While individual strategies achieve similar average gains and Unified offers no consistent advantage, strategy differences become more pronounced under specific generation-ranking configurations, with embedding-based and LLM-based rankers favoring different information dimensions. Increasing the hint budget further improves rankings with diminishing marginal gains. These findings establish an offline benchmark for studying ad-side ranking optimization in LLM advertising and highlight opportunities for model-specific hint selection and budget-aware generation and aggregation.

title: Bistatic UAV-Based 3D SAR Imaging Using Integrated Sensing and Communications Transceivers
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks enable autonomous systems to jointly perform radar sensing and wireless communication using common spectral and hardware resources. Prior art on ISAC-enabled UAV for SAR focused on monostatic configurations for two-dimensional target imaging. In this work, we propose a bistatic UAV tomographic SAR framework in which the IEEE~802.11ad waveform, RF hardware, and spectral resources are jointly utilized for communication and radar sensing for three-dimensional (3D) localization of complex targets. Specifically, we demonstrate how communication packets transmitted from a master ISAC transceiver UAV to a passive receiver UAV are exploited for timing and frequency synchronization, motion compensation, and 3D localization of targets, without requiring auxiliary infrastructure on the passive receiver for these tasks. We evaluate the proposed framework for localizing automotive targets over elevated terrain, with Monte Carlo simulations modeling synchronization and platform motion errors. The results demonstrate improved localization accuracy compared with conventional InSAR-based localization. The interplay between radar and communication performances are further evaluated using diverse modulation schemes.

title: Measurements of $C\!P$ violation with charm hadrons at Belle and Belle II
abstract: Recent searches for $C\!P$ violation in charm-hadron decays at Belle and Belle II are presented. The measurements cover $D^+_{(s)}\toηh^+$, $D\toππ$, $D^0\to K_S^0K_S^0$, and $D^0\toπ^+π^-π^0$, together with the singly Cabibbo-suppressed baryon decays $Ξ_c^+\toΣ^+h^+h^-$ and $Λ_c^+\to ph^+h^-$, where $h=π,K$. The Belle II analyses use the Run~1 data sample of $428\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, supplemented by $980\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of Belle data for the $K_S^0K_S^0$ measurements. We report preliminary results for the $ηh^+$ modes, complementary tests of the isospin structure of $D\toππ$, and an application of inclusive charm-flavor tagging. The first individual decay-rate asymmetries in these three-body charmed-baryon modes also provide tests of $U$-spin symmetry. All reported asymmetries are consistent with $C\!P$ symmetry within the present precision.

title: OriDynamics: Towards a World Model for Biomolecular Dynamics
abstract: Biomolecular recognition and regulation depend on atomic interactions that change as molecular partners fluctuate and adopt alternative conformations. Modeling these processes requires ensembles that capture both conformational diversity and coordinated atomic fluctuations between interacting molecules. Here we present OriDynamics, a unified framework for all-atom ensemble generation across protein monomers and complexes with small molecules or protein partners. OriDynamics introduces a latent ensemble decomposition that couples broad conformational exploration in a compact structural latent space with local all-atom sampling around generated proposals. Ensemble-level supervision constrains mean positions, fluctuation amplitudes and joint coordinate covariance to capture coordinated atomic variability within and between molecular partners. Across benchmarks of proteins and their complexes, OriDynamics demonstrates superior overall performance in conformational coverage, atomic fluctuation fidelity and interaction geometry compared with leading baselines. Application studies further demonstrate recovery of alternative functional conformations and partner-dependent changes in conformational ensembles alongside sampling of configurations associated with ligand dissociation. These capabilities provide a foundation for a biomolecular world model that represents accessible molecular states and their dependence on interaction context.

title: On the Instance-Specific Sharp Rates for Constrained Least Squares Estimators in the Sequence Model
abstract: We develop a general methodology based on the Feature Space Decomposition framework for establishing explicit, instance-specific sharp rates for the expected estimation error of convex-constrained least squares estimators in the sequence model, without requiring estimates of localized Gaussian mean widths. We apply this methodology to $\ell_q$ ellipsoids, $\ell_1$ balls, and $kB_1^N\cap B_\infty^N$, obtaining matching upper and lower bounds in the nondegenerate regime. Our methodology also extends beyond Gaussian noise to symmetric noise distributions satisfying a Poincaré inequality. We also provide an elementary proof of the instance-specific sharp rate for isotonic regression for any well-specified signal and any noise level. Combining this result with Han's asymptotic reduction, we further obtain explicit instance-specific sharp convergence rates in probability for isotonic regression in Gaussian linear regression under general signal-dependent asymptotics conditions.

title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment
abstract: Unplanned 30-day intensive care unit (ICU) readmission is a critical benchmark for evaluating healthcare quality. Most predictive models assume readmission risk depends solely on a patient's individual pathophysiological state, ignoring hospital operational context and resource capacity. In practice, discharge decisions are dynamic trade-offs between patient stability and bed turnover pressures. To address this gap, we develop an Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for ICU discharge risk assessment. The system combines multi-agent collaborative extraction with self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to eliminate template noise from progress notes, while constructing departmental workload indicators alongside admission flow features, continuous vital signs, and sparse medical codes (ICD/DRG). Addressing severe class imbalance (about 10.5% readmissions) and alarm fatigue, we implement data normalization, class reweighting, and decision-threshold calibration. In 20 independent runs across 20,000 ICU stays from MIMIC-III, empirical findings demonstrate that: vital signs alone have limited predictive capacity under real-world class imbalance (PR-AUC of 0.1387 +/- 0.0086); directly concatenating raw text embeddings degrades decision tree performance (XGBoost and LightGBM PR-AUC drop to 0.3893 and 0.4030); whereas an end-to-end multimodal fine-tuning architecture (Transformer E2E FineTune) utilizing layer-wise parameter freezing and differential learning rates reverses text negative transfer, achieving the highest AUROC of 0.8288 +/- 0.0110, PR-AUC of 0.4373 +/- 0.0310, and F1-Score of 0.4757 +/- 0.0196. Operational indicators supply independent risk signals, laying an engineering foundation for high-utility clinical decision support tools.

title: Semiclassical Asymptotics of Entanglement in Torus-Link States
abstract: We investigate the entanglement entropy of topological quantum states associated with $T_{d,\,dn}$ torus links in (2+1)-dimensional SU(2) Chern--Simons theory at level $k$. These links consist of $d$ components with pairwise linking number $n$, and the corresponding link-complement states provide a natural setting to study multipartite entanglement in topological quantum field theories. We analyze the semiclassical limit $k\to\infty$ of the entanglement entropy by deriving the asymptotic behavior of the moments of the reduced density matrix. To achieve this, we decompose the integrable-representation space into left-edge, right-edge, and bulk regions and employ the stationary-phase method to evaluate their respective contributions. We find that the leading asymptotic behavior is governed entirely by the two edge regions, while the bulk contribution is asymptotically suppressed. The resulting expression for the limiting entanglement entropy is given in terms of Hurwitz zeta functions and exhibits a dependence on the residue class of $k$ modulo $n$. We further investigate the dependence of the limiting entanglement entropy on the winding parameter $n$ and the number of link components $d$. In the large-$d$ limit, the entropy reduces to a binary entropy determined by two normalized weights associated with the left and right edges. Finally, we show that the two iterated limits, $k\to\infty$ and $d\to\infty$, commute, reproducing the result obtained previously by taking the large-party limit first.

title: Shaping Useful Noise: Energy Distributions Predict Visual Pretraining Quality
abstract: Synthetic data can scale visual pretraining, but current selection criteria only partially explain which datasets train strong representations. We propose using the energy profile of a dataset--the distribution of log-probability levels it occupies under a normalised real-image density model--as an audit and curation principle for synthetic data. To operationalise this view, we introduce Energy-Level Distribution Distance (ELD), which compares real and synthetic energy distributions. Real images span sparse high-likelihood scenes and dense low-likelihood textures, so useful synthetic data should cover this energy range rather than collapse to likely but low-variation samples. Across diverse synthetic datasets, ELD exposes mismatches missed by FID and predicts pretraining performance beyond FID, LPIPS variation, and feature-space recall, including across CNN and ViT self-supervised settings. We then use ELD to resample and mix synthetic sources, matching the real-image energy histogram while preserving diversity and improving downstream transfer.

title: Curve theory in $S^2\times S^2$ with applications to ruled surfaces in $S^3$
abstract: The Riemannian product $S^2\times S^2$ of two unit spheres admits several important geometric interpretations. It can be identified both with the complex quadric $Q^2$ and with the space $\mathcal{L}(S^3)$ of oriented geodesics in the unit $3$-sphere $S^3$. In this paper, we first develop a unified framework for the geometry of curves in $S^2\times S^2$. We introduce projection-regular curves in $S^2\times S^2$ and their curvature data, and prove a congruence theorem for these curves. As an application of this framework, regarding $S^2\times S^2$ as the complex quadric $Q^2$, we classify Kähler magnetic geodesics associated with the product Kähler--Einstein structure. For closed generic projection-regular curves, we establish a sharp Fenchel-type inequality. We then identify $S^2\times S^2$ with the space $\mathcal{L}(S^3)$ of oriented geodesics in the unit $3$-sphere $S^3$ and apply our curve theory to ruled surfaces in $S^3$. In particular, we prove that every nonsingular closed generic projection-regular ruled surface attaining equality in the Fenchel-type inequality is an embedded torus.

title: 3R-Adapter: Retrieval, Rewiring, and Refinement for Efficient Adaptation of 3D Reconstruction Model
abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models have demonstrated strong generalization under large-scale pre-training, yet they struggle in long-tail scenarios such as low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation. We observe relational attention structure collapse, manifested as the failure of cross-view correspondences, as a primary cause of these limitations. While adaptation offers a practical way to bridge this gap, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches mainly perform channel-wise feature adjustment and lack mechanisms to explicitly adapt relational structures, leaving correspondence failures unresolved. In this work, we formulate adaptation of 3D reconstruction models as a problem of correspondence recovery under domain shift and propose 3R-Adapter, a PEFT paradigm for long-tail 3D reconstruction scenarios. Our method consists of three components: Deformable Retrieval for task-adaptive relation candidate retrieval, Relational Rewiring for reconstructing cross-view relational structures, and Consistency Refinement for injecting the rewired relations into stable predictions. Extensive experiments on low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation demonstrate that our approach significantly improves robustness over existing PEFT methods while maintaining efficient lightweight adaptation. Our code is released at https://github.com/PKU-OV3-LAB/3R-Adapter.

title: ChainCheck: Near-Perfect Evidence-Sufficiency Scores Can Conceal Sensitivity to Construction Artifacts -- Paired Conditional Contrasts that Expose an Evaluation Confound
abstract: Evidence-sufficiency benchmarks ask whether a model can tell a complete passage set from one whose reasoning chain is broken. When broken sets are made by editing text, near-perfect sufficiency scores--and even positive crossed-control scores--need not demonstrate multi-hop reasoning. We present ChainCheck, an evaluation-validity audit that pairs validator-certified counterfactual cells with artifact-only baselines. In an exploratory crossed control on 2,214 HotpotQA pairs, a language-model scorer that never reads the chain reaches a nominal AUC of 0.997, and a one-string match reaches the maximum of the crossed chain-sensitivity statistic CS4 (0.500), while the 11 evaluated systems score from 0.308 to 0.484; the two statistics are different metrics. We therefore read positive CS4 as operational bridge-consistency sensitivity, not as semantic multi-hop reasoning. Every system is also sensitive to one extra edit, and the edits are detectable according to model-based naturalness ratings. On an independent HotpotQA set of 2,276 pairs, patterns pre-specified on MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA did not replicate: 5 of 6 trained readouts were edit-dominated, and the reference judge's selectivity interval [-0.007, +0.042] includes zero. Judge scores also depended on batch layout. The MuSiQue and 2Wiki records are public; the HotpotQA records and the fine-tuned checkpoints are not, so external reproduction is partial.

title: On Non-Deterministic Representation of Boolean Functions
abstract: We study non-deterministic representation of Boolean functions by polynomials, introduced by (de Wolf, 2000). A polynomial $p(x)$ is said to be a non-deterministic polynomial for a Boolean function $f$ if for all $a\in\{0,1\}^n$, $p(a)\neq 0$ iff $f(a)=1$. The non-deterministic degree of $f$, denoted $\mathsf{ndeg}(f)$, is the minimal degree of a non-deterministic polynomial for $f$. In this work, we show the following main results: - Almost all Boolean functions on $n$ variables have non-deterministic degree at most $n/2 + O(\sqrt{n\log n})$. This confirms a conjecture of (Iyer et al., 2023). Together with the lower bound of (Iyer et al., 2023) it establishes a tight bound on the rational degree of a random Boolean function up to lower order terms. - We disprove a conjecture of (Kothari et al., 2026) about effective hypercube nullstellensatz for more than two polynomials. On the positive side, we also identify a constraint under which an effective hypercube nullstellensatz holds for many polynomials.

title: Pairwise distortion distribution for compression and quantization
abstract: Choosing the latent dimension is a critical challenge in data compression, where conventional hyperparameter optimization is costly and ad hoc. Intrinsic dimension provides a good alternative, which connects information-theoretic notions such as Renyi information dimension (RID) to rate-distortion dimension and random codebook compression. In this work, we introduce the pairwise distortion distribution (PDD) and its asymptotic limit, pairwise dimension (PD), which generalize the correlation integral to general distortion measures. We show that PD bounds RID, and PDD provides a lower bound for random codebook quantization performance, which can guide a practical use for compression, quantization, and dimensionality reduction applications.

title: Khintchine's limit theorem for monotone convolutions
abstract: We prove that every weak limit of monotone convolution powers is monotonically infinitely divisible. In contrast, we prove that every probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ can occur as a weak limit of monotone convolutions of an infinitesimal triangular array. We also discuss similar limit theorems for multiplicative monotone convolution on the unit circle.

title: Executable Human Study Programs with Silicon Participants
abstract: We introduce HumanStudyProgram, a framework that represents a documented human study as an executable program with configurable LLM-based silicon participants. Its computational abstraction separates study logic from participant implementation through standardized APIs for presenting information and collecting responses. We implement a researcher-facing authoring tool that reconstructs source-linked study descriptions from papers and supplementary materials, supports researcher review, and generates executable HumanStudyProgram artifacts. Researchers can then configure silicon participants, run the programs, and analyze results from aggregate findings to individual responses. We demonstrate the approach through study cases and evaluate the tool through a hands-on expert review with 12 social science researchers. All completed the workflow and identified potential uses in understanding published protocols, prototyping studies, and examining AI behavior. We aim to improve the reproducibility of human studies by reconstructing their documented procedures as programs that others can reuse and build upon.

title: Five-Entropic Matroids Are Quinary
abstract: A finite matroid is representable over a field if its elements can be assigned vectors over that field such that the rank of every subset equals the dimension of the span of its vectors. For an integer q >= 2, a matroid is q-entropic if there exists a random vector indexed by its ground set, with each coordinate taking values in a common q-element alphabet, such that the entropy of every marginal subvector equals the rank of the corresponding subset multiplied by log q. It remains open to determine for which values of q every q-entropic matroid is representable over a field. For q=2 and q=3, representability over F_q has long been known. More recently, it was established that every 4-entropic matroid is representable over F_4 and that the 6-entropic matroids are precisely the regular matroids, that is, those representable over every field. We settle the previously unresolved five-symbol case, proving that a finite matroid is 5-entropic if and only if it is representable over F_5. For the nontrivial implication, we use Matúš's equivalence between entropic and partition representations. We show that a degree-five partition representation induces, on each embedded U_{2,4}-minor, an F_5-linear representation after coordinatewise relabeling, with a rescaling class independent of the chosen linearization. Using the foundation presentation of Baker and Lorscheid, we verify the compatibility relations among these local classes and thereby obtain a global F_5-representation.

title: Harness Matters: Measuring and Dissecting Security Resilience in Web Agents
abstract: Web agents extend LLMs from text generation to real-world web interaction by relying on execution harnesses that interpret user goals, perceive webpages, plan actions, and ground model decisions into browser operations. While prior work has recognized that agent security depends on more than the backend model alone, how harness design quantitatively shapes web-agent security remains insufficiently measured. To systematically study web-agent harness security, we first characterize web-agent harnesses as a four-stage execution workflow covering goal interpretation, webpage perception, reasoning and planning, and action execution. Based on this abstraction, we build WebTrap Farm, a systematic and extensible evaluation framework covering three representative attack categories: malicious user prompts, malicious prompt injection, and deceptive web design. To avoid conflating security with task capability, we use paired usability calibration tasks to separate genuine defensive behavior from capability limitations. Our evaluation shows that existing web-agent harnesses remain vulnerable to typical attacks, with some unsafe behaviors occurring even without explicit attack content, revealing harness-intrinsic security failures (RQ1). Statistical analysis further shows that both harness and backend model significantly affect security outcomes, indicating that deployed-agent security is jointly shaped by the harness and backend model (RQ2). Finally, we localize where defensive behavior emerges across workflow stages and identify more secure design mechanisms, providing actionable guidance for building more robust web agents (RQ3). These findings highlight the web-agent harness as an important security boundary and motivate moving beyond model-centric defenses toward harness-level security design.

title: An Analytic Evaluation of Euler Sharp Sums
abstract: We give a direct analytic evaluation of the Euler sharp sums $ζ^\sharp(2,\{1\}^{d-3},\overline{2})$ for all even integers $d\ge4$, expressing them in terms of ordinary multiple zeta values of depth at most two. The proof reduces these sharp sums to a harmonic-number series and evaluates it using a generating-function identity, thereby proving the even-depth case of a conjecture of Xu and Zhao.

title: Beyond Prediction Residuals: Conformal Regret Calibration for Robust Contextual Linear Optimization
abstract: Predict-then-optimize systems convert contextual forecasts into decisions, yet conformal robust optimization typically calibrates prediction residuals rather than downstream loss. For linear optimization, this parameter-space geometry can be badly misaligned with decision risk: large objective perturbations may preserve the optimizer, while small boundary-crossing perturbations may cause substantial regret. We introduce Conformal Regret Sets, a post-hoc, model-agnostic framework that conformalizes an optimization-derived regret surrogate and uses its calibrated level set for minimax-regret refinement. We first show that directly conformalizing exact regret, although sufficient to certify the nominal predict-then-optimize decision, yields a degenerate robust problem: absent an exogenous bounded support, every alternative decision has unbounded worst-case regret. We therefore use SPO+, a pointwise upper bound on exact regret, as the conformal score, obtaining distribution-free finite-sample marginal regret guarantees under exchangeability. For contextual linear programs, the resulting set decomposes into polyhedral pieces aligned with the normal fan of the feasible polytope. A vertex is active if and only if its predicted suboptimality gap is at most half the calibrated threshold $η$, enabling local, output-sensitive generation of all relevant pieces. Moreover, if $Γ$ is the predicted gap to the closest competing vertex, the nominal and refined decisions admit the sharper worst-case-regret certificate $(η-2Γ)_+$, with an exact early exit when $η\leq 2Γ$. Experiments on contextual fractional knapsack validate the geometry and certificates: continuous refinement reduces the $0.95$-quantile and $\operatorname{CVaR}_{0.95}$ of regret by $9.1\%$ and $13.1\%$ relative to nominal PTO, while vertex-restricted refinement changes only $10.0\%$ of nominal decisions.

title: Polynomial Sample Complexity of Noninteractive Simulation over Finite Alphabets
abstract: We study noninteractive simulation from a finite correlated source. Alice and Bob observe independent copies of the source and generate outputs without communication. We give a quantitative construction for arbitrary finite output alphabets: for every fixed source, a joint law that is simulable with arbitrarily many samples can be approximated using a number of samples polynomial jointly in the output alphabet sizes and the inverse accuracy. We first study binary outputs. A one-sided Wright--Fisher comparison gives a source-dependent explicit exponent and a finite-head Gaussian-threshold representation. We then handle arbitrary finite output alphabets through averaged influence regularity, simplex-preserving Gaussian moment lifting, and a common Gaussian projection for all correlated-prefix states. The sample exponent is independent of the output alphabet sizes. For a concrete biased binary source we certify an explicit exponent below $19$.

title: AutoQS: Automated Quantization Strategy Design with Large Language Models
abstract: Quantization reduces LLM deployment costs, but effective strategies must balance model quality and storage. LLM-driven search can automate strategy design through repeated proposal and evaluation. This process must identify useful strategies within a limited evaluation budget. The key challenge is that \textit{actual quantization is expensive, while inexpensive proxies may not reflect quantized-model performance.} To address this challenge, we present AutoQS, an \textbf{Auto}mated \textbf{Q}uantization \textbf{S}trategy Design with LLMs. AutoQS keeps weight precision fixed and searches group-size allocations across layers and operators under deployment constraints. Evaluation history guides coordinated LLM proposals, while deterministic validation ensures compatible allocations. An inexpensive quality proxy evaluates candidates, and an candidate repository retains alternative allocations to inform subsequent proposals. Periodic actual quantization complements these proxy evaluations with measured quality and checkpoint storage, providing feedback for further search within the evaluation budget. Experiments on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct show that AutoQS improves seven-task average accuracy over uniform-group GPTQ and AWQ by 0.70 and 1.12 percentage points, respectively, at four-bit weight precision.

title: ShiftCache: Fast and Exact Indel Effect Prediction by Reusing Shifted Reference Encodings
abstract: Sequence-to-function models such as AlphaGenome and Borzoi read up to a megabase of DNA and score a genetic variant by comparing their predictions for the reference and alternate sequences. Insertions and deletions (indels) are costly to score, because an indel usually shifts the unchanged DNA after it onto a different pooling grid, which prevents direct reuse of the reference's encoder activations. The AlphaGenome Atlas scored more than 100 million indels with three full model passes each, although the DNA after an indel matches the reference shifted by the indel's length. We present ShiftCache, an exact reuse system that encodes each shifted reference once and shares it among all variants scored in the same window with the same shift. ShiftCache copies every encoder output a variant can reuse and recomputes the rest in batched tiles. On held-out AlphaGenome windows shared by many indels, in strict fp32 on one A6000, ShiftCache is 3.5 to 6.5$\times$ faster than deduplicated dense execution and 1.6 to 2.7$\times$ faster than our adaptation of layer-by-layer reuse to indels. It is 3.5 to 4.1$\times$ faster than dense reimplementations of two published analyses with Borzoi and AlphaGenome, and 2.6$\times$ faster than dense execution with Enformer. Scoring each variant in its own centered 131 kb window makes ShiftCache only 1.36$\times$ faster than deduplicated dense execution, and highly diverse insertion lengths or many dispersed edits can make it slower than layer-by-layer reuse or dense execution. For encoders that meet our conditions, ShiftCache computes the same predictions as dense execution in exact arithmetic. On an A6000, every checked output of the default AlphaGenome and Borzoi runs matches dense execution within an absolute and relative tolerance of $10^{-5}$. With larger tile batches, with Enformer or on an H100, a small fraction of values exceeds this tolerance.

title: MixRoute: Rethinking Single-Distribution Training for Generalizable Neural Routing
abstract: Neural Combinatorial Optimization (NCO) is a promising paradigm for solving routing problems, yet its generalization across diverse data distributions remains a critical bottleneck. Existing methods typically tackle cross-distribution generalization through complex multi-distribution training or intricate meta-learning schemes, implicitly presuming that single-distribution training yields a weak zero-shot baseline. In this paper, we demonstrate that the potential of single-distribution training has been substantially underestimated and can be unlocked by a simple architectural inductive bias: Mix Normalization. To approach this, we first construct a comprehensive benchmark spanning three representative routing problems and 179 fine-grained datasets, capturing diverse shifts in node coordinates, customer demands, capacity and time windows. Building on this benchmark, we propose MixRoute, a neural framework that adaptively combines normalization statistics at different granularities to mitigate varying distribution shifts. Trained exclusively on uniform distributions, MixRoute generalizes effectively to a wide range of unseen distributions without any distribution-specific adaptation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MixRoute consistently achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot generalization. Our work revisits normalization as a parsimonious alternative for zero-shot generalization against complex training-adaptation schemes.

title: CSG-Nav: Confidence-Aware Semantic-Geometric Fusion for Robust Exploration and Accurate Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation
abstract: Zero-shot object-goal navigation requires autonomous agents to explore unseen environments and locate target objects without task-specific training, posing challenges in perceptual reliability under observation uncertainty and physically grounded goal termination. Although foundation-model-based approaches improve generalization, they remain vulnerable to unreliable long-range perception, hallucination-induced directional bias, and semantically plausible but geometrically incorrect stopping decisions. To address these limitations, we propose CSG-Nav, a zero-shot navigation framework centered on confidence-aware multimodal information fusion. CSG-Nav integrates three complementary fusion mechanisms. First, semantic-source fusion integrates open-vocabulary detection results, detection confidence, scene observations, and relational reasoning to produce more reliable direction-level semantic scores and suppress hallucination-induced directional bias. Second, spatial-confidence fusion weights multi-view semantic evidence using a Gaussian decay function, suppressing unreliable distant observations while accumulating spatially consistent exploration preferences. Third, semantic-geometric decision fusion combines semantic target detection with depth-based 3D localization to support physically grounded stopping decisions. Experiments on HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, and MP3D demonstrate competitive zero-shot performance, achieving success rates of 58.9%, 71.6%, and 44.3%. Fusion-level ablations and real-world deployments in indoor and outdoor environments further verify the effectiveness and practicality of CSG-Nav for robust navigation under uncertain perception. Code is available at https://xr-ui.github.io/CSGNav.github.io/

title: FireGate: Bounding Behaviour Change Before Training in Continual RL Fine-Tuning
abstract: Fine-tuning a deployed language model on one task after another can change behaviour that should stay fixed, such as earlier skills, general chat or refusals. Today, such forgetting is found only after training, on the benchmarks someone chose to run. This work bounds, before training, how often its outputs change on chosen prompt distributions. FireGate places each task's update, such as a new LoRA, behind a gate, which is a classifier on the model's frozen lower layers that decides for each prompt whether the update is used. Where no gate fires, the model computes exactly what the old one computes. As a result, on any prompt distribution, every bounded behaviour score changes by at most the gates' firing rate there over a whole task stream. Calibrating each gate on unlabeled prompts of what must not change fixes that rate before training, with a PAC guarantee, whatever weights training produces. Forgetting is thus bounded by the gate's false-alarm rate, and its price is the gate's power: no update, gated or not, that changes as few protected outputs can change new-task outputs more often than the best test of that level tells new-task prompts from protected ones. On reinforcement-learning streams of up to five tasks, gated training keeps the earlier tasks and changes 3.3% of held-out chat responses, whereas ungated training changes 91.8%. Across seven models, the gain kept behind the gate follows its firing rate on new-task prompts, measured before training. The certificate covers the gated model as deployed, on the prompt distributions sampled for calibration, not against an adversary who searches for prompts that fire the gate.

title: AnyBreak: Towards Jailbreaking Any T2I Model for Any Concept
abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in image generation and editing, yet this progress has also introduced significant security risks. Prior work has shown that adversarial prompt can induce the generation of Not-Safe-For-Work (NSFW) content, including pornographic, violent, and graphic imagery. However, such attacks are typically mitigated by prompt filters and often rely on white-box assumptions. In this paper, we propose AnyBreak, a novel jailbreak framework that constructs adversarial images via multi-scale progressive semantic alignment. During the generation process, these adversarial images steer the generation trajectory in latent space towards unsafe data manifolds, enabling cross-modal transfer of malicious concepts from the text modality to the image modality. AnyBreak operates using only clean textual prompts and adversarial images at inference time, and can jailbreak any T2I models towards any malicious concepts in a fully black-box setting. We further introduce AnyBreak-V, an enhanced variant that incorporates a compensation term to bypass post-hoc safety checkers. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AnyBreak achieves high attack success rates while preserving visual fidelity and semantic consistency with the input prompts under black-box and clean-text constraints. Our findings reveal that existing T2I defense leave critical cross-modal attack surfaces insufficiently addressed. The code is available at https://github.com/luqi-glory/AnyBreak.

title: Thermo-VLA: A Thermal-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Gated Residual Modulation for Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have begun incorporating thermal sensing, but existing approaches typically treat thermal images as ordinary visual inputs, providing limited support for temperature-aware relational reasoning in manipulation. To address this limitation, we propose Thermo-VLA with a ThermoRes Encoder, which decomposes thermal images into cold and hot attribute representations and injects them into the RGB token through language-conditioned residual modulation, enabling temperature-driven target selection and continuous manipulation. We further construct six real-world robotic tasks on a dual-arm Unitree G1 platform, spanning basic grounding to relational reasoning. Experiments show that Thermo-VLA achieves an average success rate of 0.86 across four thermal-dependent tasks, outperforming a pi_0.5 baseline that directly incorporates RGB-thermal observations by 18 percentage points. Under unseen-object and scene variations, Thermo-VLA maintains an average success rate of 0.78, achieving the best generalisation performance among the compared methods. Beyond thermal sensing, we transfer the same residual modulation mechanism to colour attributes and observe consistent improvements in both simulation and real-robot experiments, indicating its potential to generalise beyond thermal attributes. Project website: https://j-x-chen.github.io/Thermo-VLA-web/

title: An invariant higher index pairing under Morita equivalence for proper étale groupoids
abstract: For suitable proper étale groupoids, we study a part of the higher index that is invariant under Morita equivalence. We capture this part by a pairing between cyclic homology classes associated with isotropy groups and cyclic cohomology classes of the groupoid convolution algebra. We show that the pushforward is compatible with the maps induced by essential equivalences. This gives a numerical invariant depending only on the Morita equivalence class of the groupoid. In the case of a finite group action, we relate the resulting pairing to the equivariant index and to the Atiyah-Bott fixed-point formula.

title: Axion-Photon Conversion in Variable-Domain Magnetic Fields and the Highest-Energy Photons from GRB 221009A
abstract: We investigate photon-ALP conversion as a simultaneous explanation of the ultra-high-energy photons observed from GRB 221009A by LHAASO and of the $\sim300$ TeV photon reported by Carpet-3. We model the magnetic field of the host galaxy as a set of domains with randomly oriented field directions and variable domain lengths, and propagate the photon-ALP system through the host galaxy, the intergalactic medium and the Milky Way. Fitting the combined LHAASO and Carpet-3 spectra, we find that a broad distribution of domain lengths raises the photon survival probability at the highest energies and accommodates the Carpet-3 point with photon-ALP conversion alone. The best fit, $m_a=3.85\times10^{-7}$~eV and $g_{aγ}=3.07\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, lies below the CAST bound, and parts of the $1σ$ and $2σ$ regions are also compatible with it.

title: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I
abstract: We introduce Forelli-Rudin type operators on the open unit ball of $\ell^2$. The weighted $L^p$-$L^q$ boundedness of these operators are completely characterized for all $p,q\in[1,\infty]\times [1,\infty]$, and every Schatten class between the weighted $L^2$ spaces are also completely characterized. Meanwhile, we derive trace formulas for corresponding operators, which cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by formally replacing the dimension parameter with infinity. These results are not only infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). They also reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the geometric and measure theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. The key ingredient of our proofs is that we also establish the Forelli-Rudin type estimates in infinite dimensions, which may shew some night on the function theory in the infinite-dimensional unit ball.

title: Trajectory Density Ratios under Weak Support: A Survey across the Sciences
abstract: Many problems across the sciences compare two stochastic processes through the sequences they generate. Reinforcement learning asks what a new policy would return from the trajectories of an old one; molecular simulation asks how much more a ligand binds from samples of the unbound state; climate attribution asks how a heat wave shifted under warming; and language-model post-training asks what a deployed agent will do from logged interactions. In every case, one quantity would answer all these questions at once: the ratio of the two probability laws over their generated sequences, the trajectory density ratio. This ratio exists only under strong conditions. When one process reaches states the other cannot, the ratio does not exist; when their overlap is thin, its variance grows without control with the sequence length; and when they concentrate on different lower-dimensional sets, the ratio is undefined altogether. Weak support of this kind is the norm for sequence data, not a sampling accident, and its price is paid in identifiability rather than in noise alone. This survey organizes the field around a three-level diagnosis of weak support and a map of the nine retreats that methods take when the full ratio is out of reach, from direct estimation and reweighting through staged decomposition, stationarization, and partial-identification bounds to smoothing, transport couplings, operator spectra, and direct estimation of a single functional. Each retreat keeps part of what the ratio offers and pays for the rest, and each application domain has standardized the retreat its data force. The survey closes with open problems: testable diagnostics at every level, partial identification at the trajectory level, a rate theory of time-amplified error, and benchmarks with ground truth.

title: Tight Bounds for Sublinear Metric Steiner Tree
abstract: In the metric Steiner tree problem we are given an $n$-point metric space $(V,w)$ and a set $T\subseteq V$ of terminals, and we seek the smallest weight $\mathrm{OPT}$ of a tree that spans $T$ and may use points of $V\setminus T$. We study sublinear algorithms in the distance-oracle model, where the algorithm knows $V$ and $T$ upfront and can query the distance function $w$. The objective is to estimate $\mathrm{OPT}$ while querying significantly fewer than $n^2$ distances. The minimum spanning tree on $T$ estimates $\mathrm{OPT}$ within a factor $2$, and its weight can be approximated with $\widetilde{O}(n)$ queries. The natural question that has been studied is therefore the query complexity of estimating $\mathrm{OPT}$ within a factor strictly below $2$. Chen, Khanna, and Tan [SODA 2023] gave such an algorithm using $\widetilde{O}(n^{13/7})$ queries, and a lower bound of $\widetildeΩ(n^{6/5})$. Later Mahabadi, Roghani, Tarnawski, and Vakilian [ITCS 2025] improved the algorithm to $\widetilde{O}(n^{5/3})$, and Mahabadi, Tarnawski, and Vakilian [ITCS 2027] improved the lower bound to $\widetildeΩ(n^{7/5})$. In this work we settle the above question. We give an algorithm that estimates $\mathrm{OPT}$ within a factor $2-η_0$, for an absolute constant $η_0>0$, with query (and time) complexity $\widetilde{O}(n^{3/2})$. We also show that the exponent $3/2$ is tight.

title: When Audio and Video Mislead: Evaluating Multimodal AI for Conversational Emotion Recognition
abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation (MERC) combines lexical, acoustic, visual and conversational cues, but accepting audio and video does not establish their effective or robust use. We audit off-the-shelf Omni models while holding the target transcript and prior textual context fixed and adding, removing or replacing target audio and video. In the primary evaluation of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, Baichuan-Omni-1.5 and MiniCPM-o 2.6 on MELD and the full five-session six-class IEMOCAP set, T+A improves Accuracy in all six model-dataset pairs, with four gains significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Across three source mappings, unrelated A/V (RandA/V) lowers Accuracy relative to Full in all 18 comparisons; all 18 remain significant under dialogue-cluster inference and BH-FDR correction, both on common-valid pairs and when invalid/OOM outcomes are treated as incorrect. Comparisons with modality-omission baselines further distinguish replacement penalties from mismatch-specific harm. A Qwen/MELD case study finds significantly greater gold-vs-best-candidate margin recovery in Late than Early or Middle under decision-query audio knockout, relative to an edge-count-matched Video-Sham control, using Holm-corrected tests. These results distinguish genuine-modality benefit from sensitivity and vulnerability to misleading input.

title: Role of Wigner SU(4) Symmetry in Low-Energy Spin-Isospin Transitions of Three-Valence-Nucleon Systems on LS Closed Cores
abstract: We investigate low-energy Fermi (F) and Gamow--Teller (GT) transition strengths in three-valence-nucleon systems from the viewpoint of Wigner SU(4) symmetry. For $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$, shell-model calculations show that the ground states contain a large component of the SU(4) representation whose spin-isospin wave function is fully antisymmetric. By varying the spin--orbit splitting in the shell-model Hamiltonian, we demonstrate clear correlations of the SU(4) overlap with both the GT strength to the ground state and its fraction of the total GT strength. For $^{7}{\rm Li}$--$^{7}{\rm Be}$, shell-model calculations show that the $3/2^-_\mathrm{g.s.}$ and $1/2^-_1$ states both belong predominantly to the same supermultiplet as the $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground states. The observed strong GT transitions to these states are therefore interpreted as transitions within the same SU(4) multiplet, split by the spin-orbit interaction. Thus, Wigner SU(4) symmetry provides a unified interpretation of low-energy GT strength concentrations in three-valence-nucleon systems. In particular, the concentration of both F and GT strengths in the same $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground-state transition is naturally understood as a three-valence-nucleon extension of the SU(4) mechanism underlying the low-energy strong GT peak in $^{18}{\rm O}$--$^{18}{\rm F}$.

title: MUTE: Multi-Level Alignment Uncoupling Against Talking-Head Exploitation for Voice Protection
abstract: Talking-head generation models, which synthesize realistic facial animations from audio, are increasingly vulnerable to misuse in multimodal deepfake scenarios. Protecting such systems remains challenging, as talking-head models fundamentally rely on precise audio-visual alignment, while effective audio protection methods remain largely underexplored. In this work, we propose MUTE, an audio protection framework that uncouples the underlying audio-visual alignment through a multi-level strategy. Specifically, MUTE combines (1) Alignment-level Disruption, which directly perturbs cross-modal attention to disrupt structural alignment, and (2) Representation-level Degradation, which perturbs temporal audio embeddings to degrade their representations. To improve robustness, perturbations are constrained in the STFT domain to high-energy regions, making them resistant to post-processing, denoising, and adaptive attacks. An optional speaker-level objective further mitigates potential bypass via TTS-based resynthesis. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MUTE consistently degrades lip synchronization across both white-box and black-box talking-head models while preserving perceptual audio quality. The proposed method remains effective under real-world transformations and can be combined with image-based approaches to provide stronger multimodal protection. The source code and project page are available at https://github.com/jindl465/MUTE.

title: Rapid high-purity loading of barium ion via relayed selectivity from naturally abundant source
abstract: Trapped ions is one of the promising platforms for realizing quantum information processing and quantum simulation. Selective and rapid loading of a specific isotope lays the critical foundation for such purpose particularly when scaling up the system size. Here we demonstrate a new method for rapid isotope-selective loading of $^{137}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$ or $^{135}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$, two types of promising ion qubits, from naturally abundant source using a three-step, ultraviolet-free photoionization scheme. Neutral atoms are selected on the narrow 791 nm $6s^2\,{}^1S_0\rightarrow6s6p\,{}^3P_1^o$ transition, resonantly transferred at 554 nm to $6s6d\,{}^3D_1$, and ionized using an existing 532 nm Raman beam. A spectral-overlap analysis based on isotope and hyperfine shifts shows relayed selectivity that the second step can further suppress undesired-isotope excitation and no contaminant ion is detected during our entire experiment. Besides, the resonant drive of the second step excitation yields a prominent loading rate of the selected species. This strategy using multi-step excitations to establish relayed selectivity can be extended to high-purity loading of other species of ions.

title: MTRDMA: Lightweight User-Space Control-Plane Isolation for Multi-Tenant RDMA
abstract: In managed multi-tenant clouds, RDMA's lack of control-plane (CP) resource isolation lets a noisy tenant exhaust shared NIC microarchitectural caches, degrading victim throughput by up to 96.4\%. Data-path schedulers leave CP resources unprotected, and hardware approaches require FPGAs or SmartNICs rather than the commodity RNICs operators already deploy. We present MTRDMA, a lightweight user-space CP isolation mechanism for commodity RNICs, applicable to managed runtimes such as containers and sandboxed processes. MTRDMA intercepts library-level CP operations to enforce hierarchical quotas while preserving the zero-copy data path, using atomic shared-memory quota state with per-process cached admission (${\sim}$0.13\,$μ$s), a hybrid garbage collector that reclaims orphaned quota within seconds, and rdma-cgroup caps with ledger--kernel reconciliation to bound and detect residual tampering. On ConnectX-6 RNICs, MTRDMA cuts victim degradation under Queue Pair (QP) cache exhaustion from 94.5\% to 0.08\%, extends protection to Memory Region (MR) cache exhaustion, and scales to 256 concurrent tenants with negligible data-plane overhead.

title: Optimal last-iterate rates for the projected decentralized stochastic subgradient method
abstract: We study the projected decentralized stochastic subgradient (PDSG) method for minimizing the average of convex, possibly nonsmooth local objectives over a common closed convex constraint set and a fixed connected undirected network. We focus on the finite-time expected suboptimality of the last local iterate generated at each node, which is the actual output locally available without time averaging or network averaging. Under the standard stepsizes $α_t=α/\sqrt{t}$ and $α_t=2/(μt)$, we establish $\mathcal{O}(\log T/\sqrt{T})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\log T/T)$ last-local-iterate rates for PDSG when each local objective is convex and the aggregate objective is strongly convex, respectively. To eliminate the logarithmic loss, we introduce a general horizon-dependent stepsize framework, termed cooldown stepsize, that combines a base stepsize with segmentwise scaling over a multistage partition and includes the dyadic construction (Jain et al, SIAM J. Optim., 2021) as a special case. For adapting to decentralized settings, we propose a long-range variation condition to make the stepsize schedule compatible with network contraction. Under this cooldown stepsize, we obtain $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ and $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ last-local-iterate rates for PDSG in both problem classes, matching the optimal centralized dependence on $T$. Experiments on a lower-bound instance and constrained hinge-loss problems illustrate the predicted terminal behavior of local iterates and the control of consensus error under the cooldown stepsize.

title: Pairwise correlation bounds for the random-cluster model with cluster weight at most one
abstract: We establish quantitative bounds on pairwise edge correlations for the random-cluster model with cluster weight $q\in[0,1]$ on arbitrary finite connected graphs. We give two explicit bounds that retain the dependence on the activities of the two specified edges and hold uniformly over the activities of all remaining edges. We also obtain a refinement of one of these bounds using connectivity information from the graph with the two specified edges removed. These results sharpen the bound obtained by a direct application of Lorentzian polynomial theory. At $q=0$, the model is supported on connected spanning subgraphs. In particular, for the uniform probability measure on these subgraphs, the joint inclusion probability of two distinct edges is at most $10/9$ times the product of their marginal inclusion probabilities.

title: EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving
abstract: Small multimodal models can misjudge emotion when words, voice, and visual cues conflict. We present EmoHarness, which runs such a model, the frozen student, inside a harness: the prompts, settings, and verification code around its calls. A human-written starting harness, the scaffold, numbers the student's visual observations, transcript, and prosody descriptions as citable evidence and has the student weigh candidate emotions against it. In Meta-Harness Evolving (MHE), a stronger LLM, the Builder, reads the student's errors and execution traces offline and edits the harness; static checks and validation gates decide which edits are kept, and the Builder never sees evaluation items. On 5,507 MME-Emotion items, EmoHarness raises task-macro Recognition by 7.6-13.4 points over a single video-only call for all four students and both Builders. Transcripts and prosody descriptions supply most of this boost (+5.38 to +10.71); the scaffold changes the audio-augmented call by -0.79 to +2.54, partly through extra multi-label predictions, and evolved edits add at most +0.95, although no evolved increment survives Holm correction. The harness's emotion context also transfers to IntentQA, with small gains for three of four students, none of which survives correction. EmoHarness thus boosts small multimodal students chiefly by supplying and organizing audio-derived evidence.

title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
abstract: In this work, we study whether frontier agent can continually improve real-world AI infrastructure over long horizons. We introduce Infrathon, a benchmark of diverse, long-horizon AI infrastructure optimization tasks across different levels. We evaluate six models across 150 runs with 24-hour budgets, totaling over 10,000 GPU-hours. Our results show that model rankings vary with the evaluation horizon, while 135 of the 150 runs achieve further improvements during the second half of their budgets. These findings indicate that shorter evaluations can overlook both optimization gains and changes in relative model performance. We also find agents can discover solutions that outperform human-designed baselines: Claude Opus 5.5 increases the mean KV-cache compression ratio from 6.82% with the human-designed Quant-VideoGen codec to 19.86%. Analysis of agent trajectories identifies task violations, unreliable testing, and premature completion as barriers to sustained improvement. Together, Our Infrathon framework provide resources for constructing long-horizon tasks, evaluating frontier agents, and discovering good infrastructure solutions.

title: OASIS: Optimization-Aware Subgoal Inference with Safety Constraints for Autonomous Mobile Robot Navigation
abstract: Navigation in dynamic environments requires mobile robots to make progress toward their goals while respecting motion limits and avoiding surrounding obstacles. Learned subgoal policies can guide model predictive control beyond its local prediction horizon, but a geometrically suitable subgoal does not necessarily lead to a successfully solved control problem. This paper proposes OASIS, a hierarchical navigation framework that incorporates recent optimization outcomes into reinforcement learning-based subgoal generation. A high-level policy trained using Soft Actor--Critic generates local subgoals, while a nonlinear model predictive controller tracks them subject to motion limits, geometric collision-avoidance constraints, and embedded high-order control barrier function constraints. The outcomes of controller optimizations over each subgoal interval are summarized and provided to the policy at its next decision, without requiring additional optimization calls. The framework is evaluated in five navigation scenarios with static and moving obstacles, including dense interactions and sensing uncertainty. Comparisons with hierarchical and direct-goal control variants show that OASIS achieves the highest aggregate navigation success. Matched comparisons across three training seeds further show a consistent success advantage over the otherwise identical hierarchy without optimization-status input. The selected-policy comparison also shows fewer primary optimization failures with similar mean controller time.

title: HyInv Technical Report
abstract: Inverse folding designs amino-acid sequences for a given protein backbone, and screening needs many candidates that are both diverse and well folded. We present HyInv, a 1.96-million-parameter backbone-conditioned graph network with an encoder-decoder architecture, trained by Hyra 2.0, the research agent developed by our team: pretrained with random-order autoregressive sequence modeling, followed by structure-reward reinforcement learning. At inference, a grouped draft-and-rewrite sampler that uses separate draft and rewrite temperatures improves refolding TM-score at matched diversity. An optimized implementation with BF16 numerics designs 128 sequences for a 402-residue backbone in 50.6 ms on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU, about 52 times faster than the reference sampler, and an exact FP32 path that returns the reference sequences is 8.7 times faster. Across five benchmark datasets and seven dataset-predictor combinations, HyInv reaches a higher average scTM than all ten external baselines at comparable or higher sequence diversity, with large margins over ProteinMPNN and ProteinZero V2. The same default setting supports de novo backbones, pocket-constrained libraries, enzyme redesign with the catalytic site kept, and loop redesign. We have released our code and model at https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hyra-results/tree/main/AI4Science/hyinv.

title: Reward-Estimated Hypergradient for Bilevel Reinforcement Learning with Black-Box Follower
abstract: Hypergradient (HG) methods for bilevel reinforcement learning (RL) typically assume a white-box follower whose reward is known. In practice, however, the leader rarely knows the follower's reward function and can only observe its trajectories. We address this black-box setting and propose Reward-Estimated Hypergradients (RE-HG), which recovers the follower's reward from these trajectories via inverse RL (IRL). Yet IRL identifies the reward only up to potential-based shaping, a transformation that leaves the follower's behavior unchanged but biases the HG. We prove that, for linear rewards, this bias cancels when IRL estimates are aggregated across sufficiently diverse dynamics, which the leader's own updates naturally supply. To handle finite samples, RE-HG truncates small eigenvalues of the aggregated feature covariance, restoring the identifiable subspace and stabilizing the estimation. Experiments show that RE-HG estimates gradients aligned with a white-box Oracle and achieves comparable performance; empirically, the truncation also suppresses HG explosions, letting RE-HG avoid local optima that trap the Oracle in sharp reward landscapes.

title: A Mathematical Multiscale Framework for Nonlinear Modeling of the Heliosphere
abstract: The inner heliosphere is a highly nonlinear continuous medium where macroscopic ideal magnetohydrodynamics is inextricably coupled with microscopic, fully developed stochastic turbulence. State-of-the-art global 3D numerical solvers, while proficient at capturing the large-scale propagation of extreme space physics phenomena such as coronal mass ejections and corotating interaction regions, are computationally constrained by grid resolution and fundamental partial differential equation formulations. Consequently, they inherently do not resolve the local small-scale turbulent cascade, magnetic intermittency, and localized thermodynamic anomalies. To bridge this fundamental scaleseparation gap, this paper presents a novel mathematical and numerical framework that harmoniously integrates global heliospheric structures with local turbulent physics. The framework generates a highly realistic synthetic continuous medium by superimposing a stochastically driven nonlinear turbulent cascade onto a bimodal deterministic background flow. This cascade reproduces theoretical constraints for fractional power spectral densities, magnetic compressibility, and small-scale intermittency via a discrete multiplicative binomial cascade (p-model). This multiscale continuous background is dynamically perturbed by analytical models of large-scale nonlinear transients, including kinematic shock steepening, continuous current sheet topological reversals, and solar ejecta formalized as asymmetric force-free magnetic flux ropes. By generating exact spatio-temporal arrays across arbitrary distributed coordinates, this unified mathematical model overcomes the spatial degeneracy of single-point observations and provides a computationally efficient analytical baseline for performance models supporting future in-situ multi-spacecraft heliospheric missions, which are currently in their feasibility study phase.

title: HyPLM Technical Report
abstract: Protein language models (PLMs) are standard tools for variant-effect prediction, protein annotation and design, but the compute needed to train and serve them keeps growing. We present HyPLM-Flash, an efficient and open PLM trained by Hyra 2.0, the research agent developed by our team. HyPLM-Flash is a 650-million-parameter masked language model trained on 726 billion tokens, 0.73 times the data of ESM-2 650M and a fifth to an eighth of the data of E1-600M and ESM C 600M. It runs on an inference engine with fused kernels and INT8 matrix multiplication, embedding about 130,000 residues per second on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU, 1.9 to 2.7 times faster than other 600M-class encoders. In a matched evaluation against 28 public checkpoints on 32 tasks, HyPLM-Flash reaches a ProteinGym zero-shot Spearman correlation of 0.409, statistically tied with ESM-2 650M, ESM C 600M and E1-600M, and the highest organismal-fitness score among self-supervised single-sequence models. It gives the best long-range contact precision of all models evaluated, including ESM-2 15B and ESM C 6B, and a lower masked-residue loss than ESM-2 650M, ESM C 600M and E1-600M on held-out sequences and on recently released PDB chains. Matching state-of-the-art accuracy at a fraction of the training and inference cost, HyPLM-Flash sets a new Pareto frontier for protein language models. We have released the model weights and the inference engine at https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/hyra-results/tree/main.

title: Online Digital Twins: Data Assimilation and Control
abstract: The online assimilation of data and the application of controls are essential ingredients of the digital twin paradigm. In this paper, we formalize the online interaction between the physical process and its virtual digital representation in the setting of continuously arriving data from the physical process and a receding horizon virtual planning process, which provides the control for the physical process. Our mathematical formulation relies on a mean field representation of the data assimilation process as well as a mean field Pontryagin minimum principle for the optimal control problem. Such mean field formulations are computationally attractive because they allow for simultaneous implementation in terms of Hamiltonian interacting particle systems. A more detailed discussion is included for the ensemble Kalman-Bucy filter in combination with affine approximations of the receding horizon control laws. This paper sets out the mathematical framework, while a computational study is left for future research.

title: SATE: Transferable Spin-Adapted Neural Wavefunctions
abstract: Accurate prediction of molecular reactivity requires both accurate and computationally efficient description of electron correlation and spin across various molecular geometries and electronic states. We introduce SATE, a spin-adapted transferable neural wavefunction architecture with effective core potentials. SATE combines a transferable neural wavefunction, the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, and effective core potentials into a single foundation model architecture pretrained on compositions containing selected elements from hydrogen to bromine. After pretraining and adaptation, our model is able to predict 3d transition-metal spin-state gaps, bond dissociation energies, and reaction energies by addressing two key issues. First, including the core potentials into the model allows us to reduce the number of explicitly treated electrons. Second, using spin-adapted antisymmetrization enforces the prescribed total spin by construction. By testing our model with 3d transition metal chemistry, we evaluate our model's description of strong electron correlation and competing electronic states in such compounds. We find that pretraining improves most tested component energies at matched adaptation budgets, while improvements in spin-state gaps, dissociation energies, and reaction energies remain system dependent. Ultimately, our work lays the foundation for more accurate and transferable modeling of molecular systems by combining the computational efficiency of effective core potentials with explicit control over total spin.

title: Anomalous regularity and scaling limit by rough transport noise for stochastic 2D fluid models on the torus
abstract: We consider the stochastic 2D Euler and mSQG equations on the torus, with $L^2$ initial data and driven by rough Kraichnan transport noise, for which we construct weak solutions enjoying anomalous regularity and dissipation properties. Moreover, we show that weak solutions in this regularity class are pathwise unique, thus establishing probabilistically strong well-posedness. We further obtain the scaling limit from these equations to the deterministic Navier--Stokes/mSQG equations, with respect to positive Sobolev norms. The proofs rest on the analysis of energy spectrum of the vorticity and on a uniform weighted discrete Poincaré inequality on the lattice, the latter being crucial for making the positive norms accessible.

title: Conformal Prediction for Multi-Step Forecasting: Conditional Coverage and Sharp Score Calibration Rates
abstract: Uncertainty quantification in prediction is a central problem in statistics and machine learning. Conformal prediction provides a flexible approach to constructing prediction sets with valid marginal coverage under exchangeability. In this paper, we investigate conformal prediction for both one-step and multi-step forecasting from a single stationary time series, addressing temporal dependence and the additional challenges of joint prediction across multiple horizons. We propose a kernel-based framework, called Time series Residual Analysis for Calibration with Kernels (TRACK), for estimating conditional quantiles of residual scores and constructing prediction sets from rolling-window forecasters. The framework accommodates heterogeneous uncertainty across horizons and accounts for dependence induced by rolling estimation, while allowing predictor memory and forecast horizons to grow with the sample size. Our finite-sample bounds quantify how temporal dependence and overlapping score windows affect calibration and coverage. We further derive bounds for conditional quantile estimation and pointwise conditional coverage discrepancy. The guarantees extend to more general predictors that admit an accurate rolling-window approximation. We also derive matching minimax bounds over classes of known score maps, clarifying how overlapping score windows affect calibration accuracy. Experimental results from simulations and applications to wind energy generation and bike sharing demand show that our methods improve regional conditional coverage while maintaining competitive interval widths.

title: Short-term associations between wild-bird and mammalian high pathogenic avian influenza detection in the United States
abstract: High pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) detections in mammals have raised concern about repeated wildlife spillover and the targeting of mammalian surveillance. We evaluated whether wild-bird detection records contained short-term explanatory and predictive information about mammalian detections in the United States. Public surveillance records from April 2022 to July 2026 comprised 18,523 wild-bird and 815 mammalian detections. Monthly state-level mammalian counts were analysed using negative-binomial mixed models adjusted for seasonality, preceding mammalian detections and state-level heterogeneity. The selected model contained contemporaneous and one-month-lagged same-state wild-bird counts. A doubling of one plus the contemporaneous wild-bird count was associated with a 57.9% increase in the expected mammalian count (95% CI 43.5-73.8%), and a doubling of the preceding-month count with a 15.9% increase (5.2-27.8%). Bordering-state exposure did not improve fit. In a six-month temporal holdout, adding same-state wild-bird exposure reduced mean absolute error by 23.8% and root mean squared error by 27.9%, although total detections remained overpredicted. After exact-row deduplication, the corresponding effects were 59.7% and 13.3%. Wild-bird surveillance records contained short-term, geographically local information about mammalian HPAI detection activity, but the associations do not establish direct transmission and require further calibration before operational forecasting.

title: Constraining Evidence Strength in Bayesian Tonal-State Inference: A Posterior-Continuity Diagnostic
abstract: Effective pitch-evidence strength governs the concentration of tonal-state posteriors. Expert local-key annotations cannot calibrate this strength because they do not specify the posterior distribution over the 24 candidate keys.
