abstract: Cloud~\ac{VR} imposes stringent latency and reliability requirements due to the closed-loop interaction between \ac{DL} video streaming and \ac{UL} tracking updates. Although Wi-Fi~7 introduces \ac{MLO} to improve throughput and reduce latency, its adoption for latency-critical applications like Cloud~\ac{VR} is not straightforward. This paper investigates Cloud~\ac{VR} streaming over Wi-Fi~7 through a comprehensive cross-layer evaluation and proposes an application-aware \ac{TXS} scheduling policy that exploits the \ac{UL}/\ac{DL} coupling to jointly serve tracking and video traffic. To evaluate our mechanism, we introduce NeXus-VR, an open-source simulator that extends OMNeT++ to integrate the complete Cloud~\ac{VR} application pipeline and the Wi-Fi~7 MAC/PHY layers. Simulation results with multiple \ac{VR} users, \ac{OBSS} contention, and user mobility show that \ac{MLO} and the proposed \ac{TXS} scheduling policy provide complementary benefits. While \ac{MLO} improves transmission opportunities and robustness, the proposed Cloud \ac{VR}-aware \ac{TXS} scheduler preserves tracking freshness by reducing contention between \ac{UL} and \ac{DL} traffic. Together, they increase Cloud~\ac{VR} capacity by up to 2.25$\times$ over conventional single-link operation while consistently reducing latency and improving application-level quality of experience.

title: ECOS: Environment-Calibrated On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Agents
abstract: On-policy self-distillation lets a language agent act as its own Teacher by conditioning on privileged context such as skills written from its own trajectories. Its guidance, however, is weighted by how much this context shifts token likelihoods rather than by whether it improves behavior, so errors in self-written skills return through later updates. We propose environment-calibrated on-policy self-distillation, which uses environmental outcomes to decide how much to trust the Teacher's current guidance and which self-written skills to reinforce. Command-level advantages, estimated by comparing commands executed at similar observations, scale each Teacher preference and reward reflections and skills whose induced preferences favor higher-advantage commands. Without skills at inference, 3B and 7B agents reach 90.5% and 93.3% macro success on seen ALFWorld tasks and 75.5% and 80.5% success on WebShop. On unseen ALFWorld tasks, they outperform GRPO under the same protocol by 11.0 and 7.6 percentage points, respectively. In an ablation study, supervising only executable commands rather than the Actor's full response raises 3B WebShop success from 52.3% to 75.0%.

title: X-ray parametric down-conversion probes radiation-induced dynamics in hybrid perovskite MAPbBr3
abstract: We report minute-timescale time-resolved measurements of X-ray parametric down-conversion (PDC) of X-rays into ultraviolet photons in a MAPbBr3 single crystal under continuous irradiation. Despite the known radiation sensitivity of hybrid perovskites and the high photon flux required to detect the intrinsically weak PDC signal, the nonlinear response remains measurable throughout the irradiation sequence. Both PDC and Bragg diffraction exhibit a slow decay consistent with diffusion-driven damage dynamics on timescales reported for bromide-vacancy and proton migration. However, despite their similar decay rates, the PDC and Bragg signals evolve toward markedly different steady states, while an additional fast decay component is observed in the Bragg response but absent in the PDC signal. Density functional theory calculations identify N 2s states of the methylammonium cation as the most likely contributors to the measured PDC response and show that their Fourier component is only weakly affected by bromide-vacancy formation. These results establish nonlinear X-ray diffraction as a channel-selective probe of radiation-induced dynamics and demonstrate that radiation damage can couple differently to nonlinear and linear X-ray responses.

title: Constraints on the Real Singlet Scalar Dark Matter Model from Higgs Self-Couplings
abstract: Taking the real singlet scalar dark matter model as a representative test case, we examine the constraints imposed on the model's parameter space by Higgs trilinear coupling measurements and perturbative unitarity requirements. For the low dark matter mass regime, the constraining strength delivered by the current highest-precision $κ_3$ measurement is notably inferior to the exclusion limit derived from perturbative unitarity requirements, while the perturbative unitarity bound itself remains considerably less restrictive than the constraints extracted from the extant experimental upper limit on the Higgs invisible decay branching ratio $\mathrm{BR}_{\mathrm{inv}} \leq 0.107$. Both the coupling modifiers $κ_3$ and $κ_4$ exhibit a well-defined decoupling behavior, with their respective magnitudes monotonically decreasing as the dark matter mass $m_S$ increases. As a direct consequence, the corrections to both couplings asymptotically approach zero for dark matter masses in excess of 60 TeV, when the parameter $a_2$ remains within its perturbative validity domain. Neither existing collider measurements of the Higgs trilinear coupling nor measurements targeted for planned future collider facilities possess the requisite sensitivity to impose more stringent constraints on the model's viable parameter space than the well-established bounds derived from experimental probes of dark matter relic density, invisible Higgs decay signatures, dark matter direct detection, and dark matter indirect detection. Nevertheless, under the scenario that the experimental measurement uncertainty of $κ_3$ reaches the $\mathcal{O}(0.1\%)$ scale or lower, non-negligible constraints acting on a subset of the large mass parameter space associated with the WIMP dark matter scenario can be expected.

title: Bayesian Kinetic Model Selection in Dynamic PET via Consistency Models
abstract: Accurate voxel-wise parametric imaging in dynamic positron emission tomography (PET), particu- larly with total-body PET (TB-PET) scanners, requires se- lecting the appropriate kinetic model for diverse organs and lesions. Conventional nonlinear least squares fitting paired with the Akaike or Bayesian Information Criterion (NLS+AIC/BIC) is computationally slow, sensitive to lo- cal minima, and prone to selecting simple models under high voxel-level noise, whereas classical Bayesian methods such as Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) and Approx- imate Bayesian Computation (PET-ABC) are too slow for whole-body imaging. In this work, we propose a consis- tency model (CM) that performs simultaneous Bayesian kinetic model selection and parameter posterior estimation. By combining the continuous kinetic parameters and dis- crete model index into one target vector conditioned on the measured time-activity curve (TAC) and input function, the CM samples from the joint posterior distribution p(θ, m|y) in seconds per slice with a GPU workstation of 4 NVIDIA A100. We validated the framework on two simulated and clinical applications: whole-body [18F]FDG TB-PET across seven compartment models, and brain [11C]raclopride PET for detecting smoking-induced dopamine release between two neurotransmitter models. In simulations, the CM achieved 97.97% model selection accuracy in the [18F]FDG applica- tion (vs. 58.67% for NLS+AIC) and 91.4% accuracy in the [11C]raclopride application (vs. 73.5% for NLS+BIC), while closely matching reference MCMC parameter posteriors. In clinical applications, CM generated whole-body FDG model selection maps, in which each regions was assigned litera- ture established sensible kinetic models; CM also success- fully mapped voxels in the brain where dopamine release was induced by smoking.

title: Commuting-check gauging for fault-tolerant logical measurements
abstract: Gauging turns a logical operator into a product of local checks, providing a route to logical measurement and lattice surgery. These checks can fail to commute outside the code space, so measuring one can randomize the outcome of another. In this work, we introduce completion qubits that make the checks commute for Clifford $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetries of qubit stabilizer codes. Adding one completion qubit per noncommuting pair preserves the gauged code space and its distance while keeping the checks Clifford. Completion also preserves the low-density parity-check property with a constant-factor qubit overhead. We generalize completion to qudits and establish bounds on the Clifford-hierarchy level of the completed checks in prime dimensions. Global commutation ensures that a fault-free round fixes the syndrome until the next fault and allows us to bound fault propagation independently of the number of measurement rounds. For qubit codes, we show that gauging and ungauging a distance-$d$ parent code implements a logical measurement with circuit fault distance $Ω(d)$ in $O(d)$ rounds. We demonstrate the construction by gauging two toric codes into the $D(D_4)$ quantum double and back, with an explicit circuit whose circuit fault distance equals the parent code distance. Our results provide a framework for fault-tolerant logical measurements using commuting checks, with applications to magic-state preparation by lattice surgery.

title: A 1.764-competitive algorithm for online fractional vertex cover on forests
abstract: We study online fractional vertex cover on forests under edge arrival. We give a deterministic algorithm with competitive ratio at most $4 - \sqrt{5} \approx 1.764$, which simultaneously produces an online fractional matching with competitive ratio of at least $1/(4 - \sqrt{5}) \approx 0.566$. This improves on the previous best competitive ratios of $11/6 \approx 1.833$ and $5/9 \approx 0.555$, respectively.

title: Off-focus detection for SNR enhancement in coherent single-pixel imaging
abstract: Coherent single-pixel imaging (CSPI) enables amplitude- and phase-resolved computational imaging with a single coherent detector, offering particular advantages in spectral regimes where high-performance detector arrays remain unavailable. In conventional Fourier-plane CSPI, the detector is typically placed at the focal point to maximize the collected power. However, this focal position does not necessarily maximize the reconstruction fidelity for image reconstruction in the presence of system nonidealities. Here, we introduce detector position as an additional degree of freedom for CSPI optimization. We show that appropriately selected off-focus Fourier-plane positions can improve reconstruction performance by suppressing fluctuation-sensitive coherent backgrounds while preserving spatially encoded signals. Experimentally, using a programmable liquid-crystal terahertz spatial light modulator and coherent heterodyne detection, we demonstrate improved amplitude and phase reconstruction from selected off-focus channels compared with focal detection. A symmetric off-focus pair with complementary transverse-wave-vector weighting further enhances image fidelity, contrast, and compressive-sampling robustness through coherent channel fusion. These results establish detector-position engineering as a new strategy for enhancing the robustness and information efficiency of CSPI.

title: Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
abstract: A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set. For lattice tilings with a triangular basis we obtain a dimension-reduction formula, and we describe every cocyclic lattice by a single normalized congruence. Along a cyclic generator, the counter of a signed bidiagonal lattice is a row of Stern's diatomic sequence; pairs of counter values realize the Calkin--Wilf tree, and complementary binary words realize the Kepler tree. For the binary lattice, the translated counter labelings of the cube carry generating face partitions, supplied by the tiling itself, which force the levels of the Kepler tree, and every nontrivial face partition has a unique lamination direction. Using finite Fourier analysis we prove that the ordered cyclic profile determines a standard cocyclic cube tiling lattice up to coordinate reflections. For lattices tiling by discrete boxes we determine exactly when the analogous statement holds.

title: Prune, Don't Merge: Expert Compression of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs on Multilingual Production Tasks
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts language models are cheap to run per token but expensive to hold in GPU memory, which drives the cost of serving them in production. One-shot expert compression shrinks them after a single calibration pass. Its two current state-of-the-art methods are REAP for expert pruning, which deletes the least salient experts, and REAM for expert merging, which merges them into the most salient ones. Both have been evaluated only on academic benchmarks. We compare the two on five multilingual production tasks of a web-hosting company, from classification to the generation of marketing HTML email templates, with two 30B-parameter models (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 and the hybrid Mamba-attention Nemotron-3.5-Lightning) at 25% and 50% of experts removed and the same calibration data. Pruning wins: on the same rows, REAP is significantly better in 16 of 20 comparisons and REAM in 2. At 25%, REAP keeps 93.6% of Qwen3-30B's generative quality and REAM 62.5%, although on benchmarks the two are within a point for the same model. The damage concentrates in the output contract rather than the content: 89.8-95.2% of each significant loss on email templates comes from hard-gate failures such as invalid JSON, broken mobile layouts and runaway generation, and most failed non-English domain descriptions copy the prompt's English opening phrase. Cross-perplexity and logit divergence, two diagnostics from the REAP paper, also track production quality, as does the rate of repetition loops; n-gram diversity does not. We close with practical guidance for compressing MoE models for production.

title: SNAPRAG: Cost-Efficient Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems via Adversarial Perturbations
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems improve Large Language Model (LLM) responses by incorporating information from external knowledge bases. However, recent studies have shown that attackers can extract substantial portions of private knowledge bases from RAG systems through repeated querying. Yet, state-of-the-art extraction attacks either rely heavily on external LLMs to generate adversarial queries or require a large number of queries. In this paper, we propose SNAPRAG, a novel and cost-efficient attack for extracting RAG knowledge bases through adversarial perturbations. Our approach algorithmically generates adversarial queries without relying on external LLMs and allows for a strictly configurable query budget. In particular, SNAPRAG uses a discrete token-mutation algorithm to generate novel queries in a strict black-box setting. Our adaptive dissimilarity threshold calibration systematically forces queries into unexplored semantic regions of the target database, enabling extraction with fewer queries. Specifically, to extract half of the target knowledge base, our method requires up to 6.77$\times$ fewer queries than existing approaches. Furthermore, within a fixed query budget, our method recovers up to 96.9%, outperforming the closest approach by 7.7-19.9%. We further evaluate SNAPRAG against active defenses, where it remains the leading attack on four of five defended targets, achieving 50.7-96.3% extraction rate.

title: Controlling Temporal Pseudo-Label Marginals for Stable Online Test-Time Adaptation
abstract: Continual Test-Time Adaptation (CTTA) methods update models online using a stream of unlabeled data to overcome distribution shifts encountered at test time. However, CTTA is often unstable, as it can reinforce biases in early predictions and increasingly predict only a few classes, resulting in drift or even collapse. In this paper, we identify narrowing pseudo-label class usage as an indicator of CTTA instability and quantify this behavior. Most existing methods have attempted to address this issue by either selecting reliable adaptation samples or re-weighting the loss to encourage diverse pseudo-labels, but they do not explicitly enforce a class marginal over a temporal window. Instead, we propose Sinkhorn Class-Marginal Regularization (SCALAR), a simple plug-and-play module that controls the pseudo-label distribution over a short temporal window. SCALAR works by maintaining recent predictions in a buffer, balancing their class distribution via the Sinkhorn algorithm to match a specified target distribution, and using the balanced soft targets for adaptation. Without changing the model architecture, SCALAR maintains the per-step runtime and increases the peak allocated GPU memory by only 10 MB on ImageNet-C. Our method is particularly effective on skewed, non-stationary data with severe distribution shifts, where SCALAR significantly alleviates drift and collapse when combined with existing stabilization methods based on entropy or diversity.

title: CADMA: Capacity-Aware Coverage Decomposition for Generative Model Assessment
abstract: Evaluating generative models requires measuring not only sample fidelity but also how well a generated set covers the real data distribution. Recent work has therefore introduced recall-oriented metrics for distribution-level evaluation. However, existing recall metrics often reduce distributional coverage to geometry-based coverage. This simplifying assumption weakens their diagnostic value and interpretability in two ways: these metrics provide only a single aggregate score that cannot distinguish essential diversity failures such as mode dropping and mode collapse, and geometry-based coverage can provide unreliable estimates by assigning high scores to poorly covered generative distributions. We therefore introduce CADMA, a capacity-aware framework for recall-oriented evaluation and diagnosis. CADMA evaluates distributional coverage through local capacity matching between real and generated samples, separating geometry-based coverage from effective coverage. This yields multi-dimensional coverage diagnostics that quantify mode dropping and mode collapse while reducing the overly optimistic estimates produced by geometry-based metrics. Through extensive experiments on toy data, real-world datasets, and generative models, we show that CADMA provides more reliable coverage estimates and more fine-grained, interpretable diagnostic signals of diversity failures than existing metrics. Our code is available at https://github.com/Open-Debin/CADMA_NeurIPS2026.

title: Prospective Action-Resource Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Electric HGV Fleets under Shared Charging Infrastructure
abstract: Electric heavy goods vehicle (eHGV) fleet coordination requires each vehicle to choose driving, charging and resting actions whose consequences depend on shared infrastructure. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods mainly represent current states, leaving action-specific futures and resource interactions to be learned indirectly. We develop Horizon-Preview and Graph-Coordinated Proximal Policy Optimisation (HGC-PPO), which integrates horizon preview and candidate-resource graph coordination into the PPO decision architecture. Horizon preview represents each legal action through its short-horizon operational consequences. Graph message passing then updates these candidates through station, charger-type and time-slot resources shared across the fleet. On the 794km Folkestone-Glasgow task, HGC-PPO achieved the lowest mean charging cost among five RL methods at £504.32 per vehicle, with a fleet completion time of 24.920h. It also completed the task 1.763h faster and cost £36.51 less per vehicle than a replay-verified finite-budget MILP benchmark. Across six unseen routes and fleet sizes from 5 to 20 vehicles, HGC-PPO delivered the lowest macro-average completion time, charging cost and charging frequency among the RL methods. A 2 by 2 ablation showed that the full preview-graph architecture performed best across all four operational metrics. These results show that prospective action information and fleet-wide resource coordination improve eHGV decisions under charging and driver-hours constraints.

title: Odd realisation numbers of rigid graphs
abstract: Determining the number of realisations of a rigid graph for a specific choice of edge lengths is a fundamental problem in discrete geometry. Gortler, Healy and Thurston showed that the number of real realisations of a generic framework is always even or equal to one. Despite being rare, there do exist graphs whose number of complex realisations is odd and not equal to one. In this article, we exhibit two necessary conditions for a rigid graph to have an odd realisation number other than one. We also provide an infinite family of rigid graphs with an odd realisation number other than one.

title: Nemotron 3 Diarization: Advancing the Accuracy-Efficiency Frontier in Streaming Speaker Diarization
abstract: Streaming Sortformer introduced an arrival-order speaker cache to maintain speaker identities across chunks in end-to-end streaming speaker diarization, with a single model supporting configurable latency profiles spanning offline operation to ultra-low-latency streaming. Nemotron 3 Diarization addresses the original model's four-speaker limitation by extending support to eight speakers while improving both accuracy and computational efficiency. The previous FastConformer-Transformer stack is streamlined into a pure Transformer encoder. A learned upsampling layer then maps the encoder's coarse 80-ms representations to 10-ms resolution, enabling fine-grained predictions. Training leverages large-scale simulated mixtures and adds activity and phantom-speaker losses to the standard Sortformer objectives. Despite doubling speaker capacity over its predecessor, the new architecture reduces training memory by a factor of 2.8, makes training $2.2\times$ faster, and delivers up to $6.4\times$ higher inference throughput. Nemotron 3 Diarization establishes a new state of the art in DER on DIHARD III and CALLHOME. When used to condition DiCoW, it also achieves state-of-the-art tcpWER on the single-microphone conditions of AMI and NOTSOFAR-1. Training code is open source, and model weights are released under the permissive OpenMDW-1.1 license.

title: Fundamental Outage and Diversity Limits of Fluid Antenna Multiple Access Under Correlated Nakagami-$m$ Fading
abstract: Existing analytical studies of fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) are largely confined to Rayleigh fading, independent-port assumptions, or asymptotic selection metrics, leaving the fundamental outage behavior under realistic fading and spatial correlation conditions uncharacterized. This paper fills this gap by presenting the first exact and asymptotically tight outage analysis of interference-limited FAMA systems under spatially correlated Nakagami-$m$ fading. By explicitly modeling the joint statistics of the desired and interference powers across fluid-antenna ports, \textcolor{black}{we first formulate the outage probability in terms of the joint desired-signal and interference distributions and then derive an explicit integral expression under a tractable single-reference-port spatial correlation model.} Building on this result, we establish a rigorous diversity-order characterization revealing that the achievable diversity is jointly dictated by the fading severity and the spatial correlation rank imposed by the finite antenna aperture, rather than by the nominal number of ports. To enable accurate and tractable performance evaluation beyond the asymptotic regime, we further introduce a Gamma-matched outage approximation that preserves both the exact diversity order and the array-gain constant. The resulting closed-form expression provides an accurate characterization over a wide range of signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) thresholds and offers clear physical insight into the role of spatial correlation in FAMA systems. Extensive Monte Carlo (MC) simulations confirm the tightness of the exact analysis, the sharpness of the asymptotic results, and the accuracy of the proposed approximation.

title: A method to automatically discover symbolic local learning rules
abstract: We present a general method for discovering symbolic local learning rules that can replace backpropagation, applicable, in principle, to any deep learning architecture and task. The method automatically discovers local loss functions specific to each layer by (1) constructing a dictionary of monomials of local tensor variables, inspired by Penrose diagram notation, (2) regressing over coefficients weighting these monomials to build layerwise polynomial losses whose gradients together minimize a target global loss. We test the method on classification, reconstruction, and self-supervised learning tasks with small multilayer networks and minimal datasets. Across all tasks, the discovered rules induce non-trivial interactions between layers, which lead to significant reductions in the corresponding global losses. Furthermore, the method selects sparse combinations of monomials, finding local rules that are more interpretable than those generated by MLP-based alternatives. The potential implications of our method range from energy-efficient deep learning to the discovery of biologically plausible learning mechanisms.

title: One2N: Recursive refinement breaks the resolution barrier for Earth-system AI
abstract: Earth-system AI models approach kilometre-scale resolution, but halving grid spacing quadruples the grid-point count and end-to-end training cost. We introduce One2N, a recursive incremental framework extending a coarse model through $N$ levels of cross-resolution residual correction. At each level the parent is frozen and excluded from backpropagation, so its activations and optimizer states are never retained; only a tier-specific module is trained. A single refinement level on the NeuralGCM-0.7$^\circ$ baseline yields the two-level One2N-0.07$^\circ$, trained on one 80 GB GPU. Against HRES-0.07$^\circ$ and ERA5-0.25$^\circ$ analyses it matches its parent's tropospheric skill while reducing upper-stratospheric errors and resolving finer structure. Tropical-cyclone track errors nearly match the parent's and are lower than Pangu-Weather-0.25$^\circ$ at medium range; RMSE is lower than that model's on 93.46% of common targets. One2N thus turns an existing forecasting system, or an inexpensively trained coarse baseline, into a reusable foundation for high-resolution development, breaking the resolution barrier.

title: Movable Antenna-Assisted Covert Communications: Robust Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization
abstract: In this paper, we study a movable antenna (MA)-enhanced covert communication system, where a legitimate transmitter (named Alice) serves multiple legitimate users in the presence of multiple aerial wardens that attempt to detect the transmission from Alice. To ensure data covertness with imperfect knowledge of warden channel state information (CSI), we develop a unified robust covert transmission framework that incorporates bounded and statistical CSI error models. In particular, we aim to jointly optimize the transmit beamforming, the artificial noise (AN) covariance matrix, and MA positions at Alice to maximize the minimum weighted signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) among the legitimate users subject to data covertness constraints. The resulting optimization problem is intractable to solve optimally due to the strong coupling among the optimization variables and the random channel uncertainty. To deal with this issue, we propose a block coordinate descent (BCD)-based algorithm. Specifically, for the norm-bounded CSI error model, we first employ the S-procedure to convert the covertness constraints into a sequence of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Then, a successive convex approximation (SCA) procedure incorporating semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and bisection search techniques is proposed to solve the resulting problem. For the statistical CSI error model, the Bernstein-type inequality is employed to derive deterministic approximations of the probabilistic constraint in terms of LMIs and second-order cone (SOC) constraints that can be efficiently tackled. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm in improving the performance of MA-enhanced covert communication systems.

title: RAIL: Representation-Aligned Imitation Learning for Student-Compatible Teacher Policies
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) from raw sensory inputs such as images or onboard sensors can be challenging due to high-dimensional observations and sparse rewards. A common strategy is to train a teacher policy with access to privileged state information and then distill it into a student policy that acts from raw inputs alone. However, when the teacher relies on information unavailable to the student, exact imitation may be impossible, creating an irreducible imitation gap. Existing approaches typically mitigate this mismatch through careful reward shaping or additional reinforcement learning on the student policy after the teacher has been trained. Instead, we introduce Representation-Aligned Imitation Learning (RAIL), which addresses the mismatch during teacher training itself. RAIL learns a latent representation shared across teacher and student observations using contrastive learning, and trains the teacher policy directly in this space. Because the teacher policy is constrained to operate on this shared space, it learns behaviors that are reproducible from student observations. This substantially reduces the imitation gap while preserving task performance. Across multiple environments, RAIL outperforms strong baselines without reward modification or post-hoc student fine-tuning, and surpasses direct reinforcement learning from raw observations. The learned representations further enable zero-shot transfer to new tasks through teacher-only training. Project site: https://merajmammadov.com/rail/.

title: Lessons Not Learned: Why Cross-Chain Bridges Keep Losing Billions the Same Way
abstract: Bridge hacks have cost billions, often without exploiting a code bug. In the cross-chain bridge hacks we catalogue from 2021 to 2026, failures of security posture, meaning how a bridge's people, code, controls and off-chain infrastructure are set up, account for 88% of reported losses since 2023, and nearly all repeat earlier failures. Code audits cannot catch these failures, so we propose a bridge security assessment rubric. It scores each bridge deployment from on-chain evidence, and a hard cap drops the score to the lowest value when a fatal risk is present. A token is only as safe as its weakest deployment if all its deployments share one backing. For attacks nobody anticipated, we show that rate limits and an emergency stop still bound the loss. We build an analyzer that applies the rubric to deployed bridges and monitors them for changes, and an agentic analyzer that runs the same checks on any bridge. Operators learn what to fix, and users can compare bridges. Our rubric's controls cut bridge hack losses 105-fold, from \$3.52B to \$33M.

title: NLO QCD corrections to $W^{+}$-boson decays into doubly heavy baryons
abstract: The next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections have been investigated for the production of doubly heavy baryons via the inclusive $W^{+}$-boson decays $W^{+}\toΞ_{cc}+\bar{c}+\bar{s}+X$ and $W^{+}\toΞ_{bc}+\bar{b}+\bar{s}+X$ within the nonrelativistic QCD framework. The decay widths, the kinematic distributions, and the uncertainties induced by the heavy-quark masses and the renormalization scale have been analyzed for both the color-antitriplet ($\bar{\mathbf{3}}$) and the color-sextet ($\mathbf{6}$) $S$-wave states. With the central input parameters $m_{c}=1.8~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $m_{b}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the $K$ factors are $2.27$ for $Ξ_{cc}$ and $2.95$ for $Ξ_{bc}$, i.e., the NLO corrections increase the corresponding LO widths by about $127\%$ and $195\%$, which shows that the NLO corrections are indispensable for quantitative predictions. The individual-channel $K$ factors range from $1.94$ to $5.53$, with the largest one occurring for $Ξ_{bc}$ in the $[{}^{3}S_{1}]_{\mathbf{6}}$ channel. The distributions show that the NLO corrections enhance the low invariant-mass region and shift the baryon energy spectrum toward smaller energy fractions. With $Γ_{W}=2.085~\mathrm{GeV}$, the inclusive branching ratios are $8.86\times10^{-5}$ and $3.63\times10^{-6}$ for $Ξ_{cc}$ and $Ξ_{bc}$, respectively, which provide an NLO benchmark for future experimental searches.

title: Certified finite-precision readout for $p$-adic kernel aggregation
abstract: In non-archimedean numerical analysis, a verified $p$-adic approximation can determine an absolute value, and hence downstream probabilistic rankings and classification decisions, with mathematical exactness long before the underlying number is fully resolved. We turn this observation into rigorous finite-precision certificates for norm-based readouts of amplitude families. For a common error radius, a nonempty resolved set already fixes every exact maximizer, ties included, at the sharp integer absolute precision $v_*+1$, and conditioning on that set yields an exact total-variation identity separating unresolved $p$-adic mass from real rounding error. For aggregates of $p$-adic exponentials, we give a centered-moment certificate with an explicit remainder bound: on rational data it runs in exact rational arithmetic without individual exponential evaluations, attains its minimal bound at an active phase, and resolves every nonzero aggregate at high order; we also obtain an aggregate perturbation bound free of summand-count factors. For multiclass $p$-adic classifiers that decode by minimizing the norm of a class discriminant, we prove a necessary and sufficient certification condition and show that the sharp common precision threshold is $v^{(2)}+1$, governed by the second-largest discriminant valuation, so the winning discriminant need not itself be resolved. We apply these certificates to discrete $p$-adic path-integral actions on uniform affine chains, deriving explicit action centers and proving exact output-independence at zero effective quadratic coupling. Pseudocode and a reproducible reference implementation accompany the theory.

title: When the Norm is Wrong: Social Norm Misspecification and Targeting with an Application to Microfinance Adoption
abstract: Structural models of peer effects typically capture peer influence through the average, aggregate, or in some cases through extreme peer actions. Such specifications, however, are imposed ex ante and are typically ad hoc. We study the consequences of social norm misspecification by extending the constant elasticity of substitution (CES) norm from continuous to discrete choices. Considering a binary-choice game with incomplete information, we derive results on existence and uniqueness of a rational expectations equilibrium and establish conditions for identification of the structural parameters. We estimate the model by the Nested Pseudo-Likelihood estimator, implemented using the spectral algorithm. Monte Carlo simulations show that the CES estimates of the peer effects approach their true values as the sample grows, whereas imposing a linear norm biases them even in large samples. We apply the framework to microfinance adoption in India and find a strongly max-leaning norm, with significant heterogeneity in curvature and peer effects across villages grouped by caste composition and wealth. In a counterfactual exercise that allocates a fixed subsidy budget to maximise adoption, the estimated and linear norms target very different households, with the former favouring village "leaders", who are more likely to adopt and were the first to be informed about microfinance.

title: Predictability of Collective Behavior in Networks of LLM Agents
abstract: As AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly interact at scale, anticipating their collective behavior becomes necessary. Unlike humans, individual LLM agents can be probed in {controlled scenarios}; however, the predictability of their collective outcomes hinges on what such measurements capture. We study information cascades on networks of LLM agents that decide whether to share a post given how many of their contacts have shared it. At the same fraction of sharing contacts, an agent's response depends on how many contacts it has and on the post. Responses that ignore the number of contacts mispredict the cascades, increasingly on heterogeneous networks, by an error we derive analytically and that network topology alone cannot reveal. Measured in context, the response predicts, through mean-field theory, the cascades of full LLM simulations, tipping points included. Anticipating the collective behavior of AI agents thus requires evaluating them in their local network context.

title: Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
abstract: We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $γ\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $γ$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-degree grading and a $\mathbb{Z}$-weight grading coming from a version of the Riemann hypothesis, which suggests a similar grading should exist for an extension of the Kauffman bracket skein module, for the framed $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Floer cohomology of Abouzaid--Manolescu, and for the quantum modular cocycle. This leads to surprising additive identities among algebraic units, which we confirm for the complement of the simplest hyperbolic knot $4_1$, as well as for $S^1 \times Σ_g$ for a closed genus $g$ surface.

title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

title: A forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models: an EFM3D case study for crime scene reconstruction
abstract: Foundation models increasingly combine geometry, semantics, and spatial context for three-dimensional scene understanding, but their suitability for forensic crime scene reconstruction remains unclear. This study presents a structured forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models and demonstrates it using the Egocentric Foundation Model for 3D (EFM3D). Four simulated indoor crime scenes were recorded with Meta Project Aria Gen~1 at Robert Gordon University's East Lodge House forensic training facility. The framework evaluates room-scale reconstruction, semantic scene understanding, computational performance, and forensic suitability. Across the four scenes, EFM3D generated meshes averaging $12{,}668\pm2{,}430$ vertices and $24{,}838\pm4{,}903$ faces, with 39,529 recorded semantic predictions spanning 21--24 categories at a mean confidence of 0.40. Because reference meshes and expert-labelled 3D ground truth were unavailable, these statistics are treated as descriptive outputs rather than measures of geometric or detection accuracy. Final inference runs processed $1{,}388\pm203$ snippets per scene at $0.69\pm0.01$ samples/s and required $50.77\pm6.12$ minutes per recording. A seven-criterion capability profile indicated stronger support for room geometry, furniture localisation, scene context, and spatial relationships than for fine-scale forensic evidence. The results position EFM3D as a complementary tool for contextual documentation and scene review rather than a replacement for high-fidelity forensic capture. The framework provides a reproducible basis for evaluating future egocentric foundation models in specialised forensic settings.

title: Variational free complement method with Gaussian expanded complement functions: extensions of general atomic framework including helium and lithium ground states with geminal induced expansion length
abstract: We expand the previous framework of hierarchical-decontraction Gaussian expanded complement functions approach (arXiv: 2603.16262v2) of the free complement (FC) method to $N$-electron atomic systems including general permutations. We consider the possibility that the Gaussian expansion length depends on the presence of the geminal $g$ function. To be more specific, fewer expansion length shall be used when the two-electron $g$ function is combined with the initial wavefunction. The present approach is applied to the ground states of the helium and lithium atoms. The complement function generations via 2s$\rightarrow$1s channel in the lithium ground state are discussed. Symmetries for the associated $N$-electron integrals are analyzed.

title: Hierarchical Multi-Channel Tip-Over Prediction via Isolated Temporal Models for Planetary Rover Safety
abstract: Reliable tip-over prevention is critical for planetary rovers operating in unstructured environments where communication delays prevent real-time human intervention. Existing learning-based approaches typically optimize a single prediction objective, limiting their ability to capture both gradual instability evolution and abrupt terrain disturbances. This work presents a hierarchical multi-channel tip-over prediction framework based on isolated temporal learning. A multi-horizon Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) learns progressive instability patterns from inertial measurements, while a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)-based forward dynamics model predicts nominal rover motion and detects unexpected dynamic deviations through prediction residuals. These complementary signals are integrated through decision-level fusion and priority-based arbitration to generate graded safety actions, including early warning and emergency braking. The proposed system is deployed as an Orocos Real-Time Toolkit (RTT)-based safety component within the Rock robotics framework, operating at 100 Hz on a planetary rover software stack. Experiments on Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) samples collected across heterogeneous terrains demonstrate 97.58% event prediction coverage with a 1.82s median lead time, outperforming individual prediction channels. The results validate that isolated temporal models combined through hierarchical decision fusion provide a robust solution for real-time rover safety in uncertain terrain.

title: Asymptotics of matrix orthogonal polynomials with non-scalar varying weights
abstract: We study the $2\times 2$ matrix orthogonal polynomials $\mathbf{P}_N$ on the real line with respect to the varying weights $\mathrm{e}^{-N\mathbf{Q}(z)}\mathbf{B}(z)$, where $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are real symmetric matrix polynomials that commute with a Hermite-type matrix weight, $\mathbf{Q}$ is not scalar and $\mathbf{B}$ is positive definite. We are motivated by the non-Abelian Toda deformation of the Hermite-type weight, in the sense of Deaño, Morey and Román. The weight depends on $N$ through a matrix exponential that is not scalar, so that its two eigenvalues have different exponential rates. The matrix orthogonality reduces to two scalar orthogonality problems on the real line, with a varying weight that has an essential singularity at the origin. Assuming that the associated equilibrium measure is one-cut regular, we obtain the strong asymptotics of $\mathbf{P}_N$ and of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$ by the Deift-Zhou steepest descent method. Our main result is the limiting zero distribution of the entries of $\mathbf{P}_N$. These zeros are complex in general, and they accumulate on a curve where the contributions of the two eigenvalues of the weight have the same size. When this curve crosses the real segment that attracts the zeros of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$, the zeros of the entries display a critical behavior, and a positive fraction of them accumulates on this segment.

title: Rates in the weak invariance principle for slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems
abstract: We obtain rates of convergence in the weak invariance principle for certain classes of slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems. In particular, for systems satisfying a Functional Correlation Bound with rate $n^{-γ} \ (γ>1)$, we establish an explicit bound in the Wasserstein-$r$ metric for $1\le r<γ+1$ whenever the variance grows at a sufficiently fast polynomial rate. The proof is based on Bernstein's ``big block--small block" method. Examples covered by our result include sequential heterochaos baker maps and sequential LSV maps. In particular, for random LSV maps over an ergodic base, we obtain rates in the quenched weak invariance principle.

title: Multichannel Phonon Interconversion Drives 90 Polarization Rotation for Stable Domain Walls in Hafnium Oxide
abstract: Polarization rotation is a fundamental mechanism in ferroelectric materials, yet how such rotation arises microscopically in fluorite ferroelectrics and gives rise to distinct domain walls (DW) remains unresolved. Phonon modes offer a microscopic route to such structural transformations, as geometric orientations can modify their frequencies, dispersion relations, and vibrational eigenstates when their characteristic wavelengths become comparable to relevant physical dimensions. Here, by combining condensed phonon mode decomposition with first-principles calculations, we investigate the origin of 90 polarization rotation in the ferroelectric phase of HfO2. Using the cubic parent phase as reference, we show that polarization rotation originates from multiple symmetry equivalent phonon modes of distinct eigenstates at different wavevectors in the Brillouin zone, whose coupling and cooperative reorientation continuously evolve to generate distinct 90 Pca21 variants and switching pathways. Among the 90 variants, the lowest-energy switching pathway through the Pmn21 exhibits an energy barrier comparable to, but slightly lower than, that of the 180 polarization reversal pathway through the P42/nmc phase, indicating that 90 polarization rotation is an energetically accessible alternative switching route. We further analyze 90 DW and find that frustrated phonon modes emerge at the wall center, where the coexistence and competition of condensed modes promote local reconfiguration of the lattice distortions, contributing to the elevated DW energies. Importantly, experimental observations with STEM imaging provide direct evidence of atomic mode distortions in stable 90 DW, consistent with the theoretically identified low-energy DW. These findings provide the fundamental structural mechanism underlying 90 switching dynamics, competing domain-wall physics, and macroscopic ferroelectric behavior.

title: Beam-beam effects on measurements at electron-positron colliders: LEP neutrino counting and Higgs factories
abstract: Beam-beam electromagnetic interactions affect the luminosity, collision energy, polarization, and particle backgrounds relevant to precision measurements at electron-positron colliders. We investigate these effects using Fast $e^{\pm}e^{\pm}$ Beam and Luminosity (FeeBL), a new beam-beam simulation framework, and compare its predictions with published results from LEP and proposed future colliders. We reproduce the analytical field-integration calculations of LEP Bhabha scattering and identify an approximately 2% bias in previously published beam-deflection simulations. Applying the corresponding luminosity correction and a revised uncertainty assessment motivated by the observed agreement among the four LEP experiments yields ($N_ν= 2.9965 \pm 0.0040$), compared with the previously reported ($2.9963 \pm 0.0074$). The revised uncertainty is conditional on an assumed common rescaling of experiment specific uncertainties and motivates further investigation of the original uncertainty budgets. We identify and correct implementation errors in the modeling of Breit-Wheeler, Bethe-Heitler, and Landau-Lifshitz pair production, with implications for detector backgrounds at Higgs factories. Simulated beam depolarization and luminosity spectra are compared with existing ILC and HALHF predictions. Finally, we investigate collision energy monochromatization for direct Higgs production, obtaining sub-MeV collision energy peak widths in exploratory linear collider configurations at substantial luminosity cost, while finding significantly weaker narrowing for the FCC-ee configurations studied. We derive a rigid Gaussian beam overlap model and estimate that FCC-ee needs roughly 10 m of horizontal only dispersion to reach widths of $\approx1~\mathrm{MeV}$.

title: Data-Adaptive Subset-Size Selection for Minimum Covariance Determinant Estimation
abstract: Subset size determines the balance between robustness and efficiency in minimum covariance determinant estimation. Conventional choices fix this balance before the extent and structure of contamination are known. Reweighting does not remove the influence of the initial subset size. We propose a data-adaptive rule based on ordered squared Mahalanobis distances. It selects the first window maximum, with window width proportional to the sample size. For a minimum covariance determinant subset, the statistic equals the smallest squared distance among excluded observations. For smooth elliptical distributions with small one-point contamination, we characterize the first population window maximum. Under suitable conditions, it is the last retained fraction at which excluding the contaminating point remains optimal. We derive a first-order expansion for this boundary and establish sample localization along the full integer path. Without contamination, the selected fraction tends to one. A fast depth-based implementation reuses one ordering across candidate sizes. Simulations under Gaussian and heavy-tailed sampling show gains over fixed subset sizes, most consistently for scatter estimation. Real data analyses show that the initial subset size affects which observations are retained after reweighting.

title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
abstract: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal that pre-existing S vacancies lower the Cr Frenkel-pair migration barrier by up to 1.1 eV, providing an atomistic mechanism for beam-induced Cr redistribution and structural transformations. Displacement threshold calculations further show that Br is the most susceptible species to electron-beam-induced displacement, identifying the relative ease of removing different atomic species. Together, these results establish a validated computational framework for investigating atomic-scale disorder and structural transformations in CrSBr, providing a basis for defect engineering in materials for future magneto-optoelectronic applications.

title: Odds-Structured Distributional Regression for Interpretable Time-to-Event Prediction
abstract: Time-to-event prediction is fundamentally challenged by partial observability and aleatoric uncertainty. In clinical medicine, for instance, the timing of disease progression or acute readmission is contingent on highly dynamic and largely latent health trajectories. Rather than forcing a deterministic point forecast, distributional regression offers a principled means to address this complexity by predicting a probability distribution over time. However, explaining these distributional predictions presents a key obstacle: raw distribution parameters output by the model are abstract mathematical quantities that do not align well with domain concepts. To gain interpretability, we propose a novel paradigm where output parameters are designed to be additive in log-odds---a widely established measure in clinical risk modeling. Our approach, called ODDS-DR, moves beyond technical convenience to deliver clear domain alignment as well as the layer-wise computational structure required for robust, time-dependent feature attribution. Validated across two real-world clinical cohorts, our framework matches state-of-the-art predictive performance while resolving distributional outputs into interpretable risk markers across flexible prognostic horizons.

title: Agent4Crypto: A Dual-Reflective and Market-Feedback-Aligned LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Cryptocurrency Trading
abstract: Cryptocurrency markets provide a natural testbed for autonomous AI agents because they are digital-native, high-frequency, and machine-speed environments, yet existing methods often struggle with non-stationary market regimes, opaque decisions, and fixed aggregation rules. In this paper, we propose Agent4Crypto, a dual-reflective and market-feedback-aligned multi-agent system. The framework coordinates specialized agents for data collection, analysis, risk assessment, reflection, and trading, synthesizing heterogeneous signals from prices, indicators, news, and charts in an interpretable decision pipeline. Our central design is a trader-centric decision mechanism: three style-specific trader agents, Aggressive, Neutral, and Conservative, generate candidate actions and natural-language rationales from the same market context, while their influence is learned rather than manually fixed. A PPO-based gating policy dynamically allocates trader weights through a dual-reflective feedback process. One reflection stream evaluates post-trade decision quality from realized portfolio outcomes and distills reusable lessons into a Financial ReasoningBank for retrieval in subsequent trader prompts, while the other estimates trader-level counterfactual contribution, indicating which style has recently aligned better with market movements. The PPO state combines Counterfactual Contribution Memory with market features, previous trader weights, and current trader actions, so trader influence adapts across bull, sideways, and bear regimes. Experiments on BTC, ETH, and XRP show that Agent4Crypto improves total return and Sharpe ratio over traditional strategies, machine learning and reinforcement learning baselines, and existing LLM-based trading systems, demonstrating the value of interpretable trader competition and market-feedback-driven adaptation in volatile cryptocurrency markets.

title: Modelling socio-economic effects of the pandemic in a metropolitan area
abstract: One of the most notorious measures taken by authorities in every country trying to prevent the uncontrollable spread of the Covid 19 pandemic was to impose severe measures to diminish the mobility of people. In recent publications we proposed a mathematical model to address the consequences of these measures and to predict the infections under different scenarios, for various different countries. In this paper we extend the model, called the BTH--SEIRS-model, to deal with the reduction of mobility in an urban area. The chosen region was the densely-populated metropolitan area around Helsinki, the capital of Finland. This choice obeyed to the fact that there are precise data related to mobility from a mobile telephone company, and that this region was completely isolated from the rest of the country for a short period during the pandemic. We also used public transport data from railways and the accommodation occupation rates in the area of interest. We show that the BTH--SEIRS model is capable of simulating the real infection data as well as the mobility-related economic activity, exhibiting the main trends present in the three indicators used for comparison. Our calculations allow us to highlight the difference of the behaviour of the pandemic in a totally different spatial scale, and to discover the hidden factors that govern the behaviour of people who are forced to commute every day from home to work.

title: Public, Identifiable, and Effectively Immutable: Ethical Lessons from Research on arXiv
abstract: Ethical decision-making is central to safe cybersecurity research. Recent studies, one of which is our own, analyzing the source files of arXiv papers bring this challenge to light - arXiv publicly distributes the source files, to the surprise of many authors. Unique aspects reveal ethical challenges and dilemmas that extend beyond established ethical frameworks, institutional processes, and community best practices. In this work, we examine this case and provide insights for similar research on other public live resources, such as Zenodo or the Wayback Machine. While such empirical studies are particularly realistic, they must account for personally identifiable information, leaked secrets, and other sensitive details that could expose, shame, or otherwise negatively affect individuals, possibly leading to both reputational and practical harm. sDrawing on our collective experience and discussions among researchers, affected authors, and readers, we make three contributions: First, we define the ethical setting and highlight that even intentionally-public data with deliberate real-name attribution can raise ethical concerns when repurposed for empirical analysis. Second, we discuss the ethical issues surrounding the use of arXiv data and derive four higher-level dilemmas that researchers may face when working with similar data. Third, we derive practical guidance for ethically navigating such settings and, in doing so, distill four lessons for research on arXiv and similar public, live datasets: public availability should serve as the starting point of ethical reasoning; research should minimize the amplification it induces on exposed information; disclosure should be calibrated to the harm, confidence, and actionability of a finding; and effective immutability must be accounted for. Together, these contribute to community resources for ethically-sound cybersecurity experiments.

title: Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator
abstract: We study the subellipticity of the analytically deformed Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and give two definitions of resonances, one based on analytic dilation and the other on analytic distortion in the $x$-variables. Due to the failure of global subellipticity of the distorted operator in dimensions $n \geq 2$, the second method can only be used in dimension one. We show that, whenever both methods are applicable, they give rise to the same set of resonances. We also prove that, when $|\na V(x)| = O(\w x^{-ρ})$ with $ρ>1$, positive resonances are embedded eigenvalues and/or scattering resonances whose resonant states belong to weighted $L^2$-spaces and satisfy an outgoing radiation condition.

title: Translation continuity for the local bilinear circular maximal operator
abstract: We prove a positive power translation-continuity estimate for the local bilinear circular maximal operator on the real line. More precisely, there is $η>0$ such that the operator applied to a translation difference in either input maps $L^8(\mathbb{R})\times L^8(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^4(\mathbb{R})$ with norm $O(|h|^η)$. This answers Question 6.3 in Borges's survey on bilinear spherical averages. The main step is a frequency-localized estimate for arbitrary bounded inputs. A $TT^*$ argument converts it into a linear maximal problem on the plane, associated with pairs of circles. We verify the corrected multi-parameter cinematic curvature condition of Chen, Guo, and Yang by proving an irreducibility and infinitesimal independence statement for the resulting quartic curves. Uniform algebraic sublevel estimates control the degeneracies. Interpolation also gives continuity for all finite exponents $2<p,q<\infty$, with output exponent $pq/(p+q)$.

title: Asymptotic spreading of Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments with time-periodic limits
abstract: In this paper, we study the rightward spreading speed of solutions for Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments. The linear growth rate has time periodic limits at the two ends of the moving frame. Each limit has a positive average and may be negative during a period. When the growth rate lies between the two limits at each time, we show that the spreading speed depends only on their averages and the asymptotic shift speed. For intermediate shift speeds, the formulas give nonlocal pulling if the right end has the larger average and speed locking if the left end has the larger average. The interior growth profile may be nonmonotone in space and aperiodic in time. We prove the formulas by constructing upper and lower solutions for a stepwise profile and then comparing with shifted stepwise problems.

title: SimpFlow: Transferable Pretraining for Fluid Dynamics via Simplified Physics
abstract: Neural surrogates enable rapid fluid simulation, but learning across diverse three-dimensional (3D) geometries requires costly computational fluid dynamics (CFD) labels. We introduce SimpFlow, a pretraining approach that generates supervision from simplified physics on unlabeled geometry libraries. A source-panel potential-flow solver generates velocity and pressure fields for approximately 9,000 3D geometries, capturing geometry-induced acceleration, stagnation, and suction while omitting viscosity and separated wakes. The solver imports only a surface mesh and reuses precomputed velocity fields across inflow directions, enabling inexpensive label generation. In our benchmark, amortized labeling takes 0.111 s per example using four CPU threads. We pretrain a neural surrogate on these labels and fine-tune it on independent CFD datasets. Across five flow tasks, SimpFlow improves over training from scratch in all 24 task-budget settings. With fine-tuning fixed at 200 epochs, interpolation indicates that SimpFlow requires 35-68% fewer CFD training cases to match the error of scratch models trained at each task's largest data budget. These results demonstrate that simplified physical solutions can provide transferable supervision, offering a practical way to reduce the high-fidelity data requirements of fluid surrogates.

title: The rank of the Fano normal function via the Fermat cubic
abstract: We prove that the canonical derivative of the Fano normal function has rank ten at the Fermat cubic threefold. This yields a direct proof of its generic maximal rank, a result also implied by a general theorem of Gao--Zhang. Our approach combines Hain's equivariance principle with an explicit representation-theoretic computation and the nonvanishing of the Griffiths infinitesimal invariant established by Collino--Naranjo--Pirola.

title: Positronium resonance of electric monopoles in quantum spin ice
abstract: Quantum spin ice attracts considerable attention due to its remarkable low-energy properties, described by the effective gauge theory, which mimics the quantum electrodynamics (QED). The ``effective" QED in quantum spin ice is beyond the ``real" QED in our universe in many respects. Above all, the effective QED hosts two kinds of gapped particles, the electric monopole, in addition to the magnetic monopole. Among the two monopoles, the electric monopole is of purely quantum origin, and its character has not been well resolved. In this work, we focus on the Rokhsar Kivelson point of the quantum dimer model, as the low-energy description of the quantum XXZ model on a pyrochlore lattice, and address the excitation spectrum of the electric monopoles, by combining the quantum Monte Carlo simulation with the stochastic analytical continuation. Most strikingly, the electric monopole spectrum exhibits clear double-peak structure, corresponding to the bound states and scattering states of electric monopoles. The lower-energy peak is attributed to the exciton-like bound state of an electric monopole pair, a signal of positronium in quantum spin ice. We found that the flippable loop operator serves as a local physical observable to excite a pair of electric monopoles, implying that monopoles can be detected through lattice or optical response.

title: Probabilistic wavefield decomposition from array covariance
abstract: Inter-sensor coherence loss carries information about the wavefield that conventional array processing discards. The array-covariance matrix is modelled using a mixture of energy distributions over slowness with analytical characteristic functions, e.g., skew-normal and angular-harmonic distributions, and inverted using variational Bayesian inference. The posterior supports uncertainty quantification, experimental design, model comparison and hypothesis testing. For a synthetic hydroacoustic T-phase, information is increased by an additional sensor and decreased by noise; the data favour a distributed source over a point source. For an observed thermospheric infrasound return, energy is skewed back towards the source. The method is implemented in the software Topophone2.

title: Deploying QKD on the fiber links of the National Quantum Communication Infrastructure in Sweden
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is being deployed across Europe to evaluate its performance and practicality in real-world scenarios. When preparing this deployment, it is important to survey the properties of the fiber links that will be used for the quantum channel, cross-checking them with those of QKD devices, to ensure compatibility and optimal performance. We report here our studies from the Swedish chapter of this endeavor, the National Quantum Communication Infrastructure in Sweden. We focus on procedures to characterize the links and evaluate their suitability for QKD. We relate measurable properties to the key factors that affect the secret key rate using a simplified model that aims at the essence of QKD performance. Finally, we confirm the feasibility of QKD on one of our links by reporting a one-month long successful test.

title: Calibration-free quantum thermometry with strain-swept two-level defects
abstract: Superconducting qubits operate within a well-defined temperature range, making local temperature monitoring important. Here we show that intrinsic two-level defects in Josephson-junction barriers can act as local thermometers by exploiting the shape of their population response, without requiring calibration of the readout offset or contrast. Marginalizing over these unknown parameters imposes an identifiability requirement absent from single-parameter thermometric bounds: for narrow sweeps, usable information scales as the fourth power of the sweep width. Hence, a narrow sweep becomes locally indistinguishable from a change in offset or contrast. We illustrate this principle with a strain-swept two-level defect in a Josephson junction. For a reported defect with tunneling energy $Δ_{0}/h=\SI{1.3}{\giga\hertz}$, swept along one branch of its hyperbola to \SI{2.69}{\giga\hertz} (an asymmetry excursion of \SI{2.36}{\giga\hertz}, or \SI{8}{\volt} of piezo voltage), the analysis projects a single-defect fit precision of \SI{0.58}{\percent} at \SI{20}{\milli\kelvin}. The resulting response enables temperature estimation without prior calibration of the readout offset and contrast, while the same sweep overdetermines the Boltzmann form and identifies significant deviations from thermality. These results establish intrinsic junction defects as a resource for calibration-free local thermometry and highlight identifiability as a key design criterion for primary temperature sensing.

title: Tuning correlated states in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene with magnetic encapsulation
abstract: Rhombohedral graphene multilayers provide a flexible platform for correlated physics associated with their flat-band electronic structure. While a variety of correlated states appear in these systems as a function of bias and electrostatic doping, promoting specific correlated flavor symmetry breaking states remains a challenge. Here we show that magnetic encapsulation by CrGeTe3 achieves this in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene, by using switchable exchange couplings induced by ferromagnetic substrates. We show that correlations in rhombohedral multilayers at charge neutrality strongly renormalize the exchange proximity splitting,giving rise to collective spin modes whose character is switched by the parallel or antiparallel alignment of the encapsulation. We further show that upon doping of the flat bands, spin triplet f-wave superconducting solutions emerge, whose layer and spin selectivity is controlled by the magnetic encapsulation, hosting in-gap excitations at the edges. Our results establish magnetic alignment as a means to control spin symmetry breaking and unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene.

title: A Self-Interacting Dark-Matter Route to Supermassive Kerr Black Holes via Super-Eddington Bondi Accretion: Mass-Spin Evolution
abstract: Recent JWST observations motivate mechanisms for rapid black-hole growth in the early Universe. Extending our previous Schwarzschild study, we show that critical relativistic Bondi accretion of repulsively self-interacting dark matter remains an efficient super-Eddington channel for Kerr black holes with rotating inflow. Within a stationary equatorial quasi-spherical framework, smooth critical solutions exist over a finite range of inflow angular momentum set by the Kerr marginally bound capture values. Rotation changes the sonic structure and accretion efficiency, while the critical density cancellation and dark-sector/halo matching retain their Schwarzschild form. The resulting rapid growth persists until the finite halo supply becomes limiting. Because the inflow also carries angular momentum, stellar-mass seeds can grow and spin up simultaneously; illustrative population evolutions therefore provide a joint mass--spin route to early supermassive Kerr black holes.

title: Large deviations, optimal trajectories and conservation of momenta in generalised Jackson networks
abstract: We study properties of optimal trajectories for the quasipotential that governs large deviations of queue lengths in generalised Jackson networks (GJN). The trajectories are shown to satisfy Hamilton equations. The Hamiltonian is identified. Optimal trajectories and associated costs are found for networks with two and three stations. A conservation law for adjoint variables is discovered to the effect that certain components are maintained along an optimal trajectory. A process is proposed for finding optimal trajectories and computing their costs in general GJN.

title: A Comprehensive Analysis of the H$α$ Luminosity Functions at $z\sim 1.3$ and $z\sim 2.0$ in the CANUCS Lensing Fields with JWST NIRISS
abstract: We present H$α$ luminosity function (LF) measurements at redshifts $z\sim1.3$ and $z\sim2.0$. We adopt JWST grism data in five lensing cluster fields and their parallel fields from the CANUCS program: ABELL-370, MACS-J0416, MACS-J0417, MACS-J1149, MACS-J1423. Based on emission lines spectroscopically identified in the F115W, F150W and F200W filters, our final sample consists of 762 H$α$ emitters, including 433 at $1.1<z<1.5$ and 329 at $1.8<z<2.2$. Through detailed effective volume and completeness analysis for each source, we construct the H$α$ LF in two redshift bins. Thanks to the sensitivity of NIRISS WFSS and gravitational lensing magnification, our sample reaches intrinsic H$α$ luminosities down to $L_{\rm Hα}\sim10^{40.6}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $L_{\rm Hα}\sim10^{41}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim2.0$ with completeness larger than 80\%. The larger survey volume and coverage of multiple independent sightlines help mitigate cosmic variance. After accounting for cosmic variance, we constrain the faint-end slopes to be $α_{\mathrm{H}α}=-1.51^{+0.06}_{-0.04}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $-1.42^{+0.09}_{-0.06}$ at $z\sim2.0$, indicating a mild evolution between the two redshift bins. We find a negligible contribution from bright active galactic nuclei in our sample. We estimate integrated cosmic star formation rate densities of $0.103^{+0.008}_{-0.007}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $0.149^{+0.016}_{-0.013}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim2.0$. The emission-line samples presented here will enable further detailed studies of galaxy properties including metallicities. The methodology presented here can be readily applicable to other JWST slitless spectroscopic datasets and future wide-field slitless surveys, including those from Euclid, Roman, and the Chinese Space Station Telescope.

title: Learning Evidence-Grounded Reasoning for Context-Aware Time Series Forecasting
abstract: LLM-driven time series forecasting has become increasingly promising by leveraging contextual features to generate future values directly or refine forecast priors. However, incorporating contextual features alone does not ensure that models can identify which features matter for forecasting and understand what they suggest about future dynamics. We argue that the fundamental challenge is how to extract predictive evidence from contextual features and when and how to leverage it to guide forecasting decisions. In this paper, we propose CastReasoner, an evidence-grounded reasoning model for context-aware time series forecasting. Specifically, CastReasoner uses a structured chain of thought (CoT) to extract predictive evidence from contextual features, infer the future dynamics suggested by this evidence, and assess these dynamics against the forecast prior to guide adaptive forecasting decisions. To enable this capability, we design a reasoning-centric two-stage post-training framework including supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL). First, we synthesize reasoning trajectories through controllable multi-teacher guidance and select high-quality ones using a novel student-aware difficulty metric. Second, we design fine-grained multi-objective rewards to further improve reasoning and forecasting. To address heterogeneous learning needs across domains in both stages, we introduce a convergence-guided data balancing strategy. Through this two-stage training, CastReasoner improves both reasoning quality and predictive accuracy. Extensive experiments across multi-domain forecasting benchmarks demonstrate that CastReasoner achieves superior forecasting performance.

title: VLA-MOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Task VLA Policy Consolidation
abstract: Physical intelligence requires embodied agents to ground language in observations and execute actions while retaining useful skills. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies offer a shared interface, but task-specific post-training often produces separate specialists. Consolidation is difficult: mixed-task reinforcement learning provides sparse trajectory-level credit, while offline distillation may miss student-visited observations and endpoint distillation does not supervise intermediate action-generation states. We introduce VLA Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (VLA-MOPD), a protocol for consolidating flow-matching VLA specialists. After acquiring task or suite experts, a shared student collects robot rollouts and queries the instruction-routed frozen teacher at each visited observation and intermediate ordinary differential equation (ODE) state. Detached per-flow-step transition targets supervise valid action chunks through a masked local matching loss; an optional reference-policy term supports retention on other tasks. Starting from one trajectory per LIBERO task, VLA-MOPD raises mean success-once from 75.4% to 98.9%, compared with 98.15% for endpoint action distillation. It improves mean RoboTwin 2.0 success from 73.0% to 89.3%; on a Piper robot, two consolidation rounds improve average success from 70.0% to 90.0%. In a near-matched Spatial-adaptation study, reference matching limits the Object suite decrease to 3.0 points, versus 13.2 without the reference term.

title: Algorithm-aware Statistical Inference in High-dimensional Estimating Equations
abstract: Iterative algorithms are integral to many statistical procedures, whereas sampling uncertainty along their iteration is generally not quantified. We develop simultaneous inference for discrete trajectories generated from high-dimensional estimating equations, with iteration-specific population estimands that preserve algorithmic regularization. Our proposed fixed-Jacobian bootstrap propagates perturbations along the observed trajectory without repeatedly running the original nonlinear algorithm. We establish uniform first-order expansions and bootstrap validity over possibly infinite sets of contrasts and iterations under stability, entropy and moment conditions. Simulations in sparse linear regression, paired Fisher discrimination, and temporal-difference learning demonstrate accurate simultaneous coverage. A micro-randomized trial application illustrates inference for a treatment trajectory with participant-level clustering.

title: ForgeSystem: An Architecture for Demand-Specific Artefact Production with AI Agents
abstract: General-purpose software serves many different demands, but this flexibility costs performance and efficiency on any specific demand. Software tailored to a specific demand avoids these losses, yet developing it requires substantial time and effort from human experts. AI agents offer an alternative: they can design, implement and test artefacts tailored to individual demands. We call this production paradigm Forge.
