title: Frequency tuning capability of self-powered piezoelectric tuned mass dampers
abstract: Tuned mass dampers suffer from frequency shift sensitivity. This paper investigates the use of tunable piezoelectric tuned mass dampers (PE-TMD) by studying their behavior with tunable resistive and capacitive loads to adapt their resonant frequency. An analytical model is developed to assess the influence of key dimensionless parameters-electromechanical coupling coefficient, mass ratio, and quality factoron vibration attenuation, frequency tuning capability, and energy harvesting. The study reveals trade-offs between attenuation, tunability, and energy harvesting. It provides design guidelines for autonomous PE-TMDs and identifies key challenges for their practical implementation, including the interest of high coupling coefficients, whose the implication is limited is with growing mass ratio. Notably, it highlights the necessity of high coupling coefficient, the influence of which on frequency tuning is limited as the mass ratio grows.

title: Bridging Task Planning and Execution for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Manipulation
abstract: Robots are increasingly expected to execute natural-language manipulation tasks in real-world environments. This is particularly relevant in household assistance and logistics, where clutter requires reasoning about both task objectives and execution feasibility. This challenge becomes even more pronounced for bimanual humanoid platforms, where coordinating two manipulators introduces additional interaction and kinematic constraints. We present a zero-shot vision-language framework for execution-aware bimanual manipulation that jointly reasons about task objectives and physical feasibility. Planning is grounded in a structured scene representation that combines semantic object relations with execution constraints, enabling the selection of obstacle relocations and execution choices while preserving task semantics. Compatible actions are organised into parallel bimanual stages with explicit pre- and post-conditions. A hierarchical validator evaluates these conditions under perceptual uncertainty and uses stage-level execution history to support local recovery or targeted replanning. Experiments on the CENTAURO hybrid wheeled-legged humanoid robot across nine language-conditioned manipulation scenarios show higher task success than a non-execution-aware baseline. In dedicated failure scenarios, hierarchical validation recovers from execution failures with fewer model queries than always replanning. These results demonstrate the benefits of combining execution reasoning directly into task planning. Videos and additional material are available on the Project Webpage: https://advrhumanoids.github.io/bridging-planning-execution/.

title: Magnetized plasma modulator for polarization-tunable ultrahigh-power single-cycle lasers
abstract: Ultrahigh power lasers with tunable polarization and few-cycle duration have long been considered the holy grail of high-power laser science, as they push light-matter interactions into an entirely new physical regime. Yet such pulses remain far beyond the reach of conventional solid-state optics and technologies. Here, we introduce a novel magnetized plasma modulator that boosts linearly polarized lasers from petawatt to exawatt powers while simultaneously enabling tunable polarization, offering a promising approach for high-power laser development. This is achieved in density-tailored plasmas by combining dispersive compression of a chirped picosecond laser pulse with magneto-chiral group-velocity splitting in a few-Tesla magnetic field. It can generate circularly or elliptically polarized pulses with extremely high compression ratios (over 1000) and extremely short durations (down to the single-cycle level) in a compact and efficient manner. These findings demonstrate a feasible pathway toward exawatt-class few-cycle lasers with tunable polarization, opening new avenues for a wide range of cutting-edge research and applications.

title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
abstract: While modern video generative models achieve remarkable visual fidelity, they remain noticeably brittle when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions. Targeted post-training is crucial, yet supervised fine-tuning suffers from offline state mismatch, and reinforcement learning is hindered by sparse, ill-defined physical reward functions. On-Policy (Self-)Distillation (OPSD) reconciles on-policy rollouts with dense corrective feedback, shifting the core challenge to designing effective privileged context. However, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts are inherently declarative, whereas real reference videos heavily entangle physical laws with visual appearance without parametric control. To this end, we propose PhysOPSD, introducing executable code as privileged physical context for video generation. Unlike static visual observations, executable code instantiates an editable physical world with intrinsic abstraction and controllability. Powered by PhysOPSD-Engine, we translate real-world physical scenarios into verifiable simulation programs. PhysOPSD then incorporates (i) dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap via an intermediate bottleneck, alongside (ii) controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose causal dynamic shifts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones, outperforming SFT and RL baselines with only $3$K samples, while preserving general video generation quality.

title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
abstract: Coordination between large language-model agents has become a central question for AI safety and software engineering, as such agents are deployed in groups that share infrastructure. Existing research tells the agents that partners exist or asks them to coordinate. Whether coordination arises through shared state alone, with nothing disclosing that anyone else is present, is the key question for deployments that share caches and memory between agents, yet it has rarely been examined, and never with independent replication; this study does both. Four agents each received a short arithmetic task and a key-value store presented to each as its own scratch space; two held complementary halves of one computation, and no prompt mentioned other agents, sharing or collaboration. For reliability, the environment was rebuilt independently from a written protocol, and both implementations ran under hashed locks on design, data and analysis. The results bear novelty value in three respects. Joint success occurred only through the shared store. Whether a model coordinated depended not on its vendor tier but on whether it wrote its intermediate result and looked at the store again, and one ordinary sentence, "check your workspace again before submitting", switched that second look on and off. The findings held under replication. For practice, state shared between agents is a communication channel and should be separated, namespaced and logged. For research, designs should be locked before the data, and the parse rule, endpoint and parameters reported. Future work should test open-weight models and separate using another agent's output from intending to communicate.

title: Derivations tangent to polar discriminants
abstract: We describe the module of logarithmic derivations along the discriminant of a stable polar representation of a reductive algebraic group. It splits into derivations along the fibres of the quotient map and a free summand lifted from logarithmic derivations along the associated branch divisor. This gives a uniform extension of previous results on full adjoint discriminants. We prove that, for visible stable polar actions of semisimple groups with finite generic stabilizer, the discriminant is a free divisor. For stable periodic gradings of arbitrary order with semisimple degree-zero group, we construct explicit Saito matrices from the infinitesimal action and the gradients of basic invariants, which yields determinantal equations for several exceptional discriminants. In particular, starting with exceptional Lie algebras, we provide examples of free discriminants of degrees 60, 120, 126 and 240 for inner gradings and a degree-72 example for an outer one.

title: Sensor placement for real-life water distribution networks, ensuring observability under uncertainties
abstract: Leakage detection in water distribution networks (WDNs) is crucial for limiting water losses. However, effective detection strongly depends on sensor availability and placement. Most existing sensor placement methods rely on extensive simulations or precise knowledge of hydraulic parameters, which are often uncertain in practice. In this paper, we propose using a scalable sensor placement framework based on structural observability that depends only on the network topology and the underlying pressure-flow interconnection structure. The approach guarantees structural observability independently of hydraulic parameters, and is therefore robust to parametric uncertainties, assuming that the network topology is correctly specified. The method is computationally efficient and its performance is demonstrated on several real-life WDNs provided by Brabant-Water. While the framework ensures full network observability, the required number of sensors can be high in large and cyclic networks, which may limit applicability in real-life and motivates future work on relaxed observability guarantees for sensor placement.

title: Gate-tunable supercurrent switching in a three-terminal quantum dot transistor
abstract: We propose and analyze a three-terminal superconducting transistor switch in which a gate-defined quantum dot region interrupts a flux-controlled loop. The output supercurrent is switched off completely when the two loop arms couple to the dot with equal tunneling strengths and half a flux quantum threads the loop. The device then operates as a symmetric SQUID at half flux. The condition follows from a single geometric factor $χ$, which reduces the three-terminal problem to an equivalent two-terminal Anderson impurity model and makes the switching mechanism independent of the Coulomb interaction, the dot level position, the total hybridization and temperature. These enter only through a prefactor and thus decide how tolerant the device is to imperfect barrier tuning. Numerical renormalization group calculations across the full coupling parameter space show that the resonance is embedded in a broad region of elevated switching ratio at intermediate hybridization $Γ\approx Δ$, while both weaker and stronger coupling reduce it to a thin isolated line. Finite temperature smooths the underlying singlet-doublet transition and lowers the supercurrent amplitude, but affects the open and closed states comparably and leaves the switching ratio largely intact. Within a zero-bandwidth two-level model, a second dot level is shown to open a leakage channel that grows as the two levels approach in energy. Raising the output barrier and the realistic presence of inter-level Coulomb repulsion, however, suppress the leakage.

title: Parker Solar Probe Flies Through the Sun's Magnetic Poles Near 10 Solar Radii
abstract: During the peak of the Sun's magnetic cycle, the solar corona can be complex and dominated by dynamics, while hidden below, the dipole component of the its photospheric magnetic field steadily reverses with respect to the rotational axis. Here, we use Parker Solar Probe (\emph{Parker}) data from two of its closest approaches in mid-2025 to show that the large-scale field at solar maximum resembled a simple tilted dipole. Similar to how Ulysses provided a complete scan of the solar rotation-aligned dipole at solar minimum, \emph{Parker} sampled the full range of magneto-latitudes, probing both magnetic poles below the Alfvén surface. Concurrent in situ data at larger distances reveal that both hemispheres contain solar wind with asymptotic speeds near 800 km s-1, yielding a picture similar to the Ulysses latitude scans but now in the equator near solar maximum. This contrasts with the disordered structure observed by Ulysses during its solar maximum latitude scan, which we attribute to the long timescale of data collection. Overall, we find the coronal field is organized as a dipole, but the fast solar wind streams are deformed by non-dipolar substructure: the positive dipole axis is aligned with one coronal hole, the negative centers over a pseudostreamer, and significant mass flux enhancements are observed at magnetic separatrixes. Our measurements suggest that even at solar maximum, the solar corona can still exhibit structure nearly as ordered as solar minimum. Moreover, by sampling rapidly and close to the Sun, the detailed imprint of source region structure can be determined in the solar wind.

title: Holomorphic integer-graded vertex operator superalgebras are purely even
abstract: We prove that a simple, self-contragredient, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, integer-graded holomorphic vertex operator superalgebra of CFT-type has zero odd part. We first show that a hypothetical nonzero odd part would be a simple current of categorical dimension $-1$ over a strongly rational pointed VOA with four simple modules. We then prove that every nonvacuum simple current of a strongly rational VOA has strictly positive lowest conformal weight. This leads to a contradiction with Dong-Jiao-Xu's theorem on the positivity of categorical dimension.

title: First-order origins of second-order supersymmetry
abstract: One-dimensional second-order supersymmetry is constructed from conserved first-order operators on a surface with a cyclic coordinate. In Witten's mechanics with two fermionic modes, a centrally extended $N=4$ algebra permits a conserved product connecting the zero- and two-fermion sectors. Cyclic reduction gives the second-order supercharge and the correlated quantum corrections in the charge and partner Hamiltonians. Isothermal coordinates identify the auxiliary Hill equation with the separated Laplace or wave equation for the gauge-transformed charge kernel, and express the correction as a Schwarzian derivative. The central momentum fixes the quadratic invariant $C$: the Riemannian construction gives $C\leq0$, and its indefinite counterpart gives $C\geq0$, with a separately chosen positive adjoint after reduction. Diagonalizing the one-fermion intermediate recovers real scalar factorizations for $C\leq0$ and complex ones for $C>0$. Pauli reductions provide a second first-order mechanism; on the hyperbolic plane they reveal a curvature-dependent invariant and additional charges of a regular free-particle--Pöschl--Teller pair in a selected momentum sector. In one dimension, a formally Hermitian two-component intermediate with a positive inner product yields local first-order chains for arbitrary $C$. For a constant superpotential, a real transverse deformation on a flat cylinder also gives a first-order surface realization of $C>0$ with a positive inner product.

title: Optimal Rates for Adaptive Private $k$-PCA
abstract: Given $n$ i.i.d. random matrices $A_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ with common expectation $Σ$, the goal of \emph{Differentially Private Stochastic PCA} is to identify a $k$-dimensional subspace capturing the leading variance directions of $Σ$, while preserving differential privacy~(DP) for each individual sample $A_i$. \citet{dungler2025iterative} introduced \kdppca, the first algorithm to simultaneously (1) achieve sample complexity $n=\widetilde O(d)$ for sub-Gaussian data, (2) adapt its privacy noise to the intrinsic randomness of the data, and (3) extend seamlessly to any target dimension $k\le d$. However, its sample complexity has a suboptimal dependence on $k$. We propose the first algorithm that achieves optimal sample complexity in both $d$ and $k$, while retaining properties (2) and (3) of \kdppca. Additionally, prior utility guarantees require a minimum sample size with exponential dependence on the eigengap. Our method removes this dependence. It also improves the dependence on spectral parameters, matching known lower bounds for the spiked covariance model. Unlike deflation-based approaches like \kdppca, our algorithm updates the full $d\times k$ subspace jointly rather than one eigenvector at a time. This non-deflation structure simplifies the algorithm, reduces the number of hyper-parameters, and improves computational efficiency, particularly when using block linear algebra libraries.

title: Path-Level Structural and Semantic Alignment for Hierarchical Multi-Label Text Classification
abstract: Hierarchical multi-label text classification (HMTC) requires models to capture both structural dependencies among labels and the fine-grained semantics of labels at different hierarchy levels. Existing methods often model hierarchy through prediction constraints or representations of individual labels and local relations. Structural and semantic supervision, however, are usually formulated separately. We instead use complete root-to-node label paths as a shared unit for both. Our framework introduces two auxiliary training objectives while retaining a standard multi-label classifier at inference. PathSimNCE aligns document representations with hierarchical paths using hierarchy-aware contrastive targets. These targets provide graded supervision for structurally related paths while preserving explicit supervision for the ground-truth paths. The complementary semantic objective uses LLM-generated, document-conditioned descriptions of the same positive paths. It thereby provides context-specific label semantics beyond static label representations. Experiments on three benchmarks show consistent improvements: structural alignment is particularly beneficial in deeper hierarchies, while semantic alignment provides additional gains for fine-grained labels.

title: Positive solutions of power equations in planar corner domains
abstract: We study positive solutions of $Δu=λu^k$ on bounded planar corner domains with zero boundary values away from the vertex. For negative-power absorption we identify the admissible interval of Martin masses and prove uniqueness at the minimum mass. Along the ordinary boundary, we identify the weak Hessian endpoint and its sharp tail when the set of zero inward derivative has positive length. For superlinear sources we prove attainment of the largest positive Martin mass in the subcritical range. At criticality we construct a family of singular solutions with zero Martin mass and distinguish its members by their second logarithmic coefficient and the endpoint integrability of their Hessian differences. Above criticality an angular eigenvalue governs the Morse index away from its zero threshold. We also give sharp physical-Hessian asymptotics for finite-mass remainders and joint corner and side estimates for negative-power sources.

title: Two-Phase Rapid Simulation-Based Inference with Differentiable Simulators
abstract: We introduce Rapid Simulation Based Inference (RSBI), a diffusion-based variational approach to likelihood-free Bayesian inference that achieves high sampling efficiency under large prior-to-posterior volumes. RSBI builds on advances in Schrödinger Bridge (SB) diffusion sampling to handle multi-modal posteriors, with an initial likelihood supplied by a distance measure via a differentiable simulator. The key innovation of this initial surrogate likelihood is that it gives a highly efficient proposal distribution, replacing sequential rounds of other methods with an efficient one-shot proposal. Subsequent refinement then transports the proposal to the true posterior as specified by the simulator and the original prior. The SB sampler is warm-started from the proposal, and its energy is corrected by a neural likelihood ratio that is learned only where the proposal places mass. As a variational method, RSBI does not suffer from prior leakage commonly observed in standard sequential posterior estimation methods. To improve mode coverage we optionally utilize the well-tempered meta-dynamics framework, which also encourages exploration of the prior volume. We observe strong performance on standard SBI benchmarks, particularly when the prior volume is increased relative to the ground truth posterior, achieving a performance degradation of only $\sim5\%$ on Two Moons under a highly constrained simulation budget. Additionally, we evaluate RSBI's performance for gravitational wave ring-down posterior estimation, in a real-world physics benchmark inspired by black hole spectroscopy.

title: Scalable Practical Synchronization of Heterogeneous Linear Systems
abstract: We study practical state synchronization of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems over directed graphs using static diffusive state feedback. Persistent mismatches between the agent dynamics generally preclude exact synchronization and are treated as bounded disturbances within an Input-to-State Stability (ISS) framework. We derive a scalable synthesis procedure based on fixed-dimension linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), whose dimension is independent of the number of agents. Local robust dissipation conditions are combined through a small-gain argument to obtain global ISS guarantees and explicit bounds on the synchronization error. The framework is formulated in a unified manner for continuous- and discrete-time systems, while highlighting a fundamental difference in disturbance attenuation between the two domains. In particular, exact ZOH discretization of a continuous-time controller need not preserve closed-loop stability, motivating a native discrete-time synthesis. Numerical experiments on heterogeneous harmonic oscillators illustrate the proposed approach and the continuous/discrete-time distinction.

title: Physics-informed neural networks in the small-data regime: A controlled comparison with classical PDE surrogates
abstract: Neural surrogates for engineering models are often trained on large collections of simulated solutions. We investigate whether physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can achieve accurate predictions from scarce labelled observations by incorporating governing equations and prescribed initial and boundary conditions. We introduce hierarchical loss weighting (H-PINN) and its gradient-direction-aware extension (HO-PINN), which adjust the emphasis on physical constraints according to higher-priority losses. Hierarchical PINNs are compared with Vanilla PINN, tuned gradient boosting, support-vector regression, and Gaussian-process regression on a heat equation and three heterogeneous two-phase-flow benchmarks. Experiments use 20--1000 labelled states and ten paired seeds. Each label is one coordinate--state observation, not a complete simulation. At least one PINN variant achieves the highest mean primary-target \(R^2\) in each interpolation and equation-assisted forecasting comparison at 20 and 50 labels. The advantage for water saturation persists across all tested budgets. Hierarchical weighting reduces variability across runs in selected settings. These results demonstrate that known physics can support accurate neural surrogate predictions from very few solution observations, at substantially higher fitting cost than the tested classical regressors.

title: Neural Multipath Fields for 6G FR3 Digital Twins: Latent Adaptation from Sparse Data
abstract: Wireless digital twins are essential for environment-aware 6G communications, motivating the investigation of frequency range 3 (FR3), an emerging mid-band regime offering a promising balance between bandwidth and propagation characteristics. Neural Radio Frequency (RF) fields provide continuous surrogates for site-specific radio propagation, but adapting a scene-specific field to a new environment can require substantial measurements and retraining. To this end, we propose the Latent-Adaptive Neural Multipath Field (LANMF), a scene-conditioned FR3 model that predicts path-resolved delays, complex channel impulse response (CIR) coefficients, and arrival and departure directions from transmitter-receiver coordinates. LANMF learns shared propagation representations across source environments and adapts to unseen scenes by optimizing only a 16-dimensional scene latent. Evaluated on six ray-traced indoor scenes at 7.5 GHz, latent-only adaptation yields improvements in prediction with just 5-10 target links (0.42-0.83% of available links). Compared with full-network fine-tuning, it updates only 16 persistent target parameters, reducing adaptation time by 28-30% and incremental peak GPU memory by 82-85%. While the proposed solution supports various wireless applications, we demonstrate its utility through beam-candidate reduction using a 64-beam codebook, retaining measurement-based final beam selection.

title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
abstract: Discrete autoregressive modeling, notably through next-token prediction, has become a cornerstone of modern language models. Extending this paradigm to vision allows visual and language models to converge on a unified framework, thereby fostering shared methodology and infrastructure. This work investigates a central question: how far can a finite discrete vocabulary go in representing the richness of the visual world? We present dNaViT, a Discrete Native-resolution Vision Transformer that produces discrete visual primitives analogous to language tokens. Built upon a frozen pretrained encoder, dNaViT applies lightweight residual modulation with a dual-branch objective to inject reconstruction-aware cues into semantic features. By leveraging grouped product quantization, it scales discrete capacity without inflating spatial sequence lengths, while a balanced training recipe maintains both semantic and pixel-level information. Consequently, dNaViT functions as a versatile discrete visual tokenizer, enabling unified encoding across downstream tasks alongside high-fidelity image decoding. Extensive evaluations show that dNaViT matches or exceeds task-specific baselines across 12 visual understanding benchmarks, 4 generation benchmarks, and an image editing benchmark. These findings demonstrate that a compact discrete vocabulary can serve as a universal visual currency and unlock the full potential of fully unified, native multimodal methodology.

title: UCB-min: Combining Bandits Under Variance Heterogeneity (Extended Version)
abstract: Multi-armed bandits are a natural framework for many real-world sequential decision problems, from recommender systems and clinical trials to educational test recommendation and online advertising. The performance of these algorithms depends on how they explore different arms, and exploration strategies range from variance-independent (e.g., UCB1) to variance-aware (e.g., UCB-V). In practice the reward variance of each arm is rarely known and varies widely across arms, and the reward support is often underspecified. In these cases no single rule is uniformly best: variance-independent methods are robust but loose when variances are small, while variance-aware methods are tight only when their variance estimates and the assumed support bound are reliable. Such heterogeneous, unknown variances arise in many settings, for instance when multiple objectives are scalarized into a single reward. We propose UCB-min, a per-arm adaptive meta-algorithm that selects, for each arm, the tighter of a variance-independent and a variance-aware exploration bonus, without prior knowledge of the variance regime and without reward normalization. We prove that, with UCB-V as variance-aware base, its regret is bounded by the sum of the two base bounds at the standard exploration constant, and by their per-arm minimum, up to a constant, for a larger one. We validate it on synthetic data, an educational tutoring task, and two group-recommendation benchmarks (MovieLens, Steam), showing that UCB-min consistently tracks the best base algorithm across diverse variance regimes and datasets.

title: An Algebraic Foundation of Rate-Product Style Quantity Calculus
abstract: Using the new notion of a scalable (right) monoid-heap, the quantity calculus in [1] is generalized to include quantities that may not be possible to multiply as well as both (weak) rates and products of quantities. Several examples are given of applications in metrology and physics

title: Can Frontier Auto Researchers Reconstruct Human Research Decisions in AI?
abstract: Scientific research has long been driven by substantial human effort, from reviewing prior work and identifying research gaps to designing specific solutions. Recent advances in harness-based agent systems have given rise to increasingly capable Auto Researchers, which can autonomously carry out these tasks and, increasingly, entire end-to-end research workflows. Yet despite their rapidly growing capabilities, how closely the research decisions and outputs produced by auto researchers align with those of human experts remains underexplored. We investigate this gap through the lens of research reconstruction and study: Given comparable research context, how similar are the research decisions and outputs produced by Auto Researchers to those of human researchers in AI research? To answer this question, we introduce AutoResearcher-Human Research Similarity (AutoHRS), a stage-wise evaluation framework for assessing how faithfully auto researchers reconstruct human research artifacts across different stages of the scientific workflow. Using 152 ICLR oral papers as our corpus, we generate 456 research trajectories spanning different stages of the research process. Applying AutoHRS to these trajectories, we find that current Auto Researchers frequently fail to recover key research decisions and their resulting artifacts across multiple stages of the research process.

title: Sensitivity of diffusion MRI to white matter pathology: a comparison between ROI-based effect size and TBSS analysis under different diffusion protocols, field strengths and post-processing strategies
abstract: We investigated how much more advanced diffusion MRI acquisitions and more complex processing increase sensitivity to group-wise white matter (WM) differences due to pathology, and how the choice of statistical analysis affects this sensitivity. Data were acquired with DTI and DKI protocols at 3T and 7T in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), athletes with persistent post-concussive symptoms (PPCS), and healthy controls (HC). Seven processing pipelines combining denoising, Gibbs removal, eddy current and motion correction, and Gaussian smoothing were applied. Sensitivity was assessed with two methods: a region-of-interest-based (ROI-based) effect size analysis over 72 WM tracts segmented by TractSeg, quantified by Cohen's d, and tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS), quantified by the fraction of significant voxels in the WM skeleton. The ROI-based analysis found significant group differences for both SLE versus HC and PPCS versus HC, whereas TBSS found differences only for SLE versus HC. Both analyses agreed that the diffusion protocol affected sensitivity more than field strength or post-processing. Regardless of pipeline, DTI-derived fractional anisotropy (FA) yielded a 0.26 higher effect size and 25% more significantly different voxels between SLE and HC than DKI-derived FA, and 3T yielded a 0.2 higher effect size and 21% more significant voxels than 7T. Smoothing reduced sensitivity in both analyses (by up to 12% in TBSS for SLE versus HC). Overall, TBSS appears less suited to localized pathology such as neurotrauma, whereas the ROI-based analysis showed no bias with respect to the nature of the pathology. Advanced protocols such as 3T-DKI and 7T-DTI may need further optimization before surpassing conventional 3T-DTI in sensitivity to WM pathology in SLE.

title: Mechanisms of Zener diode and ohmic contact resulting from a heavily doped p-n junction: A novel explanation in terms of impurity-photovoltaic-effect resulting from infrared self-emission at room-temperature
abstract: In textbooks, a quantum-mechanical tunneling mechanism based on electron-wavefunction is used to explain Zener diode as well as ohmic contact resulting from a heavily doped p-n junction. In this study, an attempt in particle description is made to explain these devices. Any object at room-temperature emits infrared (IR) photons. The process of heavy doping can cause many defects. The self-absorption of the IR emission could be achieved through sub-band-gap excitations due to defects, creating carriers. In a heavily doped p-n junction device, some of the IR-generated carriers diffuse into the junction which has a built-in field. The built-in field sweeps out the carriers, creating IR photocurrent. The reverse leakage current of the p-n junction is regarded as the IR photocurrent according to a precedent where impurity-photovoltaic-effect is used to explain circuit devices (arXiv:2510.18226). Heavy doping results in not only a great many IR-generated carriers but also an avalanche effect at low voltage, producing Zener breakdown. Additionally, the impurity-photovoltaic-effect can make a reasonable contribution to explaining the temperature dependence of Zener breakdown. If the doping is very heavy, the heavily doped p-n junction can be altered to create an ohmic contact, which can also be explained in terms of impurity-photovoltaic-effect. Not only quantum mechanics, but also this photovoltaic mechanism in particle description can explain the above devices. Considering the wave-particle duality, the combination of quantum-mechanical and photovoltaic mechanisms is suggested to explain these devices. Each mechanism plays a big or small role in the explanation.

title: Lattice dynamical properties and interatomic force constants of transition metal oxide perovskite superlattices
abstract: In this study, we investigate the construction of efficient model potentials for perovskite heterostructures by transferring relevant dynamic quantities from bulk systems and short-period superlattices. Through first-principles calculations, we provide a comprehensive analysis and comparison of the dynamical properties of different perovskite-based superlattice structures, including (PbTiO3 )n /(SrTiO3 )m superlattices, (ATiO3 )n /(AO) 2 superlattices, and An+1 Tin O 3n+1 Ruddlesden-Popper phases, where A can be Sr, Ba, or Pb. We demonstrate that as the thickness of these structures increases, the dynamical properties of the perovskite blocks converge rapidly towards their bulk counterparts. We discuss this convergence in terms of phonon density of states in reciprocal space and inter-atomic force constants in real space. Our findings suggest a straightforward strategy for developing transferable model potentials that accurately capture the dynamics of layered oxide compounds with progressively thicker layers.

title: N-Layer quasi-geostrophic modons in a vertically sheared flow
abstract: Modons, or dipolar vortices, are a form of propagating vortex solution consisting of two counterrotating regions of fluid and moving together under self-advection. They are common features of the upper ocean that can remain stable over long times, thereby transporting fluid over large distances. Here, we present a semi-analytical method for finding modon solutions in a vertically-sheared background flow using the multi-layer quasi-geostrophic framework. This method works for arbitrarily many fluid layers and builds on our previous studies of multi-layer modon solutions. We present three example of modons in a background flow, highlighting the effect of varying relative potential velocity between layers and the impact of depth-dependent potential vorticity gradients arising from surface deformation and velocity shear.

title: Frontier AI Safety and Governance 2026: Risk Understanding and Coordinated Governance
abstract: Frontier AI Safety and Governance 2026: Risk Understanding and Coordinated Governance is a key outcome of the AI Safety and Governance Program of World Internet Conference Specialized Committee on AI in 2026. Drawing on the latest developments in frontier AI capabilities and applications, the report systematically examines the evolving risk landscape, analyzing key risk areas, their severity and response priorities. Building on a review of existing global governance practices and an assessment of frontier AI governance readiness, it identifies key governance gaps and weaknesses and proposes directions and practical mechanisms for coordinated responses. The report provides a reference for government departments, international organizations, businesses, research institutions and other stakeholders. It aims to strengthen the international community's understanding of and consensus on frontier AI risks, enhance preparedness and collective response capacity, and advance the safe, reliable and responsible development of frontier AI to better serve the common well-being of humanity.

title: To SIMD or Not to SIMD: Comparing RVV vs. CGRA SoCs for Non-Linear Functions in AI
abstract: Non-linear functions are an important class of operations in modern large language models. However, chip vendors building for AI have so far relied on traditional vector or scalar processing units for non-linear functions. The performance of these units has not kept pace with matrix multiplication units (MMUs), which can be found in both high-performance and edge-computing devices from almost every vendor. Reconfigurable units such as FPGAs and CGRAs have been proposed in the literature, but have not been systematically compared with traditional units backed by MMUs. In this paper, we build two SoCs: one using an RVV vector processor and the other using a latency-insensitive (\emph{elastic}) CGRA, both coupled with an MMU and driven by a single-core CPU. We then propose mappings for common feed-forward networks on our SoCs and find that the CGRA reaches a maximum speedup in clock cycles of 7.12x over RVV on the activation stage of simple point-wise non-linear functions like SiLU, whereas the RVV reaches a maximum speedup of \textbf{9.8x} over the CGRA on complex non-linear functions such as $\mathrm{softmax}$. Over the enclosing feed-forward block the corresponding maxima are 3.16x and 4.24x.

title: Patching Up Circuit Learning via Parameter Sharing
abstract: Probabilistic circuits (PCs) have emerged as generative models guaranteeing tractable probabilistic inference. However, tractability comes at the price of larger model sizes than in other generative models. As such, to scale PCs to high-dimensional data such as images, previous work has devised several parameter sharing techniques as well as fast evaluation protocols that consider learning PCs on independent image patches. In this work, we revisit this practice to highlight a surprising learnability issue: models that assume independence counterintuitively can yield better likelihoods than models that do not. To break this apparent bottleneck and to scale PCs further, we introduce a recursive parameter sharing construction (RePA) that fosters efficiency without assuming independence. We show empirically that RePA can greatly reduce time and memory consumption while yielding competitive likelihoods. Inspired by these results, we further generalize the approach to data modalities that do not inherently exhibit patch-structure (NoPA), such as tabular data, showing similar efficiency improvements, with marginal changes in likelihoods and sample quality on seven tabular datasets. Code available at https://github.com/april-tools/RePA.

title: Occupancy Modelling of Biased Landslide Inventories: When Does Separating Occurrence from Recording Improve on Neutralisation?
abstract: Landslide susceptibility models are trained on inventories that record where landslides were seen, not where they occurred. The established remedy fits bias-describing variables and neutralises them when mapping. We adapt occupancy-detection modelling from ecology, treating several inventories as imperfect observers of one event and separating occurrence from recording, and ask when this improves on neutralisation. We use near-complete inventories of the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi, 2015 Gorkha and 2010 Haiti earthquakes with simulated reporting bias, and three real Gorkha inventories. Compared with standard practice, the occupancy model reduces road bias in 24 of 25 paired draws and raises AUC by 0.08-0.14 on Gorkha and 0.03 on Haiti, but only 0.01-0.02 on Iburi. Its median predicted-to-true landslide rate is 0.99 (range 0.44-1.89), against 0.24-0.30 for the baselines. Rescaling the baselines with the same anchor area corrects their median but leaves larger errors (range 0.20-4.34). Cell-level probabilities remain too extreme (calibration slope 0.59). Compared with the best neutralised model, AUC is higher on Iburi (by 0.03-0.07) and lower on Gorkha and Haiti (by 0.01-0.05). Transplant experiments tie the Iburi advantage to the structure of its true landslide pattern, not to its terrain or road network. In all eight settings with a low interaction gap, computable from biased records, neutralisation was at least as accurate, including a prespecified test on Haiti; a high gap did not guarantee an advantage. The real Gorkha inventories are slope-biased, not road-biased, and there the model brings no meaningful gain. Report-based catalogues remain the main untested case.

title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
abstract: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $ζ(s)$ and its derivative $ζ'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $ζ'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $ζ$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

title: KPG193-ext: A Synthetic Korean Power Grid Test System for Stability Analysis
abstract: Growing shares of inverter-based generation and constrained transmission expansion increase the need to assess stability across operating conditions. Production-cost models provide chronological commitment and dispatch, but stability analysis requires corresponding electrical detail and device dynamics. This paper introduces KPG193-ext, an extension of the synthetic Korean power-grid test system KPG193 that links chronological operating points with detailed electrical and dynamic models. The extension adds synchronous-machine, controller and renewable-converter models, together with explicit voltage levels, generation terminals, inter-voltage and step-up transformers, and reactive compensation. The resulting 731-bus network retains the original 193 regional locations. Daily unit commitment followed by hourly AC optimal power flow establishes 8,760 operating points for 2025, each distributed as paired steady-state and dynamic-model files. Selected-hour studies examine generation-loss frequency response, steady-state flow-voltage characteristics, and rotor-angle response with special protection system actions. The results reveal differences in delivered frequency support, internal voltage stress along regional transfer paths, and the angle-frequency tradeoff of corrective generator tripping. The database provides a common basis for examining the stability implications of commitment, dispatch and corrective action across daily and seasonal operating conditions.

title: Exploring public-private data sharing practices through the lens of Open Data Ecosystems: A multiple case study on municipal and regional freight logistics
abstract: Background: Freight transport is expected to increase, contributing to air pollution. There is, therefore, a critical need for increased efficiency that can reduce emissions. Data sharing is one approach, where actors within Open Data Ecosystems (ODE) collaborate and share data among stakeholders to plan and operate more efficient and sustainable freight transport. Aim: In this study, we explore how public-private data sharing practices in municipal and regional last-mile freight logistics in Sweden may improve efficiency. Method: Following a prolonged participation process, we conducted a multiple-case study involving three different cases, built upon initial meetings, semi-structured interviews, supported by a thematic analysis, and validated through a follow-up workshop. Results: The findings show that data sharing in public-private freight logistics (ODE-PPF) is shaped by interrelated socio-technical aspects, including platform design, roles of actors, handling of sensitive data, data quality, and procurement processes. We synthesize our findings in an actor model and a conceptual model, highlighting how these aspects contribute to the functioning of ODE-PPF, and derive seven proposition sketches as a foundation for future research. Conclusion: Data sharing is a central mechanism enabling integration and value creation in last-mile logistics. It depends on the interaction between technical and organizational aspects. Public actors can undertake a key role as a neutral keystone actor by orchestrating the ecosystem and facilitating data sharing through governance practices such as procurement.

title: Deriving Tsallis Entropy from First Principles
abstract: The kinetic approach for q-distribution is extended through a "bottom-up" procedure to the corresponding entropic formula. In this way, the validity of Tsallis' formula, S_q(W) = k_B ln_q(W), is established from first principles. The resulting q-entropy is additive and the zeroth law of thermodynamics is automatically satisfied because the conventional identification beta = 1/(k_B T) remains valid. Entropy, energy, and all relevant quantities for both discrete and continuous cases are evaluated using standard (linear) averages. The "bottom-up" and "top-down" approaches yield the same q-distribution for velocities. The standard results are naturally recovered in the limit q -> 1.

title: When Handshakes Go Dark: An Adaptive Semantic-Sequential Fusion Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification
abstract: Encrypted traffic classification is essential for network security monitoring and traffic management. Self-supervised pre-training can learn reusable representations from large-scale unlabeled traffic, but TLS 1.3, QUIC, and privacy mechanisms such as Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) increasingly conceal application, handshake, and service-identifying information. Observable upper-layer bytes are therefore dominated by ciphertext, weakening the link between raw-byte patterns and application semantics and limiting model generalization. Moreover, the availability and discriminative value of observable information vary across protocols, protection profiles, and tasks, complicating classification across diverse scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose FLARE, a Field-aware Learning and Adaptive Representation Fusion framework for encrypted traffic classification. FLARE pre-trains a BERT-based packet encoder through Masked Field Prediction, which reconstructs masked tokens from field-structured context. During downstream fine-tuning, the parameters of the pre-trained packet encoder remain frozen, and a packet-level gated module adaptively combines protocol-semantic representations with directional packet-length representations. A flow-level encoder then models inter-packet dependencies for classification. We evaluate FLARE on eight datasets spanning diverse encrypted-traffic tasks, including CipherSpectrum and VisQUIC for strongly encrypted scenarios. FLARE achieves superior performance over baselines across the eight datasets, exceeding the strongest pre-trained baseline by 10.92 percentage points on QUIC website fingerprinting. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of field-aware pre-training and adaptive semantic-sequential fusion under constrained observability.

title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos
abstract: Generalizable deepfake video detection remains challenging because forgery artifacts vary substantially across manipulation types and often combine diverse spatial and temporal inconsistencies. Existing parameter-efficient adaptation methods typically rely on a single shared representation, rendering them prone to manipulation-specific bias and limiting transfer to unseen forgeries. To address this challenge, we propose Mixture Of Spatio-Temporal Experts (MoSTE), an adaptation framework that enables conditional specialization of forensic representations. Instead of forcing one adapter to model all forgery patterns, MoSTE decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts through an unsupervised token-level routing mechanism. This allows experts to naturally specialize in complementary forgery cues without requiring explicit manipulation labels or multi-stage training, while effectively transferring representations from CLIP to the video domain. Extensive experiments across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that MoSTE sets a new state of the art in average generalization while preserving strong performance across diverse manipulation families. Additional analysis of expert routing and attention behavior reveals the emergence of expert diversity, suggesting that MoSTE learns complementary spatio-temporal forensic features. Code is available at https://github.com/charbelyah/MoSTE

title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
abstract: We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$. The achieved color range therefore approaches the tree uniqueness threshold and improves over the previously best achievable number of colors $q > 1.763 d$ due to Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic, and Vigoda [SODA 2018]. Moreover, our mixing-time bound is $O(n^{2+o_d(1)})$, and hence almost quadratic as $d\rightarrow\infty$. Our proof is based on establishing a spectral gap for block dynamics resulting from a suitable decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ into blocks and singleton vertices, ensuring that every high-degree vertex is encapsulated within a block. Our main technical contribution is a novel way of establishing rapid mixing of block dynamics via an integrated Bochner-Bakry-Émery approach, which we expect to have applications beyond sampling colorings. We further devise a new block decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ that strengthens and simplifies similar constructions used in previous work. Finally, to compare block and Glauber dynamics, we establish a novel recursive separator decomposition of tree-like blocks, together with a coupling argument that avoids the need for nearly uniform color marginals at vertices adjacent to hubs. This comparison argument might be of independent interest.

title: LongSCOP: Semantically Consistent Long Video Outpainting
abstract: Video out-painting is an important problem, yet existing research focuses primarily on short clips, leaving long video out-painting largely underexplored. Extending video out-painting to long videos poses substantial challenges. A natural solution is iterative out-painting, i.e., generating videos chunk by chunk, but this introduces two major issues: generation instability or even failure caused by inter-chunk inconsistencies and error accumulation, and semantic drift over long temporal horizons. In this paper, we propose LongSCOP, short for Semantically Consistent long Video Out-Painting. First, we introduce a training recipe with three components for smooth and stable long-horizon generation: self-forcing training, latent calibration, and future references. Beyond generation stability, we recognize that the rich temporal context of long videos provides valuable references for maintaining semantic consistency. We therefore develop a VLM-based agent that automatically selects the most informative reference frames from the entire video to maintain consistent subjects, scenes, and backgrounds throughout long-horizon generation. We also construct a high-quality training dataset of 62K video clips. To facilitate research on this underexplored problem, we introduce LVO-Bench, a benchmark curated by human experts to assess long-horizon stability and semantic consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in both generation stability and semantic coherence.

title: Pricing Symbolic Rules by What GNNs Leave Unlearned
abstract: Symbolic knowledge (motif counts, ring counts, label constraints) is routinely added to graph neural networks (GNNs) and justified by their limited expressivity. We replace this yardstick with an exact one. The largest log-loss reduction a rule $S$ can give a model family is $I(Y;S\midσ)$ given what the family computes; every realised gain splits exactly into this term plus repaid neural debt; and for a trained network with representation $T$ the value is $I(Y;S\mid T)$, the label information training failed to extract. Rule design thus becomes rule discovery: we score candidates on the network's out-of-fold residual against calibrated permutation nulls with family-wise error control. On ZINC, discovery recovers the hidden ring term $\max(0,\ell_{\max}-6)$ of the target in three independent runs ($p_{\mathrm{adj}}=0.001$) and beats expert cycle counts; frozen and applied to five unseen datasets it is never significantly worse than the plain network or the expert rule, and on BBBP it significantly beats both.

title: Total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers
abstract: Sampling from high-dimensional, multimodal target distributions plays a fundamental role in scientific computing, statistics and machine learning. Recently, the Schrödinger-Föllmer sampler (SFS) has been proposed by Huang et al. (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 2025) as an efficient sampling algorithm that transports the degenerate distribution at $t=0$ to the target distribution at $t=1$, without relying on long-time ergodicity. In this paper, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds for SFS in the total variation distance by deriving regularization estimates for the associated Kolmogorov equation via the Bismut-Elworthy-Li formula. When the drift can be computed exactly, a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|)$ was obtained under certain smoothness conditions on the drift with a uniform time step-size $h>0$. When the drift is approximated by Monte Carlo methods, we obtain a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|+ 1/M)$, where $M$ is the number of samples used in the Monte Carlo approximation. This yields a sharper dependence on $M$ than the existing bound $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{M})$ in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance in the aforementioned paper, by turning the total variation error to the weak error analysis in the setting of non-smooth test functions. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the convergence rate with respect to the time step-size $h$ and the Monte Carlo sample size $M$ and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Revisiting the Einstein Cross with X-shooter spectra: New estimates of accretion disk parameters and broad emission line profiles from microlensing
abstract: We present a spectroscopic study of the lensed quasar Q2237+0305, the Einstein Cross, assessing the best wavelength coverage to date with the X-shooter instrument (from $3000$ to $20000$ $\mathring{A}$), and thus improving the available spectroscopic data for this system. Using as a reference the characteristic emission lines for each quasar macro-image, we estimate the chromatic microlensing effect between pairs of images and calculate the extinction curve, confirming no significant differences between spectra $C$ and $A$ caused by extinction in the lens galaxy. In addition, we model the accretion disk characterized by a temperature profile with logarithmic slope $1/p$ and size $r_{s}$, assuming a thin-disk model with a power-law function of the form $r_{s}$ $\propto$ $λ^{p}$. To do this, we calculated a set of three chromatic microlensing measurements compiling previous estimates from the literature to test the wavelength dependence. This temperature profile was also compared to the canonical thin-disk model with $p=4/3$. Finally, we estimated the likelihood between the disk model and the observed data collected from multiple epochs through mock microlensing magnification maps and determined the probability density functions of each parameter from a Bayesian analysis. As a result, our estimated values for the accretion disk size and its exponential index are $r_{s}=4.9^{+2.3}_{-2.6}$ $\sqrt{M/0.3M_{\odot}}$ (lt-day) and $p=0.77^{+0.47}_{-0.28}$, respectively, reinforcing a departure from the standard accretion disk model ($ T \propto r_s^{-3/4}$).

title: Unique continuation property for $\bar\partial$ with $L^{2n}$ potentials
abstract: We establish the sharp unique continuation property for the Cauchy--Riemann operator $\bar{\partial}$ in higher dimensions. Let $0\inΩ\subset \C^n$ be a domain. Suppose $u \in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(Ω; \C^N)$ satisfies the differential inequality \[ |\bar{\partial} u| \leq V |u| \quad \text{a.e.~on } Ω \] with $V \in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2n}(Ω)$. If $u$ is $L^2$ flat at the origin, then $u \equiv 0$ on $Ω$.

title: $λ_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
abstract: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $λ_gψ^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.

title: A proof of the Theta conjecture
abstract: We prove the touching refinement of the Theta conjecture of Interdonato and Iraci, giving a formula for $Θ_{e_\ell}Θ_{e_k}\nabla E_{d,j}$ as a weighted sum over parking functions with decorated rises and valleys and touch number $j$. Summing over $j$ gives the Theta conjecture. As corollaries, we prove the valley Delta conjecture of Haglund, Remmel, and Wilson and its generalized version proposed by Qiu and Wilson. Our proof compares algebraic and combinatorial recurrences using an extension of the plethystic substitution $X\mapsto(q-1)X$ to quasisymmetric functions. The algebraic recurrence follows from an endomorphism constructed by D'Adderio, Interdonato, Iraci and Pagaria on the Dyck path algebra of Carlsson and Mellit. The combinatorial recurrence is obtained by introducing signed labels and deleting the main diagonal. The two recurrences have the same initial conditions, which identifies the corresponding generating functions.

title: V3DSAM: Semantic-Geometric Loop Verification and Geometry-Anchored Persistent Instance Mapping for Feed-Forward Dense SLAM
abstract: To address unreliable cross-view association in long-sequence feed-forward dense SLAM, this letter presents V3DSAM, an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that establishes physical correspondences at both the scene and object levels. The system combines feed-forward geometric estimates from VGGT-SLAM 2.0 with open-vocabulary semantic observations from SAM3. We introduce semantic-geometric dual-scale loop verification, which identifies false loop closures using pixel-level bidirectional reprojection and object-level 3D spatial correspondences, without accessing backbone-internal features. We further propose geometry-anchored persistent instance mapping, which defines physical instances through class-constrained 3D connectivity in an optimized global coordinate system and assigns global IDs without inter-frame identity propagation. The proposed verifier rejects all four false loop candidates in our TUM RGB-D evaluation, while long-sequence ScanNet experiments show improved instance identity consistency. Thus, V3DSAM reduces dependence on internal backbone features and temporal ID propagation for robust long-term cross-view association.

title: Exact local spectral thresholds for loose and tight Hamilton cycles in $3$-graphs
abstract: For an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$, let $σ(H)$ denote the minimum adjacency spectral radius of its vertex links. We determine the exact thresholds for $σ(H)$ that force loose and tight Hamilton cycles for all sufficiently large admissible orders, and give constructions showing that each bound is best possible. The loose threshold is $(1+\sqrt{13})n/8+O(1)$, with two forms according to $n$ modulo four. The tight threshold is $2n/3+O(1)$, with four forms determined by $n$ modulo three and, when $3\mid n$, modulo nine. The resulting spectral conditions and the corresponding minimum vertex degree conditions do not imply one another. For loose cycles, we combine fractional packing stability and absorption with exact completion near a space barrier. For tight cycles, spectral stability and rooted sampling reduce the problem to three extremal configurations. We resolve these configurations by controlling the spectral loss caused by missing triples and constructing short paths that extend to Hamilton cycles, including in the presence of exceptional vertices.

title: Real Topology on Symmetry-Invariant Loops Enforces Superconducting Pairing Zeros
abstract: Normal-state topology can obstruct superconducting pairing and give rise to gapless nodes in the quasiparticle spectrum. However, existing pairing-obstruction mechanisms largely rely on Fermi-surface topology or global Bloch-band topology. Here, we establish a new and general mechanism: one-dimensional (1D) real topology, defined on antiunitary-symmetry-invariant loops, enforces pairing zeros without requiring Fermi-surface or global Bloch-band topology. We derive sufficient conditions and lower bounds for pairing zeros across diverse pairing channels, for both zero and finite Cooper-pair momenta. The theorems apply to systems of arbitrary spatial dimensions without requiring the pairing bands to be globally isolated. We further show that such topologically enforced pairing zeros, if isolated, necessarily carry odd vorticity and can give rise to Bogoliubov-de Gennes nodes and zero-energy boundary modes, as demonstrated in a minimal two-orbital model. Our results reshape the understanding of how normal-state topology can obstruct the superconducting order, highlight the significant role of 1D real topology beyond single-particle band phenomena, and provide a general framework for identifying candidate materials hosting nodal superconductivity.

title: A capillary logarithmic Gauss curvature flow and the capillary Minkowski problem
abstract: We study a logarithmic Gauss curvature flow of strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. For an acute contact angle and an arbitrary positive smooth prescribed function, we prove that a suitable initial dilation yields a global solution which converges smoothly after a horizontal translation with a uniquely determined constant velocity. As an application, we provide a logarithmic flow proof of the capillary Minkowski problem, previously established by Mei-Wang-Weng [Adv. Math. 469, 110230 (2025)].

title: The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane
abstract: We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $λ$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.

title: Grid Design for Near-Field Channel Estimation with Uniform Linear Arrays
abstract: This paper develops deterministic grids for line-of-sight near-field channel estimation with uniform linear arrays (ULAs) and hybrid receivers. A normalized channel approximation squared error (NCASE) criterion leads to geometric covering problems under a constant-amplitude parabolic model and an elliptical approximation of the correlation regions. For a horizontal ULA, transformation and scaling yield a disk-covering problem, addressed by adapting a hexagonal lattice to the mapped ground-plane region. For a vertical ULA, a reciprocal-distance interval cover is solved optimally by a farthest-reaching greedy procedure. Numerical evaluation with exact spherical-wave channels yields empirical maximum approximation errors close to the target and improved P-SOMP estimation relative to the tested polar-domain grids of comparable size.

title: Causal discovery from Bayesian symbolic regression
abstract: Causal discovery from observational data is central to scientific reasoning, yet established constraint-based and score-based methods often recover only a Markov equivalence class and provide no signal in bivariate or strongly autocorrelated regimes typical in some areas of science. Here, we recast causal discovery as a Bayesian symbolic regression problem. Given a set of candidate parents for each target variable, the Bayesian symbolic regression samples closed-form expressions from a posterior over symbolic models. The fraction of sampled expressions in which each candidate variable appears defines a posterior inclusion probability that we use as the causal score. This replaces pointwise model selection by an ensemble of plausible mechanisms. We evaluate the method on coupled nonlinear bivariate dynamics, on the CauseMe benchmark suite spanning linear, chaotic, nonlinear, higher-dimensional and high-noise settings, and on a four-variable biogeoscience structural causal model under Gaussian, heavy-tailed and mixed-noise regimes. Our approach is competitive with, and often outperforms, specialized causal discovery algorithms. Additionally, the method returns closed-form mechanisms leading to explicit causality and interpretability.

title: Fiscal Commitment and the Additionality of Philanthropy: Heterogeneous Donor Purposes in a Shared Public Budget
abstract: Philanthropic donors often value different public services, while a budget authority allocates public spending across a shared portfolio. Policy frameworks frequently seek to ensure that private finance supplements rather than displaces public funding. We distinguish baseline additionality, which preserves pre-gift public funding, from portfolio preservation, which preserves a service's provision after all gifts are pooled under discretionary budgeting. A larger gift to one service raises the discretionary provision of every service and reduces the protection slack available to the others. This cross-donor fiscal externality yields an exact feasibility result: if a service's maximum permissible floor lies below its discretionary post-gift provision, every effective protection reform reduces that service relative to the portfolio reference, including full protection of its own appropriation. Conversely, a reform that expands at least one donor-backed service while preserving all others exists exactly when every maximum floor reaches the reference. The paper characterizes the complete preservation set and its welfare-maximizing element. Under logarithmic preferences, donation shares determine protectability, while heterogeneous donor valuations determine welfare incidence. Baseline additionality may therefore hold while a service loses fiscal benefits generated by other gifts.

title: Revealing laser-induced modification of weak ferromagnetism through a spin-reorientation phase transition in iron borate Fe$_3$BO$_6$
abstract: In the iron oxide Fe$_3$BO$_6$ weak ferromagnetism stems from competing contributions from two-site Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions (DMI) and from on-site anisotropies at the two $4c$ and $8d$ types of nonequivalent Fe$^{3+}$ sites. As a result, spin reorientation (SR) transition $Γ_2$ $\rightarrow$ $Γ_4$ in Fe$_3$BO$_6$ uniquely comprises 90$^\circ$ spin switching and a 35% change of weak ferromagnetic moment. We explore ultrafast kinetics of such a transition as a proxy for weak ferromagnetism contributions modified by femtosecond laser pulses. Using magneto-optical pump-probe technique we reveal that the SR transition is triggered by an abrupt decrease of the weak ferromagnetic moment in the $Γ_2$ phase, and relate it to the laser-induced modification of the DMI and anisotropy contributions to the spin canting. By tuning the pump pulse phonon energy between different optical absorption ranges, we show that laser-driven impact on spin canting possesses a nonthermal character and is achieved through the charge-transfer transitions $2p\rightarrow3d$ within Fe$^{3+}$O$^{2-}_6$ octahedra rather than by localized $3d\rightarrow3d$ transitions at Fe$^{3+}$. The decreased weak ferromagnetic moment controls the threshold and the latency of the SR transition, as well as a final state. The latter is achieved via the precessional switching to the $Γ_4$ phase activated by the laser-induced heating. Final state is found to be a coexistence of $Γ_4$ and $Γ_2$ phase with modified spin canting persisting even at hundreds of picoseconds.

title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
abstract: We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $ϕ$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $ϕ$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses. Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $ϕ$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Borůvka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.

title: VEM-bubble discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for a fluid induced seismicity model with rate-and-state friction
abstract: This work addresses the discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for an induced seismicity model accounting for fault reactivation and slip driven by subsurface fluid injection. The model couples single-phase Darcy flow in both the porous matrix and the fault network with a quasi-static poroelastic mechanical response in the bulk and fault slip governed by a rate-and-state friction law with radiation damping stabilisation leading to a quas-dynamic formulation. The contact mechanics problem is discretised using the Virtual Element Method with bubble stabilisation of the facewise constant Lagrange multiplier. It is combined with a Hybrid Finite Volume scheme for the mixed-dimensional Darcy flow model. The time discretisation is implicit and the nonlinear system is solved at each time step using an iterative coupling algorithm which iterates between the Darcy flow, the frictional contact-mechanics, and the state differential equation. The contraction of this iterative coupling algorithm is established with a smallness assumption on the time step independent on the mesh size. This proves convergence of the fixed-point as well as well-posedness of the system. The frictional contact-mechanical model is solved using a semi-smooth Newton algorithm based on a local nonlinear inversion of the friction rate-and-state law and a block Gauss--Seidel preconditioner exploiting the structure of the VEM-bubble-$\mathbb{P}^0$ mixed discretisation.

title: An almost sharp $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$-$L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
abstract: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}} f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} whenever \begin{equation*} \mathcal{U}:= \min{\left\{ \min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}>1, \end{equation*} and we necessarily have $\mathcal{U}\geq 1$.

title: Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target
abstract: Speculative decoders raise throughput by banking more target tokens per forward pass, and Medusa, EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark all do it the same way: more candidates that survive verification. All of them draft in the target's own vocabulary, so one node of the candidate tree is one target token, and the tokenizer makes that unit look like a constant. It is not. BPE's pretokenizer splits on whitespace before merges are learned, so no multi-word string can ever become a single token: in Qwen3-4B, "United States of America" is four tokens and no adjacent pair of them exists as one entry, so a phrase is out of reach of any method drafting in the target's vocabulary. We change the unit. A small MLP head reads the frozen target's hidden state and predicts a one- to three-word phrase as one entry in a separate draft vocabulary; greedy longest-match expansion maps it back into the target's own tokens, and N candidates are verified in one forward pass behind a prefix-tree mask, so the change is orthogonal to tree depth and width. The target and its tokenizer stay frozen and a candidate is accepted only while it matches the target's own argmax, so the served output is identical to greedy decoding up to floating-point tie-breaking. On one A5000 at batch 1, against HuggingFace generate(), a 21.94M head (0.545% of Qwen3-4B) reaches 2.391x on GSM8K, 2.444x on MATH-500 and 1.544x on MT-Bench. Because the head's output layer is one row of 257 parameters per entry, the draft vocabulary size is the parameter budget: an 8,000-entry head is 3.434M parameters, 0.0854% of the target and 64x smaller than EAGLE-3's drafter, and keeps 92.3% of the larger head's GSM8K tokens per pass. With EAGLE-3 run on same prompts and baseline, our 21.94M head is ahead of tree-16 on both maths sets and behind tree-60 on every set.

title: Giant Diffusion at Flocking Transitions
abstract: We simulate dynamics in two-dimensional aligning active-matter models exhibiting order-disorder transitions in the velocity field. Analysis reveals that the single-particle diffusivity, $D_s$, exhibits strong enhancements at criticality which we quantify via a finite-size scaling method. This dynamical behavior at nonequilibrium flocking transitions is fundamentally different from that at the criticality of equilibrium systems, where diffusivities either vanish or remain non-critical. Furthermore, $D_s$ exhibits pronounced finite-size effects throughout the ordered phase, which also are absent in equilibrium settings. We interpret these counterintuitive transport anomalies within the framework of a flocking theory. Our results suggest that enhanced diffusion generates effective long-range interactions. This relaxes the constraints of the Mermin-Wagner theorem that otherwise prevents order-disorder transitions in two dimensions for systems possessing continuous symmetry. These results are of much experimental relevance and have important implications in formulating quantitative theories for nonequilibrium transports.

title: Prediction with Foundation Models under Deployment Budgets
abstract: Foundation models can supply predictions for a downstream task that draw on knowledge from extensive pretraining, but they differ in task-specific accuracy and query cost. We develop a framework that improves prediction for the task under a budget on the average query cost per input, using training data to learn which models to query and how to combine their outputs with features available without querying. The first method queries the same models for every input; the second lets them vary across inputs and uses Q-learning to decide which model to query next and when to stop. For the first method, we show that several individually inaccurate outputs can jointly outperform the best single one. It attains the minimax rate when the regression function depends on the outputs only through models within the budget. Otherwise, any method within the budget can be forced to a slower rate, which the first method attains. For the second method, we show when varying the queried models across inputs strictly improves on querying the same models for every input, and bound its prediction risk and average cost in finite samples. In simulations and a multimodal laptop price application, both methods outperform existing methods.

title: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
abstract: We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant.
