Current agents remain far from saturating wet-lab outcome prediction, with substantial performance disparities across models: on the public benchmark, configurations separate into two distinct tiers, with task-adjusted Spearman correlations ranging from 0.227 for the lowest-performing configuration to 0.478 for the best. Analysis of 1,155 scored public trajectories (227,103 tool calls) suggests that the bottleneck lies in scientific judgment rather than tool execution: agents rely on shared monotone priors, agreeing far more with one another than with experimental reality (0.52 vs. 0.33), and frequently compute trivial physical or chemical proxies that do not influence the final outcome.

title: A consistent formulation of stochastic inflation II: Reassessing its role in nonlinear cosmological perturbations
abstract: We question whether the conventional formulation of stochastic inflation can provide a quantitatively reliable description of cosmological perturbations. More fundamentally, we reassess the role and motivations of the stochastic approach to study cosmological perturbations, distinct from its well-founded motivation for resumming IR secular divergences. To provide a quantitative basis for this reassessment, we extend stochastic inflation beyond the linear regime by incorporating non-Markovian effects arising from infrared-ultraviolet interactions and terms quadratic in ultraviolet fluctuations, which generate non-white noise. We derive three-point correlation functions for a spectator scalar field in de Sitter space and a slow-roll inflaton including metric perturbations, demonstrating exact agreement with in-in quantum-field-theoretic predictions for superhorizon nonlinear evolution. Our results show that both non-Markovian effects and quadratic (higher order) noise terms are essential for quantitative accuracy, implying that the conventional stochastic-inflation framework is, at best, quantitatively justified only at linear order.

title: A Time-Frequency-Condition Multimodal Fusion Foundation Model for Universal Rotating-Machinery Fault Diagnosis under Multi-Element Heterogeneous Scenarios
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis models are typically developed for a single machine under a specific set of operating conditions, such that each new machine or condition requires retraining from scratch. This one-machine-one-model paradigm scales poorly. Although transfer learning and domain generalization can reduce the labeling burden, they primarily seek domain-invariant commonality, potentially discarding machine-specific characteristics that are critical for diagnosis. This paper proposes TFC-MMFD, a time-frequency-condition multimodal fusion foundation model for rotating-machinery fault diagnosis under multi-element heterogeneous scenarios. Statistical indicators, time-frequency images, vibration sequences, and textual machine and condition descriptions are tokenized into a unified language-like space, allowing inputs of different physical origin to be represented as a single sequence. A LLaMA backbone, together with cross-modal bidirectional attention and a Q-Former, then distills this sequence into fault-mode queries. Diagnosis is performed by matching these queries against natural-language fault-mode anchors rather than fixed class indices, while regression-adversarial condition disentanglement and condition-conditioned masked pre-training improve robustness to changing conditions. Across four progressive tasks on ten public bearing datasets spanning diverse bearing types, speeds, and loads, TFC-MMFD attains 99.40% accuracy and 99.16% macro-F1, maintains over 80% accuracy on most interpolated unseen conditions without adaptation, and improves from 20.26% to 95.63% accuracy on an unseen machine with only five labeled samples per class. It outperforms the strongest of eight domain-generalization baselines by 10.57 percentage points and compares favorably with a recent bearing foundation model while using less than half of its fine-tuning data.

title: Common-DAG Support from Targeted Covariance Changes under Confounding
abstract: Targeted covariance changes couple structural rows through a common directed acyclic graph. We study the graph support determined by these experiments when structural errors may be correlated. A positive-gap four-node family has a shortcut identified by common acyclicity. A response indegree of at most two additionally gives unique complete support and two compatible coefficient matrices. The same experiments admit a stable feedback model with the shortcut absent. The result extends to connected graphs with repeated branching and merging. Finite response-column alternatives yield exact bounded-parent compatibility decisions through Horn propagation and partial-target completion. Certified ancestry then supplies an observed-ancestor covariance restriction. Gaussian regression and Fieller inversion reduce inference to a scalar confidence set, and quadratic elimination retains the shared nuisance coefficients with finite-sample edge-error control. In 2048 Gaussian conditions, the scalar procedure reports 127/128 positive edges at gap 1/4 and 524288 observations per cell. Its decisions agree with the joint outer-polynomial reference on the same inputs in all 2022 qualified conditions, with zero reports in 512 null conditions. Exact 16-, 32- and 64-node evaluations verify support and target-coverage conclusions. A root-target characterization connects the identifying information to intervention design.

title: PhysXAI: A Theoretical Framework for Diagnosing Physical Hallucinations in Weather Foundation Models
abstract: Modern machine learning models for global weather forecasting achieve remarkable predictive accuracy, yet they frequently produce states that violate fundamental physical laws, including conservation of mass, hydrostatic balance, or spectral energy scaling. We term these outputs physical hallucinations and propose PhysXAI, a rigorous diagnostic framework that detects, localises, and attributes such inconsistencies. Unlike existing post-hoc metric suites, PhysXAI is a learnable system that explicitly decouples forecast error from physical plausibility. We formalise the problem through a novel joint condition on numerical and physical residuals, and introduce a multi-branch encoder that extracts representations from conservation, dynamical, spectral, cross-variable, and spatiotemporal residuals. A key innovation is a physics-consistency contrastive learning objective, which we theoretically show the latent representation to be approximately isometric to the physical residual space, ensuring that diagnostic decisions remain grounded in physically meaningful deviations. We further derive an adaptive multi-objective loss with gradient-based weighting to balance competing diagnostic objectives. The framework produces spatially resolved hallucination maps, violation-type classifications, and calibrated Bayesian uncertainty, enabling both detection and interpretable attribution of physical inconsistencies. We conduct a comprehensive comparative evaluation of PhysXAI across ERA5, WeatherBench 2, and MERRA-2, using forecasts from GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, and NeuralGCM, with Python-written code and a fully reproducible experimental protocol. Our theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation establish PhysXAI as a principled framework for diagnosing physical hallucinations and advancing trustworthy AI for weather forecasting.

title: Reduced-Complexity WMMSE Approach for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links
abstract: We propose a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links. To maximize the system capacity, we need to jointly design beamforming vectors at distributed access points (APs) and fronthaul quantization noise covariances. Such a task would be addressed using conventional WMMSE algorithms and their variants. However, existing WMMSE-based methods either assume ideal infinite-capacity fronthaul links or incur high computational complexity when jointly optimizing the network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression variables. To this end, the proposed method jointly optimizes beamforming and fronthaul compression by leveraging a sequential per-AP optimization strategy. Since each subproblem is efficiently solved via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, the overall computational complexity can be significantly reduced compared to the conventional WMMSE method. To further reduce hardware cost, we extend the R-WMMSE framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming systems, tackling the joint design of digital beamforming, fronthaul compression, and analog beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to that of the conventional WMMSE while reducing the runtime by over 99%.

title: Frank-Wolfe Theorems for Mixed Integer Quadratic Optimization
abstract: The Frank-Wolfe theorem states that a quadratic function bounded from below on a polyhedron attains its infimum. We study when this remains true in the presence of integer variables, for sets defined by quadratic inequalities. Our main result is a complete classification for sets defined by convex quadratic inequalities with rational coefficients and a rational affine hull, a condition that holds for all full- dimensional sets. One integer variable never destroys attainment: if every rational quadratic objective that is bounded from below attains its infimum over the set, even after adding rational linear constraints, the same holds with one integer variable. In dimension at most 2, integer variables never destroy attainment. In dimension at least 3 and with two or more integer variables, attainment holds for every such objective if and only if the set has bounded curvature, that is, it is bounded except along directions in which all constraints are linear. Without convexity, these results remain valid, except that bounded curvature is no longer necessary. Moreover, integer variables can destroy attainment only if there are at least two of them and at least one continuous variable. The result for one integer variable follows from a lifting theorem, which also extends known results for cubic objectives and convex polynomial constraints. Finally, for convex constraints and rational data, attainment holds when the objective is bounded from above, convex, or quasi-convex over a full-dimensional convex set containing the feasible region.

title: Prospects for probing supermassive binary black holes in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei via microlensing effects
abstract: Gravitational microlensing in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei (AGNs) provides a powerful probe of accretion-disk structure and may offer a unique opportunity to identify sub-parsec supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) through distinctive signatures. Upcoming wide-field surveys are expected to discover a large sample of strongly lensed AGNs, a fraction of which may host SMBBHs detectable via microlensing. In this paper, we employ semi-analytic models to assess the detection prospects of sub-parsec SMBBHs in lensed AGNs, focusing on systems with resolvable multiple images suitable for microlensing analysis. Accounting for galaxy-scale strong-lensing statistics, and including the cluster-lensing contribution as an optimistic statistical extension, we estimate that up to approximately 87 such systems could be spatially resolved by individual upcoming surveys, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (Rubin), Euclid, China's Space Survey Telescope (CSST), and the Roman. For the Rubin WFD survey, we estimate that periodic oscillations in microlensing light curves could identify $\sim0.12-0.68$ short-period ($<5$\,yr) binaries, whereas diagnostics based on the reconstructed size-wavelength relation apply to a broader population, potentially identifying $\sim0.4-5.3$ systems, depending on the model assumptions. CSST, Euclid, and Roman may also reveal up to $10.6$, $8.9$, and $1.2$ systems exhibiting size-wavelength features, and $2.3$, $1.9$, $0.3$ systems showing periodic oscillations, which should be regarded as imaging-selected candidates whose microlensing-based identification requires adequate time-domain follow-up, including cadence, monitoring baseline, photometric precision, and reliable time-delay measurements. Our results show that strongly lensed AGNs provide a promising, though observationally demanding, pathway for finding candidate SMBBHs via microlensing.

title: Sensing frequencies at the discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit using a single qubit
abstract: We consider a fundamental quantum sensing task: detecting weak oscillating fields with unknown strength and frequency. Recent work by Allen et al. established a fundamental lower bound on the required sensing time, which they named the "Grover-Heisenberg limit", and gave a protocol attaining this limit. The protocol relies on auxiliary qubits, which are used to run Grover's algorithm as a subroutine, leaving open the question of whether a single sensing qubit can achieve the same scaling. We show that a single qubit suffices for a discrete version of this problem, in which the signal strength is known and the frequency belongs to an arbitrary, but known, finite set of candidate frequencies. Our protocol's sensing time grows only as the square root of the number of candidate frequencies. We prove that this square-root dependence, which we refer to as the "discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit", is optimal in the worst case.

title: FIBER: Bayesian Fusion of Fast-DetectGPT and IRT-Informed Detector Evidence for LLM-Generated Text Detection
abstract: Detecting large language model (LLM)-generated text remains challenging under domain and generator shifts. Supervised detectors may generalize poorly, while zero-shot methods often rely on individual statistical signals without leveraging historical detector behavior. We propose FIBER (Fast-DetectGPT with IRT-informed Bayesian Evidence Recalibration), which integrates continuous Fast-DetectGPT scores with auxiliary detector outputs through Bayesian evidence fusion. Item response theory (IRT) models historical detector-correctness patterns, providing class-conditional detector-output likelihoods through marginalization over latent text representations. These likelihoods are combined with Fast-DetectGPT score densities and a historical class prior for prediction. When historical Fast-DetectGPT scores are unavailable, a variant called FIBER-Stream estimates class-specific score distributions from an unlabeled batch. On a 32,000-text multi-domain benchmark, FIBER achieves the highest accuracy (0.620) and improves mean AUC over Fast-DetectGPT (0.664 versus 0.600) under five-fold cross-validation. FIBER also consistently improves AUC across four individual domains. Under out-of-distribution transfer, FIBER-Stream achieved an AUC of 0.911, compared with 0.889 for FIBER and 0.922 for Fast-DetectGPT alone. These results demonstrate the potential of integrating complementary detector evidence and historical information to improve detection performance across heterogeneous settings.

title: Test-Time Selective Adaptation for Cross-Modal UAV Object Tracking with Token Shift
abstract: Cross-modal unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) object tracking faces modality-induced appearance discrepancies and abrupt target-position shifts that can arise from modality switching, UAV motion, and inter-sensor offsets. Although existing methods model modality and spatial variations, they primarily rely on offline representation learning and offer limited localization-oriented adaptation during testing. To address these challenges, we propose Test-Time Selective Adaptation with Token Shift (TSAT), which derives spatial and temporal adaptation signals from unlabeled test sequences for online optimization. Specifically, we design a controllable token shift auxiliary task, which imposes explicit spatial correspondence between predefined token translations and resultant localization offsets, generating stable annotation-free spatial adaptation signals. Furthermore, we introduce a temporal backward prediction auxiliary task to exploit frame-wise temporal dependencies, effectively mitigating cumulative localization errors in continuous tracking. To suppress interference from unreliable tracking samples, we develop a reliability-aware update gating strategy to screen valid adaptation signals and stabilize online parameter updates. Experiments on CM-UOT demonstrate that TSAT achieves state-of-the-art performance against existing test-time adaptation methods, exhibiting superior robustness under frequent modality switching and severe spatial displacement. Experiments across tracking frameworks and datasets further validate the effectiveness and generalization capability of TSAT.

title: Defective $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ from first principles
abstract: $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ is a two-dimensional van der Waals material with promising applications involving ferroelectricity. However, the presence of native defects can significantly influence its structural and electronic properties. In this work, we employ density functional theory with a state-of-the-art meta-generalized gradient approximation (meta-GGA) exchange-correlation functional to investigate the electronic structure of bulk $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ and the formation of neutral point defects, including vacancies and antisites, under Se-rich and In-rich growth conditions. Our calculations reproduce the experimental structural parameters of the pristine material and reveal that the Se vacancy in the middle layer exhibits an unexpectedly low formation energy under both chemical environments. Structural analysis shows that the neighboring tetrahedrally coordinated In atom undergoes a substantial local relaxation along the three-fold axis, which preserves its $C_{3v}$ site symmetry even as its coordination is reduced from four to three, providing a microscopic explanation for the remarkable stability of this defect.

title: Evolutionary Characteristics of the Solar Coronal Rotation: Revealed by a Century of Observations
abstract: The 10.7 cm radio flux time series from 1874 May 9 to 2017 June 30, the longest available observational proxy of the solar corona, is used to systematically investigate the multi-scale evolution of coronal rotation period lengths (RPLs) using wavelet analysis and linear regression. Throughout the time interval considered, the coronal rotation is characterized by a dominant synodic period of approximately 26.72 days, which varies in a complex manner with the advancing solar cycle. The relationship between the coronal RPLs and sunspot number (SN) changes over time: anticorrelation during 1874.9-1943.1, correlation during 1943.1-1958.2, anticorrelation during 1958.2-1987.4, and correlation during 1987.4-2016.9. Overall, RPLs show a negative correlation with SN, but their relationship is complex. This scenario is reflected in the phase dependence of the RPLs on the solar cycle. The variation of RPLs is complex, but a distinct pattern emerges: during weak activity phases, coronal rotation is slower, whereas during strong activity phases (approximately years 3 to 6 of the solar cycle), it becomes faster. Several statistically significant periods are detected in RPLs. Cross wavelet transform and wavelet coherence further confirm that the complex evolutionary pattern of RPLs fundamentally results from the combined modulation of two factors: the direct and dominant effect of the ubiquitous small-scale magnetic fields on the coronal rotation, and the modulation of the entire solar atmospheric rotation by the solar magnetic activity level.

title: Probabilistic State Space Enumeration in Neural Network Computation
abstract: Deep neural networks typically realize dense computation by propagating information through all intermediate channels, while many approximation methods rank and retain individual computational components. We ask whether dense neural computation can instead be represented exactly as an expectation over a combinatorial state space, and approximated by evaluating only its most probable configurations. We introduce a novel probabilistic state-space framework for Transformer MLPs. The framework partitions the intermediate dimension into channel groups, defines an input-dependent distribution over binary inclusion states, and uses importance-corrected masked outputs such that the full expectation exactly recovers the dense MLP output. The key algorithmic novelty is NORDER-II, which enumerates complete joint states in decreasing probability without constructing or sorting the exponentially large state space. Truncating this ordering yields an anytime approximation governed by cumulative probability mass and a state budget. On Llama-3.2-1B and Gemma-2-2B, NORDER-II at a state budget of B=2048 achieves 92.4% and 93.8% MLP-output approximation accuracy, compared with 76.9% and 79.8% for Channel Top-k. When the first, middle, and last MLP layers are approximated jointly, WikiText-2 perplexity remains within 0.06% and 0.54% of dense inference. Relative to expected-count Grouped Top-k, NORDER-II yields 82.6% to 126.4% relative accuracy gains with only 0.18% to 0.19% additional local analytic FLOPs. These results establish the significance of joint-state structure beyond atomic salience and point to a new paradigm for neural computation: dense layers can be viewed as structured probabilistic inference over combinatorial computational states. This framework opens a path toward adaptive, probability-mass-controlled computation in pretrained neural networks.

title: Strict Monotonicity of the First Positive Steklov Eigenvalue on Eccentric Spherical Shells in Every Dimension
abstract: For $d\ge2$, consider the region between two nested spheres of fixed radii, with the inner sphere translated a distance $\varepsilon$ from the outer center. We prove that the first positive eigenvalue of the Steklov problem, with the spectral boundary condition imposed on both spheres, decreases strictly with $\varepsilon$ throughout the noncontact interval. This settles the planar monotonicity conjecture formulated by Nigam and establishes its higher-dimensional counterparts. In dimension two we use a double-center holomorphic expansion and a pair of positive compact coefficient operators. For every $d\ge3$, solid Gegenbauer harmonics yield analogous axisymmetric and transverse operators, with a positive rank-one monopole correction. Weighted angular-mode comparison for $d\ge3$ and a direct matrix comparison for $d=2$ identify the first positive eigenvalue as the unique level-one crossing of an associated spectral radius. The first eigenspace has dimension $d$ in the concentric case and dimension one for every nonconcentric configuration. Convergence and reconstruction estimates justify the coefficient reductions at the two boundaries.

title: Entanglement, correlations, and resource costs for symmetry-adapted quantum simulations of light through medium-mass nuclei
abstract: Entanglement governs both the classical cost of simulating correlated many-body systems and the quantum resources needed to treat them. In this work, we use nuclear symmetries to investigate the entanglement and correlations in nuclei using \textit{ab initio} symmetry-adapted no-core shell-model nuclear wavefunctions, illustrated here for $^{4,6,8}$He, $^8$Be, $^{12}\mathrm{C}$, $^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, and $^{48}$Ca. In this many-body approach, deformation and collectivity naturally emerge from the underlying chiral potential, and we show that the Sp(3,$\mathbb{R}$) basis concentrates the ground state in far fewer basis states than the SU(3) basis. We compute single-mode entropies and two-mode mutual information, and examine the organization of like-particle two-nucleon correlations into symmetry channels. Single-mode entropies are largest in the valence shells, while two-mode mutual information reveals substantial correlations both within and between shells. In all cases considered, the dominant pair correlations are captured by fewer SU(3) channels than angular-momentum channels, which reduces the number of variational parameters. Since the number of operator components within the channels is comparable in the two schemes for the heavier nuclei, this gives the SU(3)-coupling scheme a clear advantage. Fiedler ordering of the correlation graph with local refinement reduces the register ordering cost by a factor of 2 to 3 relative to the original shell ordering, and by 10 when two more shells are included in the register. Together, these measures link nuclear correlations to the selection of active modes and candidate excitation operators and to the design of quantum register layouts, offering guidance for the development of hybrid quantum-classical calculations of nuclei.

title: Face rings and the cohomology of unions of Schubert varieties
abstract: The cohomology ring of a union of Schubert varieties $X_{W}=\bigcup_{w\in W}X_w,$ for $W\subseteq S_n$, in the complete flag variety is well known to be a quotient of the coinvariant ring $R_n$. We determine exactly when the ideal defining this quotient is generated by squarefree monomials, i.e. when it can be identified with the image of a Stanley-Reisner ideal $I_Δ$ in $R_n$. We prove that a single Schubert variety $X_w$ has this property exactly when $w\in S_n$ avoids a set of seven patterns, and in this case we describe the corresponding doubly-pruned simplicial complex $Δ$. We then show this is equivalent to $X_w$ being cut out of the complete flag variety by particular inclusion conditions on the pieces of the flag. We prove these complexes are vertex decomposable, and are Cohen-Macaulay precisely when $X_w$ is smooth. We then give a closed formula for the Poincaré polynomial of $X_w$. For unions $X_W$, pattern avoidance is necessary but no longer sufficient, and we prove a necessary and sufficient condition we call prunable that describes how the individual complexes associated to each $w\in W$ may be glued in the union. Quotients of $R_n$ by squarefree monomial ideals appear naturally in the Adams-Reiner conjecture on resolutions of Stanley-Reisner rings over certain parameter rings. We prove their conjecture for a family of simplicial complexes that includes the doubly-pruned complexes.

title: MiniPose: Miniature-Based Real Data Collection for 6D Pose Estimation of Large Industrial Pipe Segments
abstract: 6-DOF pose estimation of large and heavy industrial objects, such as large piping systems in shipyards and structural components in petrochemical plants, remains relatively underexplored in robotic perception. Repeatedly repositioning large objects is physically and spatially demanding, making it difficult to acquire real training data with sufficient pose diversity. Synthetic data offer a scalable alternative, but faithfully reproducing real RGB-D observations, particularly the structured measurement errors of real depth sensors, remains difficult. We propose MiniPose, a practical pipeline for miniature-based real RGB-D data collection that addresses both the data-acquisition burden and the sim-to-real gap. We fabricate a scaled-down replica and capture RGB-D data of it in diverse poses using a real RGB-D camera. RGB images are used directly, while depth maps are converted to a geometrically consistent representation of the full-scale object via a simple inverse scaling transformation. This allows training to incorporate real appearance and sensor measurement characteristics that are difficult to reproduce using synthetic data alone. To examine whether the benefit depends on a particular network, we evaluate two RGB-D pose estimators with different formulations, PVN3D and RDPN6D. Mixing at most 1,000 miniature images per pipe type, less than 10\% of the training data, with 10,000 synthetic images improves the mean ADD-S AUC across pipe types over synthetic-only training for both estimators. A comparison with training on full-scale real data further suggests that miniature data can serve as a proxy where full-scale collection is difficult, reducing the data-collection burden for large industrial objects.

title: CoLaX: Context-Aware Local Explanations for Time Series Classification
abstract: Post-hoc explanations for time series classifiers usually score local patterns, such as subsequences or shapelets, without regard to the rest of the sequence. Yet the same motif can carry different predictive meaning under different global temporal conditions, such as trends or regimes. We propose CoLaX, a context-aware post-hoc explanation framework that builds on shapelet-driven Shapley attribution and conditions local-pattern relevance on a learned representation of the full sequence. Global context acts at two levels: it produces sample-specific prototype weights and a temporally resolved signal that reweights the local activation map. The resulting context-conditioned segments are the players of a Shapley attribution game whose values come only from the frozen black-box classifier. On synthetic benchmarks where identical motifs change relevance across contexts, CoLaX improves AUPRC over the strongest baseline by 30\% on average. On real-world data, it achieves the highest AUPRC on ECG. Additional ablations indicate that the gains come from input-dependent conditioning rather than from additional learnable weights. CoLaX is therefore most useful when recurring local motifs change relevance across sequence-level contexts.

title: Abelian covers and the index of the centre in a group
abstract: Let $h(n)$ be the largest number of abelian subgroups needed to cover a group in which every set of more than $n$ elements contains two distinct elements that commute, and let $ζ(n)$ be the largest index of the centre under the same constraint. Erdős asked for the growth of $h$, Neumann proved that both quantities are finite, and Pyber bounded both $ζ$ and $h$ exponentially. We determine $h(n)$ for every positive integer $n$ and prove that $h(n)=1+\sqrt{ζ(n)}$ whenever the constraint admits a nonabelian group. The covers are built directly from the commutator geometry of a scalar quotient, and the comparison with $ζ$ is made afterwards. Beyond finitely many small cases, both maxima are attained by the same groups, those isoclinic to an extraspecial $2$-group of order $2^{1+2\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}$, confirming Pyber's prediction for the central index in this range.

title: DiFiT: Distribution-Fidelity-guided Visual Token Pruning for Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Visual token pruning reduces the inference cost of multimodal large language models, but answer accuracy only partly reflects its effect. Pruning can change the probabilities of alternative response tokens even when greedy answers remain correct and unchanged. We compare full and pruned response distributions under shared reference prefixes. Average predictive drift grows with compression on fixed correctly answered samples. Separate analyses associate larger drift with more confidence-decision disagreements and sampling failures. We propose DiFiT (Distribution-Fidelity-guided Token pruning) to learn discrete selection from reference answers and full-token response distributions. Dual-View Distillation matches probabilities across the vocabulary, while answer supervision supports task quality. A learned scorer and differentiable Top-$K$ learn which visual evidence to retain. A multi-budget mask objective supports different retention ratios through one shared ranking over a frozen model. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, DiFiT reduces sampling-induced negative flips by 30.3% relative to FastV at 10% retention on four-task greedy-correct controls. It preserves 98.74% of baseline performance on MME at 30% retention.

title: Solving spectral flow in AdS$_3$: from covering maps to pencils
abstract: Strings in AdS$_3$ with pure NS-NS flux are described by the exactly solvable SL(2,$\mathbb{R}$) WZW model, yet correlators of winding strings, given by spectrally flowed operators, were so far known only up to three points. We obtain all of them, for any number of insertions and windings, in terms of unflowed correlators, proving the four-point conjecture of Dei and Eberhardt. The key ingredient is a pencil of rational maps from the worldsheet to the boundary which exists for generic insertion points, unwinds all insertions at once, and collapses to the covering map when the latter exists.

title: Improving Efficiency and Power in Small Rare-Disease Trials Through Prespecified, Data-Adaptive Covariate Adjustment
abstract: Covariate adjustment can potentially improve efficiency in randomized clinical trials, but in rare diseases, limited prior knowledge makes it difficult to specify an adjustment at the design stage. Targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) with the Super Learner (TMLE+SL) can outperform fixed adjustment methods, such as the G-computation estimator, by leveraging machine learning to learn both the covariates and the functional form of the adjustment from the trial data. Estimating the known treatment mechanism can improve efficiency further. In simulations reflecting real rare-disease trials, TMLE+SL yielded valid inference and achieved greater efficiency and power than conventional analyses. Finally, we also provide practical guidance on specifying TMLE+SL in rare-disease trials.

title: Solitons of the intermediate long wave equation with residue source
abstract: We revisit the bilinear formulation of the intermediate long-wave (ILW) equation by interpreting its principal-value integrals in the framework of Sato hyperfunctions. When the tau-functions have no zeros inside the relevant contours, the conventional source-free ILW equation is recovered. When zeros enter the contours, their residue contributions must instead be retained, leading naturally to a residue-extended ILW system with self-consistent sources determined by the tau-functions themselves. We introduce a residue index that counts the zeros enclosed in each analytic strip and use it to classify the resulting soliton sectors. The conventional elevation-soliton belongs to the zero-residue sector, whereas depression-solitons and higher elevation branches generally carry non-zero residue indices. Exact one- and multisoliton tau-functions are constructed, including mixed elevation--depression configurations with factorised two-body interactions. Their residue indices are additive and remain invariant during collisions, provided that no zero crosses a contour boundary. A Fourier-space analysis shows that the soliton spectra decay exponentially at large wavenumbers, with a decay rate determined by the distance of the nearest complex singularity from the real axis. This rate vanishes as an odd-multiple boundary between adjacent residue sectors is approached, providing a direct spectral signature of the transition between them.

title: When Does Causality Help in Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection?
abstract: Causality-aware scoring is common in multivariate time-series anomaly detection, yet the literature rarely states when it helps. Holding one causality-guided autoencoder (DeCauAE) fixed, we vary graph quality, anomaly type and protocol against ground truth. Graph quality fixes the payoff: on a twenty-variable DAG the gain over a graph-free autoencoder decays as the graph is corrupted. Anomaly type fixes the target: the structural factor lifts window F1 from 0.800 to 0.976 where anomalies break conditional structure, and its advantage vanishes below a break severity s 0.3. Protocol fixes the ranking: point-adjusted F1 lets a random score match the full model, while range-aware VUS separates the autoencoder family from the classical baselines. On real benchmarks the causal module pays only where density makes a system eligible and cross-subsample reproducibility selects entities inside it; enabling it everywhere costs 0.012 VUS-ROC. The structural factor also transfers to classical detectors .

title: Tokenization: Hardness and Bicriteria Approximation Algorithms
abstract: We study Binary Tokenization: given a corpus of binary strings over $\{0,1\}$ and a vocabulary budget $K$, select at most $K$ substrings (called vocabulary) to minimize the total number of tokens needed to represent the corpus. The primitive symbols $0$ and $1$ are always available, and each document must be segmented separately. Letting $n$ denote the total corpus length and $M$ for the maximum document length, we prove that, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, Binary Tokenization problem does not have polynomial-time $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-approximation algorithms unless $\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP}$. To complement the hardness result, we give a polynomial-time $(γ,γ)$-bicriteria algorithm, with $γ= \sqrt{M}\log n$: The algorithm outputs a vocabulary of size at most $γK$ with number of tokens at most $γ{\rm OPT}_K$, where ${\rm OPT}_K$ is the optimal number of tokens under the original budget $K$. We also study a storage-budget variant, in which the sum of the selected substrings' lengths is bounded by $B$. For $2\le B<n$, we obtain an $(O(\log n\log B),O(\log n\log B))$-bicriteria approximation algorithm.

title: Sharp weighted bounds for reverse fractional integral operators
abstract: In this paper, we prove the one-weight reverse fractional integral operators \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^q(w^q)}\geq C_w\|f\|_{L^p(w^p)} \] holds for all nonnegative measurable functions $f$, with $\frac ns<p<1$ and $\frac1q=\frac1p-\frac sn$, if and only if $w^{p/(1-p)}\in A_{\frac{p(s-n)}{n(1-p)}}$. Furthermore, we show the lower bound \[ C_w\gtrsim_{n,s,p}[w]_{p,q}^{\min\left\{\frac{p(n-s)}{n(1-p)},\frac{p(n-s)}{sp-n}\right\}}, \] and the exponent is sharp. We also investigate when the reverse weak-type estimate \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^{\frac{n}{n-s},\infty}(w^{\frac{n}{n-s}})}\geq \frac{n}{s}\,v_n^{(n-s)/n}[w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}]^{(n-s)/n}_{A_1}\|f\|_{L^1(w)} \] holds if and only if $w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}\in A_1$.

title: Scalable Compilation of Resource-Efficient Tapers for High-Confidence Quantum Phase Estimation
abstract: Quantum phase estimation is a key component of many quantum algorithms. Recently, high-confidence, tapered QPE (tQPE) has been introduced, significantly reducing the number of ancilla qubits necessary for a given failure probability, $ε$. We consider tQPE with $p = l+m$ ancillas, where $l$ represents the number of ancillas necessary to estimate a phase to a given resolution and $m$ represents the number of ''confidence'' qubits added to ensure a desired success probability. With tQPE the failure probability decays double exponentially in $m$, implying that only a few confidence qubits suffice for virtually any problem of interest. A key challenge for tQPE is the construction of the quantum circuit for preparing the taper state on the ancilla register. Here, we develop scalable tensor network methods (previous work was limited to ($l + m = 24$)) giving highly optimized state preparation circuits for optimally concentrated DPSS (Slepian) tapers. We provide an accompanying database of resource-efficient state preparation circuits for $l = 1, \dots, 50$ and $m = 1, \dots, 4$. Our circuits are shallow enough for a demonstration on near-term devices for small values of $l$. We run tQPE circuits for a 1-qubit system initialized in the ground state on Quantinuum's H2-2 quantum computer, demonstrating a $3\times$ to $18\times$ reduction in failure probability for $l=1,\ldots,10$ on a noisy device.

title: Magnetized strange quark matter in hypersurface-homogeneous $f(R,T)$ cosmology: physical closure, isotropization and late-time observational constraints
abstract: Cosmological models of magnetized strange quark matter in $f(R,T)$ gravity have so far relied on kinematic ansatzes and lacked observational tests. We revisit them for $f(R,T)=R+2μT$ on a hypersurface-homogeneous background containing the locally rotationally symmetric Bianchi I, Kantowski--Sachs and Bianchi III geometries. Treated exactly, the Maxwell field couples minimally. Because kinematic ansatzes contradict a magnetized source, we close the field equations with the bag-model equation of state and magnetic flux freezing and, adding dust and radiation, solve them exactly in limiting cases and numerically in general. Without primordial shear, the field-induced anisotropy keeps, as in general relativity, a nearly constant radiation-era level for $μ\ge0$, then decays as the model approaches de Sitter space; an assumed present field of 1 nG leaves $(σ/H)_0\simeq5.8\times10^{-11}$ today. A joint fit to 32 cosmic chronometers, 1590 Pantheon+ supernova light curves and baryon acoustic oscillations from the second data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument gives $μ=1.12^{+0.65}_{-0.58}$ and $H_0=69.1\pm3.2$~\kmsMpc, and the null, weak and dominant energy conditions hold throughout. Relative to the flat $Λ$ cold dark matter model, the Akaike (AIC) and Bayesian (BIC) information criteria give $Δ\mathrm{AIC}=-1.4$ and $Δ\mathrm{BIC}=+4.0$, and the Bayes factor is inconclusive. The fitted bag term, $B_c^{1/4}=2.15$ meV, is an effective vacuum energy, not the quantum chromodynamics bag constant. The preference for $μ>0$ depends on the supernova sample and the prior, a constant coupling would shift matter--radiation equality, and the sign of $μ$ depends on the matter Lagrangian; $μ$ is therefore an effective late-time parameter.

title: CrowdMAPS: Crowdsourcing Multiple Actions per State for Real-World Imitation Learning
abstract: Real-world robot imitation learning is often limited by the cost of collecting physical demonstrations, which typically yield only one action label per visited state. We present CrowdMAPS, a web-based crowdsourcing paradigm for augmenting real-robot datasets with Multiple Actions per State (MAPS). After or during standard robot data collection, CrowdMAPS distributes visited robot states to remote annotators through a web-based 3D interface, where they specify alternative valid actions without requiring access to physical robot hardware. This expands robot datasets along a complementary "width" dimension--by increasing the number of actions per visited state--rather than only by collecting more trajectories. We evaluate CrowdMAPS using keyframe-centric goal-pose annotations supplied by non-expert annotators and train imitation policies on the resulting MAPS data. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, increasing MAPS width from one to ten actions per state improves sample efficiency and increases average success rates by 35.6 percentage points for keypose policies and 33.0 percentage points for trajectory policies. These results show that software-mediated human annotations can augment physical robot data to afford denser supervision, establishing CrowdMAPS as a scalable digital layer for real-robot data collection.

title: SAVE: Less is More in Agentic Video Reasoning
abstract: Agentic video-reasoning frameworks iteratively explore a video, choosing what to observe based on the query and evidence gathered so far. Existing methods are typically evaluated with different backbones, preprocessing pipelines, and computational budgets, making it difficult to determine which components actually drive performance, how much they cost, and whether agentic inference is preferable to native video reasoning in the first place. We conduct a controlled evaluation of a diverse set of recent agentic video-reasoning systems across two strong contemporary backbones, with explicit token and monetary-cost accounting. Across Gemini 3 Flash and Gemma 4, most existing agentic frameworks fail to consistently improve over native video inference and often increase computational cost. We investigate two primary questions: (1) How much agentic framework complexity is necessary for effective video reasoning? (2) When, if at all, is agentic video reasoning preferable to just using the backbone directly? To answer the first question, we introduce a deliberately minimal Active Exploration Baseline and show that it remains competitive with substantially more elaborate agents. We then propose targeted extensions to this baseline, yielding SAVE (Simple Agentic Video Explorer). SAVE outperforms all evaluated prior agentic methods in five of six backbone-benchmark settings. Turning to the second question, our results indicate that the advantage of agentic exploration grows when dense processing would otherwise represent answer-relevant events too sparsely, particularly for long videos and temporally concentrated evidence. Overall, our results suggest that agentic video reasoning should favor simple frameworks over increasingly elaborate pipelines and focus primarily on long-form video, where selective evidence acquisition offers the clearest advantage over native inference.

title: Structure-Aware Quantum Circuit Equivalence Checking via Sparse Pauli Propagation
abstract: Quantum circuit equivalence checking is essential for validating compiler optimizations, but its computational cost can vary substantially with circuit structure. We present a structure-aware equivalence checker for unitary quantum circuits based on sparse Pauli propagation. It combines two complementary verification strategies: generator propagation compares the conjugation actions of the circuits on Pauli generators, while Cut-Miter exploits cancellation between circuit products at selected cut points. A structure-aware verification procedure uses circuit characteristics to select between these strategies while explicitly accounting for numerical and approximation errors. We evaluate our framework against three existing equivalence checkers on two benchmark suites containing circuit pairs with up to 512 qubits. Across 434 scored circuit pairs, our framework produces reference-consistent decisions for 96.3% of the pairs without any incorrect verdicts, while the evaluated baselines achieve at most 68.7% reference-consistent decisions. It also achieves the lowest aggregate runtime among the evaluated tools, reducing total runtime by 48.5%--76.0% relative to these baselines. Ablation studies confirm the benefits of cut-based verification, Pauli-term pruning, and bounded propagation attempts. These results indicate that structure-aware sparse Pauli propagation, combined with complementary verification strategies and explicit error accounting, can provide an effective approach to practical quantum circuit equivalence checking.

title: Maximally Chiral Eigenstate from Inverse Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
abstract: We show that an ordered quantum state can support waves with a finite speed in one direction and exponentially small energies in the other. We prescribe this spectrum for a spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg eigenstate and reconstruct a nonlocal Hamiltonian. The thermodynamic construction selects the ordered, current-carrying state as a ground state. Its magnetic moment remains finite while its response to a weak field has a divergent slope. The entropy per spin vanishes only inversely with a logarithm of temperature, with an exact coefficient containing the golden ratio. Our spin-response calculations reveal a bound pair whose energy can be tuned without changing its intensity. Added exchange and smoother mode selection restore quadratic excitations at the lowest energies. These results connect the design of interactions to directional dynamics and unusual thermodynamics. We propose momentum-resolved spin spectroscopy, weak-field magnetometry, and low-temperature entropy measurements to probe these counterintuitive signatures.

title: Prediction or Persistence? What Future-Prediction Scores Miss About World Models
abstract: Pretrained video world models are compared and chosen as components for robot learning largely by future-prediction scores. On its own, such a score cannot be read as evidence of prediction, because it mixes encoder quality, the near future's resemblance to the recent past, and the predictor's own contribution. We separate the three with a matched control. On 27,000 future-retrieval trials from household egocentric video, a model must pick the true continuation of a clip among eleven candidates from the same video (chance 0.091), ranked zero-shot by its own training criterion. Each model is paired with a persistence control, an identical copy whose predictor is never invoked, so the paired difference isolates the predictor. Score and contribution dissociate within the native-video V-JEPA family alone: the predictor adds +0.291 top-1 for V-JEPA 2.1 but +0.03 to +0.04 for V-JEPA 2 on the identical trials. Across five models the contribution ranges from +0.291 to negative, and it is negative only for the two action-conditioned models, which we evaluate outside their training regime. Persistence alone recovers the encoder ordering expected from pretraining, a sign that the probe tracks real signal. We suggest reporting each future-prediction score together with its persistence baseline. The gap between them, not the score, is what makes the number interpretable: a necessary check costing one forward pass. Establishing downstream usefulness is a separate matter, for a planning or control evaluation.

title: Rayleigh--Taylor instability and Hadamard ill-posedness for the rotating free-boundary Euler equations in three dimensions
abstract: The free-boundary incompressible Euler equations linearized at a rigidly rotating equilibrium on the flat product of the unit disk and a circle are Hadamard ill-posed in Sobolev spaces of order at least two. The equilibrium violates the Taylor sign condition, under which local well-posedness is known. Eulerian linearization retaining free-surface advection reduces the spectral problem to a modified Bessel equation; Rouché's theorem yields an unstable root whose real part grows as the square root of the axial frequency. Eigenmode Sobolev norms grow as the corresponding power of that frequency. Rescaling gives data tending to zero whose solutions are unbounded at any prescribed positive time. At zero axial frequency the analysis recovers Ebin's rotating-disk rate (Communications in Partial Differential Equations 12 (1987), 1175--1201). The product lift gives nonlinear ill-posedness on the invariant class of axially independent data.

title: Parallel Spanning Forest and Biconnectivity for Well-Connected Graph in Sub-Logarithmic Time
abstract: We give a randomized ARBITRARY CRCW PRAM algorithm for computing a spanning forest of an \(n\)-vertex, \(m\)-edge graph. Let \(d\) be the maximum component diameter. With good probability, the algorithm runs in \(O(\log d+\log\log n)\) time using \(O(m+n)\) processors and outputs a rooted spanning forest of original edges with maximum depth \(2^{O(\log d+\log\log n)}\). For finding bridges, our algorithm identifies every bridge edge in \(O(\log d+\log\log n)\) time. For biconnectivity, it outputs all blocks in \(O(\log d+\log d'+\log\log n)\) time, where \(d'\) is the bi-diameter. All these problems are fundamental in graph algorithms with numerous applications. Our results improve the best previous time bounds parameterized by the number of vertices and diameter. Finally, we prove deterministic \(Ω(\log n/\log\log n)\) lower bounds for outputting a DFS Sequence, a weighted spanning forest, and an ear decomposition.

title: Quantum unique ergodicity and the critical crossover for 1-d Gaussian band matrices
abstract: We consider an $N\times N$ complex Gaussian random band matrix in one dimension with band width of order $W$, in the periodic block form of Yau and Yin. The $N$ sites are split into $n=N/W$ blocks of size $W$ on a ring, and the entries are nonzero only within a block and between adjacent blocks. The conjectured localization--delocalization transition occurs at $W\sim\sqrt N$. We prove quantum unique ergodicity for bulk eigenvectors at every deterministic rank whenever $W^2/N\to\infty$, with no power or logarithmic separation between $W^2$ and $N$. At the threshold $N/W^2\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, we show that the rescaled bulk eigenvalues and the block-mass profiles of their eigenvectors (the probability measures on the circle placing at $k/n$ the squared norm of the eigenvector on block $k$) converge jointly to a unique law. This law is encoded by a random entire function whose zeros give the limiting eigenvalues, and its derivatives there give the limiting profile integrals. The law of this function is determined by the Dorokhov--Mello--Pereyra--Kumar (DMPK) diffusion of the unitary class. In the critical law, the profiles have strictly positive variance against every nonconstant smooth test function, so they are not concentrated on the uniform profile. As $τ\to0$ this variance vanishes and the local spectrum tends to the sine process. As $τ\to\infty$ it tends to a Poisson process where both limits taken after the critical one. The critical family thus interpolates between the delocalized and localized regimes, confirming for this model the prediction of Fyodorov and Mirlin that at $W^2\asymp N$ the joint law of eigenvalues and eigenvectors depends only on $N/W^2$. The full content of this work has been autoformalized in Lean4 by AxiomProver.

title: Metropolis Random Walks Escape Deep Basins Faster in Higher Dimensions
abstract: Simulated Annealing (SA) is a widely used stochastic optimization algorithm. It is of great interest to understand how its ability to escape local minima at a fixed temperature depends on geometry and dimension. In prior work, we derived closed-form expressions for the expected basin escape time of a constant-temperature SA process on a one-dimensional piecewise-linear landscape. In this paper, we extend the analysis to $D$-dimensional cubic basins defined by the infinity-norm energy $V(x)=\|x\|_\infty$. The walk proposes nearest-neighbor moves uniformly and escapes upon first reaching the outer shell, that is, any site with $\|x\|_\infty=N$. We construct a one-dimensional birth-death shell-quotient chain by collapsing each concentric shell in the Metropolis electrical network to a single node while retaining its total stationary mass. We derive a closed-form expression for the mean escape time $Q_D(N)$ of this shell-quotient chain as a function of the acceptance probability $p$, the basin depth $N$, and the dimension $D$. For fixed $D$ and fixed $0<p<1$, the quotient escape time scales as $Θ(α^N/N^{D-1})$ as $N\to\infty$, where $α=1/p$. Relative to $D=1$, this gives an asymptotic speedup of order $N^{D-1}$ within this family of cubic basins. We prove that the true Metropolis mean escape time $H_D(N)$, without shell averaging, has the same $Θ(α^N/N^{D-1})$ scaling, establishing a lower bound via Rayleigh monotonicity and a matching upper bound through an explicit low-energy flow construction using Thomson's principle. Numerical solutions that exploit the walk's symmetries quantify the discrepancy between the quotient and true-chain means for $D=1,2,3$.

title: Scaffolding Self-Transduction with Alignment Attention Mask for Aligner-Encoder ASR
abstract: End-to-end ASR systems must jointly solve speech- text alignment and token prediction from sequence-level super- vision. We study this problem in Aligner-Encoder ASR, where alignment is performed inside encoder self-attention and can thus be directly intervened on with an attention mask. We use forced alignment to build an attention mask that confines selected encoder self-attention heads to a narrow window around the alignment path. The mask is faded out over training, leaving a deployable model with an unmodified inference architecture; alternatively, kept active at training and inference, it serves as an oracle that measures recognition performance once alignment is externally resolved. On LibriSpeech, the faded alignment mask improves test-clean/test-other WER from 3.9/6.4 to 3.5/5.9 over an Aligner baseline. The oracle masks are far stronger, reaching 1.2/2.9 WER, which can be thought of as an upper- bound accuracy in the 100M-class Conformer regime without an external language model. This indicates that alignment inference is a major bottleneck in Aligner-Encoder ASR, and suggests that improved alignment mechanisms might yield substantial accuracy gains for end-to-end ASR.

title: Relative-energy stabilization of an irreversible port-Hamiltonian tubular reactor
abstract: This paper develops a relative-energy control approach for a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model of a non-isothermal tubular reactor around a spatially nonuniform stationary profile. The starting point is a thermodynamic duality between the entropy-based availability used in earlier reactor control and the relative Hamiltonian induced by the irreversible port-Hamiltonian representation. Under physically interpretable stability conditions---positive heat capacity, positive compressibility and positive compositional susceptibility---the Hamiltonian density is shown to be strictly convex, while the corresponding entropy representation is strictly concave. The resulting relative Hamiltonian decomposes into kinetic, compressive, thermal and mixing contributions and yields an exact relative-energy balance in which irreversible dissipation is separated from profile-dependent terms. This structure leads to a bounded monotone distributed jacket feedback that injects thermal damping without cancelling the nonlinear PDE dynamics. A continuous coercivity condition gives a local a-priori decay estimate for sufficiently regular nonlinear solutions, while a composite energy functional provides an exponential estimate for the linearized closed-loop initial-boundary value problem. Structure-preserving PFEM simulations are used to verify the predicted dissipation mechanisms and constrained profile regulation.

title: Well-Posedness for the Cauchy Problem with Free Boundary in Half-Space Arising from Combustion Problem
abstract: In this paper, we address the local-in-time well-posedness of an obstacle problem arising from a combustion model. The equation under consideration is a linear inhomogeneous heat equation on the moving domain $(s(t),\infty)$, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet and inhomogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Our main result establishes the existence and uniqueness of a positive classical solution. Although several results are known for the homogeneous heat equation, much less is known about the inhomogeneous case. We show that the boundary function $s(t)$ is $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder continuous in time when the forcing term has a singularity of order $O(1/\sqrt{t})$ as $t \to 0$. We also prove that if both the initial data and the forcing term are smooth, then $s$ has higher regularity than $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder continuity.

title: A Diffusive T-Matrix Unifying the Electric and Magnetic Polarizability Tensors in Conducting Layered Media
abstract: Electromagnetic induction is used to detect and classify buried and submerged objects, such as unexploded ordnance in soil and on the seabed. A small object is commonly described by its magnetic polarizability tensor (MPT), which is independent of its position and of the sensor. The MPT assumes that the surrounding medium does not conduct. In seawater at extremely low frequency, or in clay at kilohertz frequencies, this assumption fails at depths comparable to the skin depth. The object then also diverts the current induced in the medium, a galvanic response that the MPT omits. We describe the object instead by its transition matrix (T-matrix), which keeps the independence from position and sensor and includes both responses. It is computed once per medium and frequency from a single finite element problem, for any shape and materials. Its inductive block reduces to the MPT when the medium conducts weakly, and its galvanic block reduces to the electric polarizability tensor in the static limit. We test the model against full finite element solutions for a conducting box, non-magnetic and permeable, in a layered sea and in clay over bedrock. Two orders beyond the dipole, it is accurate to within 1.4% over two decades of frequency and for sizes up to 0.7 of the depth, whereas the error of the MPT carried into the conducting medium reaches 91%. Blocks coupling the two responses, contained in neither tensor, contribute up to 13%.

title: Advancing Weighted Partial MaxSAT Solving via Differentiable GPU Guidance
abstract: We present a GPU-CPU hybrid framework for Weighted Partial MaxSAT (WPMAX-SAT) that complements state-of-the-art CPU solvers with differentiable GPU optimization. The GPU stage directly optimizes instance-specific categorical decision parameters without a training dataset or a pretrained predictive model. The central challenge in extending differentiable optimization to WPMAX-SAT is the hard/soft clause asymmetry: hard clauses represent inviolable feasibility constraints while soft clauses carry weights. We introduce a hierarchical differentiable loss that prioritizes hard clause satisfaction before optimizing the weighted soft objective, ensuring that GPU gradient descent leans towards the constraint structure of WPMAX-SAT. Our framework transforms the GPU-optimized variable logits to high-confidence assignments and transfers them to CPU solvers via two complementary modes: partial guidance, which injects the most confident perturbed partial variable assignments as soft clauses into $N$ parallel solver instances, and phase initialization, which guides the CDCL solver's internal branching polarity with the full GPU assignment as a warm start to preserve the problem's originality. We evaluate on all 229 instances of the MSE 2024 (most recent due to cancellation in 2025) anytime weighted benchmark with the top 2 winners as baselines; our hybrid framework improves the average solution score by up to 4.9% over tt-open-wbo-inc-Glucose and 4.8% over SPB-MaxSAT-c-FPS at a 300-second time limit, with the potential to obtain better solutions surpassing the best known solution recorded in the competition evaluation.

title: One molecule, many outputs; many molecules, one output: exact diagnostics for atom-level compositional quantum encoders
abstract: Quantum natural language processing (QNLP) turns the grammar of a sentence into a tensor network and then into a quantum circuit with trainable angles. We build such a model for molecules: each heavy atom is a word with one wire per bond, and each bond is a ``cup'' joining two wires, so the circuit's wiring is the molecular graph. We work out exactly what these circuits keep. With the typed angle sharing of lambeq, the circuits separate every isomer pair we tested. Yet for isomers that simpler sharing confuses, the output states stay almost the same, before and after training. On 7 Tox21 pairs and 1,988 MOSES pairs, nearly all the difference lies in how often the measurements succeed, which a standard readout ignores. Simpler sharing, by element and bond type, shows why: the output then depends only on a graph whose vertices are the bonds. This explains all but one of the identical-output pairs we certify, including 1.19\% of 232{,}191 MOSES molecules, and for alkyl side chains it reduces to a tree shape that tells chains apart up to 15 atoms but not from 16. On small pairs, this circuit and the 1-WL graph test each separate pairs the other misses. We also show that SMILES writing order can change the output, that a run succeeds with probability at most $2^{-n}$ for $n$ bonds, and that a cup-free design avoids this cost. No circuit beats a simple atom-count model on Tox21, and we claim no quantum advantage.

title: Decide Before You Move: Diffusion-Generated Search Reference for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation in Semi-Static Environments
abstract: Open-world navigation requires a robot to locate a user-specified target in an indoor scene under open-vocabulary queries. Realistic indoor environments are semi-static: walls and furniture largely persist while smaller objects move, relocate, or vanish between visits. Prior-map systems answer queries from object poses recorded at reconstruction time, which expire as soon as objects move, whereas online methods re-derive where to look from current observations every few steps, often through expensive calls to a vision--language model. Assuming that walls and large furniture do not move, we keep their map to plan paths, but use a target--furniture co-occurrence prior to decide where to search. We present PreNav, an ObjectNav framework on semi-static environments. Rather than invoking a vision-language model at each step, PreNav generates a single global search reference before the robot moves: an LLM converts target--furniture co-occurrence into a spatial prior, a conditional diffusion model turns that prior and the persistent structure into an ordered centerline with a band around it, and the robot approaches the target once it is detected online. Experiments on a Gibson ObjectNav benchmark show that PreNav outperforms a strong online baseline under matched structural priors, using a generator trained only on room-level ScanNet++ scenes and applied to floor-level Gibson without fine-tuning. Real-world experiments under object relocation and open-vocabulary queries further validate the approach.

title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
abstract: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. Although artificial intelligence has advanced image interpretation, existing medical models often address restricted tasks, while general-purpose proprietary models lack access to private clinical imaging required to achieve medical expertise. Developing models that can interpret complex examinations and communicate their findings in the context of clinical decisions remains a major challenge. Here, we show that Neuro-VL, a vision-language model trained on nearly one million neuroimaging studies from routine clinical care, can interpret complete imaging examinations and engage in natural language conversations about their findings. Across internal and international datasets, Neuro-VL outperformed frontier general-purpose and specialized medical models in diagnosing, localizing, and describing abnormalities, as well as generating comprehensive radiology reports. The model also compared serial examinations to assess disease progression and more reliably resisted misleading clinical assumptions than leading frontier models from OpenAI and Google. These results extend health system learning beyond individual predictions to interactive image interpretation and longitudinal disease monitoring. They demonstrate how the collective clinical experience of health systems can be used to develop medical AI with specialized expertise and broad clinical capabilities.

title: Data-driven non-contiguous photon-energy groups for fast multigroup radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas
abstract: Opacity of mid- and high-$Z$ plasmas is dominated by thousands of overlapping spectral lines. Examples are laser-produced plasmas for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, inertial-fusion hohlraums, and stellar interiors. Radiation transport in such plasmas needs more than 1000 photon-energy groups in the EUV case, and this makes radiation-hydrodynamic simulations very expensive. We show that the accuracy of a small-group opacity model can be recovered by choosing properly \emph{which} fine bins are put into the same group. We present a data-driven method that assigns the fine bins of a detailed opacity and emissivity table to $K$ \emph{non-contiguous} groups. Each group has a fixed spectral shape inside it. The groups follow from one requirement: the reduced absorption operator must be diagonal for every plasma state. They are determined from a Gram matrix of spectra, taken from detailed-group solutions of a small part, for example 5\% in this work, of the parameter space. The reduced model is a set of $K$ uncoupled flux-limited diffusion equations. It can be used in an existing multigroup code by replacing the opacity table. For a Sn plasma with electron densities of $4\times10^{15}$--$1.1\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-3}$, electron temperatures of 5--250~eV, and scale lengths of 2.5--6900$\um$, the model with $K=100$ reproduces the total flux of the 1500-group reference with a median error of 2\% and a 90th-percentile error of 8\%. The 90th-percentile error is ten times smaller than that of a conventional 100-group model at the same cost.

title: Secular Dynamics and the LFL for $β$ Corner Process
abstract: In this paper, we consider the Gaussian $β$ corner process, whose edge particles are known to converge to the Tracy-Widom $β$ law. We study the almost sure behaviour of the extrema of the whole trajectory of the edge particles and establish a law of fractional logarithm (LFL) for the corner process for every fixed $β>0$, extending the previous known results in the case $β=1,2$. Our proof relies on the upward Gamma and downward Dirichlet secular equations, which can be regarded as two discrete dynamics to form the corner processes. The secular dynamics are used in both the correlation estimate and the decorrelation estimate, which are known as two key steps of proving LFL in \cite{BCEHK-LFL} for the Wigner minor process. Especially, in the decorrelation part, they are used as discrete analogues of the continuous Dyson Brownian motion.

title: GuardianAgentFlow: Multi-Agent Coordination for Web Privacy Protection
abstract: Web agents need to use private context without unnecessarily disclosing it. Effective protection must distinguish between requests that may be sent after sanitization and those that must be withheld, while preserving the information needed for authorized tasks. We present GuardianAgentFlow, a multi-agent framework that mediates outgoing Web requests through an explicit release contract. A dedicated restriction check grounds permission in the user's instruction; a shared protection scope aligns rewriting with disclosure checking; and candidate-grounded feedback guides revision before transmission. Experiments on Web requests with human-reviewed intent labels show improved request-contract success, while controlled comparisons and role ablations identify the contributions of restriction handling, policy evidence, and candidate checking. Evaluations of action proposals from PrivacyLens and AgentDAM demonstrate complementary protection when mediation is composed with privacy-aware agents. Experiments with smaller mediation models show that the coordination benefit persists with reduced model capacity. Dedicated-server measurements show lower mediation latency than full-policy reasoning, while real-site browser tests quantify integration overhead.

title: Exact Output Steering with Vanishing Controls in Weighted Shift Dynamics
abstract: Exploiting the rich dynamics of wrapped weighted shifts and their residualizations, we characterize exact projected steering with vanishing initial controls. For wrapped shifts, steering is characterized by an expansive cycle multiplier and a residue separating the source and control channels. For residual shifts, a distinct spectral--toral mechanism emerges: steering through selected conjugate planes is equivalent to radial expansion and an arithmetic parity condition on phase resonances, yielding bounded-gap steering times and quantitative control estimates. For structured machine-learning representations built from orbit dictionaries, we derive a two-scale gain condition for steering coefficients while preserving decoded outputs.

title: Fast Radio Burst Population Constrained by Source-Count Growth and Burst Clustering
abstract: Whether all fast radio burst (FRB) sources repeat, or whether some produce only a single burst, remains an open question. Using 3,950 bursts from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, we measure how the numbers of apparently single and repeating sources change with observing time, correcting for the declination-dependent, beam-weighted exposure and possible variations in the detection rate. Both source counts increase approximately linearly over 300--44,000~hr, as $N_{\rm s}\proptoΔt^{0.98\pm0.02}$ for single sources and $N_{\rm r}\proptoΔt^{1.06\pm0.14}$ for repeaters. Consequently, the observed repeater fraction remains nearly constant at $2.6^{+0.4}_{-0.6}\%$. We interpret these results using population models that account for a distribution of detected burst rates and temporal clustering. The source counts are reproduced by a population spanning a range of rates, including sources expected to produce approximately one detectable burst over the observing time. Its detected burst rates follow a distribution close to $r^{-2}$ over 0.01--1.5~hr$^{-1}$. The burst timing and burst multiplicities provide additional constraints. Among 77 repeaters, only 6 have their first two detected bursts within a single CHIME transit, the median interval between them is 101 days, and 31 of the 52 repeaters with at least three bursts have five or more. These observations support this population and favor moderately clustered emission (Weibull shape $k\simeq0.5$) and active phases lasting months to about a year. Our results are consistent with both a single population of repeaters whose rate distribution steepens below the range probed by CHIME and a mixed population that includes genuinely one-off sources. Thus, the current data do not require a one-off population, but cannot exclude one. Longer observing baselines are needed to distinguish these possibilities.

title: Keep Images in Sight: Visual Position Re-Anchoring for Long-Context MLLMs
abstract: Long-context multimodal intelligence requires revisiting earlier images as conversations and documents accumulate, yet retaining an image does not guarantee reliable access to its details. By varying context length, redistributing a fixed text passage around the image, and changing positions without adding text, we identify the positional relation between images and questions as a direct influence on visual access. To address this gap, we propose Visual Position Re-Anchoring (VPR), a training-free method that shifts cached visual-key rotary phases toward a short-context reference before question processing. It operates directly on the existing KV cache, preserving standard attention computation without extracting attention maps or adding model forward passes. We develop static and continuous compensation schedules, using the static schedule by default. Across ten checkpoints and ten benchmarks, static VPR improves 97 of 100 model--task scores. Further analysis shows greater attention to regions containing answer evidence across six checkpoints, with minimal runtime overhead under fixed rotary frequencies. These findings demonstrate an efficient way to sustain visual access through positional adjustment within the cache.

title: CFGComposer: Compositional Audio-Text-to-Motion Generation via Copula Score Correction
abstract: Generating whole-body gestures that are simultaneously rhythmically synchronized with speech audio and semantically aligned with text descriptions is a fundamental challenge in embodied AI and social robotics. We tackle this Audio-Text-to-Motion (AT2M) problem by composing two independently-trained diffusion models at inference time and refine bias in joint inference by modeling the copula score $s_I$. A rigorous theoretical analysis reveals that naive epsilon blending corresponds to a Product-of-Experts formulation that omits the copula score $s_I$: the cross-modal interaction between audio and text that neither marginal model can capture. We propose CFGComposer: a jointly-trained AT2M diffusion model that estimates $s_I$ via a CFG analogy and injects it as an $ε$-space correction. Experiments on BEAT demonstrate best-in-class semantic fidelity (SRGR $0.9916$, FID $27.18$) with GT-level beat alignment (BA $0.1826$ vs. GT $0.1743$), and 76-83% win rate in blind pairwise human evaluation against all prior methods. Physical deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid confirms direct sim-to-real transfer.

title: One Fabrication Is Enough: A Fake News Article Changes the Forecasts of LLM Forecasting Systems
abstract: LLMs are increasingly used for forecasting, and the best forecasting systems retrieve news as evidence to strengthen their predictions. This also opens them to attack. We study the weakest attacker of this kind, who knows only the forecasting question and publishes fabricated news articles, with no access to the model, the retriever or its queries. We evaluate how far this attack reaches on stock questions and real prediction-market questions. Once the article is in the model's context, it reverses 74% to 82% of the forecasts that opposed it, on every frontier model we tested. The model cannot verify the fabrication and follows it anyway. Retrieval is the attack's entry point, and the systems built to retrieve well are the most exposed: the architectures of two leading deployed forecasting systems, whose agents search for every related article, retrieve the fabricated one in about 90% of runs. Accuracy cannot reveal this harm: the attacked forecaster is right when the attacker's direction turns out right and wrong otherwise, so its average accuracy barely changes while its forecasts follow the attacker's guess. We also propose a second attacker, who publishes two articles that argue opposite directions to make the forecaster unsure. The model does not hedge; it returns a confident forecast in a direction the attacker no longer controls. We then evaluate the two strongest published retrieval-time defenses, passage filtering and partitioned retrieval. Each stops the one-article attack but is bypassed by a one-prompt change to the attack. Together they stop both bypasses at four articles, but sixteen distorted copies beat them, and they change 29% of clean decisions and discard 39% of the genuine news. Partitioned retrieval also requires control of the retrieval index. Systems that search the open web have no such control and are left with the filter alone. For them, the attack still works.

title: Solvability of $L^2$-Neumann Problems for Fractional Laplace Equations on Bounded Lipschitz Domains
abstract: Let $n\geq2$, $s\in(0,1)$, and $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. In this paper, we study the solvability of the fractional Neumann problem \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{aligned} (-Δ)^su&=0 & & \text{in}\ \ Ω,\\ \mathcal{N}_s u&=g & & \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ, \end{aligned}\right. \end{equation*} with $\mathcal{N}_s$ denoting the nonlocal normal derivative in $\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ$ and $g:=a_sq$, where $a_s(z):=(1-s)\frac{δ(z)^{-s}}{1+δ(z)^{n+s}}$ with $δ(z):=\mathrm{dist\,}(z,\partialΩ)$ for any $z\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ$, and $q\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,a_s\,dz)$ satisfies $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ}a_sq\,dz=0$. For the weak solution $u$, we obtain the non-tangential maximal function estimate \begin{equation*} \left\|\left(δ^{1-s}|\nabla u|\right)^*\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)} \leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)}, \end{equation*} where, for any function $f$ on $Ω$, $f^\ast$ denotes the non-tangential maximal function of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ$.
