A reference-grouped split reduced copying to 0.119; a rerun on 374 units in 118 independent target groups found no statistically distinguishable memory effect (0.005 [-0.003, 0.017]) and no policy effect. A separate Oracle-grounded evaluation on 216-224 real PL/SQL units showed that 10-22% of PostgreSQL-accepted units were behaviorally incorrect; a human-gated fix cycle increased demonstrably correct units from 98/216 to 167/224. A write-back study showed a 54% decline in retrieval margin as the knowledge base grew from 12 to 1,200 entries. We derive six evaluation rules that distinguish cross-task learning from reference leakage, copying, metric artifacts, and unstable feedback.

title: Fast circular convolution with periodic kernels
abstract: We study the periodic circular convolution or PCC, where the convolution kernel depends periodically on the spatial location. We introduce two fast algorithms to compute the PCC that rely on the Discrete Fourier Transform. One of the algorithms reveals that the matrix representation of the PCC is unitarily equivalent to a block diagonal matrix, which facilitates the analysis of PCCs and operations such as their product and inversion. We present two sample applications. One to deconvolve the action of an optical system whose point spread function depends periodically in space. The second is to compute dispersion relations for a periodic chain of masses.

title: Congruences Modulo 16, 32 and 64 for a Restricted Overpartition Function
abstract: Let $\overline{t}^{(3)}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ in which consecutive parts differ by a multiple of $3$ unless the larger part is overlined, and the smallest part is overlined unless it is divisible by $3$. Using dissections of theta functions, we establish two infinite families of congruences modulo $32$ and $64$. We also obtain two residue formulas modulo $16$ and use them to derive four further infinite families of congruences modulo $16$. In particular, for every positive integer $M$ and nonnegative integer $n$, the residue of $\overline{t}^{(3)}(M^2(18n+12))$ modulo $16$ is $8$ if $6n+4$ is a square and $0$ otherwise.

title: Two-Stage Secret Sharing
abstract: We give an information-theoretic formulation of two-stage secret sharing for situations in which secret information becomes available progressively. In the proposed model, shares for an initial part of the secret are distributed before the remaining part becomes available, and additional shares are distributed to new participants after the remaining part becomes available, without updating the shares already distributed and without using any additional information other than shares. To characterize this setting, we propose the notion of a two-stage access structure and provide its characterization. We further quantify the amount of information about the first-stage secret that the dealer must retain between the two distribution stages, derive a universal lower bound, and present a construction that achieves this bound for every two-stage access structure. We also position advance sharing as a special case of the proposed model and give its characterization and a related construction in classical information-theoretic secret sharing.

title: Humidity-modulated Ostwald Step Rule in $\rm FAPbI_3$ Martensitic Transitions
abstract: Experimental observations reveal a dual role of moisture in $\rm FAPbI_3$ phase transitions. During fabrication at high temperatures, humidity improves the quality of the perovskite ($α$ phase) films, whereas at low service temperatures, humidity accelerates degradation of the photoactive $α$ phase into the photo-inactive hexagonal $δ$ phase. Despite extensive experimental evidence, the microscopic mechanisms by which moisture modulates phase stability and transition pathways remain unknown. Here, using large-scale atomistic simulations powered by an ab initio machine-learned potential, we reproduce the experimentally observed increase in the $δ$-to-$α$ transition temperature under increased humidity. Our simulations reveal a layered metastable intermediate along the Burgers transition pathway that exhibits a strong affinity for water. The competing water uptake of this intermediate and the $δ$ phase governs the humidity dependence of transition kinetics. These findings elucidate the dual role of moisture in perovskite phase transitions and demonstrate how environmental species can stabilize metastable intermediates and reshape transition pathways, providing an environment-dependent perspective on Ostwald's step rule.

title: Calibrated Early Termination with Bounded Optimality Gaps for Constrained Vector Search
abstract: Vector search over learned embeddings is the retrieval layer of recommendation and retrieval-augmented generation, and many applications cap how many answer items one category may contribute. Graph indexes answer a query by best-first traversal, and where it stops determines its cost and whether its answer is exact. We study early termination for such constrained $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) queries, with plain $k$-NN as a special case, and seek the cheapest stopping rule whose answer is exact with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$. Learned early-termination methods instead target average recall, which does not guarantee exact answers. Multiple testing can calibrate any parameterized stopping rule to our target, but it cannot tell how much a better rule with the same risk and observations would save. Answering this needs a lower bound on the optimum of a rule family too large to enumerate, valid for the query population. Our key idea is to declare the observations a rule may use and to consider every rule monotone in them. Risk-constrained stopping then becomes a linear program over an order polytope, whose Lagrangian minimizers form a nested chain of staircase rules computed exactly by dynamic programming. Fixed-sequence binomial tests along this chain calibrate our rule, CaST, whose failure probability is at most $\varepsilon$ with confidence $1-δ$. Lagrangian weak duality bounds the optimum of the declared class from below at all risk levels at once, without a union bound over the rules. On two datasets of one million items each, CaST replayed on logged searches costs at most 1.132 times the class optimum for risk levels from 0.03 to 0.10, at 95% joint confidence per setting. Larger savings thus need a rule outside the class. At a common risk target on held-out queries, CaST is faster than every other calibrated rule we time, which take 4.8% to 45.5% more mean time.

title: HyperPage: Learned Page Layouts for Disk-Resident Graph Vector Indexes
abstract: Disk-resident graph indexes such as DiskANN store each vector with its graph edges as one record on SSD pages. A search needs the page of every record it expands, so its page reads depend on the page layout, that is, which records share a page. Search agents trained with reinforcement learning query one such index run after run, and every graph traversal can be logged with the records it expands. We therefore use the logs of a finished run to lay out the index for a declared memory budget, so later runs read fewer pages. In contrast, existing layouts such as Starling and MARGO are computed from the graph and vectors and use no logs. Learning a layout from logs is challenging, because the logs must stay valid under every layout, the saving depends on what the budget caches, and the best layout is NP-hard to find. Our key observation is that DiskANN-style search routes on in-memory codes and the records it expands, never on their page-mates. As a result, the logged traversals price every layout by replay, and cached records add no page reads. Accordingly, we propose HyperPage, which first builds layouts for the declared budget on the logged traversals of uncached records. It then selects one layout, together with the budget split between hot records and a page cache, by replaying validation steps. In addition, a Lagrangian lower bound shows how far a layout may be from the optimum. We learn from one Search-R1 agent run and test on a later run with a different reward, over 1M and 21M passages. Across seven cache budgets, HyperPage reads 5.2% to 21.2% fewer pages than MARGO, and no compared layout reads fewer. The advantage is largest when the cache is small. For example, at 1% of the 1M index, MARGO needs nearly 3 times the budget to read as few pages. On the 21M index, HyperPage also cuts search time per step by up to 10.4%. The saving holds for a second agent model and a second corpus.

title: Globular Clusters in the Time of JWST. II. Looks like the second, moves like the first: the syrphid-like intermediate population of NGC 2808
abstract: The present-day kinematics of multiple populations in globular clusters can retain information about their initial conditions and can therefore help trace how the different populations formed. We combine JWST and HST photometry and proper motions to study the internal dynamics of four populations in NGC 2808 out to about eight half-light radii: the first population (1P) and three second-population groups with increasing light-element processing (2Pa, 2Pb, and 2Pc), providing the first detailed kinematic characterisation of the chemically intermediate 2Pa. We find significant kinematic differences between the populations. While all four have similar sky-projected radial velocity dispersions, 2Pb and 2Pc have lower tangential dispersions than 1P and are strongly radially anisotropic, whereas 2Pa shares the only mildly anisotropic kinematics of 1P. Therefore, chemically distinct 2P groups have different dynamical properties, suggesting that they formed under different conditions and/or experienced a different subsequent dynamical evolution. In the outer JWST field, the velocity dispersion depends only weakly on stellar mass, with hints of inverted equipartition. The difference between radial and tangential equipartition is similar for 1P and 2Pa and decreases towards 2Pc, a trend that remains tentative given the uncertainties. Our results show that 2P is not a dynamically homogeneous group, and that the kinematics of its individual groups provide a key constraint for multiple population formation scenarios.

title: Fault Injection Attacks on Q-Learning: Analysis, Vulnerabilities, and Countermeasures
abstract: Hardware fault injection attacks threaten machine learning systems, yet their impact on reinforcement learning (RL) has received little attention despite the use of RL in safety-critical applications. This paper presents a security analysis of Q-Learning implementations under voltage and clock glitching attacks on a ChipWhisperer platform, evaluating five variants: Standard, Robust, Resilient, Linear, and Deep Q-Learning. In standard Q-Table implementations, faults corrupt reward computation, action selection, and Q-value updates during learning, and change the selected action during inference. Robust Q-Learning does not prevent these attacks: NaN and infinite values injected during learning persist in the Q-table, and its greedy policy uses the same code as standard Q-Learning. This paper also evaluates a Resilient Q-Learning variant that applies triple modular redundancy with majority voting. It corrects corruption of a single Q-table copy, but inputs shared by the copies, such as the reward, and the voting code itself remain outside its protection. The analysis extends to Linear and Deep Q-Learning, where faults corrupt stored weights during learning and change actions during inference. Moving beyond benchmark environments, this work evaluates an online traffic light controller in a microscopic traffic simulator, where a single injected infinite value degrades accumulated vehicle waiting time by 148x while corrupting under 4% of the Q-table, and where triple modular redundancy corrected the faults injected in our tests, although glitching could still halt the device. Altogether, this work provides a basis for understanding and securing RL deployments against fault injection attacks.

title: Bounded Metrics for Probability Measures on the Sphere
abstract: Directional distributions can have the same normalized mean direction while differing substantially in shape. Comparing them requires a distance whose response to geometric displacement and probability overlap matches the statistical question. We examine ten bounded metrics or metric families for probability measures on the sphere, scaling each to have maximum value one, covering transport, sliced transport, kernel and energy distances, and comparisons based on probability mass. We explain which metrics describe weak convergence, which admit Hilbert-space norm representations, and which pairs attain the maximum distance. Examples and counterexamples show how these distinctions affect empirical comparisons and numerical approximations. A summary table and relationship diagram support the choice of a distance. The discussion separates exact metrics from finite representations, unbiased estimators, and regularized transport costs.

title: Enumerating Pyranim Isomorphisms
abstract: We study a Nim-adjacent poset game, where chips are arranged in a pyramid and two players take turns removing chips that do not currently support chips to the upper-left and upper-right; upon removing this chip, all supported chips above are also removed. Play continues until the final chip is removed. We use a bijection between the game states, Dyck paths, and unit interval graphs to count the number of possible game states up to isomorphism.

title: Conditional Gaussian Limits and Character Laws for Randomized Symmetric-Group Representations
abstract: Let $ρ_n$ be a real orthogonal representation of the symmetric group $S_n$ of dimension $d_n\to\infty$, let $σ_n$ be a uniform random permutation, and let $O_n$ be an independent Haar-orthogonal matrix. We study the linear statistics $\operatorname{Tr}(A_nO_nρ_n(σ_n)O_n^T)$ for deterministic real test matrices $A_n$ normalized only in Frobenius norm, which allows tests that isolate individual entries. Conditionally on $σ_n$, the statistic has mean $s_nχ_n(σ_n)$, where $χ_n$ is the character of $ρ_n$ and $s_n=d_n^{-1}\operatorname{Tr} A_n\to s$. We show that the centered statistic has conditional Gaussian limit $N(0,1-s^2)$ for every such test if and only if the trivial and sign constituents of $ρ_n$ occupy $o(d_n)$ dimensions, and that this limit is asymptotically independent of every convergent $σ_n$-measurable observable. The key input is a tensor-square estimate, based on the Frobenius-Schur identity and the minimum degree of non-linear irreducible representations of $S_n$, which shows that this single condition controls both normalized traces needed in the Haar-conjugation argument. For the uncentered statistic, convergence in distribution of $χ_n(σ_n)$ to a law $Ξ$ is necessary and sufficient for every test statistic to converge to $sΞ+\sqrt{1-s^2}G$, with $G$ standard Gaussian and independent of $Ξ$. For every irreducible sequence with $d_n\to\infty$, finitely many entries scaled by $\sqrt{d_n}$ have independent standard Gaussian limits. Finally, we compute $Ξ$ explicitly for diagrams with a fixed first-row tail, their transposes, and diagrams with sublinear largest hook, answering in these cases a question of Tsou.

title: Accelerating Distributed Variational Quantum Computing over Wireless Networks with Incentive Mechanism Design
abstract: Distributed variational quantum computing (DVQC) appears as the emerging paradigm to address the limitations of near-term quantum devices by decomposing large parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) into smaller subcircuits executed across multiple quantum processors. In this context, how to incentivize quantum processors to participate actively is crucial for accelerating DVQC, yet remains largely unexplored in the literature. To address this significant gap, we propose a novel two-stage incentive framework for wireless DVQC. In the first stage, we minimize processor-side energy cost via a joint optimization of subcircuit parameters, number of noise measurements, and transmit power, efficiently solved using block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA). In the second stage, we maximize aggregator-side system utility by selecting an optimal subset of processors based on their optimized energy costs derived from the first stage, formulating a non-convex combinatorial selection problem addressed using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Extensive numerical experiments on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that our DVQC framework achieves training and testing performance comparable to centralized quantum computing in terms of accuracy and loss, with similar convergence behavior on MNIST and slightly slower initial convergence on CIFAR-10. Moreover, our optimization approach consistently outperforms baseline schemes in energy efficiency and system utility, revealing a strong synergy between processor-level energy minimization and incentive-driven processor selection, where reduced energy costs directly enhances a processor's likelihood of selection and contributes to higher overall system utility.

title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
abstract: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $ζ(3), ζ(5), \dots, ζ(s)$, where $ζ$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.

title: the limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of erdős problem 521
abstract: We resolve Erdős Problem~521 by proving that the normalized real-root count $N_n/\log n$ of Rademacher polynomials almost surely has no limit. More generally, consider the Kac polynomials \[ P_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}ξ_jx^j \] with i.i.d.\ real coefficients of mean zero, variance one, and a finite absolute exponential moment. Let $N_n$ denote the number of distinct real roots of $P_n$. We prove that, almost surely, \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π+C_*, \] and the set of subsequential limits is exactly \[ \left[\frac1π,\;\frac1π+C_*\right]. \] Here $C_*>1/π$ is a constant uniquely determined by an equation. The lower-limit identity remains valid under the weaker assumption that $\mathbb{E}|ξ_0|^{2+δ}<\infty$ for some $δ>0$.

title: PolicySniff: Inferring Agent Policy States through Shared-GPU Execution
abstract: LLM agents apply approval settings, such as whether to ask before a consequential tool call, through instructions in their system prompt, and operators keep these settings confidential by restricting access to prompts and responses. Audits check whether an agent obeys its setting, not whether a neighboring process can infer which setting is deployed. PolicySniff infers an agent's approval-policy state through shared-GPU execution. A co-resident attacker that knows the candidate settings and the task first profiles both settings, then times only its own GPU kernels while the agent processes the task. The policy prefix is cached before capture, so the attacker observes processing of a task suffix that is identical under both settings. On an eager sparse mixture-of-experts runtime, where each selected expert runs as separate work, a frozen and blinded study identified the deployed setting at 94.17% balanced accuracy on its primary estimand. Across all authorization conditions, accuracy was 88.82% on tasks for which both settings produce the same decision and 91.98% on tasks where they differ. Hardware replays of expert routing show that its temporal density and layer-and-bucket alignment carry the policy information. Behavioral compliance does not imply configuration confidentiality: deployments that keep their approval setting private should measure its distinguishability on the serving runtime and enforce authorization outside the model.

title: From Tokens to Behaviors: Rethinking Generative Recommendation for User Trajectory Prediction
abstract: User behavior trajectory prediction (UBTP) aims to capture how a user's needs evolve over time by predicting the sequence of future interactions from that user's interaction history. Recent generative recommendation (GR) methods address this task through autoregressive generation of semantic IDs (SIDs). However, serial SID decoding couples token generation with behavior state transitions and requires multiple dependent steps per interaction. Discrete item feedback overlooks predictive uncertainty, and teacher-forced training leaves a training-inference gap in trajectory generation. To address these limitations, we propose TraGR, a behavior-aware generative recommendation framework that aligns generation, feedback, and learning with successive user behaviors. Its behavior-level architecture predicts SID tokens in parallel within each interaction and models behavioral transitions through recurrent state updates, with joint SID and item-level supervision. Probability feedback combines the selected behavior with a probability-weighted summary of alternatives to guide subsequent predictions. Relation-aware trajectory learning incorporates collaborative transition signals and later credit assignment into training on model-generated trajectories. Experiments on four public datasets demonstrate that TraGR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across different prediction horizons. Code: https://github.com/CalmaQi/GR4UBT.

title: Contiguity of unions of perfect matchings and random regular uniform hypergraphs
abstract: For fixed integers $s\ge3$ and $r$ satisfying $\log(r!)>\frac{r(s-1)}s\log r$, the union of $r$ independent uniform perfect matchings of the complete $s$-uniform hypergraph is mutually contiguous to the uniform simple $r$-regular $s$-uniform hypergraph, as $n\to\infty$ through multiples of $s$. In particular, $r=\lceil e^s\rceil$ suffices. The main input is the sharp entropy inequality for random permutations of Bristiel and Caputo. It proves the global maximization needed for the second moment of the number of complete factorizations. The remaining calculation, including its lattice factor, matches the short-cycle contribution required by small-subgraph conditioning.\\ This is an expanded version of a proof provided by ChatGPT-Astra.

title: Emergence of Phonon Hydrodynamics as a Non-Hermitian Symmetry-Breaking Phase Transition
abstract: Phonon hydrodynamics enables collective heat flow beyond the classical diffusive limit and offers a promising route to controlling thermal transport in low-dimensional materials and nanoscale devices. However, quantitative criteria for determining when this hydrodynamic state emerges and where its boundaries lie remain a longstanding challenge in condensed matter physics. Here, we show that the onset of phonon hydrodynamics can be formulated as a non-Hermitian dynamical transition that converts microscopic phonon scattering properties into predictive boundaries for wavelike heat transport. Starting from the Peierls-Boltzmann transport equation, we derive an effective Schrodinger equation for the coupled dynamics of temperature and phonon drift fields, allowing the hydrodynamic regime to be identified directly from material transport properties. Within this framework, a pair of exceptional points quantitatively define the lower and upper boundaries of the hydrodynamic window, providing a critical design criterion beyond the qualitative scattering-rate inequalities proposed by Guyer and Krumhansl six decades ago. Furthermore, we derive an analytical criterion for the existence of hydrodynamic transport, showing that a finite hydrodynamic window can be supported only when the effective thermal diffusivity exceeds the phononic momentum diffusivity. Using ab initio phonon properties as inputs, our theory accurately captures the experimentally observed temperature- and length-dependent ultrafast second-sound dynamics. These results establish a symmetry-based framework for understanding collective energy transport and provide quantitative design principles for identifying the materials, temperatures, and characteristic length scales that support wavelike heat transport in low-dimensional materials and functional devices.

title: GOOSELoc: A Multimodal Benchmark for Ground-to-Aerial Localization in Unstructured Off-Road Terrain
abstract: Cross-view pose estimation estimates a ground camera's geographic pose by matching onboard sensor data with geo-referenced overhead imagery. This is particularly relevant when GNSS is unreliable, for example under forest canopy or in urban canyons. Existing metric cross-view benchmarks, such as VIGOR and cross-view KITTI, are dominated by urban and road scenes with strong human-made structure without off-road terrain. We introduce GOOSELoc, a multimodal benchmark for ground-to-aerial localization in unstructured environments, including forests, fields, and rural tracks. GOOSELoc comprises 9,356 scenes recorded across all four seasons around Munich, Germany, pairing geo-referenced aerial orthophotos with surround-view RGB imagery and 3D LiDAR point clouds. Paved/unpaved labels enable analyzing the impact of terrain structure, while the seasonal recordings allow studying the appearance gap to mostly summer-captured orthophotos. To assess the transferability of existing methods, we adapt and fine-tune four state-of-the-art cross-view localization baselines on GOOSELoc. Despite task-specific fine-tuning, the performance degrades substantially in off-road environments. We therefore propose a multimodal baseline combining surround-view imagery and LiDAR geometry, improving localization performance and providing a stronger reference for future work. Data and baselines are released at https://gooseloc.github.io.

title: Generative AI models for exploring diffusion dynamics from multi-frame particle tracking
abstract: Particle-based volumetric flow measurement techniques have proven their efficacy in quantitatively assessing the dynamic characteristics of unsteady flows within the realm of fluid mechanics. Despite recent advances in multi-frame particle tracking, an open challenge in this area is maintaining trajectories in temporally under-sampled 3D sequences, where inter-frame displacements are large. In this work, we develop DiffTR-Flow3D, a diffusion-based model that estimates flow motion from spatiotemporal three-dimensional particle recordings via a stochastic diffusion process. DiffTR-Flow3D conditions the diffusion process with both global and local particle dynamics and enhances flow estimation by leveraging historical particle trajectories. Extensive experiments, including numerical simulations and real-world measurements, demonstrate that DiffTR-Flow3D achieves state-of-the-art displacement estimation accuracy compared with learning-based flow estimators, and, when integrated into particle tracking pipelines, substantially improves their long-term tracking performance, while exhibiting robustness and generalization across diverse flow patterns. This work is expected to provide fluid researchers with an effective tool for the consistent and precise analysis of particle trajectories in temporally under-sampled 3D sequences with large inter-frame displacements.

title: Exact and Approximation Algorithms for Computing Smallest SESs and BMSs
abstract: Compression schemes represent repetitive strings compactly by using repeated substrings. Computing the minimum size of a representation of a given input string is important for compression and for understanding relationships between compression schemes, although this task is NP-hard for several schemes. In this paper, we introduce exact and approximation algorithms for finding smallest substring equation systems (SESs) and bidirectional macro schemes (BMSs). Specifically, for an input string of length $n$, we give deterministic and randomized algorithms for computing a smallest SES using $O^*(4^n)$ and $O^*(2^n)$ time and space, respectively. We also give a deterministic algorithm for computing a smallest BMS using $O^*(2^n)$ time and space. We further give deterministic and randomized $(1+α)$-approximation algorithms for smallest SESs using $O^*(4^{e^{-α}n})$ and $O^*(2^{e^{-α}n})$ time and space, respectively, for every $α\ge 0$. A conversion from SESs to BMSs gives $4(1+α)$-approximation algorithms for smallest BMSs with the same time and space bounds. All time bounds hold in the worst case, and the randomized algorithms return correct answers with high probability. Our algorithms adapt several approaches to exact and approximation algorithms for combinatorial problems, such as dynamic programming over determinant expansions and a greedy algorithm for monotone submodular functions.

title: Congruence density under sublattice inclusion
abstract: Gábor Czédli introduced congruence density and investigated how it changes under sublattice extensions. We prove that density cannot increase: if $S$ is a sublattice of a finite lattice $L$, then $\cd(L)\leq2^{-d}\cd(S)$, where $d$ is the larger of the increases in the numbers of join-reducible and meet-reducible elements. We also determine when equality holds: $\cd(L)=\cd(S)$ precisely when every element of $L\setminus S$ is comparable with every element of $L$. The theorem of Czédli and Szabó relating quasiorders to pairs of congruences gives the corresponding results for quasiorder density.

title: The ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR): Initial Data Release (DR1)
abstract: The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) has observed the northern sky observable from Palomar Observatory since March 2018, accumulating a median of a thousand photometric measurements across $gri$ for each of more than a billion sources. Among these billions of objects are millions of periodically variable stars, active galactic nuclei, stellar remnants, and substellar objects. We describe the initial data release (DR1) of the ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR) which provides image difference forced photometry, candidate periods, and variability metrics for approximately 1.3 billion sources in ZTF having an identification in Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (PS1). The data cover the 5.37 year interval between March 2018 and July 2023. ZVAR is sensitive to periods between 5 minutes and 2.7 years. We also describe tools for accessing the ZVAR data.

title: Admissibility of unbounded complexes of smooth representations
abstract: Let $G$ be a $p$-adic Lie group and $k$ a field of characteristic $p$. We prove that a complex of smooth $k$-representations of $G$ has admissible cohomology if and only if it is globally admissible, i.e., its hypercohomology with respect to a torsion-free open compact pro-$p$ subgroup is finite dimensional in every degree. This extends the bounded-below and bounded-above comparison of Schneider--Sorensen to arbitrary unbounded complexes.

title: A Universal Law for Horizon Formation in Black Hole Mergers
abstract: When two black holes merge, a common horizon appears around them as a single surface, which immediately splits into an outer and an inner one. We show that this event has a universal local form. Without any symmetry assumption, the two surfaces separate as $(t-t_*)^{1/2}$ along a single, everywhere positive mode and share a drift linear in $t-t_*$. Three numerical simulations, including an eccentric, precessing one, confirm the exponent to half a percent, and the reconstructed formation surface is marginally stable, as predicted.

title: Feature-Aware Edge Sampling for Approximate One-Step Laplacian Propagation
abstract: This paper studies how to approximate one-step combinatorial Laplacian messages in graph neural networks using edge sampling. We propose a spanning tree based hybrid sampler that combines feature-conditioned message scores and effective-resistance leverage scores, derive the expected one-step message error and obtain the optimal sampling probabilities and error frontier for a given expected edge budget. Preliminary experiments on synthetic community graphs show that message error decreases, while classification accuracy increases slightly, as the edge budget grows, and performance of the hybrid sampler is in between of optimal selection uniform random sampling. We leave multi-step propagation and evaluation on larger and real graphs for future work.

title: Rational contractions in quasi-Banach spaces: convergence, multiplicity of fixed points and applications
abstract: We study self-maps $f$ of a complete $b$-metric space $(U,d)$ (constant $b\ge1$) satisfying the rational contractive condition \[ d(fu,fv)\le\frac{d(u,fv)+d(v,fu)+κ}{b\,[d(u,fu)+d(v,fv)]+1}\,d(u,v)\qquad(u,v\in U), \] with $κ\in[0,1)$. We first observe that the two-parameter family of conditions studied in our earlier work reduces, after a rescaling of the $b$-metric, to this one-parameter form. We then prove: (A) every Picard sequence converges to a fixed point, with an explicit a~priori estimate whose geometric ratio depends only on $b$, $κ$ and $d(u_0,fu_0)$, an a~posteriori estimate, and asymptotic rate at most $κ$; (B) a structure theorem: such maps are automatically continuous, every fixed point attracts the whole ball of radius $(1-κ)/2$, distinct fixed points are at distance at least $(1-κ)/2$ (sharp), basins of attraction are clopen, and the number of fixed points does not exceed the number of connected components of $U$; in particular the fixed point is unique on connected spaces; (C) Ulam--Hyers stability of the fixed-point problem. The class of such maps is not invariant under passing from a quasi-norm to the equivalent $p$-norm metric, so the quasi-Banach results are not formal consequences of the metric ones. A gluing principle shows that the multiplicity permitted by (B) occurs. As applications we obtain existence, exact multiplicity and error estimates for infinite nonlinear systems with relay-type forcing in $\ell^p$, $0<p<1$, and for nonlinear perturbations of Volterra-type equations $f=\pm a+T_gf+ψ(f(z_0))k$ in the Hardy space $H^p$, $0<p<1$, where $T_gf(z)=\int_0^z f(ζ)g'(ζ)\,dζ$ and $g\in\BMOA$.

title: MRxD: A Usage-Pattern Framework for Mixed-Reality Cross-Device Interaction
abstract: Mixed reality (MR) cross-device experiences often combine MR headsets with non-immersive devices such as laptops, tablets, and phones. Yet such cross-device design remains challenging because users must coordinate workflows across heterogeneous devices with different roles. This motivates our focus on usage patterns: recurrent ways in which people distribute and coordinate work across devices. Through a systematic analysis of 238 MR cross-device papers, we developed MRxD, a usage-pattern framework organized around three dimensions: user attention, task relatedness, and cognitive symmetry. Using these dimensions, we identified six usage patterns and synthesized the design strategies commonly used within each pattern. We further investigated the framework's application in design practice through a workshop (n=6) and the results suggest that MRxD can guide pattern-based design exploration and identify blind spots. We further discuss how usage patterns may shift or combine, and outline research gaps and design implications for future MR cross-device systems.

title: Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction
abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is a critical semiconductor manufacturing process where material removal rate (MRR) is a key metric for process monitoring and advanced process control (APC). Virtual metrology enables MRR estimation from process time series signals, supporting run-to-run(R2R) control and process optimization while reducing reliance on physical metrology. Existing approaches typically rely on simplified linear assumptions or require handcrafted feature engineering. In this paper, we propose Global Regression Pretraining(GREP), a self-supervised, attention-based framework for CMP MRR prediction. GREP learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression, followed by supervised fine-tuning for MRR estimation. The framework is evaluated against a feature-engineered supervised baseline under three conditions: limited labeled data, sensor noise, and temporal process drift. Experiments on the PHM 2016 CMP dataset demonstrate competitive performance under limited labeled-data conditions, with improvements in selected cases and performance largely comparable to the baseline across different labeled-data fractions. Both models exhibit relatively small changes in prediction error with increasing noise, while GREP achieves a 17.0% RMSE reduction in the final temporal interval.

title: Between Niti and Nyaya: A Society-Centered Framework for AI Governance
abstract: Governments are making decisions about AI before they can measure its public effects, and those decisions determine whether a person can learn that AI influenced an outcome, challenge it, and see it corrected. Research has documented what AI governance produces: principles, strategies, registers, and audits. However, we lack shared language for understanding AI policy while it is still being made. We introduce the Society-Centered AI Governance Framework, which gives policymakers, researchers, and the public a way to assess instruments in any jurisdiction by whether a person can get notice, challenge a decision, and see it corrected. It reads a jurisdiction's instruments together by date and binding status, separates an agency duty from a right a person can invoke, and traces which later instrument must enforce each commitment. We evaluated it in North Carolina using interviews with nine AI Leadership Council members, conducted before and after the state's 2026 AI roadmap, and a provision-level reading, with human-reviewed model-assisted coding, of 49 AI governance documents from 19 states. For the state's own AI systems, we find visibility-first governance: visibility duties are in effect, notice exists as an agency duty with no right a person can invoke, and AI-specific challenge and correction remain advisory. The roadmap assigns owners and dates to the missing protections, so the gaps are documented but not yet closed. Recent federal preemption proposals focus on AI development, so recourse for a state's own systems is likely to remain a state decision. We identify "legitimacy before protection" as a testable risk of visibility-first governance and name the milestones that would test it. More broadly, judging AI policy by who can act on what it makes visible lets the field assess recourse while policy is still forming, before harm occurs.

title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories is a standard paradigm for training LLM agents. However, it suffers from a well-known training-inference distribution mismatch, calling for target-aware data synthesis strategies that ground the training data in the target model's native state distribution. To bridge this gap, emerging approaches incorporate the expert either to guide mixed rollouts alongside the target model, or to provide dense step-wise supervision. Nonetheless, existing methods apply expert assistance blind to the target model's inherent behavior: they either disrupt the rollout using sub-optimal random intervention heuristics, or they enforce indiscriminate uniform supervision that unnecessarily overwrites the model's already-correct actions. We introduce JudgeMix, a judge-guided data synthesis framework that dynamically interleaves the target model and expert based on step-wise semantic evaluations. JudgeMix queries expert guidance precisely when the target model struggles, ensuring high trajectory success rates while keeping the state distribution aligned with the target model. It additionally uses the judge evaluation to reweight expert supervision on different steps, preserving model's inherent valid behavior while correcting its errors. On two agentic tool-use benchmarks, AppWorld and AutomationBench, JudgeMix demonstrates consistent superior performance to existing methods, with improvements up to 10 pass@1 points.

title: Stack more levels: how to get general and human-like Mario playing
abstract: Super Mario Bros. is widely used in game AI and procedural content generation (PCG), yet it remains unclear whether a model-free agent can reliably win unseen levels. To address this question, we train Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agents on increasingly large sets of PCG-generated Mario levels and evaluate their generalization on 1000 held-out test levels. We then shape competent PPO policies into three gameplay archetypes---runner, killer, and collector. Finally, we fine-tune these PPO policies using Diffusion-Reward Adversarial Imitation Learning (DRAIL) with human gameplay demonstrations. We find that increasing the number of distinct PCG-generated training levels generally improves unseen-level performance, and that fine-tuning PPO policies with DRAIL increases action-level human-likeness while preserving much of the persona induced by PPO pretraining.

title: A One-Sided Sublinear-Query Tester for Bounded-Degree 2SAT
abstract: We give a one-sided tester for satisfiability of 2CNF formulas in the bounded-degree model. For every degree bound $Δ$, distance parameter $\varepsilon>0$, and $ν\in(0,1/2)$, its query complexity on $n$-variable formulas is $\widetilde O_{\varepsilon,Δ,ν}(n^{1/2+ν})$.

title: Real-Time Low-Complexity Zak-OTFS with Superimposed Spread Pilots on GPUs
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation offers robust performance under high-mobility scenarios. Spread pilots distribute pilot energy across the delay-Doppler grid and are superimposed with data symbols, enabling full-grid resource utilization. However, pilot-data separation challenges the design of the real-time receiver pipeline: cross-ambiguity in channel sensing incurs high computational complexity, and pilot-data interference cancellation requires repeated processing through turbo iterations. Leveraging the chirp structure of OTFS spread pilots, we reduce cross-ambiguity to a single 2D IFFT with element-wise chirp operations, achieving over 7000x speedup compared to partially vectorized direct evaluation on GPUs at a frame size of (M, N)=(2053, 31). Our real-time GPU baseband processing pipeline for OTFS with superimposed spread pilots supports (M, N)=(2053, 31) with one turbo iteration within a 1.03 ms latency budget. We further show that larger frames increase processing gain, allowing lower pilot power and near-converged bit error rate (BER) after one turbo iteration.

title: Null designs and switching in polynomial spaces
abstract: Null designs are finite point configurations with real weights whose polynomial moments vanish up to a given degree. In Godsil's framework of polynomial spaces, we give elementary proofs of sharp lower bounds on the number of points in the Euclidean and spherical cases. We characterize the spherical null designs attaining the bound and give explicit formulas for their weights. We then study how null designs can be used to replace part of a weighted design while preserving its polynomial moments. We give conditions ensuring nonnegative weights and apply the minimum-size classification to switching on circles. Examples on spheres and in Hamming and Johnson spaces illustrate these results, including a replacement between noncongruent spherical $5$-designs that preserves equal weights and the number of points.

title: Concatenated Codes with One Inner Code: Low-Rate Gilbert-Varshamov Asymptotics from Algebraic-Geometric Codes
abstract: Constructing codes that attain the Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound while admitting efficient encoding and decoding is a fundamental problem in coding theory. We study concatenated codes that reuse a single binary inner code across all outer coordinates. To exploit existing encoding and decoding algorithms, we restrict the outer codes to random subcodes of scaled copies of prescribed algebraic codes and investigate their minimum distance. Our first contribution is a general upper bound on the minimum-distance failure probability that separates two terms controlled by the inner code's bias moments and the dual weight distribution of the prescribed code, together with sufficient conditions for exponential decay. Our second contribution is a concrete construction satisfying these conditions using algebraic-geometric codes from the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a family of random binary codes $C_m$ whose rates approach $\varepsilon^2$ and satisfy \[ \Pr\left[δ(C_m)\geq\frac12-\sqrt{\frac{\ln 2}{2}}\left(\varepsilon+\frac{\varepsilon^3}{2}\right)\right]\geq 1-2^{-c\varepsilon^4N_m}, \] for all sufficiently large $m$, where $N_m$ is the block length and $c>0$ is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $m$. Thus, the distance guarantee matches the leading coefficient of the GV bound at low rates. For each fixed $\varepsilon$, the construction uses a single inner encoding map throughout the family and admits polynomial-time encoding and unique decoding within a guaranteed radius. This answers the question of Doron, Mosheiff, and Wootters for subcodes of scaled algebraic geometry codes at low rates.

title: Fast Serverless LLM Cold Starts by Sharing and Prewarming Startup Work
abstract: When a serverless LLM platform launches a model worker on demand, the cold start lasts roughly a minute, yet only 5-11% of it is spent loading weights. Most of the remainder goes to compilation, memory profiling and runtime setup, which each server performs again even though the outcome is identical across servers or independent of the model. We present Cairn. The server that is first to start a model publishes the weights and engine artifacts to a CXL memory pool shared across the cluster, and the remaining servers read them in place. Model-independent setup is completed ahead of time inside warm containers, and a template process replaces each container as soon as it is used. With ServerlessLLM on vLLM v0.20, six models from 1B to 14B, and two servers that share an emulated CXL pool, Cairn speeds up cold starts by 4.1-5.2x on servers without a checkpoint of their own and reduces median TTFT on a request stream by 64%.

title: Holomorphic Sectional Curvature of Flag Manifolds via Kähler Reduction
abstract: We give an alternative proof of Li and Petersen's theorem that every invariant Kähler metric on a compact generalized flag manifold has positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For a unitary partial flag manifold, we realize the given metric by Kähler reduction of a Hermitian vector space. The defining equations place the level set on a sphere of radius \varrho, where the radial component of its second fundamental form gives the explicit lower bound 4/\varrho2 through the quotient curvature formula. Finally, we use a holomorphic isometric totally geodesic embedding to transfer the bound to generalized flag manifolds of every Lie type.

title: Same-State Pairs Make One JEPA Proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis Vacuous
abstract: In a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), the JEPA proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) assumes that every observation determines the world state and that a spectral gap makes minimizers unique up to rotation. Under the hard-whitening population objective, same-state positive pairs make the induced world kernel the identity: every centered whitened state function is a global minimizer, and, when $d_z-1\ge 2k$, two minimizers can have best-rotation squared residual $2k$. The uniqueness claim is conditional; for $k<d_z-1$, where $d_z$ is the number of world states, this limit makes its premise unsatisfiable, so the claim has no content there. The experiments that motivate it leave the assumption: a caption sees only part of an image, and the paper states no experiment meets its hypotheses exactly. The theorem does not reach those experiments, and for $k<d_z-1$ its idealized same-state limit is vacuous. One of the paper's four quantitative results survives: a gap-free lower bound. Its bound vanishes only at perfect scene-explained fraction; it bounds alignment error but cannot certify good-view alignment. A canonical frame is determined only up to a rotation and a latent permutation. Paired samples fix the relative frame at effective rank $k$; a global rotation remains. Component semantics fix the relative permutation only up to signs; value anchors fix it once the mixing frame is pinned. A resource--gauge ledger records which resource fixes which gauge.

title: Data-Efficient LLM Safety Alignment Guided by Interpretable Features
abstract: Existing large language models typically rely on massive fine-tuning datasets for safety alignment, which results in higher costs for safety alignment and often leads to the problem of over-refusal. We propose Less is Safer (LIS), a compact yet highly effective dataset for safety alignment, constructed through interpretable feature-guided selection and adversarial synthesis. Specifically, we leverage Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) activations to efficiently select prompts that cover diverse and interpretable safety features. Then, we employ a multi-agent adversarial synthesis framework to generate harmless prompts that nevertheless elicit unnecessary refusals. LIS contains only 2.4K samples, yet outperforms much larger datasets, e.g., TRIDENT-Core (26K), TRIDENT-Edge (19K) and WildJailbreak (262K), in overall performance on four safety and five over-refusal benchmarks. Through ablation experiments, we demonstrate that neither safety data nor over-refusal data alone can achieve optimal results. We also used safety features from SAE, annotated by an LLM, for data filtering, but the results were inferior to those obtained using the pipeline proposed in this paper.

title: Flow-CAD: Flow Matching for Contextual Anomaly Detection and Explanation in Tabular Data
abstract: Contextual anomaly detection in tabular data aims to identify objects whose behavior is unexpected under their contextual conditions. In data-engineering pipelines, this task screens table rows whose measurements violate context-dependent integrity relationships. Most existing approaches rely on either shallow conditional models with limited distributional expressiveness or localized estimators that require per-context modeling, making it difficult to capture complex conditional relationships and scale to high-dimensional settings. We propose Flow-CAD, a new framework for contextual anomaly detection based on Flow Matching. Flow-CAD learns a single global and amortized conditional generative model that flexibly represents behavioral distributions conditioned on context, without assuming simple parametric forms or retraining local models. To enable robust and interpretable anomaly scoring, we introduce a scale-normalized and truncated residual energy derived from the learned conditional flow, which stabilizes anomaly scores, mitigates domination by extreme deviations, and supports feature-wise attribution. We further provide theoretical insights showing that the proposed residual-based anomaly score is stable under velocity estimation error, and that its Monte Carlo estimator satisfies concentration bounds. Experiments on 20 benchmark datasets with 13 competitors demonstrate that Flow-CAD has the best average rank for PR AUC, ROC AUC, and P@n, highlighting its effectiveness and practicality for contextual anomaly detection in tabular data. We provide the source code at https://github.com/ZhongLIFR/FlowCAD.

title: Enabling Versatile Human Sensing through Wi-Fi Beamforming Feedback
abstract: Wi-Fi sensing enables contactless human sensing, while most existing systems rely on Channel State Information, which is accessible only on a limited range of Wi-Fi chipsets. In contrast, Beamforming Feedback Information (BFI) is standardized in modern Wi-Fi and readily accessible on a wide range of commodity devices, offering new opportunities for human sensing. In this paper, we present BeamLens, a Wi-Fi sensing system that extracts fine-grained spatial information from BFI to enable versatile human sensing. Specifically, we jointly estimate the angle of departure and relative time of flight from BFI to extract fine-grained spatial information and leverage two AP-STA links to capture complementary azimuth and elevation views. We further design a sparse physical antenna array and construct a uniform virtual antenna array to enhance spatial resolution. Moreover, we fuse complementary views through self-supervised learning, combining temporally aware cross-view contrastive learning and temporal masked reconstruction to learn a versatile backbone for diverse human sensing tasks. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that BeamLens achieves 90.16\% accuracy in human activity recognition, a mean per-joint position error of 8.64\,cm in 3D human pose estimation, and 70.64\% intersection over union in human silhouette estimation, while exhibiting strong generalization to unseen environments and subjects.

title: Counting doubly labelled trees and one-component networks
abstract: A phylogenetic network is one-component if the child of every reticulation is a leaf. This class of networks has been widely used as building blocks in the combinatorial study of phylogenetic networks. We establish a bijection between one-component networks on $k$ taxa and rooted binary multi-labelled trees in which every label occurs exactly twice. Using this bijection and Burnside's lemma, we derive a closed formula and a two-term recurrence for the number of one-component networks. We further obtain explicit formulas for counting one-component networks with a prescribed number of reticulations.

title: Holographic Counterterms from Restricted Weyl Symmetry in Even-Dimensional Einstein-AdS Gravity
abstract: We develop a symmetry-based approach to renormalization for even-dimensional Einstein-AdS gravity based on infinitesimal bulk Weyl transformations that preserve its field equations asymptotically. We determine a bulk-covariant completion of the Einstein-Hilbert density by requiring its variation under restricted Weyl transformations with parameter $Σ(X)$ to vanish modulo terms whose integrals remain finite as the radial cutoff is removed. This requirement induces two types of compensating terms with fixed couplings: the Euler density and a hierarchy of covariant total derivatives. The resulting recursive relations admit a factorized solution in terms of shifted Laplacians, yielding a closed-form completion in arbitrary even bulk dimensions. On Einstein backgrounds, these expressions agree, after matching normalizations, with those obtained through the ambient construction of conformal invariants. The associated renormalized-volume identity establishes on-shell finiteness for Euclidean AlAdS Einstein geometries in arbitrary even dimensions. The prescription reproduces the known conformally renormalized actions in four, six and eight dimensions and provides an explicit ten-dimensional completion involving powers of the Laplacian up to $\Box^3$. Applications to eight- and ten-dimensional AdS black holes with non-conformally-flat Einstein horizons yield finite on-shell actions in agreement with Holographic Renormalization.

title: PERA: Plug-in Experts for Robotic Actions in Continual Whole-Body Control
abstract: Motion imitation enables humanoid robots to acquire whole-body skills such as walking and dancing. However, fine-tuning an entire policy for a new skill can affect existing behaviors, while training a separate policy for each skill increases training and maintenance costs. We present PERA, a method for learning new skills by reusing existing motion capabilities. PERA freezes a pretrained mixture-of-experts policy and trains an additional task expert and its routing score using task rewards or teacher-action supervision. In Unitree G1 simulation, each added task module contains approximately 1.03% of the parameters of the base actor. Built on our pretrained policy, PERA successfully completes all ten new tasks. Disabling the expert restores the original computation path of the base policy, which still fully executes all 126 original motions. Enabling the expert also improves the execution of some dance motions not used to train that expert, indicating that its benefits extend beyond its training motions. Experiments with HoloMotion further demonstrate the applicability of PERA to different base policies.

title: SBA: A Practical Memory Performance Denial-of-Service Attack
abstract: Modern cloud platforms use memory bandwidth regulation to isolate co-located workloads, implicitly assuming that high aggregate bandwidth consumption implies high interference. We show that this assumption is fundamentally flawed. We present the Single-Bank Attack (SBA), a practical memory denial-of-service attack that induces extreme cross-core slowdowns---over three orders of magnitude on memory-intensive victims (e.g., LLM decode)---while consuming less than 1 GB/s of memory bandwidth. SBA exploits the gap between peak and worst-case DRAM throughput by concentrating memory write operations on a single bank, forcing persistent row conflicts and frequent write draining, thereby collapsing the memory service rate. Across Intel and AMD systems, including DDR5- and HBM2E-based platforms, SBA consistently causes orders-of-magnitude slowdowns under realistic multi-tenant settings, revealing a fundamental limitation of bandwidth-centric memory isolation. We further show that this localized contention propagates system-wide: single-bank congestion saturates memory controller queues and induces back-pressure into shared cache and coherence structures, ultimately throttling memory request injection across cores. Consequently, severe interference can arise even at low aggregate bandwidth, evading existing bandwidth-based QoS mechanisms such as Intel RDT MBA. To address this limitation, we propose IQ-MemGuard, a lightweight, software-based memory bandwidth regulator that detects sustained contention using microarchitectural signals and selectively throttles pathological request injection. Our implementation on an Intel platform effectively mitigates SBA, whereas Intel's hardware QoS mechanism fails completely.

title: When can an interpretability claim be trusted? Stability and certification of feature dimensionality, ridge leverage and the feature recovery rate
abstract: Interpretability tools increasingly support safety claims, such as that a sparse dictionary has recovered most of a model's features. Such claims rest on measurements with arbitrary thresholds, and small changes to the model weights, a different training seed or a different threshold can reverse them. We study two widely used measurements in toy models and synthetic dictionaries with known ground truth: the feature dimensionality of Elhage et al. and the feature recovery rate (FRR) with a cosine threshold. We characterize exactly where feature dimensionality is discontinuous and replace it with a regularized (ridge) version with sharp stability bounds: the ridge leverage score changes by at most $3\sqrt{3}/(8\sqrtλ)$ times the operator-norm change of the weights, and this constant cannot be improved; for the regularized dimensionality the stability constant grows like $ρ/4$ in the scale $ρ=R/\sqrtλ$, with explicit upper and lower bounds. We also prove certificates stating when a claim "feature $i$ is recovered" must survive a given change of the dictionary. The certificates held in every test and are informative for small perturbations, but certify no feature non-trivially across independently trained dictionaries; at the standard threshold, whether a feature counts as recovered changed with the training seed for 55 percent of features. Experiments use toy models only. The proofs, code and text were drafted by AI agents directed by the authors and checked by an independent blind AI reviewer and by numerical tests; the authors take full responsibility for the content.

title: Connecting Electroweak Fine-Tuning, Tens-of-GeV Dark Matter, and Exotic Higgs Decays in the GNMSSM
abstract: In the general next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model (GNMSSM), we connect electroweak fine-tuning, a singlino dark matter candidate with mass around tens of GeV, and Exotic Higgs Decays, identifying a natural region characterized by the mass hierarchy $m_{\tilde{S}}<m_{\tilde{B}}<m_{\tilde{H}}$ and $μ_{\rm tot}\in [200, 500]$ GeV. For fine-tuning measure $Δ\leq 40$, the branching ratio $\mathrm{Br}(h\to a_sa_s)$ falls in the range 7\%$-$25\%, with the pseudoscalar mass $m_{a_s}$ lying mostly between 10 and 20 GeV. This region splits into two viable scenarios consistent with LZ 2024 direct detection: one where the lightest CP-even Higgs $h_1$ is SM-like ($h_1$ case), and another where the second-lightest $h_2$ is SM-like ($h_2$ case). LHC searches for $h\to a_sa_s \to b\bar{b}τ^+τ^-$ exclude 12\% (10\%) of samples with 12 GeV $\leq m_{a_s} \leq$ 15.5 GeV in the $h_1$ ($h_2$) case, while a substantial fraction remains accessible at the HL-LHC in the $h_2$ case. Our analysis unifies naturalness, dark matter, and observable exotic Higgs decays, yielding concrete targets for future experiments.

title: Weak Composition Theorems for Randomized Communication
abstract: We present two results towards the randomized communication complexity of composed functions. Our contributions include: - \textbf{Lifting-by-Influence.} For any binary function $f$ and any outer gadget $g:\{0,1\}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, we show that up to additive terms, computing $g \circ f^n$ information-theoretically requires solving at least $\operatorname{Inf}(g)$ instances of $f$, where $\operatorname{Inf}(g)$ denotes the total influence of $g$. To our knowledge, this is the first composition lower bound for randomized communication that applies to \emph{every} choice of $f$ and $g$. - \textbf{Symmetric Composition.} When $g$ is a symmetric function with a value transition at Hamming weight $d$, we strengthen the number of required instances to $\min\{d,n+1-d\}$. As an implication, this recovers the previously known direct-sum theorem, XOR lemma, and majority lemma. Our proofs develop novel and distinctive usages of the classical \emph{input embedding} argument of Barak, Braverman, Chen, and Rao (SICOMP 2013). As an additional ingredient, we introduce a new public sampling framework that avoids auxiliary communication during the recovery phase of the protocol, ultimately reducing the extra cost from $O(n)$ bits of information to just $O(1)$.

title: Local Intensity-based Correction for SMFT Longitudinal Magnetograms: Validation with SDO/HMI Observations
abstract: The Solar Magnetic Field Telescope (SMFT) at Huairou Solar Observing Station (HSOS) derives photospheric magnetic fields from single-wavelength Stokes measurements using a linear calibration based on the weak-field approximation. In sunspot umbrae, this linear approach systematically underestimates the true magnetic field strength---a well-known effect of magnetic underestimation. To mitigate this bias, we apply the Local Intensity-based Correction (LIC) as implemented in the standard HSOS data reduction procedure and validate its performance against SDO/HMI full-disk longitudinal magnetograms that are co-temporal and co-spatial with the SMFT observations for 26 active regions observed in 2019 and 2024. Pixel-level alignment between SMFT images ($992\times830$, $0.242^{\prime\prime}$~pixel$^{-1}$) and HMI snapshots ($4096\times4096$, $0.505^{\prime\prime}$~pixel$^{-1}$) is achieved using SIFT feature matching and RANSAC-based homography estimation, yielding inlier fractions of 40\% to 88\%. The LIC correction consistently improves the Pearson correlation coefficient $r$ with respect to HMI for all these 26 regions, with a mean improvement of $Δr = +0.041$ and a maximum of $Δr = +0.197$ for AR24114 (NOAA 13667). Residual discrepancies persist in the most severely underestimated pixels, highlighting an inherent limitation of any single-wavelength linear calibration. Nevertheless, our results demonstrate that the LIC correction is a robust and effective preprocessing step, and we recommend its routine application in quantitative analyses of SMFT longitudinal magnetograms.

title: GA-HEL: A Knowledge-Driven Expert System for Open-Set, Granularity-Aware Hierarchical Event Linking in Social Media
abstract: Social-media event intelligence requires a system to determine whether a post belongs to a registered event space, identify the supported hierarchy path, and stop at the deepest level warranted by the evidence. We formulate this requirement as open-set hierarchical event linking over frozen Storyline--Episode--Atomic Event Cards. GA-HEL implements a three-stage, knowledge-driven expert-system funnel: open-set scope control limits candidate exposure before hierarchical reasoning, hierarchy-aware decoders select a supported path and depth, and deterministic legal-path validation checks each record before database-compatible use. A 200-post Pilot supports task and mechanism development, while a separately annotated 497-post Expansion set evaluates transfer across four held-out Storylines and a hard-negative pool. Method implementations, prompts, Event Cards, candidate order, and six systems' predictions were frozen before Expansion Gold annotation. The resulting evaluation combines end-to-end hierarchical matching, open-set rejection, structural validation, ablation, cross-Storyline analysis, and an independent expert reannotation of a fixed audited subset. GA-HEL remains competitive with strong global full-card reasoning while providing explicit scope control and hierarchy-valid structured records. Error analysis identifies unsupported descent from Episode-level evidence to Atomic Events as the dominant remaining challenge. The task definition, frozen resource, and auditable protocol provide a reproducible foundation for scope-aware event intelligence. Code, Event Cards, labels, frozen predictions, and evaluation scripts are available at https://github.com/SHbiao/GAHEL_release.

title: Asymptotic analysis of infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with squared Bessel arrival intensity
abstract: This paper introduces a model for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with stochastic intensity given by a squared Bessel (BESQ) process. Exploiting the affine structure of the underlying dynamics, we derive a closed-form expression for the joint moment-generating function (MGF) of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval. The asymptotic properties of the model are also analysed. We establish laws of large numbers, central limit theorems, large deviation principles, and moderate deviation principles for several quantities of interest. More precisely, these results are obtained for three important settings: cumulative occupancy over a finite time interval, system occupancy under a diverging long-run mean arrival intensity, and the superposition of independent infinite-server queues with Cox-BESQ arrival intensities. Numerical experiments illustrate the associated rate functions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the resulting rare-event approximations.

title: Evidence of anisotropic surface state residual loss in UTe$_2$ amid isotropic low-energy excitations
abstract: We explore the pairing mechanism and possible topological properties of the unconventional superconductor UTe$_2$ through their influence on both the inductive and resistive channels using resonant cavity perturbation techniques. We measure a composite surface impedance for a variety of UTe$_2$ single crystals at microwave frequencies, where the inductive and resistive channels are comparable and can be treated on equal footing. By studying the composite electrodynamics for a large number of resonant modes, we are able to provide a comprehensive picture of the directional dependence of the excitations out of the ground state. We find similar power-law temperature dependencies at low-temperature for both the penetration depth and surface resistance, which in aggregate across modes, are quadratic and isotropic. On the other hand, we find a distinct and systematic anisotropy of the residual loss. The power-law results are inconsistent with a single pair of point nodes on the Fermi surface under weak scattering. We discuss the possibility of topological superconductivity as an interpretation of these isotropic power-laws in conjunction with the anisotropic residual loss.

title: Mechanical behaviour of the intact brain-skull interface under tension, compression and shear
abstract: The brain-skull interface governs the boundary/contact conditions of the brain in computational head models, yet its mechanical behaviour remains poorly characterised experimentally. We characterised the brain-skull interface by testing brain-skull complex samples (skull bone, meninges and brain tissue in their native arrangement) excised from 19 sheep cadaver heads under uniaxial tension and compression at strain rates of 0.002, 0.02 and 0.2 s$^{-1}$ and simple shear at 0.02 s$^{-1}$. Histology confirmed that the meningeal layers remained intact and attached to the brain and skull after excision. We acquired magnetic resonance images of every sample, reconstructed their geometry and developed a sample-specific finite element model of each experiment. We represented the brain tissue using a second-order Ogden hyperelastic model and the brain-skull interface using a cohesive zone model. Using inverse finite element analysis, we first calibrated the brain tissue parameters for each subject. Keeping these parameters fixed, we then identified the interface parameters from the corresponding brain-skull complex specimen. The brain tissue shear modulus increased with strain rate from 0.94 $\pm$ 0.16 kPa at 0.002 s$^{-1}$ to 1.60 $\pm$ 0.30 kPa at 0.2 s$^{-1}$. In contrast, the interface properties (maximum normal traction 2.35 $\pm$ 0.81 kPa, maximum tangential traction 4.14 $\pm$ 0.97 kPa, and fracture energy 0.35 $\pm$ 0.14 N m$^{-1}$) showed no significant dependence on strain rate or loading mode. In all samples, failure occurred within the subarachnoid space. Neither a rigid brain-skull connection nor frictionless sliding contact with separation reproduced the measured mechanical response or failure mode of the brain-skull interface. Our experimentally derived cohesive zone model provides a realistic representation of the brain-skull interface for computational head models.

title: "We Are the Dirty Hands": Reimagining an Ambient Intelligence Care System with Professional Caregivers
abstract: While ambient assisted living (AAL) sensing systems offer promise for aging in place, their impacts on professional caregivers are overlooked. We conducted two collective speculation workshops (N=24) with personal health aides (PHAs, n=18) and certified nursing assistants (CNAs, n=6) to examine the ethical implications and value tensions of a care system with ambient intelligence (CSAI), our conceptualization of an AAL. Participants anticipated different implications across care roles and settings. PHAs anticipated additional responsibilities from CSAI, including learning how it operates and supporting older adults in its use. CNAs, who had greater access to workplace resources and protections, similarly noted that CSAI could create additional work. Participants also identified tensions around visibility, as sensing could support caregivers by documenting difficult working conditions while simultaneously making their behavior more vulnerable to misinterpretation. Through their modifications and surfaced discussions, we propose design guidelines for AAL systems, such as integrating context-aware sensing.

title: Testing Density Discontinuity Using Spacings
abstract: In the regression discontinuity design, researchers assess the credibility of assumptions by testing the running variable's density for a discontinuity at the cutoff. This paper proposes a novel such test. The test uses q spacings on each side of the cutoff, where spacings are the widths between ordered observations. Spacings yield a continuous statistic that behaves well under weak assumptions. I study its properties in two asymptotic frameworks: one where q is fixed as the sample size increases and one where q slowly diverges to infinity. With q fixed, the test achieves exact asymptotic size control without user randomization. When q increases slowly, the test becomes consistent without sacrificing exact asymptotic size. Compared to the preferred version of Bugni and Canay's (2021) test, the only other test with comparably weak assumptions, this test reduces sensitivity to the tuning parameter and performs similarly when theirs is well-chosen.

title: Proliferating against the current: how multistep branching nucleation can sort microtubule polarity in the spindle
abstract: The spindle, which segregates chromosomes during cell division, is a paradigm of cytoskeletal self-organization: a highly ordered structure that persists for hours is assembled from dynamic microtubules that branch, grow, slide, and turn over within tens of seconds. Its microtubules point inward, with minus ends clustered at the poles and plus ends extending toward the chromosomes at the center of the structure. In large meiotic spindles this arrangement is puzzling, since microtubules nucleate near the chromosomes and grow at their plus ends much faster than motors slide them backward. One would therefore expect the plus ends, rather than the minus ends, to radiate outward. Here, we propose a resolution to this seeming paradox through a kinetic model that integrates the core filament-level processes. When branching complexes assemble with a sufficient delay, for instance through several sequential rate-limiting steps, they accumulate on old microtubule lattice sites near the backward-sliding minus ends of mother microtubules. Each generation is then born farther back than the last, so the self-renewing population drifts toward the minus ends even though each filament's center advances toward its plus end. For the sliding and growth velocities measured in Xenopus egg extract spindles, a multistep mechanism requires at least four rate-limiting steps. The kinetic theory has a surprisingly amenable structure: the filament length configuration variable can be eliminated exactly, yielding a finite space-time hierarchy, and the direction of population drift follows from a general criterion comparing the mean lattice age at branching sites with the ratio of plus-end advance to sliding speed.

title: An Extensive Evaluation of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches for Sentiment Analysis: Insights from Amazon Customer Reviews
abstract: The rapid growth of user-generated text on online platforms creates opportunities for understanding customer opinion and supporting data-driven decisions. This study compares five traditional machine learning classifiers (Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Bernoulli Naive Bayes, Linear Support Vector Classifier, and Multinomial Naive Bayes) and six deep learning architectures (LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU, RNN, Attention, and FastText) for three-class sentiment classification of 568,454 Amazon Fine Food Reviews. Machine learning models used Bag-of-Words (BoW) and TF-IDF features limited to 5,000 terms; deep learning models used learned embeddings over a 20,000-word vocabulary. Models were evaluated on the original imbalanced data and on a random-oversampled balanced set of 1,070,469 reviews, using accuracy, macro and per-class precision, recall, and F1-score, and training time. On the balanced set, Random Forest with BoW achieved 99\% accuracy and the Attention model achieved 98.7\%. Linear SVC reached 89\% accuracy in 1 min 15 s, and Logistic Regression reached 90\% in 3 min 37 s. On the imbalanced set, the Attention model achieved 97.8\% accuracy, and FastText achieved 95.3\% in 3 min 26 s, while the RNN reached 91.9\% with a neutral-class F1-score of 0.08. Deep learning models were more stable across class distributions, whereas the best classical model depended on balancing. We also report a user-facing application that applies the trained Random Forest and Attention models to new review text. Because the labels are derived from star ratings, the results measure agreement with rating-derived sentiment classes rather than annotated sentiment; the dataset is a single source, and the findings should be read with that limitation in mind.

title: An Agentic Python Framework for LLM-Driven UVM Testbench Synthesis with Closed-Loop Compiler Feedback
abstract: Protocol bridge verification is a persistent bottleneck in SoC development: for every new bridge instance, engineers hand-craft a full UVM testbench from scratch, consuming 40--100 engineering hours of bring-up effort. We present an agentic Python framework that generates complete, protocol-aware UVM testbenches for arbitrary IP and subsystem configurations from a structured Verification Manifest---a JSON specification encoding interface topology, protocol semantics, and coverage intent. The framework employs a dual closed-loop architecture: an inner compiler feedback loop that injects categorised UVM diagnostics rather than raw tool output, and an outer coverage loop driven by intent-gap analysis against the Manifest. Validated on the AMBA AHB-to-APB bridge---a representative production protocol bridge with a 7-state control FSM, two-phase APB handshake, and non-trivial burst serialisation logic---the framework achieves 96.8% functional coverage, a $4.7\times$ bring-up speedup, and a Protocol Verification Completeness score of 0.87, with only 2.1% of the generated 4,623-line testbench requiring human correction. The generated scoreboard independently identified a critical RTL functional fault that the manual baseline missed entirely. Generalisation across four protocol families confirms that speedup increases with protocol complexity, ranging from $3.1\times$ (APB Subordinate) to $6.1\times$ (CHI Subordinate).

title: Controlled Growth and Disorder Mitigation of GaAs1-xSbx/InAs Core-Shell Quantum Wires
abstract: We report the growth and transport properties of GaAs1-xSbx/InAs core-shell nanowires. Compared with the well-studied GaAs-InAs system, incorporating Sb substantially reduces the lattice mismatch between the core and shell. Accordingly, both the nanowire crystal quality and device performance improved significantly. Increasing x from 0.15 to 0.35, the density of crystalline defects, such as stacking faults in the InAs shell, decreases by half. Moreover, the field-effect mobility increases from 3850 cm2/Vs to 4800 cm2/Vs, consistent with the reduction of the lattice mismatch. The incorporation of Sb makes the nanowire easier to pinch off via the gate voltage, enhancing the electric field tunability over the nanowire.
